Eventually, Donald Trump purchased this for a song and it is where he periodically resides now. In essence, what Ms. Post wanted she got but not in the way she expected.

I found this book to be incredibly interesting. I did sometimes find it hard to follow with all the people and changes that were mentioned. I definitely do not remember most of this story, but now at least I know how Mar-a-Lago came about and how Donald Trump came to be the new owner.

title: A tale of two forgotten towns in Bayshore area of Cumberland County, New Jersey
text:
Hurricane Sandy made landfall in New Jersey in the fall of 2012 and Money Island and Bay Point located in the Bayshore area of Cumberland County, New Jersey were never rebuilt. Instead they are like ghost towns with only a resident or two remaining as of 2019.

I never heard of these shore towns on the New Jersey side of the Delaware Bay. I also thought it was mostly the ocean-side communities that were hardest hit. This author grew up in the Bayshore area and then left and came back to write this story. These towns were forgotten during Sandy's rebuild mostly due to the fact that it did not make economic sense to put money where tourism dollars were unlikely to be spent. Instead many homeowners sold out to the Blue Acres program that bought up the properties to turn it back into nature.

What I found very disconcerting was that the Health Department in Cumberland County started issuing violations to Sandy victims for septic failures that were either the result of years of decay or Sandy's storm damage. How can these poor victims pay for daily fines and fix issues when they do not even have the money to rebuild? We can always depend on the government to destroy a person further when victims are homeless due to no fault of their own. Although, I can understand that the cost benefit analysis of investing in infrastructure for "ghost towns" does not make economic sense, it also does not make sense that these towns were not even known by the bureaucrats when allocating funds. One has to be aware of a problem before it can be fixed.

In summary, I found this story to be very interesting and also sad. I am amazed at the fortitude of the couple of homeowners who remain behind and did not sell out (particularly Mike and Kate).

title: Educational and interesting stories of animal rescue work & author’s personal experience
text:
The author, Susannah Charleson, is a Search and Rescue Volunteer (SAR) who worked mostly with her dog Puzzle on locating missing, lost, and deceased persons. She has recently gotten into Missing Animal Response (MAR) work and is training her dog Ace on locating missing, lost, and deceased pets.

This book is a smattering of various interesting stories about her life and her rescue missions of various pets. She was brought up by two parents, who at a very young age, taught her to respect animals and lead by example in rescuing many homeless animals or owned animals who were just lost and needed help getting back home.

The end of the book provides an excellent list of what to do if your pet goes missing and how to prepare for such an event.

I learned that animals get loose when we think they never will. I also learned that making direct eye contact, calling out to them, or running after them actually does more harm than good and could result in getting them killed in traffic. She mentioned that many animals are found along the greenbelt which is the periphery of where land meets civilization. A lot of times animals are not far from home. Also, that wonderful pet at home acts very differently, if not aggressively when lost.

This was an excellent and enjoyable read to me. Other than the minor grammatical errors typical of a pre-release book, this author has certainly matured in her writing style since I read her first pre-release book, "The Scent of the Missing." Overall, this is well done.

title: This PREP book delivers on its goal to educate the newbie cook but on a higher level
text:
I read this from cover to cover, including all the recipes and am totally impressed. It is a small, thin book. There are just a few pages of basic guidelines and tools for the new cook. Most of what follows are recipes and they are step-by-step in an easy to understand form. Included with each recipe are the list of tools needed and some ideas and tips on how to elevate the meal to the next level. Included are salads, veges, meats, desserts, etc. Also the ingredients are by no means bland. There a plethora of spices in some recipes but not so much as to be overwhelming.

The two disappointments I have with this text are below.

First, the author never mentions that quinoa has to be washed BEFORE cooking and not AFTER. There are saponins in quinoa that cause a filmy and soapy taste, unless the quinoa is of the pre-washed kind. Instead, the recipe calls for washing after cooking--not a good idea if one is venturing beyond the step-by-step instructions and adding their own ingredients to the dish as it cooks.

Second, the author talks about making beans and using any kind. That is generally fine, but what is not fine is that there is no mention that kidney beans are poisonous (toxic) if not cooked correctly. The cooking method mentioned in the text for beans is not sufficient enough. I am sure there are other recommended methods but the best way to prepare them is to soak them overnight, drain the water, then boil them for ten minutes in more water to destroy the toxins, then drain and rinse again, and simmer them in fresh water for 45 to 60 minutes.

Other than the two caveats above which I feel is a must to mention in the text, this is an excellent primer for new high-school and college-aged cooks. I know I am going to keep it in my library for the simple recipes alone. I already made the exceedingly simple softly scrambled egg recipe which comes out great and I am looking forward to trying her version of French toast.

UPDATE 7/6/2019: I finally made the one-bowl chocolate chip cookies and they are very good. The recipe was exceptionally easy to follow and perfect for a college-aged adult who does not have many cooking implements. I attached two photos.

title: Four years of Rene Redzepi’s mission to discover the world’s culinary treasures
text:
René Redzepi is a Danish chef who co-owns Noma (now Noma 2.0), which is a restaurant in Copenhagen, Denmark. He invited the author on his quest to discover the best culinary flavors throughout the world and to publish this book about the effort. These discoveries, such as the worlds best mole, came at a price. He closed Noma (1.0) in order to create pop-up Nomas in Japan, Australia, and Mexico.

Most of this culinary story takes place in Mexico, whose eatable delicacies Redzepi loves. What I learned about this quest is the difficulty of foraging and procuring ingredients to make the best and most astonishing culinary delights possible. The author is a gifted writer in being able to weave a story that is somewhat lacking in substance but which I still found to be incredibly enjoyable. It is a journey of discovery of what the natural world can offer up that will excite our palate and also about the man and his disciples that formulate these culinary creations. The difficulty in finding superb ingredients and the stress associated with their use is front and center throughout this text.

title: A fictional diary of life from a husband’s death to a new beginning
text:
I tend to avoid fiction but I ordered this thinking it was a real story. At first I was disappointed in this book but after reading beyond the first few "diary" pages, I was pulled into the narrative like a fly on the wall.

This is a fictional diary written from the soon-to-be windows's point of view and takes place in Denmark. It starts with the main character's husband at the end of life and evolves into life after his death with occasional flashbacks to her younger self. I enjoyed the narrative and its evolution and read it in about six hours.

This novel would have received five stars from me if it was written in story format instead of diary entries and if it had more substance.

title: Ninja Foodi users will have to make adjustments with this air fryer book
text:
I ordered this book because I recently purchased a Ninja Foodi and it has an air fryer option besides being a pressure cooker, dehydrator, and slow cooker.

This text is thin but has a good overview on the best air fryers to buy and why they like a particular type of air fryer. It does not mention the Ninja Foodi at all. There are about 13 recipes in this cookbook that I would make. For this review, I decided to make the big Italian meatballs with zucchini noodles. It came out delicious and the prepared dish is shown in the last photo.

However, as I started to cook the meatballs, I realized the Foodi does not go lower than 300 degrees for the air fryer option. The recipe calls for 250 degrees. I did keep checking the meatballs during cooking. Unfortunately, I overcooked them just little bit on the last cycle that called for 160 degrees. They just came out a tiny bit dryer than they should have. Nevertheless, I was more successful with cooking the zucchini noodles since that required 400 degrees. The end result was delicious.

Note that the recipe called for salt and pepper but the amount of those two ingredients were listed in the text instead of the recipe so one has to be careful to read everything first.

In summary, this is a good air fryer recipe book. However, it is not written for someone who has a Ninja Foodi because the temperatures on the Foodi do not go as low as some of the recipes call for. Of course, one can make adjustments and keep watch over the cooking cycles to approximate the necessary cooking times in this situation.

title: Good primer for Office 2019 and some info is usable across other Office versions (like 2016)
text:
This is a good, yet basic primer for the Office 2019 suite of tools that include Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Access. In fact, a some of the instruction is usable across other Office Versions such as 2016.

Part 1, which is the first two chapters, goes over just basic information on copying and pasting, modifying pictures, drawing, etc. This was actually the part I was disappointed with the most because the text leaves out which software package is being used for the examples provided. I just used the text as a guide (not necessarily verbatim) and created an outline of the image that is on Page 58 of the book (see photo). However, I should have used PowerPoint and not Word to do it. It was unclear to me until I looked at Figure 3-15 that the author was using PowerPoint.

Other than this, the other sections are dedicated to each tool and the instructions are step-by-step. Unless one wants to go through all the basic functionality of each package, this book is best used as a reference with the help of the Table of Contents and the Index.

title: I could not relate to the first 42 pages but as I read on, I found many inspiring quotes
text:
The author starts each chapter by writing a letter to his baby daughter, which is very touching. What follows those letters, are small words of wisdom. Unfortunately, none of the quotes before page 42 resonated with me and many others throughout the book are equally cryptic. However, after page 42, the inspiring messages to his daughter and us increased exponentially. As a result, this book is a gem for those about thirty quotes I found that made perfect sense. If it were not for those messages, I would have been disappointed in this book.

INSPIRING EXAMPLES:

"Thinking big but acting small is the same thing as thinking small."

"Only do those things you want to do with whom you want to do them"

"Dimming your light in sadness or empathy over the suffering of others doesn't help anyone"

"Nothing you might ever do can ensure anyone else's happiness."

title: By degrading the victims, we glorify the criminal
text:
This author gets 100 stars for the extensive research she had to do to produce this book. Her intention is to dispel the myth that all five victims of Jack the Ripper were prostitutes. Even if they were, none of them deserved to die. Only one of the five was a known prostitute and one of the others dabbled in it. In the Victorian era, poor, homeless, or drunken women were sort of considered dispensable--as if it is no big deal that they died.

However, we glorify Jack the Ripper by remembering the serial murderer, promoting the falsehood that they were all prostitutes, and forgetting the victims -- who were mothers, daughters, sisters, wives and humans whose life was no less valuable than anyone else's life.

The author sets the era and place at the start of the book. At first I was a bit lost in understanding why I was reading that but then I realized she was just setting the stage to tell each of their stories. The stories are unfortunate and very sad. It is easy for us to blame the women so that somehow we can justify that what happened was not so bad. However, we would be wrong. Instead, we must remember them and know no matter what their situation, a worthy life was lost.

These are the women that should be remembered:

1) Mary Ann "Polly" Nichols
2) Annie Chapman
3) Elisabeth Stride
4) Catherine Eddowes
5) Mary Jane Kelly

title: Intensely aromatic Moroccan recipes full of spices & ingredients
text:
I read this book from cover to cover and most recipes seem very healthy to me but they include many ingredients and lots of spice and other aromatics.

This is mostly a straight up recipe book with only an intro story and a descriptive paragraph preceding each recipe. There are many recipes that call for ingredients not normally in my cabinet such as preserved lemons, chermoula paste, harissa, etc. Nevertheless, I found several I could make with what I had on hand.

I decided to make the Harira Soup because it looked delicious and wholesome. There were 22 ingredients in this recipe but only 21 for me since I left out the cumin seeds as I dislike that spice immensely. I attached a photo of most of the ingredients in this recipe. The soup came out absolutely delicious. It was very aromatic with a blend of wonderful flavors. I would definitely make this again and again and again (see last picture).

This book also includes desserts, salads, etc. There is only one chapter dedicated to cooking in a tagine but unfortunately, most of those recipes call for a Dutch oven, slow cooker, etc. This is disappointing to me as a tagine is the cooking implement I think of for Morocco. Nevertheless, there are several recipes I might try one day in this book, no tagine necessary.

Overall, I am pleased with the selection I can choose from even though these recipes take time and are the furthest from bland. The fact that I also consider most of these dishes healthy is an added bonus.

title: Healthful advice with mostly smoothie and Japanese / Asian influenced recipes
text:
I enjoy reading health books and books about healthful ingredients for the mind and body. This recipe book contains recipes ingredients that are designed to give a person a healthful glow and keep them looking younger. However, the healthy advice is really for the entire body.

I read this cover to cover and made a couple of recipes so far. I usually prefer to eat my food and drink water most of the time. In essence, I am not really a smoothie person. However, the "yellow" smoothie I made (see first two pictures) came out good. I should have used water instead of milk. It called for a plant-based milk but I used regular milk and that is not really a good idea when lemon is involved in the ingredient. Nevertheless it tasted good.

I also made the miso with mushroom, sweet potato, and tofu soup (last two pictures) and that was delicious. I would have reduced the miso paste by half, however, because I found it salty. Of course for these and the other recipes I will be trying, I had to buy all sorts of stuff I did not have in my house, like tofu, dried mushrooms, miso paste, vanilla powder, ginger, etc.

After reading the recipes, I would make about 15% of them. To me a book is a keeper if I find two good recipes in it and there are more than that in this text. However, these recipes are not for everyone. I had to be willing to go beyond my comfort zone in mixing all these ingredients together. I normally eat very healthy but Asian-influenced and smoothie-based staples are not something I carry in my house nor am I use to eating at home.

title: Excellent recipe book more for the "seasoned" home cook with a smattering of tool tips
text:
I have mixed feelings about this book that I have been reading and reviewing for the last 35+ days. On one hand it is five stars because it is chock full of wonderfully rich recipes, two of which I made (pictured - Tortilla Espanola ala Michelle and Pots de Creme). On the other hand it is also full of great recommendations for essential kitchen tools but which are more for the slightly advanced cooks.

I actually had to buy stuff, such as this [[ASIN:B0023PVZD6 Scanpan CTX 12-3/4-Inch Covered Chef's Pan]], [[ASIN:B072BRFK2N HERBS DE PROVENCE]], and several other items in order to make the recipes because they were not part of my kitchen arsenal and I have a tremendous amount of cooking tools.

The book starts out with which rolling pin is the best and moves on from there to recipes using a rolling pin and techniques on how to roll noodles, etc. She also provides cooking tips with some of the recipes, many of which I never heard of. For example, on troubleshooting slurry, you need a small amount of liquid with cornstarch whisked in instead of sprinkling it on which creates a lumpy slurry. Personally, I do not even know what slurry is and she does not explain it. It is apparently a semi-liquid mixture per my Internet search.

I do wish she defined things more so the novice cook would understand what is meant. For example, when I was making the Pots de Creme recipe, she says to simmer until "steam starts to wisp around the edges." I had to assume it was when bubbles formed around the edge because my boyfriend and I never saw any steam around the edges.

In summary, this is an absolutely fabulous book that is a great complement to a well-stocked cooking library. It is NOT for the novice cook but for one who is more seasoned or wants to become so. The recipes are stupendous and rich. My boyfriend was blown away by both of the ones I made. It has more recipes than tips, in my opinion. I also would have preferred pictures of some tools (like the spider she recommends; I did not even know what kitchen tool that was). In addition, a glossary of some terms would be great as well. Nevertheless, the only reason I rated this 4 stars is because the title of the book is not true to what is inside. It is more cookbook than anything and the tools are not for the home cook but are more for the more ADVANCED cook in my opinion. I also would expect a book with this title to start with utensils such as knives, forks, pots, and pans instead of rolling pins, sheet pans, cast iron, etc. in that order.

title: A totally FICTION work that makes me wonder what genetics humans will steal from other species in order to achieve perfection
text:
This book is absolutely nothing like I expected. After reading that this novel is "An alternately charming and horrifying exploration of what it means to be human and how far we'll go in pursuit of personal and societal 'perfection," I thought I was going to read a non-fiction work exploring what people do to themselves (plastic surgery, implants, designer babies, use of stem cells, sperm donation, etc.) to enhance their appearance or have a "designer" child. However, this is NOT that at all. Instead "Stronger, Faster, and More Beautiful ..." is a FICTION work of some phantasmal creation in the author's psyche where she explores several scenarios (she says six but I thought there were more) of how people alter themselves over time.

The book starts out with a boy and girl who are semi-identical twins. I got the impression that they were once co-joined but cannot be absolutely certain from the story. However, the boy lives and the girl dies but the boy gets her parts (heart, liver, part of her large intestine, kidneys, and pancreas). From this story evolves several more chapters of other stories whereby near the end of the book we have humans with bird wings, extra toes and eyes and legs, moving tattoos, etc., etc.

I found the first few chapters difficult to follow but after I got into the book, I absolutely loved it and could barely put it down. I personally avoid reading FICTION unless I am tricked. In this case I was tricked by that one introductory sentence above. Nevertheless, this novel makes one think that the human race could eventually evolve into this and to some extent we are not far off. Just Google the artist Simon Huck who produces fake human "skin" implants that the stars like Kim Kardashian wear as jewelry and it is like "experiencing" a prelude to this book.

title: This book's intention is to get everyone talking about death and not making it such a taboo topic
text:
I am one of those people who has been consumed with thinking about death since a very young age and those thoughts have increased as I get older. What this book does is get people thinking and talking about death. The author hosts death dinners where people discuss death.

I think it's wonderful in the way he may start a dinner by saying "Before we eat, I would love if we could each honor someone who is no longer with us, someone who has died who had a positive impact on your life." To me this is a wonderful idea. He provides many examples in the book about how some people faced death. Some even go so far as to have a living funeral where their family and friends eulogize the living person so that they can be in attendance. In one instance, a man requested a living funeral the day before he was scheduled to die via a death with dignity request.

Many people avoid the subject of death but this seems to increase the physical and emotional pain the dying person experiences. We are all going to die and I believe we can die in peace if we find a way to express our wishes, discuss our concerns, and basically wrap up all our emotional business before we leave this life.

title: A remarkable and somewhat speculative account of the February 1856 sinking of the John Rutledge & its lone survivor
text:
This is a remarkable recreation from historical accounts and the author's speculation of what happened when the John Rutledge sank on a voyage from Liverpool to New York in February of 1856. The author creates a narrative around historical accounts he gathered during his research. He used his imagination to effectively describe what experiencing this tragedy might have been like. Thomas W. Nay was the only survivor who was rescued by the ship Germania.

The story sets the stage with a prologue about the lives of some of the crew before the John Rutledge set sail. Some parts of this narrative were a bit mundane but the remainder of the book was mostly riveting. I was impressed with the author's ability to weave a tale around such a horrific tragedy that was typical in those times.

title: Healthy herb book with esoteric ingredients & geared to a niche user
text:
I love to read health books and this one on adaptogens is in that category. Unfortunately, this text is really geared to select users.

A herb has to be considered both non-toxic and safe for extended use to be called an adaptogen. Adaptogens are used to help the body resist physical, chemical, and biological stressors and have been used for centuries in China and India.

Prior to reading this book, I never heard of an adaptogen. Only ginseng, astragalus, licorice, and nettle were ones I heard of and sampled before. The author provides a brief summary of many others such as ashwagandha, tulsi, jiaogulan, maca, rhodiola, shatavari, etc.

I read this from cover to cover but there is not one recipe that I am interesting in trying now. There are only four recipes that I might consider trying in the future and they are the night garden sachets for improving sleep, raspberry & rhodiola chia yogurt for improving mental focus, or matcha & peach chia seed pudding with gynostemma also for improving mental focus. The only recipe that comes close to anything in a cookbook is the roasted sweet potatoes with rosemary but even then that requires powdered rosemary and not the fresh kind.

In addition, these herbs are not ones that I have access to nor are they always easily attainable. However, for those who are interested in making recipes or potions with these ingredients, this book is superb in its explanation and guidance. Besides describing each herb, there are sections for all sorts of issues like improving mood, men's and women's health, immune function, hair/skin/nails, stamina/energy, etc.

Overall, this is both a good reference source, tutorial, and recipe book on adaptogens, but it is just not for me.

title: The author goes on a quest to find himself by biking from Oregon to Patagonia
text:
I ordered this book not knowing that the author, Jedidiah, is the son of Peter and Barbara Jenkins who wrote the book "Walk Across America" that I read and so absolutely loved.

Jedidiah sets off on a bike trip from Oregon to Patagonia. In an effort to appease his mother, he travels with a guy named Weston that he recently met at work. The two men have different life philosophies to an extent but both have the quest to try something different. Jedidiah felt there was more to life than just working and wanted to experience living instead of just letting life pass by him.

He is gay and partially religious and spends a lot of the journey contemplating both. Weston on the other hand is spontaneous, heterosexual, ill-prepared, and without much money (other than what he squirreled away to buy dope). They both experience challenges on the road but nothing too earth shattering. Their trip is a combination of biking, buses, boats, and hitch hiking to get where they are going.

In the end, Jedidiah winds up finishing the bike trip alone when Weston goes away to Hawaii for a wedding and decides not to return. To the author this is both a blessing and disappointment. I enjoyed being the "bird in the sky" experiencing his adventure through his story. The section where he travels to Macchu Picchu, writes about his in-depth religious discussions with an acquaintance, and recites a portion of the book "The Conquest of the Incas" by John Hemming was the only part of his tale that bored me. Other than this, I thoroughly enjoyed going along for the ride even though nothing contained within was over-the-top riveting. It is just a good story about a 1-1/2 year bike trip with the author and periodically some of his family, friends, and thoughts.

title: This book may resonate with mothers who have lost a newborn, but not every reader will appreciate the story's chaotic style
text:
The author lost one of her premature twin sons shortly after birth and this book is about her loss. Her story and grief process is written in a chaotic style, many times fluttering from one thought to the next with limited cohesiveness. However, this chaotic thought process will probably resonate with those who have experienced the loss of a child, especially a newborn. Some of her story I could relate to even though I never lost a child. The reader will understand what it is like to experience thoughtless comments from those who know nothing of her misery or who want to avoid thinking about it because it causes them pain. I can relate because when my best friend (who also happened to be an ex-boyfriend) committed suicide by hanging himself in his bedroom, I was treated to thoughtless comments by others such as "wow that must have been a high ceiling." Of course, there are those who react appropriately, but that is less often the case.

In summary, some mothers who have lost a newborn or young child will be able to truly feel that someone else has experienced what they are going through. However, not everyone will relate to the chaotic style in which this is written. It is not so much a succinct tale from beginning to end as it is several short stories with jumbled thoughts thrown in-between that really demonstrates the upheaval and utter sadness such a death imposes on the mother.

title: A mostly excellent book that will guide a perfectionists into accepting both their strengths and faults
text:
I ordered this book thinking it was about detoxifying one's body from poor nutritional choices. However, this is a self-help book about accepting yourself and moving forward positively and without fear instead of striving for perfection.

This text went from a 3-star book to a 5-star book as the story progressed. The first couple of chapters were about the author telling the reader that she was a perfectionist and that the text that follows will allow the reader to be detoxed from perfectionism. I thought I was reading an infomercial and kept hoping the author would keep her promise. Eventually, she did.

Once I got into this book, I loved it. She provides wonderful insights on how we can embrace our imperfect self and provides daily detox methods at the end of each chapter that we can work on. There were many quotes in the book that resonated with me and here are two of them.

1 - Acceptance is not about ignoring our weaknesses, but instead requires a shift in how we react to our imperfections and mistakes.

2 - She reiterates a quote from a therapist she knows, "Forgiveness is not letting people off the hook (including yourself) for doing unforgivable things, but it is about unhooking yourself from the negative actions of the past so they do not affect your positive future."

There are many excellent points in the chapters of this book. Self-acceptance is about balancing your strengths and doubts--be curious, be free from fear, live in the moment, focus on the positives, exercise for fun not for the scale, etc. etc.

Overall, the is an enjoyable read once the reader gets a few chapters in.

title: After reading this, I feel like wildlife trafficking will never be eliminated no matter how much we educate the human race
text:
I spent every evening over two full weeks reading this book. This is neither an easy read nor a quick one. The author believes in conservation and letting wildlife live out their lives in nature where they belong. In this text she describes her extensive personal travels to Africa (Chad, South Africa, etc.) and Asia (Loas, Thailand, Vietnam, etc.) in search of all the animals served as food and used for medicine or illegal trade. She expertly describes the plight of the abundant poached wildlife without becoming overly gruesome except in a couple of rare cases. Asians, Africans, Americans, etc. and the top echelon of society partake in Pangolin for meat and scales, elephants for ivory, rhino horn for medicine, civet for meat, bear for bile, etc. etc. Many believe with a religious ferocity that these animal parts cure various ailments. Others do not believe it but feel superior in being able to dominate an animal by hunting or just because they want to eat something exotic.

The author tries very hard to describe the complexity of why illegal animal hunting continues and she does a pretty good job. Sometimes measures taken to help an animal wind up hurting it via a bending of the rules imposed by CITES (the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) or the regulations of a particular country. On the positive side, she also mentions the good work of a couple of sanctuaries helping to save some of these animals, but it appears to be a revolving door with no elimination in site.

Most of what is written in this book I already knew. However I did learn a few things. For instance, I thought all animal medicine was hocus-pocus but bear bile actually works. However, a synthetic form works just as well, so there is no need to use bears. It is the high concentration of ursodeoxycholic acid in the bile which may slow the progression of some diseases; however, one may get sick form the bile because it is full of other things like pus, etc. as a result of the harvesting. It never ceases to amaze me how humans can be so utterly cruel.

Overall, I am glad Rachel Love Nuwer wrote this book. It was a difficult read both due to the subject matter and also due to so many facts and places she visited that caused me to re-read passages to ensure I understood what was being said.

title: A versatile academic planner that is a good choice among many available on the market
text:
This is a nice academic calendar with several neat features and a couple I do not understand. If counting the ring binder, the dimensions are 7.5" by 9" and it is almost an inch thick.

NEAT FEATURES
- There are monthly tabs for each weekly and monthly calendar sections.
- The monthly calendars have generous proportioned squares.
- There are quotes, etc. peppered on the bottom of some of the calendar sheets.
- There's a double sided pocket in front for storage.
- A property label is on the inside front cover.
- A holiday, reference (includes 2020 planning section, emergency numbers, etc.), and notes section are included.
- The notes section has perforated "Post-It-sized" sections for easy removal.
- This comes with an attached elastic band that can be used to keep the planner shut.

FEATURES I AM UNCLEAR HOW TO USE OR DO NOT FIND USEFUL
- There are a couple of sheets of stickers in the back. I guess these can be used to highlight certain calendar entries.
- There's a habit tracker sheet in front of each month section. I'm not really sure what to do with this or even how to use it. If I already have a habit, then it is well established and I do not need to track what day of the week I performed that task.

Overall, I like this planner. The binder is a little bit sticky initially but after a bit of use, it turns easier. I think this is a good choice among many other good and competitively priced alternatives on the market.

title: "Cancerland" is more about how the science of cancer has evolved than anything else from one doctor's point of view
text:
The Amazon description that states "A doctor’s riveting story of loss and hope in the world of cancer. What is it like to encounter cancer? How does it feel to face the unknown, to enter a world of hope, loss, and dread?" lead me to believe that this book was more about individual stories of cancer patients one doctor has encountered over his career and its emotional toll on patient, doctor, and family. However, this book is not about that at all.

It is true that Dr. Scadden knew of three people who died of cancer when he was a child living in Wykcoff, New Jersey. One was a friend's mother, then a lady neighbor, and the third was a classmate in second grade. His mother and father also died of cancer when he was an adult. Other than this and a few mentions of people who have been cured of cancer or died as a result of this or that trial, he really discusses how cancer research has evolved over the years.

This is a book more about the science of cancer than anything else and how various researchers or doctors made scientific discoveries as it concerns cancer or stem cells. Unfortunately, this was not the type of book I was expecting or would have selected to read had I known what was inside. Nevertheless, it is written in an engaging manner and is easy for a lay person to understand. Although I am unable to maintain any knowledge of the science, doctors, and researchers involved in this or that discovery, I did learn several things from this text.

- First, cancer is extremely complex and the treatment is just as complicated.

- Second, not everyone responds to the same therapy. Some people have cancers with a genetic profile that makes them more susceptible to a specific drug regimen or cure.

- Some therapies that seem promising in the beginning can turn out to not be such a breakthrough in the end.

- In some cases, finding the cells that can fight cancer and regenerating them outside the body and then injecting them back into the body, can cure cancer for particular patients. This is the gist of what I understood.

- The research done on mice does not necessarily translate to humans. Human stem cells may be the answer to solve this dilemma (and perhaps save a few mice from suffering in the future--my hope, not the author's).

- Stem cells hold tremendous promise in the cure for cancer and other medical disciplines such as generating certain organs. Dr. Harald Ott invented a method of working with cells that allowed other researchers to develop human heart muscle cells in a lab that beat like a human heart. Of course, this technique is in its infancy, but the potential is profound.

- Despite how detached a doctor may seem when they loose a patient, all (or at least most) are saddened by the loss.

It comes through loud and clear in this book that Dr. Scadden is an M.D. (no longer practicing) that is now passionate about doing scientific work with blood stem cells to try to find some cure for cancer or at least to explore its potential in reducing human suffering. I believe it consumes him.

Even though I expected something different from this book than what was delivered, I still enjoyed getting a better understanding of what goes on behind the scenes in research. I do feel, however, "Cancerland" will be of more interest to medical researchers, scientists, and those enthusiastic about the historical evolution in search of a cancer cure and not as much interest to a lay person like me.

title: Techniques for promoting & capitalizing on one's business & brand mostly for free on TV
text:
Areva Martin is a civil rights attorney whose "brand" is associated with "promoting" women's, children's (special needs like autism), and political / celebrity issues. She uses mostly TV broadcasting coupled with social media as a way to capitalize and promote that brand. In this book she provides snippets of what has worked for her. She stresses the importance of staying on point --meaning do not post anything that does not relate to your brand.

As I was reading this I was trying to formulate examples in my head of how I could formulate my brand if I were so inclined to do so. If I started out talking about vacuums one day, tea infusers the next, and then steamers another day, no one would associate me with any one thing. I would be sending a confusing message to people that would lead them to question "What does she do exactly"? Instead, the brand I should be promoting would be that I am a reviewer of consumer products. People would then associate reviews to me and would come to eventually know that I have a special interest in reviewing teas, tea products and implements, steamers, etc. Once I formulate my brand, then I would have to put in a lot of legwork to see what would work for me. I would need to see which target audience I want to pitch, which show producer is most likely to be receptive to my pitch, etc., etc.

Overall, this is a book not only about formulating a brand but about how one goes about popularizing it mostly via free TV. The social media side of the advice is tied mostly to using it to get that TV appearance. One must do their homework, use social media like google alerts and google trends to stay on top of current events and hot button issues that might relate to their brand, network with others, etc. so that they can pitch a producer at the right time. The timing of a social media post is key whether it be on Twitter, Instagram, or Facebook. It is also important to put in a lot of effort cultivating the brand, learning who the producers are of shows that might be interested in it, determining how that brand might be tied into some current event with a twist not discussed by other experts on the show, etc., etc., etc. "Make it Rain" provides some great advice to those who what to pursue this avenue of "advertisement" and should be one of several resources consulted on how to go about doing this. Overall, this is a highly recommended read but should not be the only read.

title: A nurse's story raw with emotion and detail on what life is like behind the scenes in a British hospital
text:
This is a British written story and so the writing style is a little different. A "theatre" is the operating room. A&E is Accident and Emergency in Great Britain, meaning the Emergency Department. In addition, I found the first chapter, which is a tale leading up to her nursing career, a slow and un-engaging lead into an otherwise great book about the author.

The author is a nurse that works mostly with children. She spares no details when expressing what it was like for her. It is obvious she cares deeply about the patients she tends to and after reading this text, I walked away with a more in-depth view of what goes on behind the scenes in nursing. If I were considering a nursing career, this story would provide a very good idea of what it is like to care for others and the various atrocities they see daily. Overall, I enjoyed the story and in many cases felt like a fly on the wall assisting her with her duties.

In her book, Christie says "Promoting dignity in the face of illness is one of the best gifts a nurse can give." Based on the story I read here, she certainly has met that standard.

title: These authors dispel wolf myths by sharing their stories of their life with the wolves of the Sawtooth pack
text:
Thirty years ago, Jim and Jamie Dutcher set out to film and learn about wolves by creating a secluded and contained wolf camp below the Sawtooth Mountains of Idaho. For six years they studied these wolves until their permits ran out as a result of locals lodging anti-wolf complaints. Each chapter is alternately written by Jim or Jamie in a way that describes a particular wolf experience or set of behaviors. For example, I learned that wolves will not attack farm animals unless they are use to eating that type of meat. The authors told a story of wolves who are seen running in the same fields as cows without attacking them but yet will attack the deer in the same fields.

It is clear from this text that wolves are emotional animals and the pack works as one cohesive unit for the safety of all. They grieve, play, and experience emotion just like we do. Even though the stories were matter-of-fact in some cases and not told in any particular consecutive timeline, I enjoyed learning about wolves through these authors' eyes.

title: Excellent advice for educational coaches helping others evolve into great leaders except I am unable to visualize the how
text:
This is an excellent guide for guidance counselors and other coaches who need to help others evolve into great leaders. The take away for me is that great leaders must attain those skills not by being told what to do but by having them take part in the coaching process and being the ones who turn themselves into great leaders through effective coaching. It is important for those being coached not to be dismissed, ridiculed, etc. The coach must listen so that the coachee can grow. Evolving into a great leader is a lifelong journey both for the coach and the coachee.

This book also highlights that coaches should not be too tied to a specific outcome (from those they coach) because they may be met with resistance. A leader should remember to LEAD (listen, empathize, appreciate, design).

There is a lot of good advice in this book; however, to me it reads almost like a textbook. Although I enjoyed reading this (and I read it from cover to cover, even the Appendix), I feel this information is only one part of what is necessary to be an effective leader. The other part is to actually see someone put this into action and this book (the text and limited examples) did not resonate enough with me where I could visual how to take action effectively.

title: Thought-provoking book that may enable caretakers & those in the helping profession embrace the pain & provide compassion
text:
The author is a counselor (psychotherapist, mentor, and clinical supervisor) to those in the helping profession (priests, nurses, doctors, other counselors, non-professional caretakers, etc.). Wicks teaches others so subtly how to take care of oneself from the perspective of how he learned to do that over the years. He also uses the appendix to provide more direct reflections.

One of several observations he made in the book that resonated with me is this quote. "Pacing ourselves in how we deal with what is painful around us is not running away. It is respecting that the self is limited and can only deal with so much." This means to me that we must face any pain we cannot avoid but do so slowly and in a controlled way without becoming so overwhelmed that we cannot function. In order words, it is okay to take a break from the pain but we must not ignore it. We must be able to handle it in a way that enables us to help without compromising ourselves

I thoroughly enjoyed his book because he uses his own personal experience to get the message across subtly. To me anyone can benefit by reading this, especially those who are in the helping professions or caretaker role.

title: Both an autobiography and a message of kindness to breach bullying conveyed in a "matter-of-fact" style
text:
Lizzie Velasquez is a motivational speaker with a rare congenital disease that has resulted in immense ridicule and cruelty in her young life. Her book is a compilation of the importance of kindness interspersed with various tidbits of her own story. The intention of this book is to teach others not to bully someone else just because they are different. Her other intention is to instill a sense of acceptance of oneself and to show that one can be happy despite their circumstances.

This is a lighthearted read and I enjoyed it. I believe in her message immensely but that message was conveyed in a "matter of fact" style. I truly feel that if there were more depth of emotion infused into this book her message would be so much more impactful.

title: Most, but not all, of the information I needed as a novice canner was in this book; my results were a resounding success
text:
I never canned before but always wanted to and getting this book was my opportunity to try it. As a novice, I looked to this book to provide ALL the guidance I needed and it just fell a little bit short for me.

First, I spent about 120 hours over 15 days (weekends and late evenings) procuring supplies, reading through the book, and making numerous jams.

I purchased the following tools for the job. Note that I already had a 16-quart stockpot, a canning funnel (never it knew it was a canning funnel but now I know), a ladle, and a wooden spoon along with various other kitchen utensils and pots I used.

I purchased one dozen Kerr Wide Mouth Half-Pint Mason Jars from Walmart

[[ASIN:B001DIZ1NO Ball Mason "PINT" Jars Wide-Mouth Can or Freeze - 12pk (by Jarden Home Brands)]]

[[ASIN:B013L5N8U4 Ball Collection Elite Half Pint Jars, Wide Mouth, Set of 4]]

[[ASIN:B01AAHHB9A Ball Regular Mouth Elite Collection Half Pint Jars, Blue (4-Pack)]]

[[ASIN:B01AAHHB5E Ball Jelly Elite Collection Jam Jar (4 Pack), 8 oz, Clear]]

[[ASIN:B00CAXLIF6 Ball Bubble Remover & Head Space Tool]]

[[ASIN:B007QT4GO4 Prepworks by Progressive Reversible Stainless Steel Canning Rack]]

[[ASIN:B00FRQVKRY Progressive Ckc-100 One Handed Jar Lifter]]

[[ASIN:B0000CFMPQ Norpro Magnetic Lid Wand]]

[[ASIN:B007CRHP4I Ball Jar Sure Tight Band Tool]] - necessary for me to tighten the lids to fingertip tight

[[ASIN:B00B80TK2K Ball Mason 4oz Quilted Jelly Jars with Lids and Bands, Set of 12]]

[[ASIN:B00004UE88 Norpro Stainless Steel Wide-Mouth Funnel w/ Handle]]

Besides procuring the above it took me hours to find the fruit (and pectin) and eventually I gave up and settled on more typical fruit. In addition to the typical fruits, I wanted to make the sour cherry jam and meyer lemon marmalade but could not find these items in any store.

Once I had all my supplies, I spent several evenings canning with the help of this book and the Internet, as some info I needed was missing. I made two batches of bing cherry, a mixed berry (raspberry and strawberry), blackberry, blueberry, peach, and strawberry jams. They all came out successfully. On my first batch, I had a mishap because I did not know how to work the Ball Jar Sure Tight Band tool that I needed to for me, but which the book did not list.

As a "Back to Basics" book, I expected it to be more hands on. These are some of the issues I have with this guide:

- First it lists the tools in one section and then in the next section it says that not many tools are needed for canning. This is not true. Even though I had a few of the items, I spent almost $125 on canning tools above including jars not counting the over $50 I spent on fruit and 25 pounds of sugar.

- Second the section on how to make jams, preserves,etc. says that one has to remove the air bubbles in the jam (Page 23) but never says how to do this. I had to look up a YouTube video. However, on Page 145 in the section on how to can tomatoes it shows how to do this. Also, the same section says the jars have to be pre-heated but never said the jars have to be fully submerged in the water; I had to find that out online as well when the empty jars started floating on me like debris in a swimming pool.

- Third, the mixed berry recipe on page 40 indicates any combination of berries (strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and/or raspberries) can be used. At the bottom it also says the same recipe can be used with just one of the berries like raspberries or strawberries. However, when I was going to make the recipe with just blueberries, I realized there was a blueberry recipe on Page 34. Apparently, blueberries need lemon to be added but no mention is made of that in the mixed berry recipe. I would have expected it to say if you use blueberries alone, then add 2 tablespoons of lemon or follow the recipe on Page 34.

- Fourth, I wanted to can tomatoes and when reading the "how to" section (Page 144), I noticed lemon juice is need. The instructional picture shows someone who just squeezed fresh lemons, yet the recipes call for bottled lemon juice. I could not find a reason why in the book so I went online and found that one should not use fresh squeezed lemons because the acidity is not guaranteed like with bottled lemon juice. (See note to article in comments section of this review.)

These are just some of the inconsistencies I found in the text. Nevertheless, with a little help from Google, I was able to clear up any misunderstanding I had. This book would have gotten five stars if all the information was included. I was able to turn out over 30+ jars of various jam with resounding success.

Attached is a picture of one of the batches of my jam cooling for the evening. I will attach links to my reviews of the items mentioned above as soon as they get posted.

title: Fun conversation starters; enables friends or family get to know each other more
text:
I purchased both the ([[ASIN:0981994644 More Chat Pack Cards: New Questions to Spark Fun Conversations]] and the [[ASIN:0975580167 Chat Pack: Fun Questions to Spark Conversations]] (this set) to add variety to my vacation time with my boyfriend. Both he and I liked how these cards stimulated conversations and allowed us to think and get to know details about each other that we did not know even though we have been together for 15 years.

Each card is the size of a tiny Post-It note at 1 inch x 3-1/2 inches. In this package are questions such as:

- Thinking back to all the great TV series finales that you have seen over the years, which show do you believe had the best final episode?
- If snow could fall in any flavor, what flavor would you choose?
- Which age, when you turned it, was the most difficult for you to accept?

Some questions made us think on the fly and make stuff up. This means that if we were answering this question again, we would give a different answer because we never actually thought about that particular question. There are some questions that were difficult to answer. For instance, I do not watch TV or movies much so I could not answer any questions related to the best movie sequel because I did not know any. One is encouraged to change up the questions if necessary.

Overall, we found this both fun and entertaining and only got though part of each pack. We're saving the rest of the pack for the next vacation or time together.
