title: Nice Nostalgic Look at the Films
text: In reality this is kind of an inane book, but it is visually stunning and brings back lots of memories, good and bad, about the franchise.  From remembering what it was like in 1977 watching New Hope for the first time to wincing through anything Annikan related.  It was a walk through the last 40+ years for me, and as long as a fan keeps their expectations in line, I think anyone can enjoy flipping through this book.  Perhaps the lists are meant to start a little debate and a little hard core fact checking.  It's a fun book for the Star Wars fan.

title: Good Learning Tool for Complete Beginners
text: This might have been much too low level for our family.  We love to collect Spanish language books and we have found that it is the absolute best way to increase vocabulary, but this book might have been far to young for us.  It is very, very basic with colors and shapes and perhaps more suitable as a toddler coloring book.  I'm sure it is perfect in the right hands but unfortunately not the right fit for us.

title: Got a Sample and it was Intriguing
text: I received a sample section of this book and I have to say that it does have some intriguing qualities.  The art work is spare and not the most masterful, but definitely works well.  Combined with spare text, the reader is pulled through the pages and I was left at the end of the sample way too soon.  I only have a hint at the plot but I am interested enough that I would love to finish the book when it comes out.  I am a little disappointed to have just a little taste of the book, but it holds promise.

title: A Decent Vegetarian Cookbook
text: This is a good cookbook with a nice amount of introductory information to start looking at a vegetarian lifestyle.  The recipes look good but I was a little disappointed that there are no photos or illustrations.  Personally, I need to have photos to inspire me into making a recipe. I mildly recommend this book for anyone looking to start a plant based diet, but I recommend other books to go along with it.

title: Interesting Story Of Relationships, Romantic and Platonic, and Confused
text: I really liked how well the characters were flushed out in this book.  The story is pretty tried and true and as old as civilisation, but well told.  The setting was pretty much now with a quarter cup of magic and witchcraft.  There were familiars and spells and magick schools, but the magik always kept in the background and actually could be lifted out with no change to the story.  The artwork is fresh and fun, although not flattering for the main character. The pages flew by.  A great novel of finding yourself in the world of newly adult relationships.

title: good Book but did not live up to hopes
text: I'm glad I got this book, but I was a little underwhelmed when it did not live up to my expectations as a "masterclass." I was hoping for far more instructional, step by step.  What it is is 100 projects done by 100 accomplished artists with a description of their one piece and basics on their technique.  It is not bad, but it is when compared to other idea and skill building books I got at the same time.  I still gleaned a lot of inspiration, and it was well worth the time, but did not live up to my hopes for a masterclass book.

title: OKay Idea Generator, but needs photos
text: I am and omnivore living with vegetarians and I am always looking for workable plant based solutions.  This book has a number of ideas that I will explore, but there are not a whole lot of eye opening ones.  Unfortunately, I am apparently not enough of a visionary to know what something should look like, so I kind of need photos to inspire me a bit.  I do wish that this series of cookbooks had better photos, but still get a lot of value out of them.

title: A Quaint Picture Book with a Small Plot
text: So we have a wonderful Spanish Learning library for our four middle grade Spanish learners and I feel wonderfully blessed to have a good library of children's books from Cuenta de Luz publishing.  I was super excited to get another reviewer book to add to it.  Imagine my surprise when I paged through it and there was not a single word of text in the book.  Oh well, it is a nice little story with wonderful and lighthearted illustrations of a dog encountering a flurry of birds that "gift" it with a flower. Perfect for very young readers, not so good for learning new vocabulary and verb tenses.  So this is the weakest book in the series for us, but we still love nearly everything from Cuenta de Luz, the stories are quirky and they have served as great learning books.  Keep up the good work, but make sure you keep text in the books!

title: A Great Find For Us
text:
We have a couple vegetarians that will be moving off to college in a few years. This book looked like a perfect way to start preparing them for life on their own. I love that there is a good variety of recipes here that are for the most part pretty easy. Somethings might be a little advanced for a starter apartment or dorm, but there are so many good ideas. We are starting now to get them in the habit of making balanced meals. Hopefully this will inspire a lot of meals.

The one gripe I have about it is that it is not particularly well illustrated. That is my biggest beef with most cookbooks. I lack the imagination to know what something will or should look like when I make it. And a good picture can totally inspire me to make something. Other than that, I am very glad we got this book!

title: Great Ideas, Not Well Illustrated
text:
I am definitely one of those who need to have pictures on recipes to give me an idea of what I am aiming for and to inspire me to try a recipte. Unfortunately, this book has very few photos, but it does have a lot of good content. The very first thing that really peaked our interest was the idea of grilled peaches. Simple idea that I could imagine without a photo. It was easy and it did make a great dessert. We also tried their idea of grown-up grilled cheese which uses the grilled peaches and ricotta cheese on flat bread which was wonderful. The recipes are simple and low on ingredients, so this is a great cookbook for novices, but is also good in that it has novel ideas for anyone looking for a change of pace.

For not having photos, this is a really good cookbook. Oh and almost forgot, I am an omnivore in a vegetarian household, this book has great vegetarian options.

title: Whoa, A Deep Philosophical Dive into Dogginess
text: I have to admit I was rather surprised at what this book ended up being.  It is a very deep existential look into dogs and where they fit into our culture.  Along the way there are a lot of interesting facts such as Trump is the only president ever to not be a dog owner, which may make him uniquely the way he is. Also, you learn how monotheism was the downfall of our esteem for dogs as godlike creatures which are now loathsomely low on the single god totem pole.  They went from revered to downtrodden.  It's a dense, almost academic book, which if you like that kind of thing, is filled with little delicious tidbits.  But if you are not into that thing I would think it would be heavy, hard reading, especially for the less academic dog lover.  It was an interesting read for sure, but I don't think it's for the mainstream masses.

title: Decent coverage of healthy and sustainable eating
text: It took me a while to get through this book, mostly because there were few surprises and I have seen this content a number of places.  It seems like a very solid book on the subject but I have read most all of it before.  I think everyone should be aware of what is in here.  I think we should all think a little more about where our food comes from and what we should eat both nutritionally and ethically, especially as we add a couple more billion mouths on the planet.  If you are not highly knowledgeable on the subject, I recommend this book.

title: If Ever a Cookbook Needed Photos
text:
I love getting inspiring cookbooks but I feel out of my element with this one. I guess I don't know Mediterranian cuisine well enough to be able to picture things. We flipped through it looking for inspiration for supper last night and ended up googling dishes so we could get an idea about what they were. In the end we made a Asparagus Risotto because we had everything we needed on hand. But even that we ended up googling so we had an image to aim for.

The book appears to have a lot of good ideas and I'm sure we will put some into our normal rotation as they seem simple yet different. If it had been better illustrated, it would have been exactly what we were hoping for.

title: Kids Had Mixed Reviews
text: Our family burned through the Wings of Fire series so this one sounded like a sure hit.  And for our daughter it kind of was. But the boys were less excited about it.  Usually I read things like this with the kids as a shared experience but the book was lost before it got back to me.  The basic criticism was not enough dragons versus our daughter who said it was great and she loved that there was so many dragons in it.  She was 11 when reading the book so perhaps her newly teenaged sons have outgrown it.  Both sides said it deserved 4 stars.

title: Good Basic Air Fryer Cookbook
text:
We are not trying Keto so much as we are trying to find more and better ways to use our inherited air fryer. I like the Keto angle though, it has brought up a number of good ideas. Unfortunately a lot of the family is vegetarian so we are limited about most of the recipes (expected) but we knew this book had a vegetarian section and it lived up to our hopes. We were immediately inspired to make buffalo cauiflower and it was an immediate hit. We are also excited to make eggplant lasagna once we can find decent eggplant... as well as frittatas, fritters, stuffed mushrooms. This is great since mostly we have been french air frying sweet potatoes and potatoes and that is about it.

The cookbook itself has a number of illustrations. I wish all recipes had quality food photography with them, and this one has some, in fact more than most I have been looking at, but still falls well short of what I would like. But the recipes are good, I feel inspired to get a lot more out of our air fryer, and as the meat eater in the family, I am a little jealous of a lot of the Keto options. All in all it is a good cookbook, and very good for our needs.

title: If ever a cookbook deserved photos...
text: This is a great subject and handling for a cookbook. I like the fish by fish strategy for getting through the ten biggest eating fish.  It is a perfect go to book on the subject, but I was really let down with the lack of images.  There are a few spread through the book, but this idea is so good it deserves award winning photography and glossy pages. I did find the content worthwhile and the recipes seem solid, I just wish it was more visual.

title: Maybe not for Dorm Life, but great for first time off campus
text:
I got this hoping that it would be perfect for our son who is heading to college after completing his Army National Guard training. He has some basic kitchen skills, but being on base made us realize that this will not be all the great while he is living in a dorm. He will have food service for at least the first year.

What it does give though is a great set of basic recipes for breakfast, lunch and dinner as well as snacks that he can make with basic ingredients and cooking tools. We ran a couple through during Christmas break and I think there will be a place for this book when the times comes. Unfortunately it is not full of images so some of the recipes need a little imagination to know what is going to come out of it. Luckily most of them are so basic that that should not be a problem.

title: Good but Basic Slow Cooker Recipes
text: This is a decent cookbook for those like me who are trying to find more uses for the slow cooker and live in a vegetarian family.  I have to say right up front that I am kind of disappointed that there are very few photos in the book, and for those of us who have poor culinary imaginations, it is hard to know what you are looking for.  For example, I still can't quite figure out what the Samosa Bites recipe will end up as, but I was inspired to make butter chickpeas because I could see what the end result should look like.  I wish all cookbooks had inspirational photographs.  Also, most recipes are pretty basic, which is good but I wouldn't mind a few more dangerous missions.  We made the corn chowder and ended up spicing it up a lot.  It seemed like a safe base recipe, but needed some cayenne to get it to pop a little.  All in all, it is a decent cookbook, but perhaps a little too safe and basic.

title: Great Entry Level Book of Projects
text: I was really expecting a more involved book and projects, but this shows how you can use the ideas of screen printing on a quick and easy level.  These are not four color photos transfers, they are simple sihlouettes that are simple and elegant.  You don't need a huge screen printing set up, just a small screen and a cut out stencil.  It is actually pretty impressive in its simplicity to make projects with minimal supplies. Would make a perfect art gift with a couple inks, a screen and a squeegee.  Very nice little book.

title: Great Intro to Food Prepping
text: With the New Year coming up, we were hoping to be a little more healthy and financially wise.  I thought this would be a great idea for keeping us to our nutrition goals and I really think it will be.  We have tested a couple days and it went ok so we are ready to scale to full weeks. I do have to say that my partner is a vegetarian so we ended up having to get a second book about vegetarian food prepping to have enough ideas to make it work for weeks, but this book was great at helping with the planning and ideas behind the system.  We find the need for quick food our biggest blocker to eating healthy and to make us want to eat out.  This definitely curbed those impulses for the two days we prepped for.  I think this has a lot of promise for our resolutions.  The recipes we could use were great but would have liked more photos of the food for inspiration.  All in all a very good book.

title: Great Reference for Traveling to Italy
text: I have always thought of Fodors as more a reference than a book I would want to read from cover to cover.  We got both this and the DK eyewitness guide to Italy and DK is far better at getting you excited about taking a trip somewhere and Fodors is better for finding a hotel in an area you know you are going to.  Rather than the DK's highly visual pages, Fodors is text content heavy.  It is fairly good at being exhaustive for food and lodging and does fine with the sites of an area, but really lacks the beautiful photos of DK.  There are some good maps, but I'm not going to carry this book of restaurant and hotels around for the maps.  It is also not nearly as good for flipping through as the DK.  Both have value for sure, but this would be a second choice for a guide.

title: Good Intro to our Air Fryer
text:
We inherited an Air Fryer without any really idea what we would do with it. This book did a couple things. One it gave some inspirational recipes and it also gave some decent technique tips of how to use it. It is strongly meat heavy in the recipes which was unfortunate for a mostly vegetarian household. But we jumped at the eggs and fried asparagus and tomatos recipe and it actually did well with asparagus. It was quick to prep and did not take long to cook to make a very nice meal. There are a number of appetizers and breakfasts that we can also make, but the best thing this book did was to show how we can make a number of recipes in the fryer. Looking forward to a lot of good and somewhat healthier food.

The one thing that really sticks out as a con for this book is the lack of photos for each recipe. That is very important for those of us who cannot imagine food that well. Photos really help inspire me to try a recipe.

title: Nice Intro to Apex, Sadly Outdated at Publishing
text:
This is a very hard genre of book. It should almost be considered a yearbook rather than a reference because they always give a review of the last year or two and will never be able to be timely. In this case it is a great intro to the game, but all these games update constantly, so you are producing a book that will be default be out of date by publication date. Especially bad is trying to publish map details. In this case they kept things pretty vague so it will not be interpreting a map that is long gone to updates, but still dated.

If you look at it as a yearbook, you can look at the avatars as they were for the last year, they are almost certain to change in the future. But the basic game play should remain similar, and in that this is a good intro book. I recommend it to die hard fans of the game. But there isn't much you would get from just a couple hours of play. It is a good attractive book, just dated out of the gate.

title: Interesting Premise
text: This was an interesting dystopic story with a weird scifi premise.  My partner was not too taken by it, but I and one of our kids were pretty well engaged in it.  I don't know that it will ever be one of my favorite books, but it was worth the time. As a bird watcher, I was a little disappointed to find that the missing sparrows were only a small part of the book.

title: Quick but Forgetable Read
text: My partner read this book and it was a quick read with a big twist ending, but even a short time after reading it, she does not really remember much about it. I appreciated the backdrop of Australia and the story of Aboriginal culture.  I found that part fascinating and worth the read.  It has an interesting ghost/spiritual side and a gritty realistic side.  There was a rich cultural background which seemed pretty genuine.

title: Good Story, A Little Formulaic
text:
This is really a pretty standard young adult plotline. Outsider kid finds that she is has a special role, in fact the world balances on her. Along the way she finds a crew of oddball friends to help her and overcomes the popular kids who are eventually won over. But there are some twists, She ends up to be not so predestined and it ends poised for book two where her closest ally is lost and will need to be fought or redeemed in the next book(s).

Things can be formulaic and be good if handled well, and this book definitely pulled me through the pages quickly. I was definitely hooked early on and it read quickly and easily. The writing is ok, the plot in the end was fairly decent and the Chinese culture introduction was wonderful. I'm definitely glad I spent the time to read it. I don't know that it is anywhere near the top 40 young adult books Ive read, but it is definitely worthwhile. I recommend it to anyone who is a voracious reader of Percy Jackson, Harry Potter genre.

title: Full of Content but Light on Inspiring Photos
text:
This is kind of the book I would expect from Fodors - It is chock full of logistic information, but a little light in photos. Most of the illustrations are maps. Good and useful maps. There are some photo spreads and they are pretty decent. The list of can't miss spots is definitely inspiring. We are looking at Guatamala and Belize so I read the intro and logistic information and it was very informative, but I think this will be come a reference more than a inspiration.

It is not the greatest visually, but it is great pound for pound in information. I flipped through Costa Rica which I am familiar with and I can vouch that is decent. And it has answered my questions about Guatamala. Glad I got it and can recommend it.

title: DC for a very young audience
text:
This was a cute read and perfect for very young readers. We used a lot of simple graphic novels like this to inspire our youngest to read and we would have loved this one if it were around. The language is easy and clean, it reads fast and has a cute, clean story. I little too straight for older readers, but it was interesting enough for a middle aged parent to make it through. I'm guessing this is best for first and second grade which is a getting pretty young for our house, but I would definitely suggest it for new readers.

The art work is very good. It is strongly cartoony without any moodiness or angst. Pages go fast and I got through it in about 15 minutes.

title: Great Size, Great Content and Scope
text: ...But, Hamburg is now off our itinerary.  We do love the books and we picked up Berlin and Las Vegas for separate trips and I love the portability and the focused scope of a specific city.  We were excited to get the Hamburg book and it had enough photos and information to sway us into visiting the city but it just isn't going to make it into our timeline unfortunately.  But I highly recommend this specific guide and any book in this pocket series.  They have nice maps, decently complete information and good quality.  Highly recommend.

title: Wonderfully Bizarre and a Twisted Unraveling of a Family Secret
text:
I love graphic novels for often being a little on the bizarre side and this collection does that in spades. Tonta is a great and believable character with depth and she is surrounded by an interesting cast of characters from an extended blended family to the homely tutoring classmate who has become a forest spirit. Characters come and go as a family murder mystery unravels, complete with an injustice in the end. It is a great interwoven tale.

The illustrations are black and white and masterful. The handling of human forms and faces is good and it keeps you turning the pages. This is definitely an adult comic book, so keep it from young children, but if you like a quirky tale and you are fine with some nudity and implied violence, I recommend this graphic novel.

title: Nice Young DC Comic
text: This is obviously meant for a young audience 8-10?  But it is a actually a cute and quick read.  The illustrations are very nice and it is wonderfully drawn and colored, but again with young reader styles which are clean and cute, not gritty or dark.  There is a nice little narrative running through a series of stories based on each DC superhero.  Each superhero gets a rather pointed fan email or letter that they need to respond to in lightly humorous, but thoughtful ways. It humanizes the heroes and makes them relatable to young readers.  A growing crisis is hinted at throughout the book and it quickly cleaned up in the end.  All in all, a great all ages comic.

title: A Good Country Guide to Germany
text: I really like this book and it has most of what I am looking for in a book.  The illustrations are good and there are lots of photos and some maps. I find this best of series to be my favorite when looking into a new destination.  They lean a little harder on photos and keep the focus more on the key sites of a country.  They do go into lodging, food and sights for the best locations, but not as in depth as other guides, but again, I like this series in the dreaming stage of trip planning and can get detailed logistics from the internet or other guides.  I definitely like these more that Fodor's country guides.  This one is proving perfect for sketching an itinerary for Europe this fall.

title: Educational, Mixed Reviews in our Household
text: I was excited to get a reviewer copy of this book from Amazon as she is my partner's  idol.  However she ended up not caring for it, saying the writing was not that great and she abandoned it.  I'm definitely less likely to abandon a book and I found it interesting and informative, at least for someone who is not steeped in law and RBG.  If you have interest in her story, I would still recommend it and it was well worth my time.  Glad I read it.

title: Perfectly Scoped Book, Could Use more Photos
text:
Cities used to be a place you flew to to get to somewhere else, until Mexico City. Suddenly my interests focused on the museums, restaurants and sights of the city almost more than the allure of 200 million Monarch butterflies. Add Cartegena, LA, New Orleans and Miami and I think I'm hooked on cities as much as field and forest, and this series of books does them justice. While I wish they were far more illustrated with photographs, the Fodor's Inside guide shows that focusing on a city and its immediate surroundings is a great scope.

Like the trip to see the Monarchs in Mexico, Portugal has been on my bucket list since I was young. For Mexico I got a lot of country guides and then tried to glean everything I could from fifteen pages featuring Mexico City. Now I realized I would have been much better served by a guide for the country, but also one scoped just on the city, so I was very happy to get a reviewer book on Lisbon and it is nearly perfect.

I have spent many hours flipping through this book getting ideas of what I want to see when we do Europe next summer. I loved the first intro chapter, especially the suggested movies and books to watch and read to get a sense of the city. I have googled that before and it is nice to see someone create a thoughtful list. We now have a number of movies and books on our wishlist. The rest of the book is descriptions of neighborhoods which are rather complete with services and sight seeing locations. The descriptions are text heavy and have casual maps and graphics. I would have much rather had a more visual description with photos of sites. It definitely has the Fodor's style of exhaustive logistical information rather than day dream inspiring illustrations.

The Book size and quality are perfect. It is smaller than a average guide and fits in hand and bag well. The cover is good. The pull out map is great! I wish they had put a smaller one in the inside cover for quick reference. The paper for the pages are good and non glossy. The content is the star though. I love the focus on the city and the thoroughness. But I think I need a glossy, photo filled guide to get really excited.

title: A Nice Relationship Story
text: To be honest, I have had some problems figure out what I wanted to say about this book.  It was engaging and I could not put it down, but I don't know that it changed my life in any way, but it was nice enough.  The illustrations were great and I liked the thin palette.  The illustrations were fantastic, the characters were rendered masterfully and went hand in hand to drive the story.  The story was a interesting relationship story with a lot of reality.  There was some swearing, but ok for most teens or older.  Glad I got a chance to read it.

title: A Good Start To Researching Chinese Travel
text:
We have a few bucket list destinations we are trying to schedule in the next few years and China is high on the list. This book did a good, but not perfect, job of getting our dreams going. I think we could have used a more general, less detailed book to start with. I think it will become a good reference later, but right now we could use more photos and more focus on the sites and less on lodging and food. Although, I did like the basic logistics pages, when they were not in error. I feel like we have a good idea of some logistical issues and such.

This book did seem to have more photos than the average Fodors which was nice, but this might not be the best book if you are looking at broad strokes. I find Fodor's better when you know the cities you will be going to and you want to make reservations to stay and dine. That makes this a great book in your library, but perhaps, not the best stand alone.

title: Very Adult Comic, Good Backstory
text:
This is a very believable backstory, and well written. It stands well on its own and fleshes out the relationship between Catwoman and Bruce Wayne very well. I feel like the table has been set for a very good Catwoman series. It is raw and gritty, but definitely for a more mature audience. There is a good amount of swearing and adult themes, and a kitten is killed by abuse. Also there are themes of child abuse, so it may not be great for very young or sensitive readers.

The illustration is strong and there is obviously a very gifted artist behind it. The story reads very fast and keeps you engaged, as do the renderings. Very good start to the series, and I plan to keep an eye on it.

title: Enjoyable, but pretty disposeable
text: My partner read this while on a business trip and said that it was entertaining, but probably will not be overly memorable.  She said it was cute and romantic but only so so.  It definitely filled the bill for entertaining reading and it read quickly, but it was nowhere near life changing.

title: Good, Digestible Information
text: We have been doing a lot of research recently about trips for the next couple of years and we thought A cruise would be a good way to hit Scandinavia. I really like the guide in general, it was a good introduction to the area and what is offered and had enough photos to kind of fire up the imagination. It is a bit more than a fodors guide but maybe not as good as the Eyewitness series, but the scope is perfect.  We have not done a cruise and Norway just seems as good a place as any to visit via cruise.  This book gave a great survey of ports of call and probably will be the only guide we will need if we are going to go this route.  Right now it seems like a great idea and this book gave us enough to feel informed about that decision.  Highly recommend if you are thinking about this cruise.

title: Wonderfully Bizarre Premise, with Wonderful Illustrations
text:
I love graphic novels because they often are a little ridiculous and random. This book gave me everything I was hoping for there. It is a mix of "Best of Show" and something else I can't put my finger on, which makes a interesting read. To tell the truth, the most unique and memorable part of this book is the comic full frontal nudity of all the pet men. Occasionally humorous, sometimes a little disconcerting.

The characters are all imperfect, a couple are a little hard to like. I definitely identified with the overly busy, overly committed comic writing cat who can't seem to say no to anything but was irritated at the stressed and quick to anger owner of the man shelter.

Be careful of getting this book if you are uncomfortable with stylized male nudity. Otherwise, it is a nice little story which I am happy to have read.

title: A Good Start to our Research
text: This is probably not going to be enough to plan our trip, but it is a good start.  Fodors is not the most visual guide out there.  I definitely prefer a visual guide for the start of planning just to get the dreaming going.  I prefer Eyewitness guides to Fodors, but there is a plethora of information here.  In fact, it looks like they may have broadened the scope too far.  We will be limited to Thailand so we do not need Laos and Cambodia.  I would have preferred more focus on just Thailand.  Reading through the travel basics was great and I learned a lot but it will take some time to digest the site and lodging descriptions.  I'm glad I got this book, but will need more.

title: Super Cute Photos, Decent Quotes
text: You can't beat this book visually.  High quality photos of puppies and kittens are pretty hard to bash.  It is an absolute beauty.  The quotes are good, although I did not find as many "life changing" quotes as I was hoping for and quite a few of them were a little long winded.  This book would make a good gift for a friend but more as a piece of sentimentality rather than a treasured gift.

title: Amusing Read
text:
This is kind of bathroom reader material. I appreciate the premises and the humor in the exchanges. It is a breezy read that you can easily put down and pick up again as each story is self-contained. To tell the truth, I thought it was funnier when I was relaying the stories to my partner but all in all it was pretty entertaining. Not sure that I would recommend it widely, but I definitely felt it was worth my time to read. Also the illustrations were good.

You would enjoy this if you enjoy things like Crank Yankers or radio shows that make prank calls.

title: Cute Book, Nicely Illustrated, Good Learning Aid for Spanish
text:
We now have a bunch of people trying to learn Spanish in the house and this was passed around to everyone from 8th graders to adults as a way to expand vocabulary in an easy and enjoyable way. It has been great reinforcement for the word volar (to fly) and nido (nest) and expanding to bandada (flock.) Childrens books are great ways to learn Spanish and this was perfect for it (especially since I'm a birdwatcher and will be trying to speak with a Costa Rican guide next week.)

The story is simple and straight forward, about some storks finding a new home. The illustrations are cute wonderfully stylized. I wish we had a library of books of this caliber.

title: Aquaman Meets Twilight
text:
This has all the romantic tension of twilight combined with the origin story of Aguaman. Granted, I think it is better than Twilight, but I don't think I was quite looking for the start of a love story. Also, since I have just seen the newest Aquaman movie, I was alternating between thinking that this is a just a rehashing of the movie and thinking, wait, that is not how it was in the movie.

Ok so that is all the negative I can say about this, because from there, it was a page turning read, the art work was very good and we all really like it. I love that the protagonist is female which is fantastic for the kids to read. I love that there was a minimum of swearing and violence and again, that is fantastic for the kids. And finally, I love that the kids passed it from one to the next and talked about it amongst themselves. Anything to get kids reading is fantastic.

title: Good Information but no inspiring photos
text: We are looking at the possibility of going to a Rio and I was excited to get a reviewers copy of the Fodor's travel guide to Rio and Sao Paulo.  However, I have to admit that I am a little disappointed by the book when I received it.  It is chock full of information, decent maps, and logistics, but hardly any photographs.  I am a big fan of the DK Eyewitness guides which are a pleasure to flip through and daydream over the wonderful photos.  This does not have that joy at all.  It seems like such a dry reference in comparison.  I did appreciate the essential section and I eventually deciphered how to browse attractions, but I think I will be getting another book before the trip.

title: Weird but entertaining
text: Ok I understand that this is a modern retelling of a fairytale, but I found that while reading it, it seemed like it was ripping off fairytales and I could not shake that feeling. The writing was good and I found it entertaining but I did not feel like I learned from it, nor was I moved particularly by the ending. Basically I felt that it was continually getting weirder as time went by. Like I said I was entertained, but I don’t honk I would recommend it to anyone.

title: Stewart Little Meets Water World
text: This is an interesting and timely setting for this book.  The great pacific gyre forms the exotic location for this quaint little story in a fantasy world where animals create a floating world full of inventions and adventure.  It is a decent read and likeable enough but somewhat disposable entertainment.  It took a while to get into the book but eventually I was engaged and enjoyed the read.

title: A fun, but silly read
text: This is kind of a silly but entertaining story. It had good humor and was a fun read. It is not a deep story with a goofy premise that a girl mixes an Asian acne medicine with a tanning bed and finds herself invisible.  Cue the antics and mild friend and family dramas.  The book got passed around the house and was well enjoyed by all, but I found it a little light, but very enjoyable.

title: Likeable, but the jury is a little out on this one
text:
First, I can't fault any book that makes it hard to put down. It reads very well and I was fully engaged but I fell short of loving this book. Initially I was pulled in because, like the main character, I read Whitley Streiber's Communion and was somewhat traumatized. For me, I slept with a baseball bat next to my bed for a few months and shunned camping for a summer. So I felt a kinship to the character and was drawn into the story, but I was never really certain where the story was going, especially as the pages dwindled and resolution did not seem imminent. I was waiting for the twist that pulled the book together and when it came it felt like the punch line ending of an episode of the outer limits.

That seems like a pretty rough criticism of the book which seems a little hard on it. I really did like reading the book and there was a good tension between what was real and what wasn't throughout the book. There was a disruptive story within the story that paralleled the main story, but seemed a little superfluous. Mostly it just made me root for the character to become a writer but did not propel the story along much.

Yeah, I'm conflicted on this book, but glad I read it and will recommend it to the kids, but there seems to be a slight dissatisfaction in the ending.

title: Interesting and Quick Reading Little Book
text:
This is rather bizarre, it has bite sized chunks of reasonable relationship advice juxtaposed next to the quirky scenes of Hey Arnold. At times it made it seem like the Hey Arnold creators had been carefully and insidiously placing relationship counseling into their series and at times it looked like they were just trying to take disjunct observations that they found in an old relationships workbook and connect them to apologetically justify their old scripts.

In the end though, it is a quick read of unsettlingly good, and many times personally relevant, advice. I actually requested a reviewer copy for my oldest son who is awkwardly entering the world of relationships. And reading through it, there was lots of advice that I probably should have figured out to tell him. Anyway, tossing this book at him is easier.

This is not a coherent, carefully and fully laid out relationship guide, but it is a fun walk down a nostalgic path eating decently written fortune cookies bites worth of real advice.

title: Interesting Read for a Mixed Vegetarian/Omnivore Couple
text:
I am in a mixed vegetarian and omnivore relationship - she's the vegetarian - and it was interesting to read this with her. We talk a lot about this and she is in a sustainability council so we get this general messaging a lot. We read it together and I think it resonated with her more than it did with my cynicism. So I can vouch that the choir is loving this sermon.

Personally, I would love to see any small fix to what is often a very cruel system. I had hope in many of the ideas he raised but rebel against moral outrage messaging, mostly because I think it is alienating and unproductive in many if not most cases. I do think that ultimately there will be a large moral shift toward better husbandry and even toward voluntary vegetarianism. I know for certain that I have become a reductitarian due to moral questions of the meat industry, but I fear even a perception of heavy handedness.

I can see for my partner, she sees a lot of logic here that I don't know the other side sees. This is great information for all to know, which hopefully will inform their eating choices. I'm not a big fan of the make a better fake meat solution, I would prefer a menu that allows vegetables to be what they are and make a meal around that. But it does seem to be a bridge for some. I'm sure it would help long run.

All in all, a worthy book full of good information, and I honestly do believe everyone should be aware of the full price of meat.

title: I really love graphic novels from different viewpoints
text:
I really love graphic novels from different viewpoints. There is something about the media that makes situations very vivid and believable. This book falls in this in that it has some interesting little vignettes from the life of the author. They are strange and disjointed themes without a central theme or direction, but many are very interesting themes. I ended up getting a feeling that this was more of a collection of stories from different projects that were brought together in book form and is more of an anthology rather than a comprehensive book. Story by story it is interesting and the art is ok.

Unfortunately, I also love to share graphic novels with my kids and this is definitely not kid appropriate. In the first story, six year olds talk about playing rape and is quickly followed by a rather artful and masterful drawing of a vulva. ...Not kid stuff, but it doesn't have to be, just be aware that this is an adult novel.

I'm glad I read this and enjoyed some of the insights. I especially like how the eyeglasses story unfolded. It showed a sense of anxiety that people in my life have had but I never fully understood. This story helped to flesh out the feelings they have had about things. And that is why I like graphic novels.

title: Good Book, But appaently causes mild amnesia.
text:
A couple of our kids read this book and enjoyed reading it and have good feelings about the book but surprisingly few strong memories of the book. We actually pulled the book out and as we read the description there was a lot of "Oh yeah's" that brought back some memories but the book definitely did not burn strong memories in their minds.

But any reading is good reading and they still say they recommend the book although they don't remember much. Will keep it at four stars.

title: Wonderfully Illustrated Book, Story is a Little Light
text: This is a wonderfully illustrated book with a nice story concept.  We read it to a couple of nieces and they caught on to the fact that a story was going on behind the backs of the books characters and looking quickly at each page to see what new details they were missing.  It is a nice little deconstruction of a picture book.  Probably not a book to reread over and over, but a wonderfully cute book to go through.

title: Nice Elementary School Comic
text:
I think our kids have all aged out of this book (sixth grade and above,) but this would be a perfect book for first through fourth graders, especially anyone that is dreading or thinking about the first day of school. The humor is clean and young and the stories are straightforward and great for these early readers. I really wish that we had this when we had some second graders in the house.

The art is nice and colorful. I can't say that I love this book, but those of us who read it liked it, just felt that it was for younger kids.

title: Relevant Story with Good Ending
text:
This was kind of a difficult book for me. It is very timely and very poignant, and I think that having kids in middle and high school made this book touch home with me and at least my youngest son. We had an interesting conversation about the whole phenomenon of school shootings and it was fascinating what he had to say and the fears that he had. I know statistically... but it is a sad fear that he had. After that discussion I put the book away and no one else read it. I'm not sure I'm ready with all the answers yet.

But to get to the book, I thought it was written well and the premise, like I said, is profoundly relevant today. The one thing I like the most was the focus on the survivors and not the shooter. Books glorifying Columbine shooters have done damage and inspired several of the shooters. This one focuses on the humanity and even the frank truth behind the stories that make it to the media.

The writing is OK as are the characters but the resolution is rather good. I don't want to give anything away, but I felt that it was worth getting to the end of the story.

title: Good Book, but it is for Absolute Beginners
text:
Be careful about ordering this because it is a very basic book, truly for Dummies and 3D printing newbies like me. For me it was perfect because I had so little knowledge of 3D printing in general. But I feel that you have the basics, this book may be far to simplistic for you. Even for me, there were a couple dozen pages about 3D modeling that were too basic for me. But I really appreciated learning the basics like .stl file types and different printing technologies which were again touched on in a shallow way, but valuable for me to even know that there are different additive printing medias and techniques.

The actual Tinkercad information was also shallow and for beginners. It walks you through signing up for a Tinkercad account which is 10 pages of somewhat filler. There are two step by step examples for working with the UI which are great but simplistic. Personally, I like what I read and it gave a good look at what was possible, but again this is a very high level, shallow look at the system. I definitely found plenty of value in the book, but I am an absolute beginner and already feel that I have gleaned all the information from this book and I'm looking for the next level book.

It did have a sizeable section that spoke about different 3D printers and 3D software packages. I am in the market for my first 3D printer so that was OK, but still seemed more filler than value, especially the software items.

So to summarize, I'm glad I got a copy of this book and found that it met me at my level because I truly knew next to nothing about 3D printing. But do be careful if you have any experience with Autocad or have used a 3D printer for a while, perhaps look for a intermediate Tinkercad book.

title: Nice Little Book, My Fiancee had some Issues
text:
This is a visually lovely book and I'm impressed that the author illustrated it with her own paintings. They are whimsical and fit the tone and the story seems magical with some bitter pieces of abuse. My fiancée believes that the stories of abuse as well as the elements where the main character is pining for Will are bad messages for a young woman who should be able to stand on her own are strikes against it. (This is why the four stars rather than five.)

Personally I thought this was a lovely little story that brought back a hint of childhood memories.

title: Great Idea, Decent Cookbook, but I think I'll need to expand beyond it's pages
text:
A long time ago I had a book that helped you cook once every 30 days then have meals ready for the rest of the month. We did it for a while and it worked but that 30th day was completely taken up by shopping and cooking. When I saw this book I thought, once a week would be a great middle ground. And all in all I like what this book delivers.

I do wish that each recipe had a picture directly associated with it. You can find a picture on a different page, like the page that displays the week laid out in containers, but I wish they were side by side. I can't say that the food is always the most appetizing in the photos, but it is true to what you end up with when packaging the meals. I like it as a reference of weekly planning and prepping. There are a number of recipes that I will incorporate in my weekly attempt, and a couple I have adapted for meals this last week. I have one other issue that makes this hard, my partner is a vegetarian so we have to adapt a lot of meals. I love that they put a meatless sample week in the cook book, but unfortunately, I think this idea works best with meat centered entres. But the idea will work for vegetarians too, just takes a little ingenuity.

We are definitely going to try this for a number of weeks ahead while my partners workload is very high. This should allow me to easy her work week by having lunches and dinners ready for her and the family.

title: A Fascinating Look into Wolf Pack and Their Emotional Capabilities
text:
I have read a lot about wolves in my lifetime and watched the Dutcher's documentaries. My partner is an attorney who has long been involved in the fight to protect wolves, so I am pretty steeped in the lore for and against the wolf. This book is an interesting addition to our library. I loved getting some of the back story about the Dutchers project, although much of that came out in the documentaries. I can't say that I found a lot of new material in this book, and many of the stories cited here I have read or heard other placed. However, if you have not read much about wolves, this is definitely a book to read.

Wolf research has advanced a lot in the last fifty years. The understanding of their lives has been very much a group effort amongst hundreds of observers and the Dutchers work with a captive pack has definitely added to our understanding of them. Due to the nature of their study with captive wolves, you don't get much insight on hunting, but loads of insights into their group structure and intimate day to day interactions within the pack. It is heavy on reporting of their emotional capabilities which are both interesting and profound. I don't know if it is the only book you should read, but it is a great read to augment your understanding of their family structure. It is fascinating.

title: Intriguing Intro to Manga
text:
I was using this as an entry into understanding Manga and to see if the kids would be interested. Perhaps in some ways this may not be the entry I was looking for. Mostly this is because Faust is a very Eurocentric story and I was looking more for a Japanesecentric book. That being said it is an experience for an American to read right to left. Also the art is fascinating in its stylized representations. It is beautiful and the story line is wonderfully strange and mystical.

The bad news is that this not a great stand alone book. It is definitely a first entry in a longer, intriguing story. I am very much looking for the second book to continue on with it. It definitely draws you into a different world and pulls you through the pages quickly. I have to admit that the story line is a little difficult to follow at times and seems a little scattered. There are characters who were added, expanded and left without truly understanding how they truly related to Frau Faust. I look forward to reading book two (and three and four when they come out) to get more clues.

It is intriguing enough that I will continue with the series.

title: A Great Journey and Adventure Through Grief
text:
This book definitely grew on me. I can't put my finger on it, but for some reason I was not that happy with the book for the first 50 pages or so, but I was pulled through it. In part I think it was because it was so heart wrenching to see Lily go through some irrational hope and denial of her father's death. I couldn't decide if I wanted to root for a pollyanic ending or acceptance by Lily and I alternated between cheering for the possibility of a miracle and hope for reality and rationality.

In the end, this turned out to be a very nice book about mourning and grief. I think the author did a great job of creating two well thought out and developed examples of grief that felt incredibly authentic for the ages of Lily and her sister Sophie. Lily had an indefatiguible optimism and denial, while Sophie had a more mature but still teen journey through grieving. Both characters seemed well but differently motivated for their adventure.

I am a huge fan of Alaska and Denali so I love their back country adventure and the place names. I love the details and reliving the hike on the McKinley Bar Trail, the water crossings, the eating while walking to keep the mosquitos at bay. Again, very authentic. It reads quick and is a true page turner with a satisfying end.

title: A Charming Story with Disturbing Elements
text:
In large part this is a warm and charming story of how wrongs can be made right. A girl from an abusive home makes a new friend and her life changes for the better. But I'm not sure I'd want a child to read about the abuse in the book, as I think it could be scary given the descriptions of physical and emotional abuse. I think that tweens would be fine with the intensity. As an adult, I enjoy young adult and children's fiction, and I enjoyed this one too. But I think it suffered a bit in that it everything worked out so simply and predictably -- it did not seem to acknowledge the lifelong struggles that a child who had suffered such abuse would face. It is also a bit formulaic: child from broken family with a special ability conquers her past and does wonderful things (compare Harry Potter). I very much appreciated the clarity of the writing and found it to be a fast and pleasant read.

Wish I could give it 4.5 stars.

title: A Good but Not Great Read, Unevenly Paced
text:
I was a little disappointed with this book after I saw the Oprah book club praised it as one of the top twenty books I'll read this year. which it might because I probably read about twenty five a year, but if it gets in the top twenty, it may be more on sample size rather than its own merits. It definitely was not a bad book, but I don't feel that it was a great book.

The development of the character was slow, slow enough that I put this book down for over a month before returning to it. The main characters childhood was developed in broad anectdotes that did slowly come together, but it did read slowly at the beginning. The book definitely sped up after he snuck out of the orphanage and started living on the streets of Point Noire. In fact I was starting to get into his progress when inexplicably suddenly, he was struck by brain lesions and the book careened in a new direction. Perhaps true to life, but as I was waiting for the character to live up to his fated name of Black Moses, his whole life is thrown into confusion and weirdness. Perhaps this section provided the best humor and tension as I hoped for a cure though.

In the end I came away thinking it was good to read, although I have a history of studying the region so I appreciated a lot of the book that someone new to west central Africa would not. I'm glad I read it, but I don't know how long it will stick with me. I will say this, hoping not to be a spoiler, The very end twist struck me as very strong. Up until the last page I think I was sitting on a three star rating.

title: Very Well Designed and Illustrated Cookbook
text:
This is the way that cookbooks should be, a beautiful picture for every recipe. For design, this is a fantastic book. Unfortunately, I didn't find as many inspiring meal ideas as I was hoping for. One of the biggest problems is that my partner and her kids are vegetarians, which is actually why I turn to a lot of cookbooks looking for recipes I can tweak or replace meat. There are definitely vegetarian options or easily tweaked meals, but compared to other Southern Living cookbooks, this one had the fewest mouthwatering inspirations. Still worth a place on my cookbook shelf though.

I do have to say that one recipe stuck out so much was the biscuit and gravy bake. Biscuits and Gravy is a southern culinary weakness of mine, and that was the first recipe I made, replacing the sausage with veggie sausage crumbles.

title: Kids Liked it Better Than We Did
text: Neither my partner or I came away from this book very satisfied with the ending.  And both of us struggled to finish it.  Reading the description, it sounded like a perfect book for our family, but I don't know.  The biggest reason I am giving it four stars is that our one son who finished it said it's pretty good and I can't be anything but a happy about a book that keeps our kids reading.  In fact, this book has been handed off to a second kid who is reading it.  So there is that.

title: A Good Reference, Wish They Hadn't Cut Corners on Production
text:
This is a great delivery of Rap history in little bite sized pieces. It kind of reads like a bathroom book with little bite sized nuggets of facts. You can pick up the book, read a few pages and put it down again, or you can flip through it enjoying the striking illustrations. Unfortunately it is a little strong on Album releases that isn't the most exciting beginning to end read. But it does have some nostalgic value remembering the songs as they come up.

It can act as something of a reference, especially since it has a somewhat robust index. Otherwise I kind of wish it was a little more narrative.

The book itself is pretty hefty and well designed, but lacks a little in manufacturing quality. The cover seems light and less substantial than I would wish. The binding is a little suspect and it feels like some corners were cut on the production, which is a shame for the effort put into the content.

title: A Good Read for Animal Lovers
text:
This was a quick read that I was able to finish on a single flight. We are huge fans of Because of Winn Dixie which this book was compared to. It was in the same vein as a basic feel good/Animal makes life better book. It was entertaining, but not quite as moving as Winn Dixie.

We are looking forward to having the kids read it, it has a satisfying, happy ending.

title: A Great Overview of Life in the New Anthropocene
text:
I heard an NPR discussion about the Anthropocene recently and was amazed at the controversy surrounding the terminology. I was especially intrigued that the rather unglamorous geologists find themselves as the key holders to confirm or deny that we are in a new era. So, I was excited to see this book, not fully understanding what I was getting into.

What I did get, I ended up really liking. It is a herky jerky and jumping ride through a bunch of related topics. Each topic (e.g. population bomb, climate, resource availability... all over really) is treated in a chapter that reads like an informative essay. It is kind of a wild ride keeping up with the topics, but the threads keep building under the theme. Each chapter is filled with thought provoking, and at least for now, amazingly timely information.

In the end, you get a very good overview of the history that brought us to the anthropocene and a good list of it's implications. It was a decently easy read, although I am well steeped and a fan of this kind of subject matter. I'm glad I read it.

title: A Decent Story with a Wonderfully, if Sadly, Developed Hero
text:
I love reading books that can help me get into someone else's mind and experiences. I enjoyed getting a sense of what OCD is like from this book. I have to admit it took me a while to get into this book, which is a little strange because looking back I feel like the writing was good, perhaps a little less action in the beginning to drive me through the pages, but enough to be pretty satisfied when I put the book down. It ends up being a decent little mystery.

The story is kind of like Rear Window meets Judy Blume with an agoraphobic youngster in place of Jimmy Stewart. The characters were well developed and as I said the writing was clean and readable.

title: A Decent Story about an Adolescent Finding Her Way
text: This is a nice fast read with good character development. Long term it may not be a well remembered book, but it did read well and takes the reader along.  It is a pretty typical story of a adolescent trying to find her place in the world, but there were a lot of nice details that made it well worth reading. It is definitely a young reader but even my partner and I felt it was worth for adults to read.

title: Kids Really Liked It, Hope It Will be a New Series
text:
I didn't get a chance to read this before the kids grabbed it and ran with it. I haven't seen it since, but two of our kids have read it and said that it is pretty good. For me, any book that gets a kid to read it pretty good, one that gets passed to other kids as a recommendation is even better. We spoke about it over breakfast one morning (another plus if they need to talk about it.) The story sounded engaging and while I don't know that I can do justice to paraphrase the story, I can say that it was an animated discussion and both kids added to what the other said.

Interestingly they bot said that the ending was a little abrupt and not that great and that's why they would both give it four stars, however, they said if the ending is because this is the start of a series, then the book should be 4.5 stars and they like it that much more. Perhaps it will show up again, but since they both enjoyed it so much and it is helping to keep them being readers, I fully endorse this book.

title: Kids Enjoyed it
text:
I have to admit that I had problems getting into this book and eventually gave up. The writing seemed rather juvenile mixed with some four letter words so that I was not sure who this book was meant for. But my partners daughter picked it up and read through it and said that it was pretty good and definitely deserved four stars. It has now been passed on to her brother who seems to be enjoying it as well and was breakfast conversation this morning.

Any book that gets kids reading is a good book, but this one never caught on for me.

title: Would be great in Classrooms for Poetry Units
text:
This was an interesting book although not going to be a family classic. The poetry was ok, as was the story. Straightforward, uncomplicated and not overly literary. It is a quick read and although I did not find it to be the best, I do think this would make an absolutely wonderful intro to poetry writing. Each poem has a title and a subtitle that tells you what kind of poetry is being used in the poem. You can then reference the back which tells more about the type of poetry. I think it would be an invaluable reference for early year poetry classes.

The art is cartoony and good and supports the narrative poetry. All in all a decent book, but not great.

title: A Surprisingly Likeable Comic, Great Character Development
text:
Hmm, I read through the story and I'm not sure what to say about it. It is profane...the effenheimers fly and it sets up a rather heretical relationship between a character who is the devil and another that is referred to as Jesus... And yet in the end, the story has you feeling very empathetically toward a devil character who is struggling to be seen as a hero. And he is a rather likeable protagonist, hero-wanna-be.

I'm actually rather impressed at the heart and character the author develops in the main character. If you took the swear words and perhaps toned down the violence (which really is not very bad) this would be a rather touching children's story. It is uplifting and is kind of a morality tale of persistence and belief in one's self that allows the main character to become what he wants to be.

The art is kind of rough cartoonish line drawings. It is not an artistic masterpiece, but the images are bold and stylized and carry the story well. I'm a little disappointed that I can't share it with my youngest children, but I did enjoy reading it. And again, I have to return to how impressed how likeable the main character is developed.

title: Decent, a Little Formulaic
text:
I have to admit that I am not the biggest fan of this genre, but my kids have consumed the Diary of a Wimpy Kid and Big Nate series, so I was interested in seeing if this is another good series for them. It is a quick read and I burned through it in an evening. The humor is standard to the genre, a little sarcastic, perhaps a little less bodily gross than most, but all in all a little juvenile. Which is fine for what it is, but probably a big reason why I am not big on the genre.

The illustrations are good, and for the most part are funnier than the text. Nearly every page has a large illustration which also makes the book such a quick read. The story is decent, a story of a boy finding his own way and place in the world, learning where his true talents lie. Characters are fine...all in all this is a perfectly fine book. We'll see how the kids like it, would love to see them tear into it and possibly the rest of the series, but our youngest is now nine, so we might be outgrowing this genre.

title: A Good, Broad Overlook of Sustainability In Web Design
text:
I have been out of the Web Design thing for a while and was just starting up on a new personal project related to sustainability so this book looked perfect. For me, I am just putting together a site to be hosted elsewhere and this book goes pretty broad in its sustainability. So I found reading about considerations for server hardware etcetera interesting, I only needed the part that suggested looking at sustainable ISP's. Ones that use renewables. For the micro level at which my decisions are being made, there were things to think about, like quick load times, but that is a pretty miniscule part of the whole.

So it is not exactly a bullseye for what I am doing, but it was fascinating reading for me and someone on the design and infrastructure team should read this in every corporation. This is all good things to keep in mind when creating a digital company.

title: Fast Paced, Easy Reading of Girlhood Struggles
text:
This was our first encounter with Manga and we were very curious about it. The most we knew about the genre was that it was read back to front, and it took a little time to master the left to right reading through the panels but it flowed well. It is a quick read but it may have missed the mark for us. This was obviously aimed more at a female audience although the three of us boys that read it made it through. The Japanese culture was interesting and just reading it felt like a cultural experience for me. The story was timeless and very human, a story of a young girl trying to fit in and find herself thrown in with some shape shifting young studs.

The art work was very good and stylized. The story was good and compelling enough to keep the pages turning and the read all told took well under an hour. Well paced, but cliffhanging at the ending when the main character speaks the horrific teen words "I Love You."

As it's our first taste we are not sure if it is great or not, but we all liked it.

title: Decent Dystopic Graphic Novel
text:
I got this for my kids to read and was a little taken back by a little bit of graphic violence and swearing (head shots and F'enheimers.) The story is decent, a little Matrix and a little Oceans 11. The story is dark, violent and has some decent twists. It held the attention of my 15 year old, but to be truthful it was a little more mature than I like for him, let alone the younger kids in the household.

The art work was good, definitely stylized cartoony, but decent. Writing and readability were also good. It was worth my time to read, but definitely not one of the top tier of graphic novels. Personally, my favorite part was a self improving robot that kept showing up at key moments.

title: A Quirky Little Story about Little Heroes
text:
I did not get a chance to read this book as it has been passed between two of our kids, but they said it was pretty good. I know the first kid to read it did not seem fully engaged but the second one got through the book rather quickly, being prodded on to read it but our youngest. I appreciate any book that gets read and even more if it is passed on to another reader.

Both kids noted that there was a likeable female heroine (I'm also happy about that.) and that they hero is truly just a flea who might unleash the plague, which I thought was a nice touch. We spoke about it over lunch and both giggled as they told of different scenes and I can tell that they both really loved the book.

the four stars is their rating. I see it as five stars since they both read and shared it and continued their love of reading.

title: Dense, Academic Rather than Practical
text:
Take the word Revolution seriously. This book does rail against the current system and promotes a solution against Big Ag. It is informative and lets say passionately delivered.

Personally I was looking for some pragmatic solutions to help on the small scale, getting urban chickens, think local ingredients with locally sourced produce. This is not that book, it is a bigger picture book. Not to say that I did not appreciate what is offered but I have read and watched some on the topic and more that a revolution, I need an evolutionary step in my personal habits. If nothing else, this book give some motivation into moving toward the goal of being more local.

It is not a simple, breezy read, but I think it's an important read. I found it a bit dense and slower reading, but rewarding in info. It is rather academic rather than practical.

title: A Good but not Overwhelming Graphic Novel
text:
This was definitely an OK graphic novel. I like that it has historic facts and I like that it's connected to the Smithsonian, in fact these two facts made me expect to absolutely love this series. I wish I could say that I loved it, but the best I can say was that it was good. It captured the kids attention for the time it took to read it, but there is not huge excitement for the next like there is in most series we have gotten involved in.

The artwork was decent. I liked many of the visuals in the book and loved the way that dinos were inserted into the altered modern world. Visually, again this book was good, but not overwhelming.

The facts were ok. I guess all around this book was good, but not a five start graphic novel. It seemed more like what a educational organization would put out rather than a strong graphic author. All the kids did read it and there were a lot of "it's ok" reactions.

title: Engrossed our 9 year old
text:
I got this book to read with my girlfriends daughter. My oldest son went through Lasky's Ga'Houle series so I had good expectations. This book appears to be at the same caliber as she read through the book quickly and adamantly said this book earns an easy four out of five stars. She liked the spunky heroine and especially liked that the TV was the portal into another world.

Personally, any book that captures a young reader as well as this one did deserves five stars but I'm leaving it at four as she is pretty adamant that this is a very good book but that five stars takes a lot to earn

title: Keep YouTube close so you can immediately listen to what you are reading about
text:
I have heard the name Pete Seeger a lot, especially with his recent passing, but I didn't know much about him. I was glad to see this book that promised a quick read to learn what I needed to know. So I sat down with this and YouTube and listened to the music as it came up in the book. It really needed the sounds to make sense of everything. Wish this had an accompanying CD.

I do feel like I understand Pete, the Guthries and folk music better than I ever have. I'm glad I listened to songs from everyone in the book but I can't say that the music really spoke to me although much was good. I liked that the author described guthry's and Seegers singing styles and I loved the back stories, but I'm not win over to this era of folk songs despite truly enjoying current artists who list these as there inspirations from Brighteyes to Beck.

Totally glad I read it though. Especially glad that I listened to every song as it came up. I do feel a rich knowledge of the times, the blacklisting, the Vietnam era and the folk spirit.

title: Cute Little Mystery
text:
We liked this book. It is a quick read, narrated by the title character and filled with juvenile digressions and social jokes and traumas. I got through the book in less than and hour and probably shorter for the two kids who read it in our house. I did over hear chuckles so it's humor does seem to strike a chord.

What I found most interesting about the book is that it really focuses on the social lives of a group of girls and their nemesi. It was interesting how much more my partners daughter liked it than my son. There are pranks, bullying, support, and friendship in the book and it is all well done. It's definitely written for younger people in mind.7-9 is where I would put it.

Illustrations are cute, the story is cute. All in all a cute little book.

title: Super Fast Read, Interesting Facts
text:
This was a nice little graphical introduction to Chinese history. It did a lot to tie together my disparate knowledge of China. It finally makes sense where the wall is (in part it traces the border of the well watered lands.) and the terra cotta army and Confucius now have a context in Chinese history.

The book is chronological and organized into a bunch of quickly digestible factoids, tables, charts and maps. It is very visual and can be breezed through. I'm sure it lacks greatly in depth, but soars in giving a quick idea of Chinese history.

Personally, I love to learn about anything and loved to have this quick introduction and will definitely look for the later volumes, especially as the importance of China increases. It was very interesting to read about the cycle of empires which solidified my idea that the current government has a idea that their place is tenuous. Fascinating read, fascinating country and culture to watch.

title: Beautifully designed, quick simplistic facts
text:
Definitely a light, high level view of US history with a highly illustrated style. It is aimed at a young audience and filled with quick engaging facts. I was married to a history teacher for 16 years so I have learned to be wary of quick, breezy facts and the most egregious thing I could see was that for state wildlife it listed Jaguars in New Mexico. (I know there is a single wild male in near Tucson, AZ, but that seemed like a stretch.)

Like many quick and dirty fact books, some things are very glossed over so the facts that might be technically true, they seem a little simplistic. But I am happy to see that the authors/editors did not shy away from scandals and controversies.

I read it in a couple hours, aided by an easy reading text and rich illustrations taking up much space. My kids love these kind of quick fact books so I'm looking forward to them reading this.

title: A Decent Book but I was Left Wanting More Resolution
text:
Perhaps my expectations were set too high for this book, but I found it to be a little bit of a let down. I do appreciate how the author handled both the transgender and bipolar worlds, but I felt a little let down by the climax. For much of the book the dilemna was whether Lily would get her hormone replacement treatments which seemed a little repetitive, but authentic. I guess what I really didn't like was that the climax which I won't give a spoiler, but the two main characters come together in a public venue to show support for each other. But for me, that seems to be when the stressors would truly start. That is the point where they would start feeling even stronger cultural pressures. I do see that there was a bravery in it, and it is a place to stop at the change of openess, but I feel cheated to not know the reaction from that point on.

OK, that all seems a little too harsh, because the book is decently written. It broaches two taboo subjects in one book and does it with respect and care. I just feel left wanting for more. It seemed like an easy place to end a book. Perhaps that is good too though. I for one am left moved and wondering about the characters futures.

title: A Very Broad Look At Sausages,even Vegetarian Options
text:
It's hard not to give this book five stars except that it doesn't have a photo for each sausage. Call it lack of vision if you like but I can't get into a recipe if it doesn't have a mouth watering photo. There is a color section of photos in the middle for a number of them and the photos are perfect, just with there were more.

Otherwise the author took on a daunting challenge of putting in all things sausage. The breadth is fantastic and the most exciting thing for me is the vegetarian section. Unfortunately the broad scope of the book shows in the vegetarian section as there was not enough to answer all the questions, but it did put me on the right track toward finding cellulose casings. I wish more time could have been dedicated to the subject, but the book is broad in scope. I don't think that's an issue because it is an impressive book. And like I said, there was plenty of information to get me down the road. We tried two sausages based on his recipes and using his vegetarian base (there is a vegan recipe as well.) I'm a big fan of biscuits and gravy and dating a vegetarian so I have a few problems to solve. We came close, definitely acceptably close bit we need a little tweaking. But thanks to the author for helping us get an old favorite back on the menu.

Where the breadth of the scope was a problem for details in the vegetarian section, it is a triumph in selection. Even in the vegetarian section, there is a wealth of ethicities and types shown. Even without photos, the titles are mouth watering. There are several I would like to try at the cabin on guys weekends. So the broad scope is both pro and con, and in the end, this is a great resource.

title: Ridiculous Book But Kids Liked It
text:
I actually like books with random ridiculous components. In this case it is kidnapping crocs who inprison various nocturnal animals for there subterranean sports. The premise is a little out there...

But I will always love a book that gets kids to read and it did do that. We have recently been talking a lot about pangolins so it was nice to see one featured, and see them finally get some legal protections before they disappear completely. The natural history facts are ok, although you would never see this cast of characters in the same place outside a zoo. At first it caused me some mental gymnastics trying to place all these species together geographically. By the time kiwis were thrown in, I gave up on trying to find scientific truth in the book.

So you get what you get, a playful book where pangolins walk with coyotes, crocs worry about their coaching skills and bats talk in a mix of English and Yiddish. It's a mild mystery with odd friends banding together to save the day. It reads well, the kids liked it, which makes it a good book.

title: A very nice general travel guide to Alaska
text:
This is a nuts and bolts guide to visiting Alaska. It has the basics of where to stay, where to eat, and what to see. It is very good for those who want to make sure they have their itinerary before they arrive. Personally, I like enough information to make sure I don't miss something, but I don't want to lose the feeling of exploration. But this book is valuable for both ends, and is a great resource for planning.

What makes this book special a step above the average AAA travel guide are the color photos and beautiful maps. They don't do full justice to the state, but they do make the book prettier than the old Fodors guides of 20 years ago. This is not a photo book, but it is well illustrated. Better than the photos are the maps which have gotten better and better over the years.

Other than the logistical information, there is a smattering of nature and historic information to give you a sense of place. It is nice, a little spare, but a good starting point. As an example, there is history information up front, but uf you want a strong sense of history you should look other places. Likewise, there are several areas that talk about animals with photos, but it could never replace decent field guides. But like I said, it is a great logistical reference.

title: An Insider's Look at the Seattle Writer's Community
text:
This was not quite what I had in mind.
