It still grates on me to hear the bad grammar that covers as "alien speak," but it seems harmless enough. This book throws a little chuckle in for the grown ups which is nice. The illustrations and construction of the book are beautiful. Quality of the book is very good.

If this book gets as many readings as the original, it too is worth its weight in gold.

title: A good historic fiction for younger readers, a litle less than I was hoping for though
text:
I got this book wondering how the story could be pieced together from bits of poetry. I envisioned something close to pointillism in art, but the poetry is actually quite narrative, almost too narrative. The story line is pretty straight-forward and the verse is pretty close to prose.

The story is clean and clear and perfect for the 9-12 graders my wife teaches history to. (She quickly nabbed this book for her classroom library.) Unfortunately I think I got my hopes a little too high, and the book didn't seem to poetically paint pictures as well as I was hoping Nor give as much insight into the world of deafness as I was hoping. The story mirrors the author's life story to a degree, so I was hoping for a stronger, more intimate treatment of the struggles of the main character.

The historic content of the book is good, although this is where the book often gets too narrative. Which might be good for the juvenile fiction audience, but it comes off a little blunt.

This all seems a little too harsh, I think I just expected too much from a book aimed at a younger audience. The book is good, just less than I was hoping for. If you liked [[ASIN:B001UEQIWY Out Of The Dust (Apple Signature Edition)]], you will like this book as well, however I came away from this book thinking that this book was not quite as strong.

title: Dense, Academic, Relegated to Reference
text: I read a lot of history and was excited to read about a time period I am not overly familiar with.  I can't really say anything bad about this book.  The parts I read were good, but it is so dense and so academic it has a slight sedative effect on me. I put the review off for this book because I kept thinking I would get back to reading it but never did. I liked what I read and I skimmed around to a few sections that I was interested in, but the book is just too dense for enjoyable reading.  However, I see a future for it as a reference for the time period.

title: It did what I was hoping for
text:
Ok, here is the dilemma I was in - I have a 60 year old father in another state and needs to be able to touch up photos. Since I am in IT, he calls me to do tasks like rotating photos. He is not computer savvy and keeps getting out-dated, garage-sale, photo programs for his PC which I have no idea how to use.

The answer was buying a copy of Photoshop Elements and this book. I shipped the software to him before I got the book but I was able to get him through the basics on the phone. When the book came I breezed through it (I use full photoshop which has a surprisingly different feature set) and was surprised about the use of albums and other photo organizational tools. The book helped me walk him through the basics of setting up the folder structure.

I also used the book to walk him through stuff like cropping. It was much easier having the book describe things and show me what the screens look like rather than have dad describe it. This book was a perfect reference for getting him up and running, although the tutorial format is a little much for what we were looking for.

Now that he is up and running, I am suggesting him to get his own copy of the book. I'm keeping this one hear because it is always easier for him to call then to look something up himself.

title: A Good Overview of a Great Man
text:
I've read a lot of Alaska mountaineering books and stories over the years, and this book stands with the best for readability and holding interest. And since there are no modern climbing books that fail to mention Washburn's accomplishments, I was happy to get my hands on a new biography about the legendary climber. He truly pioneered Alaskan Climbing with the use of glacier landings and air drops to bringing a more alpine style of climbing to the state.

For the most part I am very happy with this book. It was a great read that I never found tiresome. However, I have to think that it might be harder for someone who is new to the climbing world to get into. The book is written from an insider from the clique-ish world of climbers, which leads to a lot of name dropping and side stories. Each story in itself is interesting, but when the names loop back it tends to get a little confusing and overwhelming. I definitely felt I had an advantage by having read a number of other climbing books first. The author does a reasonable job of introducing the names, but it is a lot to digest at one time

Probably the best thing a biography can do is give a sense of the person. In that, I don't feel that the book put me inside Washburn's head, but I did get a strong sense of what it was like to be in his presence. The author builds a strong portrait of his character - driven and stubborn but also wonderfully sharing with his knowledge. I can see why he reached the top of Denali three times and I am so happy below 5000 feet. The worst thing a biographer can do is deify his subject which I think the author steered clear of. He is free with pointing out shortfalls but paints a likeable portrait that seems to ring true while reading.

Toward the end of the book there were a few episodes that seemed to be forced in, from a family scandal to what may be a few too many of the author's personal climbing stories. However as a whole the book was well worth the read.

title: I was hoping for some project management tips and a little cheerleading - I got a dose of reality
text:
I was looking for a book that would help me lay out a course toward achieving a fairly reasonable dream. What I got was a book that had me look very realistically at that dream and see how likely it was that I would achieve it. I turned out alright, but I have to admit I have a few questions that I could not answer as strongly as I should.

The book is not intentionally unsupportive, but it does lay out a few facts and questions that can point toward potential difficulties in reaching your dream. The good news is that if you "fail" the test questions, it does show you where you need to be to achieve your dream. But it also does explain the possibility that your dream may not be achievable or may be misguided. For me, my dream is definitely not achievable without a little more sacrifice and motivation but ultimately well within my abilities, control, and passions.

The book also spends time questioning if this dream is really what you want. It has a strong message throughout that pursuing your dreams and passions is a great way to happiness and satisfaction. To get there though you need to be picking the right dream. I tested myself on this and was surprised to find that what I saw as the end products do not seem to be my biggest aspiration, but rather the process to that end. I had never written down what my dream was in specific details before, but after doing that, the simple end goal is the smallest part of my dream.

There is some self help-type babble and quotes to help motivate, but the core message of the book is aligning yourself up with your real dreams and realistically evaluating where you are on the path to achieving it. I really feel closer to achieving my goal now that I have a much clearer vision of what I want. And I'm happy that my dream passed the test (with room for improvement!)

I don't typically care for "self help" type books, but this one was a winner.

title: A Decent Comic that held our kids attention and seemed to have taught him a little
text:
Our household has a seven-year-old and a history teacher in it, so this book seemed like a perfect combination for us - a historical fiction comic book. And for the most part it was successful. My son sat down and read it without stopping, very much engrossed in it. Then later on a walk he mentioned a few things he had learned from the book like the fact that British soldiers were call "Lobster Backs" by some of the colonists.

The best thing historical fiction can do is to create a sense of time and place and allow the reader to feel the spirit and realities of the time. In some ways I think the comic format took away from this since the images were provided so your imagination does not work as hard. Also it ends up seeming that the entire revolution revolved around the two fictional main characters who somehow found themselves in the middle of every major event from the Boston Tea Party to Bunker Hill. It seemed a bit of the stretch but it did give a storyline to string together historic events.

The comic is adequately illustrated, it is by no means a masterpiece of art but the images are clear and effective. There is a little bit of adolescent material like hiding in the sewage cart and some flirtatious banter between the main characters to help kids stay engaged. My wife was not completely won over and will not be adding it to her curriculum, but she said it was a good way to introduce kids to some of the events.

Personally, I kind of enjoyed reading it.

title: An Good Starting Point, Lacks a Little Depth.
text:
This is a decent little book, but since it covers the entire state, it
needs to stick to the main attractions and does not got too deep into
any location. There will be just a couple of recommendations for
restaurants for example, and attractions like Gatorland are missing from
the Orlando coverage.

Quality: This book seems a little more glossy than the run of the mill
Frommer's book and it did an excellent job when I was flipping through
and showing my seven year old possible things we could do while on our
vacation. It is not crammed with photos, but it has enough to make page
flipping worthwhile.

Coverage: Since my son is into nature and fossil collection, we needed a
lot more resources to find a fossil expedition and specific nature
stops. Also, since our trip was mainly concentrating on the southwest
coast, the other 3/4ths of the book did not help much. And as stated
above, there were not a whole lot of different options, this is a pretty
general book possibly because the targeted audience are British
vacationers focusing on Disney and Universal theme parks. The travel
information was decent, although quaintly British again.

British thing: Forgive me if I am missing something about Frommers, but
this book is strongly aimed at the British visitor to Florida. For the
most part this is no problem as long as you can get over hire car
instead of rental car or the idea of "liquified baby food," But there is
a decidedly British tilt to attraction selection as well, for example
biplane rides for kids with Biggles fascination. Very few kids on this
side of the pond have any idea what Biggles is about. The book does not
say it is written for Brits but it seems to have been. (Even tells you
where you can get British newspapers.) It still worked for us as a very
high level overview of Florida, but to match our families interests, we
had to go other places as well.

Overall impression: Decent book, but light on specifics or depth of
choices. If you are looking for off the beaten track options you might
want

title: An Interesting Pop Historical Read
text:
This is a book you can sit down and read for mild, non-fiction entertainment. I was kind expecting a book with obscure stories that I had not heard about, but what it ended up being was a kind of overview of fairly well known historical "failures." I'm not complaining it was still entertaining and somewhat educational but there wasn't anything shocking. The writing is not academic and is mostly general overviews backed up with a good supply of quotes and some fantastic photos and illustrations. The author does some analysis but does not go too in-depth.

One thing I hate is getting a book like this is finding out that it was written by a political pundit who blames the worlds ills on Clinton/Bush, GOP/Dems or liberals/neocons. When I saw that they skipped from Reagan's Iran Contra Gate to Bush 43's Iraq war, I immediately worried that this is just another book of punditry. But I am glad he left out Clinton/Lewinsky/Paula Jones. They were sad political events, but as the author explains, these were personal failures that actually only impacted a small group of people. (compared to Bay of Pigs or Japanese internment camps.) However, I'm surprised that he would include a chapter on Bush. There is still a lot of history to be written. The Iraq War may not even end up being his biggest failure. I think I would have given that one another decade to reflect.

I read this book backwards, because I could better judge the author's coverage of the events I knew best. I was impressed, I spent the first day having thoughts like "Oh yeah, I remember that plane going down in Nicaragua." It was kind of a nice look back now that the pieces have fallen into place. Between me and my wife, who is a history teacher, we could only find one thing we did not agree with, and that may have been a typo. The author claims the Spanish American war had the most casualties of any war between the Civil War and World War II, which we both had problems with since it seems that World War 1 should have beaten it pretty soundly.

The book itself is a very high quality book. The pages are thick paper and the chapters are richly illustrated. Physically, I have seen very few books that stand up to it for quality of production. For content, it is very good although it stays to the surface of the events pretty much. There are things that will make some people with certain political leanings a little irate, but it seems fair the parties involved, which is refreshing.

I recommend it to anyone looking for a pop history book that might fall under the category of bathroom reading.

title: A Patchwork History filling in the times from Columbus to the Revolution
text:
It is nice to see a book that covers what American history text books usually gloss over. We don't hear much between the discovery of North America until the American Revolution, at best we get Pilgrims, Jamestown, and then the Boston Tea Party. This book points out that there was a lot going on during these years and a lot of it was of international significance and also pretty bloody.

The book is a collection of historic events, mostly involving wars between the different colonizing nations or between colonists and Amerindians. Also, the stories are mostly pretty bloody. The one half exception to the war stories is the story of Anne Hutchinson who defied her role in church and society but in the end she is also killed in an massacre.

Each event is covered as a encapsulated story with little or no attempt to link them together in a narrative. The events basically run in chronological order, however a couple overlap in a disconcerting manner. In the end I was wishing there was at least a simple timeline so I could keep the stories straight and understand the chronological relationships between the events.

The physical construction of the book is very good, with nice heavy paper. I like the vintage design, the type font and lay out echoes colonial book design. And it is richly illustrated with woodcuts and reproductions of etchings and paintings.

All in all, I really enjoyed the book. It was very readable, but it left me feeling like it was a bunch of anecdotes more than a history book. It also left me with a very brutal vision of life in Colonial times, which may be pretty close to the truth.

title: A gripping but violent novel
text:
As a word of warning: My wife and I are huge fans of historical fiction. She grabbed this one off my reading stack before I could get to it and returned it shortly after saying that it was too graphically violent for her. After reading the book, I can see her point. So be careful if you are not into violence.

That said, this is a well-crafted book. Bondurant does a great job of creating characters and weaving his story and time lines into a book which I could neither put down, nor get out of my mind. It vividly brought to life a violent and hard-scrabble time in our history with characters which were both larger than life and yet terribly human. The fact that this was generally a true story made it all the more compelling.

Personally the violence seemed a little heavy, but there was a frank brutality that seemed to ring true to the realities of the lives and time of the characters. I loved the descriptions of the distilling process and illicitly running liquor as well as the intrigues of the trade.

It is interesting how the author uses author Sherwood Anderson in the book. Where the reader is given access to the thoughts, motives, and actions of all the characters in their own good time, Anderson shows how closed the local society is. His attempts to get to the bottom of the moonshine culture are for the most part thwarted, blocked by a wall of silence that illustrates the secrecy of the business.

The descriptions of the time period and locality are rich with details. Events like the Spanish Flu, the depression, and the trial are all sewn seamlessly into the narrative. Any read that can capture my imagination like this is one did was well worth my time and deserves my recommendation.

title: A good book that was hard to put down, but might be hard to remember
text:
This book was slightly reminiscent of [[ASIN:B0018RN4NY Girl With Pearl Earring by Johannes Vermeer,21.9 in. x 27.9 in.]], it combines a bit of the painter's style as well as the society in which they live. It was a good book that kept me engrossed and entertained throughout the tale, but I am not sure that the story have the lasting impact that great books have. Very much worth the time to read, but not a life changer.

Ivy's red hair catches your eye on the cover (and be honest we do choose books based on the cover!) just as her hair catches the eye of a great many characters. Her story however is all about how she drifts through them. She is a bit likeable, but she has a spine like the cabbage in her meals. She becomes addicted to laudanum and at times you get pulled right down into her drug addled life leaving you wondering when she will get some gumption. She makes a few decisions toward the end of the book which leads to a surprisingly decent ending.

I liked the descriptions of poverty and the unscrupulous con artists and roustabouts in the book. It shows the filthy, dirty life of the poor in 19th century England much like Dickens, but in a much lighter, easier read. Unlike Dickens though, I don't think this book will give me lifelong images. I would recommend it, but not put it on a must read list.

title: Hard to put down...
text:
My family's roots and a little of my gene pool are from the Lakota and the area covered in this book, so I was instantly interested when I saw it. Also, my wife is an American history teacher, so there were a few discussions about who got to read it first, or where did it disappear to, or what happened to my bookmark...

We were both pleased with the book, it reads well, it is very believable and it is well thought out. We did have some issues with some of the facts and how they were presented, but they were very minor. Some examples were things like hearing the bullet whiz by and then see the muzzle flash (bullets luckily go slower than the speed of light.) and the narrative introduction of preloaded cartridges for muzzleloaders seemed a little off. But on the other hand, after research on our part, other historical questions we had ended up being right on in the book. So it seems very well researched. I do have a problem with the sequence of Fetterman being led into the ambush. It seems a little contrived and I have read better, more likely scenarios. This story pretty much follows the account that rose just after the incident which most likely has some inaccuracies from the accountable officers.

Perhaps the ultimate sign of value, my wife has already thought of using quotes and reading some sections in the classroom. It is a good answer to European centric histories much in the vein of [[ASIN:0972475303 Dances with Wolves]]. It is a great piece of historical fiction.

title: Great High Level Overview of Bear Viewing in Alaska, But You Will Still Need to Research the Details to Plan a Trip.
text:
This is a very well written book, but I had high expectations when I heard it was coming out. I envisioned a glossy but informative, "Frommer's" or "Eyewitness" type guide that had good maps and beautiful images for each viewing location, with very specific transportation, lodging, timing, tips, and suggestions.

This book seems to be a high level guide mixing the current Bear Viewing industry and a how to act in bear country guide. The facts are presented in a general manner. For example, rather than saying "Use guides A or B" or plan to travel the second or third weeks of July, they have a list of questions to ask of your guide and suggest mid-summer visits during salmon runs. This is understandable, specific information would go out of date quickly and bears' habits are variable. So, the more vague information has a longer shelf life and is weather-proof. The information in the book is valuable, but the book does not contain all the answers you'll need to plan a trip.

Location descriptions take up a third of the book, but they are short and again somewhat vague. Brooks River, which deserves pages, is given a paragraph of a hundred or so words. I was hoping for at least a map, description of camping availability, maybe a timing chart showing average peaks in bear presence and at least the iconic photo of a Brooks River bear catching the salmon mid-air. They spent 28 words describing the picture. I would have preferred a thousand words worth of photo.

Where the book soars is when it discusses bear etiquette and ethics. The author is knowlegeble and prudent in his advice. His descriptions of bear behavior and ideal viewer behavior is what should be taken away from this book. Techniques is a strong word to use in the title, they're more like guidelines, but I think this is the meat of this book.

Also, the book is filled with great photos, but again, I was hoping glossy national geographic type photos rather than black and white textbook images. I'm sure it was a cost saving compromise but they lost some of their power in the printing process.

Sounds like I am slamming the book. I really can't, it's a good book. I was just hoping for something different. I guess my advice is to expect a fantastic general overview of the subject. What is there is great, what is missing are the specific details you need to start your trip planning.

title: Great little field guide for Minnesota Fishermen, wish it covered all species
text:
This is a beautifully designed book. The durable, waterproof pages and compact size make it perfect for tossing in the boat or tackle box. The illustrations are great and are helpful in identifying the basic sport fish from the state of Minnesota. Each species has a good, but not overly thorough description including habitats, distribution, etc. The best part of the description is comparison to similar species.

All in all, this is a good book, but unfortunately it is not comprehensive. While it does cover the common game fish, but is spotty for others. For example, it only covers the River Redhorse and omits all other redhorse species (shorthead, Greater, Silver....) Similarly the only carpsucker covered is the quillback (no mention of river or highfin carpsuckers.) For nearly all fishermen, this is no problem, but we do a lot of multi-species river fishing (trash fishing) and keep a life list of species caught so this book sorta lets us down, but most fishermen will not need to differentiate a chestnut lamprey from a silver lamprey.

If you are looking for a comprehensive field guide to Minnesota fish, try [[ASIN:0816609829 Fishes of the Minnesota Region]] (out of print.) But even that book is not as complete as I would like. Not all species are illustrated, although all are described (even the obscure ones.) Also, it is not nearly as well designed as this book.

All in all, I would say, if you are looking for a handy, very-usable, beautifully illustrated book, that will identify 95% of the fish you catch get this book. Definitely get it if you are fine with writing off all junk fish as either carps or suckers. This book will definitely remain in my tackle box. If it had all species, I would rate this 5+ stars.

title: Beautiful Book - but Make sure it is what you want
text:
This is a typically well designed and beautifully illustrated book from the National Geographic Society. It is great to flip through and grabs your attention. Note though, this is not really a guide to just the National Parks of Alaska. It is more a guide to all the wild areas and tourist sites of Alaska as they relate to the eight National Parks in the state.

For example, of the 42 pages dedicated to Denali National Park, 12 were about the park itself (of which 3 were full page illustrations) 30 pages of the chapter were dedicated to "Exursions from the National Park." This included everything from briefly describing Fairbanks and Talkeetna to a description of the Yukon-Charley Preserve on the Canandian border.

It is a great book, and well worth it for someone looking for a reference to put together an multi-day itinerary based around one of the parks, but if you are looking for more in-depth information about a certain park, you may want to pick up a different reference. On the other hand, if you love nature, Alaska and beautiful photos, this might be a book for you.

title: A Great Stocking Stuffer or Gift for anyone interested in Alaska Birds
text:
This is a great little book (definitely pocket sized). Great images, good information, good design. Do be careful though, this is not an advanced field guide. If you are looking for a field guide to take on a serious Alaskan birdwatching trip, look at getting the Sibley's Western or National geographic.

The book would be good for a casual or novice bird watcher or feeder watcher. The book is organized by bird color which would make more sense to a novice when compared to the family organization found in other guides.

If nothing else, it would make a great gift. Any birdwatcher would appreciate the quality of the photos. Especially good for daydreaming about that once in a lifetime Alaskan Birding trip.

title: A great guide, but look for the new edition.
text:
This is a great guide book to hiking and photography Denali, but if you are considering buying this book, look for the new edition. It is titled Denali National Park Guide to Hiking, Photography & Camping, or search on the Ike Waits.

This book has a lot of great suggestions for day and overnight hiking trips. Also, Waits gives lots of practical advice earned from his years of experience. He goes right down to which side of the bus is better to sit on to get pictures while heading into the park and where to sit heading out. I would highly recommend this book, except that the new edition has more of everything that makes this book great.

title: Interesting Read, Horrible Example to Follow
text:
Like many people I read this book shortly after Timothy's fatal mauling. I was expecting an academic book about bears that laid out the research findings of Timothy Treadwell. What I got was something of a cross between the horse-whisperer and that crazy woman who used to live down the street who had tea parties with her 50 stupidly named cats.

I have to admit I found the book intriguing although I was constantly feeling uneasy about what he was saying and doing. I think spreading information and love for animals, especially animals that could be at risk, is good. In the end we truly will only save what we value. But, by the end of this book I was deeply concerned about what kind of an example Timothy is giving the world. Bears, especially the coastal Browns in Katmai, are not blood thirsty killers, but the nature of bears is unpredictable, and much like people, different from individual to individual. Timothy does make this clear in his different encounters with bears.

What Timothy does not point out or even seem to consider is that historically any time bears become habituated to people, bears suffer. Timothy's close approach to bears did nothing to help the bears or bear research. At best it only boosted his celebrity. In the book, he mentions several of these irresponsible encounters, in one example he leans over to kiss a yearling bear on the nose.

I recommend reading the book, even if at times it seems like watching a train wreck. If possible, read it with Grizzly Maze by Nick Jans or Death in the Grizzly Maze by Mike Lapinski. After you realize that he embellished nearly all parts of his life; claiming to be Australian, claiming to be an orphan .... You will get the grain of salt you should take with this book.

title: A Happy Surprise
text:
I started this book with very few expectations other than it would be about sharks. What I got was not at all what I was expecting, but I feel it was well worth reading. The book is not a series of shark attack stories, but the story of one person's attempts to get near to white sharks. When she discovers the Farralones, the author is taken in by not just the sharks, but also, the whole lifestyle of the researching them. She revels in the hardships, histories, thrills, disappointments, and humanity of researching and living in the Farralones, and this is what this book is about.

I have always dreamt about living the life of a research biologist so I loved this book. It is well written and kept me engaged throughout the book. If I had one criticism, it's that after the 10th person she ran into that was "ruggedly handsome and athletic," I started wondering if she ever met anyone she didn't think was irresistibly attractive. Seems like she tries too hard to paint everyone in a good light.

Important Note ---- If you are looking to read a "Jaws, 2005," don't get this book

But ---- If you want a well written book that explores the Farralones Islands, the world of field research biologists, and ones person's quest to live her dreams of being near Great White Shark and nature, get this book.

title: A truly beautiful book but not necessarily enough
text:
Armstrong's book is filled with beautiful photographs and covers all the regular species that you will see in Alaska. It is a great introduction to the birds that inhabit the area. Every Alaskan birdwatcher should have a copy.

But, if you are a beginning birder, or new to the Northwest you might need a different field guide. Animals are illustrated with one, two, or three photographs. Unfortunately photographic guides are often deceiving in the field. I recommend you take another good field guide with you.

Each species has 90 to 100 words to cover field marks, similar species, voice and habitat. In some cases like the Black-Backed Woodpecker, only 56 words are used. The writing is great, but the scope of the book does not allow in-depth coverage of each species.

Range finding is limited to a chart with six rows for regions and four rows for seasons. In Alaska, six regions are equal to six average states in the lower forty eight and saying Common, Uncommon or Rare in a region doesn't help pinpoint the species much. A map would do better to give an idea of locations (at least pointing out a species as coastal, or centered on mountain ranges in a given area etc.)

I wouldn't talk anyone out of getting this book, it is beautiful and well written, but if you are planning a birding trip and need to find locations - try West's A Birders Guide to Alaska, and if you are unsure of your ability to indentify birds in Alaska, at least augment this book with the Sibley or National Geographic Guides. If you going to one of the shorebird festivals, definitely get a specialized guide like Paulson's Shorebird Guide.

***** Update *******
There is now a new edition of this book since this review was written, for the most part, the strengths and weaknesses are the same. However, the one thing that has changed strikingly is that many if not most of the photos were replaced and are even better than those from the last edition. A beautiful book just got more beautiful.

title: If you read Treadwell's Among Grizzly, read this too.
text:
It seems like people either blindly love or hate Timothy Treadwell. Lapinski tries to walk the line, although he clearly is at odds with parts of Treadwell's message (Rightfully so when people take his message to be that bears can be encroached on or treated lightly. Treadwell's story is the perfect anectdote for bear attacks - Bears are not bloodthirsty killers, but they are unpredicactable enough that you must respect their space and habits.)

If you haven't read Among Grizzlies, you may want to read it before this book. Lapinski spends a lot of times referring to and reacting to specific passages in Treadwell's book.

I do think that Lapinski did a good job of trying to stay unbiased, but I always question biographers agendas. Often they spend too much time attacking hypocrasies or covering up shortfalls. For Lapinski, the most interesting and telling parts of this book are the stories from Treadwell's "friends." The information that Lapinski gathers from Tim's friends and supporters show interesting patterns in a complicated personality.

Also, I appreciated his handling of Amy Huegenard who often is a neglected side of this tragedy.

title: Fast, Entertaining Read - Not a Guide to Visiting Bear Country
text:
Larry Kaniut has made a career of writing white-knuckled real life thrillers. This book is no different. It's kind of like a car accident, once you start reading you can't turn your eyes away. It's easy to get into the book but hard to put down. What better material than bear attacks to capture your imagination.

There are lessons to learn from this book, but for the most part it is a collection of sensational bear stories presented for their entertainment value. If you are looking for a scientific look at bear attacks, this might not be the book for you - Try Stephen Herrero's Bear Attacks, Their Causes and Avoidence.

If you want a book that throws one gripping bear attack after another, get this one. And if you didn't get enough from this book, try More Bear Tales by Larry Kaniut.

One more bit of advice, read this one in your bedroom, not in a tent in the middle of Denali National Park.

title: A Great Guide if you don't know where to begin.
text:
This is a great book for anyone who just doesn't know where to start on planning their first trip to Alaska. The book is filled with valuable information from the writer of Frommer's Alaska. Be sure not to get both Alaska for Dummies and the Frommer's Alaska guide because there is a lot of overlap.

Unfortunately, this book is completely void of photographs which is a shame in a state as picturesque as Alaska.

If you are looking at purchasing this book, the second edition is being released on March 14, 2005. I just finished the book so I thought I would put my two cents in about it.

title: Great book but isn't right for everyone
text:
First, I have to say the scope of this book is amazing. It covers over 750 bodies of fishable waters that can be reached by the Alaska road system. There aren't any other books that come close to describing that many locations. Of course the trade off is that the individual descriptions are not very deep or detailed.

I can't say anything bad about this book because I have found it to be very helpful in locating new fishable waters, but I think there are better books out there for those who are going for a once in a life time trip. Try Scott Haugen's Flyfisher's guide to Alaska (even if you don't plan to flyfish) or if you can find it Renee Lemere's Fishing Alaska which Pedersen helped write, there are many others.

So who should get this book? Anyone who will be spending a lot of time in Alaska. If you are cruising the highways in your RV, this is a great resource to find a place to fish within a short drive of anywhere. It also has a place on any resident fisherman's book shelf too. It's an impressive book with great but shallow information, just make sure it fits what you are looking for.

title: Relishing Life Every Lurch of the Way!
text: As a woman of a certain age, I enjoyed this book much as I would a lengthy conversation with a friend I’d known for years.  I enjoyed Charlie  creating and sharing his life lessons, his sometimes sweet, occasionally slightly acrid internal commentaries.  The editing was superior to many books I’ve read, with only a couple of minor errors.  The Chapter-opening jokes were a pleasant lead-in, and some of them were new to me!  I will recommend this author to others who are making their way through aging-as well as their children, now in their fifties, who are finally seeing their parents as having more questions than answers.

title: Gritty, raw, believable journey of a broken woman officer.
text: The economy of the writing perfectly suited the tale of a woman once confident and proud in her police work, being unable to surmount a disastrous confrontation that broke her spirit and body.  Acknowledging her descent into alcohol abuse, neglecting herself ..all are laid bare without whining or self pity.  Some small spark of survival instinct becomes fanned, almost against her will, and she stumbles.lurches and vomits her way to a sort of redemption.  Or it it?

title: Handy and accurate
text: MapEasy's Guidemaps have accompanied us to places around the world. The Rome map is another reminder of why we continue to use them. It's accurate, up-to-date, and helps describe where you are and what you are looking at all with just a glance. We've taken to circling areas we don't want to miss and to making our own notes on the maps. The drawings help one locate specific areas more easily and MapEasy always seems to include those places you'll want to be sure to see. It's also far easier to carry a Guidemap than cumbersome travel books!

title: Cute, Wish They Had Hardback Option
text: This is really cute, but it should honestly be made into a hardback book. I would give it 5 stars for that. Otherwise, great serk and find book centered around a favorite character.

title: Cute Way to Add in Education; Little Flimsy
text: These are so fun for nightine to learn things under a flashlight. It makes bedtime a fun way to add in education! I only wish the cards were thicker. These are quite flimsy. We decided to laminate ours to hold up longer. It does hamper the light coming through as cute, but it works.

title: Great All in One Resource for Swapping Out Your Cleaning Cabinet
text:
I've been following her blog for awhile and decided it would be nice to have her written resource. I've been working on building a small collection of cleaning resources, particularly for when people ask me for tips, I can hand them a nice copy!

I LOVED the section on what is in mainstream cleaning products and why you want to avoid them. That really helps to have a one stop resource for that! It was nicely written and easily understandable! I love that there is the WHY and the recipes all in one spot.

I learned a lot more about peroxide than I had known before so that was great! I have been studying cleaning products for over a year, so some of the recipes and tips about baking soda and vinegar weren't new to me, but would be FANTASTIC for someone just starting out. This is a book I want to send to many of my family and friends - READ THIS! It helps explain so much and help you step by step swap out products. I really liked how there was room by room analysis of products to switch out!

There are some things that start to feel overwhelming. I personally am not anywhere near buying 100% cotton or looking at specific mattresses etc. That's probably not going to happen for me. But I do love that she gives you a thorough examination of what all the products around us entail. Just be prepared if you're just starting out that it could seem like everything is bad for a second. ha I don't think she makes you feel that way because she reminds you it's all a process. Just a heads up :) Definitely recommend this book!

title: Cute and Engaging
text: We had found another Priddy Slide and Find at the thrift store and my kid loved it. So we went searching for more and found this one. These slide and finds are so fun and great for motor coordination! This trucks one is neat because even I learned the names for some trucks I didn't know! Educational and fun!

title: Four Stars
text: works for my needs

title: Pretty good
text: Not as good as the first one but still good, I am interested in seeing how the series progresses in the next book.

title: Give it a read
text: Definitely entertaining. A new world in magic based fantasy with its own terms and rules.  A society with a class system and where Aric is the norm. The better your talents, the more useful you are and the better position you secure. An original storyline and plot. Worth the read!

title: The Monsters are Real
text: A new type of horror from author Stephen King shows us that horror does not have to lie in the supernatural but in ordinary humans.  The story about a murderous young man and a retired investigator is a suspenseful  story that shows that the real monsters can be the people in our everyday lives.  The book takes us into the mind of the killer and gives us a background to try and explain how he became the twisted mind he is.  It is a good story and not like the other books by King has written which I found exciting and refreshing.  It was definitely a bit terrifying but I think that lent to the horror we all seek when we pick up a book by King.

title: Nice for kids and beginners
text: This is a nice little selection of stencils for someone who just wants mostly simple designs and for the kids or beginners. I gave four stars because I had hoped for more intricate designs included. But very nice for kids and beginners.

title: The Tanakh, not so sugar coated
text: I bought this for my 6yo but after looking at it decided the presentation of the stories might be a bit much for him. I gave it to my 11yo instead, and she enjoys it. I think it's a nice companion to The Children's Illustrated Jewish Bible.

title: Kid pleasing punchline
text: This adorable bunny has a charming time while the humans are away, trying out all kinds of human things and meticulously setting everything right at the end. It would be a sweet enough story, but the punchline is that there are (ahem!) little bits of "evidence" that the family is sure to notice. It's not gross; it's gentle, cute and funny. The rabbit was so careful -- darn that poop!

title: Beautifully made, only one quibble
text:
I ordered this book because my 2 year old is really into colors right now, but is having trouble with shades (e.g.: he'll point to a darkish yellow chair and say orange). The book is gorgeously constructed with a hardcover style spine and thick, almost board book pages inside. It's a nice substantial size. The illustrations (yellow lion, orange goldfish, red wagon, pink piggy bank, purple balloons, blue train, green frog, brown teddy bear, white/black/grey panda, and back page with lots of colorful objects) are cute and incorporate several shades. My only quibble is that the grid of 20 shades of each color could show more variety. It's as though they wanted it not to clash. So on the orange page for instance, there are no really bright, obnoxious shades of orange. On the brown page, there are greenish and purplish browns, which is cool, but there are no light brown shades like tan. This is a minor complaint -- the book is awesome and I'll be stocking my gift closet with it to give to every 0-3 year old kid I know.

**Update**
It took me months to realize the color grid only contains the shades used in the facing page's illustration -- that's why the shades for each color are all in the same palette. Makes perfect sense, but it still would have been nice to have more variety. We still love the book!

title: Small; story disappointing
text:
**UPDATE** 9/24/2014
I wrote the original 2 star review (below) when I had one toddler. I'm on my third child now, and my kids have loved this book. It may be tiny, and I may think it lacks resolution, but they are charmed by the sweet Papa, the nifty fold out illustrations, and the little girl dancing with the moon. Time to admit I was wrong and upgrade my rating!

ORIGINAL REVIEW 7/18/2008 -- TWO STARS
This book was much smaller than I expected (I bought the hardcover edition). It's about the size of my hand. The story disappointed me too. It starts out fine, but you're left hanging at the end. I don't think I'd have bought it if I had read it in the store.

SYNOPSIS
Monica sees the full moon, asks Papa to get it. Papa gets long ladder, goes to moon. Moon is too big; moon tells Papa to wait. Papa waits until moon is smaller, brings it to Monica. Monica plays with the moon. "But the moon kept getting smaller and smaller and smaller and finally it disappeared altogether. Then one night, Monica saw a thin sliver of the moon reappear. Each night the moon grew... and grew and grew..." That's how it ends -- with a two page illustration of the full moon.

title: Terrific Plot
text: We have 24 year old grad student Cassie an only child cut adrift to sink or swim by her parents when she won't continue the medical degree they pushed her to pursue (the parents are upper class they gave her a Lexus and took it away I am assuming to force her to go back and get the degree they want her to get and not the advanced degree she wants). The parents basically killed it for me when Cassie's grandmother is driving a 25 year old Honda, jees what a bunch of cheapskates! Cassie is smart, attractive and ambitious, she finds a way to support herself, she gets a contract job as a nanny for 38 year old wealthy Brook, this is a complete win-win, Brook has a cute 6 year old and Cassie has plenty of free time to pursue her degree, Brook has a live in nanny who is smart, fun and loves her kid.  The story line was completely delightful. Very realistic as both Brook and Cassie make some bad decisions. I found the whole thing entertaining. Book Club worthy.

title: Yowzer did this book have impact!
text: I could not stop thinking about this story for at least two days. This title really needs a book club, it will totally elicit animated discussion. Centered around life in upstate New York. 33 year old Julie left her hometown age 19 in pursuit of big city excitement. She had no burning career ambitions so she followed her heart. Now she is back home, living in her grandmother's home under the aegis of her parents, driving her grandmother's car and luckily employed in her parent's wine tasting room. She was dumped by her wife of 8 years without a penny to her name and we slowly find out the whole back story. Luckily she becomes close friends with someone she knew slightly in High School. Taylor is a terrific self assured woman who owns her own business, living her dream. Taylor encourages Julie to follow her arrow, opening Julie's life and leading to one of the most interesting scenes back in NYC that I have ever read.

title: Terrific story set in Nashville
text:
Mason is a record producer and is quite a character. We meet her in the historic Nashville hotspot 'Skull's Rainbow Room' where she 'couldn't help but stare like a horny teenage boy" a burlesque performer Belle.

Victoria is an interesting character too. She has been emotionally abused by her alcoholic mother, the queen of country music, her whole life except for the 4 years she was away at college. It was fascinating to see her 3 years out of college as she currently functions as her mother's assistant.

The author is a born storyteller and this is a book you will not put down or soon forget, I only wish I was in a bookclub that is reading this because there is so much juicy plot to talk about.

title: Hollywood Romance
text: The author had me at Hollywood Romance. In this case we have city girl Lauren with the top job, at age 31, as the go-to Production Stage Manager of the prestigious Majestic Theater in Minneapolis. Into her life comes, late as always, superstar actress, Carly. Carly has burned one too many bridges in Hollywood, and now no studio will hire her because no one who has worked with her wants to work with her again, no matter how many tickets she sells. Everybody who meets her loves her but she has zero work ethic and no consideration for how her actions adversely effect everyone she works with. Luckily for them both Lauren figures out what makes Carly tick, and she might be the key to Carly's woes, if Carly doesn't blow it. As always, this author is natural storyteller and it's her expertise in setting a scene and creating perfect dialogue that make this novel so enjoyable.

title: A Tsunami of a read
text: I live on the Oregon Coast and this author captured not only the locale but also the residents in all their charming, unique, funny and irritating glory. I found myself thinking 'Wow" on more than one chapter. While this is the 3rd in the series there is no need to read them in any particular order to enjoy them all. This is a highly original story that will leave you gasping at the antics of all the characters.

title: Cruise Around Australia
text: I really enjoyed living through Faith she is a terrific character and the descriptions of shipboard life aboard a residential cruise ship was fascinating. This would be a terrific book for a book club choice, I have so much to say about Lowe but it would be spoiler heavy!

title: Not the best
text: I have read them all. This one meanders, a lot. It goes off in a direction that you think will be significant and 200 pages later you are still wondering why the story went there. Still, enjoyable enough for a slow, rainy winter's day.

text:

title: Terrific Christian Book
text: Franklin Graham, who praises the book on the opening page, turns my stomach but if he is someone you admire you are going to love this book. Captain Tammie Jo Shults is a hero in every sense of the word and has my greatest admiration. This is a VERY well told story of her life, culminating in the explosion of her commercial airplane and the saving of nearly every life on the plane.

title: The time to buy this was back in July of 2019
text: The end of October is only going to give you a 14 month calendar. I saw '17" month calendar and jumped at it thinking it was for 2020 to 2021.  FYI the week starts on a Monday rather than the traditional Sunday (Monday makes sense to be because it is the start of the work week for me. The other thing is that the name of the month is too subtlety incorporated into the design - I like big bold lettering for an item like this. The stickers are a great idea to make special information really 'pop' out at you and stores in a pocket in the back of the calendar. No Bleeding through when you use a marker. Unique idea to have a column beginning each week with 5 lines per day that you can write a person's name so that line will carry what that person has coming up that week.

title: Delightful!
text: Maykaya and Spenser are in their early thirties and living a life of childlike joy, whether it's making love with loud exuberance in a public shower at the local gym where they train as competitive fencers or fly in to Hawaii for a family wedding and propose marriage by accident in front of your girlfriend's mother - oops! Like most vacations this didn't start off perfectly, like not telling your girlfriend that while you are staying at her parents home for two weeks it will be in separate bedrooms, ut-oh! But then the vaca makes an unexpected trip, to 1884! Fasten your seat-belt it's going to be a bumpy ride!

title: The most unbelievable Jack Reacher of them all (I've read them all)
text:
The good guys eventually all come to talk and think like Reacher. At least once person seems to have been forgotten altogether. Meanwhile, Child's rhythm continues and the reader stays in it to the end, and it was hugely enjoyable.

Lee Child's novels have a rhythm. It's forceful and regular and pushes or pulls the reader along.There are always bad guys, a nice woman, someone in trouble, and sometimes military or police trained volunteers. Reacher always happens on trouble, gets pulled in while trying to avoid it, and accepts responsibility for fixing what ever is wrong.

In this case, two rival Eastern European mobs in a small US city.There is also a genius geek in Russian hands controlling the mobs and making money by other nefarious means.

This book has more characters than any previous Reacher novel that I remember. Therefore, more violence, mostly perpetrated by Reacher. It's kind of like watching an amusement park shooting gallery. A figure poops up, is shot, or otherwise disposed of. There is a pause for dialogue or planning or transport and then maybe one, maybe nine, targets try to subdue Reacher and he subdues them instead. Neatly and logically.

Finally, what's up with Reacher allowing his picture to be taken? It just felt so wrong.

title: adventure and a rescue mission deep into the Andes of Peru.
text: Interesting combination of comic and abhorrent, fantasy and criminal mystery. The story opens on the bucolic California town of Merryville outwardly an ideal American town with a gentile underbelly of racism, bigotry and homophobia. A cast of characters both American and German, Elvin and Fairies set off for adventure and a rescue mission deep into the Andes of Peru and the Amazon rainforest.

title: Not too big, not too small - just the perfect size
text: LOL I love the premise and the colors, but I really think it needs to be pre-filled with dates to make it practical for me. PLENTY of room to write in. I think it is ideal if you want a mid year calendar say from the day you start a job or a fiscal year or a student/teacher calendar that runs August/September to the following July/August so you don't mind writing in the dates.

title: 5th in the series, but reads as a standalone
text:
Being a Jersey girl myself I have loved reading all 5 in the series set in Northern New Jersey between 1910 and 1920. The latest novel opens up in New Jersey but the action moves to another location Chevy Chase, Maryland, as Americans prepare for possible war and the Kopp sisters do their bit. The main characters are vividly drawn, realistic and if you have any interest in books set 100 years ago this will be enjoyable without being an information dump of facts. Only disappointment for me was not enough Constance Kopp becuase she is such a great character in the earlier books, so I hope is the focus in the next book.

Book 1 - Girl Waits with Gun Constance Kopp doesn’t quite fit the mold. She towers over most men, has no interest in marriage or domestic affairs, and has been isolated from the world since a family secret sent her and her sisters into hiding fifteen years ago. One day a belligerent and powerful silk factory owner runs down their buggy, and a dispute over damages turns into a war of bricks, bullets, and threats as he unleashes his gang on their family farm. When the sheriff enlists her help in convicting the men, Constance is forced to confront her past and defend her family — and she does it in a way that few women of 1914 would have dared.

#2 Lady Cop Makes Trouble In 1915, lady cops were not expected to chase down fugitives on the streets of New York City. But Constance Kopp never did what anyone expected. Constance and her sisters aren’t living the quiet life anymore. They’ve made headlines fighting back against a ruthless silk factory owner and his gang of thugs. After Sheriff Heath sees Constance in action, he appoints her as one of the nation’s first female deputies. But when a German-speaking con man threatens her position—and puts the honorable sheriff at risk for being thrown in his own jail—Constance will be forced to prove herself again.

#3 Miss Kopp's Midnight Confessions Constance Kopp is back—with a badge and a taste for justice. She has finally earned her deputy sheriff’s badge and is ready to tackle a new kind of case: defending independent young women brought into the Hackensack jail on dubious charges of waywardness, incorrigibility, and moral depravity. Such were the laws—and morals—of 1916. Constance uses her authority as deputy sheriff, and occasionally exceeds it, to investigate and support these women when no one else will. But it’s her sister Fleurette—who runs away from their sleepy farm to join the glamorous world of vaudeville—who puts Constance’s beliefs to the test. Is there a wayward girl in her own family?

#4 Miss Kopp Just Won't Quit After a year on the job, New Jersey’s first female deputy sheriff has collared criminals, demanded justice for wronged women, and gained notoriety nationwide for her exploits. But on one stormy night, everything falls apart. While transporting a woman to an insane asylum, Deputy Kopp discovers something deeply troubling about her story. Before she can investigate, another inmate bound for the asylum breaks free and tries to escape. In both cases, Constance runs instinctively toward justice. But the fall of 1916 is a high-stakes election year, and any move she makes could jeopardize Sheriff Heath’s future—and her own. Although Constance is not on the ballot, her controversial career makes her the target of political attacks.

title: Delightfully Quirky Small Town Romance
text: I have been a fan since 2011 when I read the author's debut novel Waiting in the Wings, if you haven't read it you are in for a real treat. This latest novel is charmingly different. Philadelphia Real Estate broker Devyn Winters is at the peak of her success, at age 30 years has achieved her latest goal in life and is super stoked. 12 years ago she left the sleepy town of Dreamers Bay, including her mother and sister, and has only been back twice. She loves her life exactly as it is.  Elizabeth Draper is not just a real sweetheart she is super funny (her humor make this book extra special) and very attractive, if I weren't already married I would wish that I caught her eye before Devyn does. She lives in a sleepy seaside town south of Hilton Head South Carolina. Bonus she has a terrific BFFs and one lives right next door. She has her own business that is both unique and useful to her community and wonderfully fulfilling to her, plus it covers the bills! They are both people I would love to get to know! How the author brings them together throughout the story is very compelling and thought provoking. This will make a excellent book club read.

title: 2020 Calendar
text: Cute calendar, I was attracted by the graphics. Light weight for easy hanging, plenty big to write in notes, we have it in our kitchen. Mari Andrew 2020 Wall Calendar: Am I There Yet?

title: Zany antics by a town of eccentric characters
text: The nuttiest, most off-beat novel I have ever read.  Read the first 3 chapters and you will know if this is the book for you. It does settle down in the last few chapters and deals with some real life hard hitting family drama. There is a huge happily ever after for every one except one guy who got every thing he deserved. so it was a HEA for the reader. Addy Tornado and Mazie Midnight, right there gives you an idea of the story path. Addy is a 29 year old who is a loveable and VERY quirky woman with a resume of jobs 9 pages long, currently driving a bus and occasionally in a fugue state where she doesn't remember how she got from one stop to the other. Mazie is a 41 year old new to the sleepy college town of Wilshire Hills, she is pursuing an advanced degree in the performing arts, the only thing holding her back is her fear of performing, hmmm. The novel has extensive cast of unconventional and very endearing characters that would give Tales of the City a challenge. This will make an exceptional book club choice.

title: For fans of the movie Casablanca
text: I became an instant fan of the author after reading last year's hit novel 'Firefly'. This is a followup to that novel and even has a cameo of Firefly himself. Terrific writing and a super suspenseful thriller ending that wraps up all the plot elements.

title: a Hurlyburly tale of Romance
text: This is a chew up the scenery journey for two women, 2 toddlers and two BFFs. Julia is San Francisco Bay area twenty-something, a semi-successful career woman who has never been lucky in love and finds herself frozen when sexual intimacy develops in her past relationships. Reed is a thirty-something radiologist with a 9-5 job in the Sacramento area raising two 4 year olds and no time or flexibility for long term relationships, nice and easy is what suits her current social situation. Mo and Kate are Julia's college roommates, Kate is engaged to be married and the 3 gals are headed to a long anticipated 2 week Hawaiian vacation, they have stayed super close since college but this will be their last hurrah before marriage. What happens when Julia and Reed develop a chemistry that ignite Julia to want more than Reed can give? Well, they chew up the scenery for 300 hundred pages and leave you gasping at all the surprises including up to the last page.

title: By Grabthar's Hammer! I enjoyed this novel
text: This book is so bookclub worthy!! Told with Kallmaker's fabulous spot on humor this is a delightful piece of froth set in Los Angeles about blended families, young love and not so young love. First of all Kesa has my heart, she is so wonderful that no one in my mind could possibly be good enough for her. Not giving any spoiler's away. From age 19 she raises her 7 year old sister, her parents died and left them with nothing but debt (that's a story worth exploring right there). Kesa is first generation Filipino and a clothing designer at age 31 getting her first A-list clients, her business is about to take off when her UCLA college freshman sister lays a bombshell at her feet.  I loved the side story with Auntie Ivy, Cami and Marisol, it made me love this story and Kesa even more.  Bonus to Kallmaker's readers Jennifer Lamont has a couple cameos!!!!  39 year old Shannon works for the US Marshall's service as an analyst, she not only is good at her job, she likes it as well. She is pretty set in her ways sharing her life with 21 year old UCLA junior year engineer (that's an interesting story there). I love their relationship, Paz is a great young adult and Shannon is super with him. Paz then lays a bombshell in Shannon's lap. You think you have one surprise coming your way, then you get another, then you get another. Wow this book could have been called Rollercoaster if that wasn't already a title by the author.

title: Practice Makes Perfect (Legal Affairs) by Carsen Taite,  June 11, 2019
text: Fascinating and riveting look at the corporate private attorney scene. This should be enjoyable for anyone who has enjoyed watching episodes of Boston Legal, The Practice, Ally McBeal, or (I am dating myself) LA Law. Three lawyers are on track to be partners in top ten law firms in the Texas state capitol city of Austin when they decide to pitch it all and go out on their own. A prestigious client gives them a shot at winning their business and huge drama ensues. Luckily for us all there is a happily ever after. The main characters are great and the secondary characters are vivid. I would love to be at an Author book club to discuss all the interesting tidbits in the story.

title: In Harm's Way: The Annie Velasquez Mystery by Ej Kindred, Paperback – April 10, 2019
text: Debut novel set in small town outside of Portland Oregon. By the end of the first chapter you will know if this is the book for you. If Annie didn't have bad luck she would have no luck it all. The story opens with Annie who has fled disaster and is working as housekeeper to a successful Doctor working on his upscale 4th wife. She gets along great with their live in chef, the Wentworths entertain extensively so it makes sense to have a live in chef. The story opens the day before Thanksgiving and Annie has the next 4 days off, in fact the doctor to tells her to "get your butt out of here" so she skedaddles. She love biking to work through the old growth forest. Vivid characters makes for a good read.

title: Hate: The Rising Tide of Anti-Semitism in France by Marc Weitzmann, Hardcover – March 12, 2019
text:
Since I was a child in the 1970's and learning about the Holocaust, that took place only 30 years earlier, I have wondered how any Jew could live in Germany post war when only a handful of Germans were accountable for the annihilation of 6 million Jews. I mean, they all looked the other way! So really I have been wondering if this day would ever come and here it is. France is home to Europe's largest Jewish community. In 2012 the murders at an Orthodox school in Toulouse, in 2015 the attack on a kosher market in a Paris suburb, a 2017 murder of a 65 year old woman, and in 2018 the murder of a Holocaust survivor are something that needs to be addressed as a whole. With the history of Europe's violence against the Jews the book points out that the powers that be and the people of France are not acting strongly enough to wipe out this rising tide of antisemitism.

It's not a perfect book, the author doesn't come off in this translation from it's original French as the most objective of writers. However he does give the US reader enough hard information to know how serious the situation is overseas.

title: Death of an Art Collector: A Nero Wolfe Mystery by Robert Goldsborough, Paperback 2019
text:
I can't say I enjoyed this as I have the other titles in this re-boot of the series. It lacked suspense and tension and the characters never came to life. I liked the premise of the art world and the daughter and the ex-wife and the cameo by Frank Lloyd Wright but it just felt tired. And the ending was lackluster.

title: Roller Coaster by Karin Kallmaker, Paperback – January 17, 2012
text: A terrific opening scene, perfectly written and very memorable, not over played, with humor and drama and vivid characters. I was looking forward to getting swept off my feet in a lovely romance with humor, some drama and Technicolor settings. This novel delivered. But for the opening scene that is set 23 years earlier the novel is set in the present and split between northern California and NYC with a one week vacation cruise to the Caribbean that left me feeling like I was aboard. Laura is so memorable I will miss her. I really don't want to give any of the story away because having the author tell it is such a pleasure. I loved all the Broadway and NYC slices of life because I know it so well. I loved all the Northern California slices of life because I know them so little but enough to have them ring true. Cass is another character I would love to see again, she is a gem. I really got sucked into the story and was super happy it took over 300 pages to end. I could go on and on, this is book club worthy.

title: Their Little Secret by Mark Billingham, Hardcover – June 4, 2019
text:
DI Tom Thorn is a middle aged detective inspector in London, England. My favorite genre is the police procedural, and this author is at the top of my always to be read list. That being said this read less as a procedural and more as a psychological thriller. Excellent writing, suspense and a couple good surprises thrown in, but the character development wasn't as vivid as his previous titles. Thorne's partner is Nicole Tanner a lesbian who is not fully developed for the reader. His best friend is Pathologist Phil Hendricks a very appealing gay man, they have a strong bond. Thorne is in the midst of what possibly a breakup with his younger girlfriend I think he will miss her young son as much as he will miss her. The plot is a disturbing portrait of scio or psychopaths, the woman is the more unhinged of the two.

I included a summary of the first book below to give new readers a bit of background:

Sleepyhead: July 9, 2002 Book 1 of 16 in the Tom Thorne Series:

Alison Willetts is unlucky to be alive. She has survived a stroke, deliberately induced by a skilful manipulation of pressure points on the head and neck. She can see, hear and feel and is aware of everything going on around her, but is completely unable to move or communicate. Her condition is called Locked-In Syndrome. In leaving Alison Willetts alive, the police believe the killer made his first mistake. Then D.I. Tom Thorne discovers the horrifying truth; it isn't Alison who is the mistake, it's the three women already dead. "An appropriate margin of error" is how their killer dismisses them, and Thorne knows they are unlikely to be the last. For the killer is smart, and he's getting his kicks out of toying with Thorne as much as he is pursuing his sick fantasy. Thorne knows immediately he's not going to catch the killer with simple procedure. But with little more than gut instinct and circumstantial evidence to damn his chief suspect, anesthetist Jeremy Bishop, his pursuit of him is soon bordering on the unprofessional. Especially considering his involvement with Anne Coburn, Alison's doctor and Jeremy's close friend.

title: Chumps to Champs by Bill Pennington, Hardcover – May 7, 2019
text: Fascinating story, really well written compulsive page turning enjoyment. Not just for Yankee fans but for anyone who has a historical interest in baseball.  I remember the days of Steinbrenner destroying the Yankees with his megalomania decisions and then Buck Showalter resurrecting the team only to be shown the door. This thorough book takes a perspective of the 1980's and then drills down in the hears 1990 to 1996 and finishes up over the next 5 years.

title: Blood Kin by Barbara Anne Pauley, 271 pages Mass Market Paperback – 1973
text: SINISTER SANCTUARY, The year was 1864, and lovely young Leslie Hallam came to the isolated plantation of Sycamore Knob to escape the horrors of the Civil War. However, Leslie soon discovered that a far grimmer kind of struggle was taking place within the magnificent old mansion. Leslie's once-beautiful cousin had turned into a creature of venomous jealousy. The handsome, dashing master of the house flaunted his mistress before his wife and child, and even Leslie was not immune to the spell he cast. Then gruesome death began to stalk the lush plantation, and now there was nowhere left for Leslie to flee as the walls of terror closed in...

title: Perennials by Mandy Berman, A Novel Hardcover – June 6, 2017
text: For Judy Blume fans. The first 4 chapters are devoted to meeting 13 year olds Fiona and Rachel at summer camp where they first met as 9 year olds.. Then it skips 6 years, they are returning to the camp as counselors the summer before freshman year in college. If you want to read a book about the summer camp dynamics you will enjoy this, I was looking for a novel centering on Fiona and Rachel and this book tells it but not as fully as I wanted.

title: And After Many Days by Jowhor Ile, A Novel Hardcover February 16, 2016
text:
Devastating loss in Nigeria 1995, with repercussions for decades. I can't think of anything worse then what happens to this family, except some do survive and thrive by the last chapter. Very evocative and compelling. A must read. By the last chapter Nigeria is where “Disputes are no longer settled with raised voices in a meeting.People no longer write strongly worded petitions to voice their dissent. If you disagree with someone these days, you simply go over to the person’s house with your face unmasked and shoot him."

Recent Nigerian history began with British colonial rule beginning in 1900 practicing indirect rule through traditional chiefdoms. Nigeria became in 1960. Suffered civil war from 1967 to 1970 and alternated between elected rulers and military dictators until 1999. Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa with 186 million and the seventh most populous country in the world (more than 90 million of its population under age 18!). There are over 250 differnt languages!

title: City Trails - Barcelona October 16, 2018 edition by Lonely Planet Kid
text:
for children ages 8-12. Having never been to Barcelona I can not vouch for the content, having a child who is eager to travel there this fit the bill. Themed trails include:
Legends From Long Ago
Animal Land
Delicioso!
Gaudi Town
Street Shows
Watery Way
Let’s Go!
Winning City
