title: Hyacinth and the Secrets Beneath by Jacob Sager Weinstein
text:
First book in an anticipated 3 volume fantasy series. 12-year-old Hyacinth, an American, moves from Illinois to London where her mother is kidnapped and Hyacinth learns that her new home is alive with magic. Hyacinth's adventures rival the famous Alice in Wonderland. Hyacinth doesn't descend to Wonderland but she and Lady Roslyn descend into the London sewers. Our 11 year old loved the humor and the suspense.

Question - what is with the Saltpetre Men?

title: Book 2 of 2 in the Sekret Series: Skandal: My mind is mine alone by Lindsay Smith
text:
Psychic Cold War espionage thriller written for teens ages 16 and up. It's now 1964, and 18 year old Yulia and Valentin have defected to the west settling in the USA intending to prevent a war between the US and the USSR instigated by the KGB psychic team that trained her and turns out her mother is part of. Once you read this thriller you will want to read Sekret but do yourself a favor and read Sekret first to avoid spoilers.

Set in the depths of the Cold war, 1963, between the USSR and the USA, Book #1 [[ASIN:1596438924 Sekret (Sekret Series)]] "An empty mind is a safe mind". 17 year old Yulia Andreevna Chernina has the ability to hold an object and 'see' it's history. Her father always taught her to hide her thoughts and control her emotions to survive the harsh realities of Soviet Russia. But when she's captured by the KGB and forced to work as a psychic spy with a mission to undermine the U.S. space program (the KGB hold her mother and brother as hostages), she's thrust into a world of suspicion, deceit, and horrifying power. Yulia quickly realizes she can trust no one--not her KGB superiors or the other operatives vying for her attention--and must rely on her own wits and skills to survive in this world where no SEKRET can stay hidden for long. Pub Date: April 15th, 2014

title: The Way to Bea: by Kat Yeh: debuts September 2017
text:
Taiwanese-American Beatrix Lee has the wind knocked out of her sails when she finds out at age 12 she is going to no longer be an only child and only apple of her parents eye. Plus her BFF, 'S, has started ghosting her. Bea thinks that now that they are in 7th grade 'S finds Bea is too much of a free spirit. So Bea is going to play it cool and keep a low profile. Bea is a poet and leaves her poems tucked into a wall that someone has begun replying to. Bea is on a hunt to figure out who in her sphere could it be?

Bea is a great kid, the kind you want living in your home or next door or who you want your kids playing with. I especially liked how normal her parents are and how they acted like a real family without the huge drama you sometimes get in a children's novel. I would love it if some parents would take this as a learning opportunity with their children to be on the lookout for the loners who may be shy and not fit in right away (adults could use the same help).

title: Birthrights (Revisions to the Truth series book 1) by J. Kyle McNeal
text:
648 page Fantasy Book#1 in the 4 book epic Revisions to the Truth series. The book summary does a terrific job of setting up the story.

16 year old Whym is about to find out what house he goes to at Hogwarts oops! I mean he is about to find out how he will spend the rest of his life, this happens at the Choosing Ceremony if you are from the lovely RatsNest neighborhood of Riverbend. His destiny lies with a career as a 'seeker' aka a bounty hunter, under the tutelage of Stern Sandoval and senior apprentice, Kutan, They hunt their first target in the Wildes of the Lost Land.

Quint is the son of the Voice of the Oracle is however he is currently living with the Dragonborn of Welloch tribe and being instructed in their ways by Nikla,

Frankly, I got exhausted in all the world building and I read Dune without an issue. And yet I know I will need to pick up book two to find out what happens next to Quint and Whym.

Age appropriate for anyone age 16 and up. 'Broken Oaths' the next book in the series is due June 2018.

title: This Raging Light by Estelle Laure
text:
Lucille turned 17 years old 3 months ago and since then her father had a nervous breakdown and strangled her mother almost to death, he was committed to a psych ward, then her mother takes a 2 week break leaving Lucille in charge of her 10 year old sister Wren and then fails to return. I only wish I lived next door so I could help these 2 kids out *sigh* I loved how Lucille and Wren interacted with each other, they both really cam alive for me. Lucille is very strong - she will need to be with the fallout she deals with in the coming months. Luckily she has known her best friend Eden since they were 7 years old, then there is Eden's twin brother Digby who has a girlfriend - until Digby and Lucille fall for each other.

I recommend for readers 16 and older. If you enjoyed this read don't miss [[ASIN:0544531264 But Then I Came Back]] where the author gives Eden's story.

title: Book 3 of 3 in the Generations Trilogy Series - Alone by Scott Sigler
text:
Sadly I didn't see this was book 3 of a series. I include below a summary of the two earlier titles for those in the same boat as me. This is an epic series that deserves to be read as 3 volumes, with a complex plot and so much backstory you will spend most of the reading filling in what you don't know. That being said, I can recommend the writing and the creativity of the plot and story lines. I can't recommend the series to anyone under age 17 due to it's noir theme

[[ASIN:055339312X Alive (The Generations Trilogy)]] For fans of The Hunger Games, Divergent, and Red Rising comes a gripping sci-fi adventure in which a group of teenagers wake up in a mysterious corridor with no knowledge of who they are or how they got trapped. Their only hope lies with an indomitable young woman who must lead them not only to answers but to survival. “I open my eyes to darkness. Total darkness. I hear my own breathing, but nothing else. I lift my head . . . it thumps against something solid and unmoving. There is a board right in front of my face. No, not a board . . . a lid.” A teenage girl awakens to find herself trapped in a coffin. She has no idea who she is, where she is, or how she got there. Fighting her way free brings little relief—she discovers only a room lined with caskets and a handful of equally mystified survivors. Beyond their room lies a corridor filled with bones and dust, but no people . . . and no answers. She knows only one thing about herself—her name, M. Savage, which was engraved on the foot of her coffin—yet she finds herself in charge. She is not the biggest among them, or the boldest, but for some reason the others trust her. Now, if they’re to have any chance, she must get them to trust one another. Whatever the truth is, she is determined to find it and confront it. If she has to lead, she will make sure they survive. Maybe there’s a way out, a rational explanation, and a fighting chance against the dangers to come. Or maybe a reality they cannot comprehend lies just beyond the next turn. Markings on their foreheads and names on their coffins are clues to who they are. Their only option is to continue to run and survive.

An alternate title for book 1 could have been CARNAGE.

[[ASIN:0553393170 Alight: Book Two of the Generations Trilogy]] M. Savage—or Em, as she is called—has made a bewildering and ominous discovery. She and the other young people she was chosen to lead awoke in strange coffins with no memory of their names or their pasts. They faced an empty, unknown place of twisting tunnels and human bones. With only one another to depend on, they searched for answers and found the truth about their terrifying fate. Confronted by a monstrous enemy, they vowed never to surrender—and, by any means, to survive. The planet Omeyocan may be the sanctuary Em and her comrades seek. But the planet for which they were created turns out not to be a pristine, virgin world. Vestiges of a lost civilization testify to a horrifying past that may yet repeat itself. And when a new enemy creeps from the jungle shadows, Em and her young refugees learn there’s nowhere left to run. They face a simple choice: fight or die. In the midst of this desperate struggle, their unity is compromised from within—and a dangerous zealot devoted to a bloodthirsty god moves to usurp Em’s command, threatening to lead them all down a path to violent doom.

title: Girls Like Me by  Lola StVil
text:
15 year old Shay Summers has a world of hurt, her father is dead, she is bullied at school, her stepmother can only focus on Shay being over weight, her BFF is dying of cancer and her other close friend is being sent to a gay conversion boarding school by his father. Anyone of those would knock my teenage self down. Her escape is an on-line boyfriend. Of course warning bells went off for me, the potential for Blake to be an adult posing as as teen is huge with danger.

The cover looks like it would be a middle school read but I think the ideal age is 13 to 16. I especially that that the author leaves open Shays race.

Written in Verse it's a nice change.

title: Paris for Two by Phoebe Stone
text:
That has got to be the most amateur book cover, it almost kept me from ordering the book. Luckily the 12 year old heroine is named Petunia Beanly (of course she is from Boston) and I could not pass up a book with a named character Petunia. Then Petunia finds a secret drawer (in the rental owned by Colette) in the place they are living in Paris (for her dad's work) - now what person doesn't love finding something hidden? I was hooked.

The only jarring thing are the family relationships, sister Ava, her mother (divorced from Ava's father) and Petunia's Flaubert loving father. they just didn't fit with the rest of the book.

title: Speed of Life by J.M. Kelly
text:
Portland Oregon teens Crystal and Amber are twins, one gets pregnant junior year of high school. They decide to raise baby Natalie together, entailing high school during the day and after school jobs. They are barely getting by but have dreams of one managing a relatives tavern and the other getting a good paying job as a car mechanic. The anguish kicks in when Crystal gets accepted to the college of her dreams - in Kansas.

The the ending was close to perfect.

title: Run by Kody Keplinger
text:
Small-town Kentucky high school seniors steal a car and hopefully won't end up like Thelma or Louise. Agnes and Bo tell the story in alternating chapters. Bo's tells us things as they are happening while Agnes flashes back to when they became friends.

Bo and her family live on the wrong side of the tracks, with family members in the local news for one run in with public misdemeanors like drinking and petty theft, she has a rep as the school tramp which is super harsh when you are a virgin - top it off her mother is a meth addict. Agnes is legally blind --- just like the author, her parents want to keep her in a cocoon, she is living la vida loca like she is 26.

title: The Fallen Star: The Nocturnals Book 3, by Tracey Hecht
text:
This is book 3 for our family and could not be more happy to dip in to the further adventures of Team Nocturnal. Now we read them 3 nights in a row and start again lol.

There is a way cool tie-in website "nocturnalsworld" with videos and games.

Book 1 [[ASIN:1944020020 The Nocturnals: The Mysterious Abductions]]A Coyote, a Honey Badger, a Kiwi, a Mink, a Possum,a Tarantula and a Wombat are MIA - what is the animal kingdom to do? To the rescue are a Pangolin named Tobin , a Fox named Dawn and a Sugar Glider named Bismark, they recruit a Wolf & a Bat to track the missing down. Jerry the Jerboa (a hopping desert rodent, aka rat, found throughout Northern Africa and Asia) enters the hunt and and the drama escalates. By the time Boris the Crocodile makes the scene their goose may be cooked!

Book 2 [[ASIN:B01IMJV9G4 The Ominous Eye: The Nocturnals Book 2]] Dawn, Bismark and Tobin (a Fox, a Sugar Glider & a Pangolin) from Book1 investigate what caused the planet to fracture (a giant beast!). The Owls and the Kiwi (I thought it was a fruit?) were the new family favorites that the 3 creatures of the night meet up with to stop further destruction. LOL Bismark is our family favorite.

title: The Whole Thing Together by Ann Brashares
text: #1 New Release in Teen & Young Adult Marriage & Divorce Fiction - compulsively readable. I must have read a different book because all the characters kinda creeped me out. And there was way to much drama. 17 year olds Sasha and Ray have a pretty normal back story, his mother Lila and her dad Robert were once married. They have 3 older sisters from that marriage. But they have never met each other because the marriage was a train wreak.Really if I tell you any more it will take away from your reading.

title: The Heartbeats of Wing Jones by Katherine Webber
text:
Set in Atlanta and prior to the 1996 Olympics in Atlanta, Wing Jones, whose maternal grandmother is from China and her paternal grandmother is from Ghana is plunged into a whole lot of hurt. Her father has died and school is not a welcoming place for Wing which is odd because her older brother, Marcus, is so popular you think he would have paved the way. Then Marcus while underage and drinking is involved in a car crash that kills 2 people and leaves him in a coma. Wing finds an outlet from all the pain on the track team where she comes into her own.

This story and Wing felt very real to me and to our 15 year old.

title: My Robot Ate My Homework: Project Droid #3 by Nancy Krulik, Amanda Burwasser & Mike Moran (Illustrator)
text:
I loved the graphics and so did our 5, 7 & 9 year olds! Authors Nancy Krulik and her daughter, Amanda Burwasser,create 3rd grader Logan Applebaum and his companion Java.

book #1 [[ASIN:1510710280 Science No Fair!: Project Droid #1]] It’s a pretty normal day for Logan Applebaum—until his inventor mother announces that she’s built him a new robot cousin. And Java may be really smart, but he’s also going to be a major handful. No one can know about his secret. This is going to be a long school year. With the third grade science fair coming up, though, Logan thinks maybe a super computer cousin could come in handy and he’ll finally have a shot at beating the nosey Silverspoon twins,Sherry and Jerry, who win at everything. But when Sherry and Jerry steal Java as their partner, and then start suspecting something is up with the new kid, can Logan think fast before this crazy experiment becomes an epic disaster?

Book #2 [[ASIN:1510710299 Soccer Shocker!: Project Droid #2]] Logan's mom tells him that Java is joining his soccer team, the Purple Wombats, he’s not thrilled. It’s a lot of work teaching his new robot cousin how to act like a human—and keeping him out of trouble—and Logan needs a break. Still, being programmed for success means that Java’s also great at scoring. He might just turn the Wombats into a championship team, beating Sherry and Jerry Silverspoon and their Red Polar Bears . . . if he’d just let the other kids play, too. After being replaced as the Wombats’ MVP, Logan’s had enough. But when Java gets wet and goes on the fritz, can the whole team—even a short-circuiting Java—come together to score the winning goal?

Book #4 "Phone-y Friends" due out – September 5, 2017

title: The Inexplicable Logic of My Life  by Benjamin Alire Saenz
text: New to me author, hardcover: ages 16 and up.  17 year old Salvador has grown up in El Paso Texas, right across the river from El Paso Mexico. His birth parents were Caucasian. He was adopted at age 3 by a wonderful man, a "Father Knows Best" type who is also gay and Mexican-American. His BFF is a girl, Sam, whose mother has no mothering interests.Sal is dealing with more than I could handle, he is involved in two fist fights in response to insults hurled at him, his beloved grandmother has died and he has a letter from his birth mother that he is holding on to unread.  I read an excellent review online at  NPR "inexplicable-logic-maps-a-teen-boys-complicated-mind" that you might also enjoy.

title: Grizzly Peak (Aaron's Wilderness #3) by Jonathan London
text:
13 year old eighth-grader Aaron, has been on 2 earlier boding trips with his dad and his desert storm buddies and their kids. Sadly it has not accomplished it's purpose. Aaron has been expelled from school for carrying a pocket knife. His mature dad can barely stand the sight of him and wants to send him a an outward bound camp in Montana for hard core juvenile delinquents. Aaron suggests option B, a two week father/son kayak adventure through British Columbia’s Cariboo Mountains. Luckily? his father almost dies on the trip and Aaron comes to the rescue. Luckily for the whole family dad grows up too.

The pencil illustrations by the author's own son are keepers.

title: Liar Liar (A Helen Grace Thriller) ... M.j. Arlidge
text:
5 star writing totally addictive story telling that I consumed in one day. Book 4 of 7 in Detective Inspector Helen Grace thriller series of sadistic, violent and determined serial killers in the English coastal city of Southampton. DI Grace is a loner, with a childhood resulting mood swings and episodes of deep depression. Neither a alcohol or drug user she lets off steam by being the submissive in a Bondage Domination Sadism Masochism provided by Jake. Where do these authors come up with this stuff?
Book #1 [[ASIN:B00GK8RV3A Eeny Meeny: DI Helen Grace 1 (A DI Helen Grace Thriller)]]
Book #2 [[ASIN:B00JQTJ8J0 Pop Goes the Weasel: DI Helen Grace 2 (A DI Helen Grace Thriller)]]
Book #3 [[ASIN:B00NCLPGJY The Doll's House: DI Helen Grace 3 (A DI Helen Grace Thriller)]]
Book #5 [[ASIN:B014K6FD6U Little Boy Blue: DI Helen Grace 5 (A DI Helen Grace Thriller)]]
Book #6 [[ASIN:B01D1Q47DA Hide and Seek: DI Helen Grace 6 (Detective Inspector Helen Grace)]]
Book #7 Love Me Not (to be published 2017-05)

title: Mercer Girls by Libbie Hawker
text:
Pioneers from Illinois first settled in Seattle on November 13, 1851 (the first settlers had been there since 8,000 BC). Fortunes were made in the logging and lumber businesses. Between 1865 and 1869 the population grew from 350 to 1,000 people. The novel is an earnest attempt to tell the story of New England mill towns toward the end of the Civil War without raw materials to mill, travel from the Eastern US to the Pacific Northwest before the continental railroad, the founding of Seattle, and a time when women had very few civil rights and fewer options.
Our heroines:
35 year old Josephine Carey has an agenda she keeps to herself through a good third of the story.
16 year old Dovey Mason is looking for adventure and freedom to make her own choices.
Sophronia 'Sophie' Brandt, the daughter of a preacher is determined to live a life of piety and find her perfect man in the new land she views as morally bankrupt.

In the first half of the novel as a group they travel from Boston to New York City to Panama, cross the panama and set sail to San Francisco and on the Seattle. Along the way their histories unfold. The second half is their story of survival, with a 7 year jump toward the end.

I enjoyed it.

FYI - The founding of Seattle is usually dated from the arrival of the Denny Party on November 13, 1851. in 1864 Mercer made a first trip from the logging and fishing area of Seattle's Puget Sound to Boston & the textile town of Lowell. He was able to bring 10 young women age 18 to 35 back with him via the Isthmus of Panama, and when they arrived in Seattle the community staged a welcoming reception. His 2nd trip the following year was grander in scope, hardship and failure. Mercer collected $300 each from 500 men willing to take part in a wife lottery. Because of the scope of the project and resulting negative tabloid fake news publicity Mercer was not able to sail until January of 1866 (this time around Cape Horn), and with only 100 women.

title: Third Grade Mermaid by Peter Raymundo
text: for tiny tots age 6 to 8 years old. Cora the 3rd grade mermaid - I just love saying the rhyming book title out loud - lol.  Cora's curriculum consist of the 4 ''S's: swimming, splashing, singing, & spelling. Guess which one has her stumped? The illustrations are brilliant - this is a total keeper!

title: Optimists Die First Susin Nielsen
text: Young Adult.  I a so glad I ordered this novel. 16 year-old Petula blames herself for her baby sister, Maxine’s, death two years ago. Her parents are in no better shape. Her dad is in over his head financially and also struggles with depression.Her mother's coping mechanism is to become the neighborhood cat lady with 6 kittys and growing.  Petula meets Jacob, is a group therapy class. He was in a car crash that killed his two BFFs abd and resulted in his arm being amputated - however he seems to be holding up and dealing well with what happened. Luckily what could have mean a tedious melodrama for the readers, however the characters have a perfect black humor that made me laugh, giggle and smirk.

title: which of course is horrible and embarrassing if it is you
text: Young Adult. Debut novel. A Cautionary tale for any teenager. Alexandria Preparatory school. 18 year old Anna is dumped by her jock basketball superstar boyfriend, Palmer, just when everyone is talking about the senior prom (serious bummer!).  She herself dropped her BFFs when she started dating Palmer - so she is ALONE. then one by one students' private social media musings are exposed, which of course is horrible and embarrassing if it is you, or hilarious if you are a teenager and it happens to someone else. Apparently Alexandria Prep has as much drama as Peyton Place.

title: Old Bones Trudy by Nan Boyce
text:
Book 2 of 2 in the Detective Sarah Alt Series. Terrific Police Procedural. A ripped from the headlines story, A southern City, Atlanta, a percieved oppressive police force, murders of black college students and a resulting riot. The characters are vivid in my mind days after finishing the novel. I enjoyed it so much I am asking my Library to order the first book in the series.Bonus - it isn't a romance disguised as a mystery. 'Salt' is fully fleshed character, she has a lover who wants to get married, her father was a suicide, and the use of deadly force has had a negative effect on her soul.

Book #1 [[ASIN:0399167269 Out of the Blues]] On her first day as a newly minted homicide detective, Sarah Alt “Salt” is given the cold-case murder of a blues musician whose death was originally ruled an accidental drug overdose. Now new evidence has come to light that he may have been given a hot dose intentionally. And this evidence comes from a convicted felon hoping to trade his knowledge for shortened prison time . . . a man who Salt herself put behind bars. In a search that will take her into the depths of Atlanta’s buried wounds—among the city’s homeless, its politically powerful churches, commerce and industry, and the police department itself—Salt probes her way toward the truth in a case that has more at stake than she ever could have imagined. At once a vivid procedural and a penetrating examination of what it means to be cop, Out of the Blues is a remarkable crime debut.

The author has 30+ years experience in the Atlanta Police Department.

title: We Are Okay by Nina LaCour
text: Literary fiction for ages 15 to 19. College freshman Marin is facing the Christmas holiday alone on her college campus in New York City, Right there that doesn't sound so bad. NYC at Christmas is AWESOME with so much to do and see and my college Freshman year I met new friends - it was very exciting. However Marin is from San Francisco which can be gorgeous or it can be foggy damp chilly and she is doing her best to keep herself together knowing that she is alone in the world. Her mother died years ago, her grandfather who she lived with and adored is gone and she has no one in her life from the last 18 years who knows her. Until her BFF from home Mabel arrives to discuss why Marin left without saying goodbye in any real way. Our young teen got frustrated at the pace of revelations and it got to a point where it marred his enjoyment. This is loaded with angst so should appeal to teens.

title: Unmade  by Amy Rose Capetta
text:
Young Adult. Book 2 of 2 in the Entangled Series.In book one (below summary) Cade comes of age and learns of her past that sends her on an epic journey. In this title Cadence 'Cade' and her family of choice set out to find her mother, and along the way locate and unite the survivors of the human race. Our teen wolfed the story down like a bags of french fries.

Book# 1 [[ASIN:0544336240 Entangled]] Seventeen-year-old Cade is a fierce survivor, solo in the universe with her cherry-red guitar. Or so she thought. Her world shakes apart when a hologram named Mr. Niven tells her she was created in a lab in the year 3112, then entangled at a subatomic level with a boy named Xan. Cade’s quest to locate Xan joins her with an array of outlaws—her first friends—on a galaxy-spanning adventure. And once Cade discovers the wild joy of real connection, there’s no turning back.

title: When We Rise: My Life in the Movement by Cleve Jones
text:
A great addition to a modern history college or graduate syllabus.A memoir of one man's life in San Francisco during the upheaval of the post Vietnam era, gay liberation and the onset of the Aids crisis in the early 80's. A fascinating, sexually frank, and absorbing read for anyone. The author was a co-founder of the San Francisco AIDS Foundation and conceived the AIDS Memorial Quilt that would one day go on display across the Mall at the us Capitol. That sounds kinda dry and this book is far from it - as terrific as any memoir I have read at times emotional and lol funny. The AIDS Memorial Quilt has grown t0 memorialize the lives of over 85,000 Americans killed by the AIDS virus.

You also might enjoy watching a discussion with the author here "Cleve Jones & Aaron Hicklin | When We Rise - YouTube"

title: Kids of Appetite by David Arnold
text:
Young Adult. Hackensack New Jersey the land of my people. 16 year old Bruno Victor “Vic” Bernucci III has an urn with his father's ashes and a last wish to fulfill. He also suffers a neurological disorder that paralyzes his facial muscles, his dad died 2 years ago and his mom is marrying a guy with sons who are sadists. The book opens with poor Vic being questioned by police about a murder. Flash back 8 days to how he landed in such a mess. Vic meets Madeline, a member of a gang they named Kids of Appetite, KoA who is stuck in an abusive home life, and refugees from the African country Congo, Baz and Nzuzi and foster care victims and 11-year-old Coco has a mouth like a sailor.

ideal for ages 15-16 and is a solid empathy builder.

title: The Memory Book By Lara Avery
text:
Young Adult. 18 year old high school Vermont senior, Sammie, is every parents dream. She is the class valedictorian and on the debate team, with plans to attend New York University get an economics degree and then go to Harvard law school. Everything horrifically crashes - every hope every dream. She develops a disease that leads to dementia and death. I felt so bad for this fictitious yet vividly come to life person I was sick.

Ideal for ages 14 to 18.

title: Lucky (A Detective Jack Yu Investigation) by Henry Chang
text:
Book 5 of 5 in the A Detective Jack Yu Investigation Series. I didn't see that it was the 5th in a series but that wasn't an issue. Terrific action - I kept reading to the end to see if Jack could save Lucky from using up the last of his good fortune. The last 10 chapters I read like I was on steroids. A perfect vacation read. Terrific ending.

I found reading the plot summaries helpful so include them here:
Book #1 [[ASIN:1616957174 Chinatown Beat (A Detective Jack Yu Investigation)]] Detective Jack Yu is assigned to the Chinatown precinct as the only officer of Chinese descent. He investigates a series of attacks on children and a missing mistress, shifting between the world of street thugs and gangs and the Chinatown of the rich and powerful. When Detective Jack Yu is transferred to New York’s Chinatown, he isn’t ready to face the changes in his old neighborhood. His childhood friends are now hardened gangsters, his father is dying, and he is constantly reminded of this teenage blood brother, murdered in front of him years before. Then community leader and tong boss Uncle Four is gunned down and his mistress goes missing. But unlike the rest of the culturally clueless police department, Jack knows his district’s gritty secrets. He will have to draw on his knowledge in order to catch this killer in a crime-ridden precinct where brotherhoods are just as likely to distribute charity as mete out vigilante justice.

Book #2 [[ASIN:1569476047 Year of the Dog (A Detective Jack Yu Investigation)]] A rollercoaster ride with NYPD Detective Jack Yu, illuminating the underground world of Chinatown gambling, smuggling, and protection. Jack Yu is one of the few ethnically Chinese officers in the NYPD. Now Jack has been promoted out of the Chinatown Precinct. With multiple murders occurring within days of his transfer, the Ninth Precinct isn’t less violent, per se, but at least Jack doesn’t know most of the perps. When a bloody shootout goes down in Chinatown though, the upper echelons of the NYPD reach out to him for help squelching the escalating gang violence, and Jack learns he cannot get away from Chinatown’s criminals—his old friends—for long.

Book #3 [[ASIN:1569479976 Red Jade (A Detective Jack Yu Investigation)]] While investigating two bodies found in Chinatown's historic Tong battleground, NYPD Detective Jack Yu's pursuit takes him from New York's Chinatown to Seattle's Chinatown, tracking a cold-blooded Chinese-American gangster and a mysterious Hong Kong femme fatale. The bodies of a young man and woman are discovered at an address on the Bloody Angle, Chinatown’s historic Tong battleground. NYPD Detective Jack Yu had thought he was done working in Chinatown, but old allegiances pull him back in. Is it a simple murder-suicide? The grieving families want him to keep a lid on any stories that might further tarnish their family names—but the Golden Galaxy club, where the young woman worked, is made for scandal. Drugs, snakeheads, smuggled prostitutes: “Girls don’t last long before getting dirty.” As a puzzling web of links between the murders and the criminal underworld reveals itself, Yu’s investigation takes him across the country to another Chinatown, this one in Seattle. In the new city, stymied by the uncooperative local cops, he tracks a cold-blooded Chinese American gangster and a mysterious Hong Kong femme fatale.

Book #4 [[ASIN:1616955325 Death Money (A Detective Jack Yu Investigation)]] When a floater that surfaces in the Harlem River turns out to be Chinese, Yu leaves his downtown precinct to investigate. Yu knocks on the usual doors, and the trail leads to the Gee family, noodle manufacturers who on the surface look like the ideal immigrant success story. When the body of an unidentified Asian man is found in the Harlem River, NYPD Detective Jack Yu is pulled in to investigate. The murder takes Jack from the benevolent associations of Chinatown to the take-out restaurants, strip clubs, and underground gambling establishments of the Bronx, to a wealthy, exclusive New Jersey borough. It's a world of secrets and unclear allegiances, of Chinatown street gangs and major Triad players. With the help of an elderly fortune teller and an old friend, the unpredictable Billy Bow, Jack races to solve his most difficult case yet.

title: Death Coming Up the Hill by Chris Crowe
text: Coming of age novel set in America 1968 with Vietnam hovering like a nightmare. The story is told in haiku, 16,592 syllables, one for each American killed in Vietnam in 1968.  17-year-old Ashe has a racist Dad and a mom in a loveless marriage after they got pregnant in 1951 I was intrigued and really liked introducing our teen to a different way of expression..

title: Something in Between by Melissa de la Cruz
text:
Young Adult. A sympathetic look at illegal immigration. I gotta say knowing her family is from the Philippines, a country with such a rich history with America and World War Two gave me a lot of sympathy for the family. I was mostly shattered for the daughter. The romance with the Congressman's son made this more a fairy tale then a fraught piece of literature. Our teen loved it. My first feeling was that rules are rules and that this is what happens when you don't follow the rules. Well written, not terribly complex and semi-autobiographical.

For ages 14 to 16.

title: The Last True Love Story by Brendan Kiely
text:
Young Adult and a bitter-sweet coming of age odessey. Living in Los Angeles 17 year olds Teddy Hendrix and Corrina feel adrift in many aspects of their lives. Corrina was born in Guatamala and adopted. Hendrix is crushing on Corrina, his Grandfather, Gpa, is a widowed Vietnam Vet in the Alzheimer's unit of a retirement home. One day they go to visit Gpa and instead of heading home after decide one last roadtrip across the US to Ithaca NY would be a blast - and it is but in different ways then they imagine. The white-privilege Teddy sees when traveling with Corrina is a bonus.

Spot on for ages 16 to 17. If you love the idea of Gpa's dog 'Old Humper' going along maybe the age group is ideal for ages 13 to 17.

title: Every Exquisite Thing by Matthew Quick
text: Young Adult. From the author of 'The Silver Linings Playbook'.  The prose is breathtakingly consuming. 17 year old Nanette O’Hare has her world turned upside down when she is given a cult classic novel of young rebellion ala 'On The Road' or 'Catcher in the Rye'.  She now questions and balks at the privilege her family has worked for generations to give her. She quits her soccer team, dumps her friends to spend time with the book's author, aptly named Booker.  Booker hooks her up with another of his fans, Alex, a troubled teen poet. When that relationship fractures Nanette's existence dives, her therapist, aptly named June, steps in to give Nanette the tools to find her way. Our teen started the book Friday and didn't do much of anything until the last page.

title: Highly Illogical Behavior by John Corey Whaley
text:
Young Adult Novel set in Southern California. 16 year old Solomon has a had panic disorders since he was a toddler. As a way to quell the panic triggers he is now agoraphobic and hasn't left home in 3 years - first of all, I can't even imagine dealing with this as a parent let alone being a teenager who has to deal with this. One of the things I could connect with is Solomon's love of Star Trek. 17 year old Lisa, and her boyfriend Clark (Kent?) come into his life as a social experiment concocted by Lisa to improve her chance getting into the college of her choice to get her degree in psychology. Adding in that Solomon is gay just muddles the story and really is not needed. Toxic Janis is a good example to readers to jettison those 'friends' who are a blight on your life.

Ideal for ages 13 and up

title: And I loved it. I guess you have to be in ...
text:
Book 2 of 2 in the Detective Cooper Devereaux Series. Grim really really really grim. And I loved it. I guess you have to be in the mood to read a book where there are no winners. As a police procedural goes this was excellent pacing, plot and finale. I recommend reading the first book in the series because it will add to your enjoyment of this title.

Book #1 [[ASIN:0345540751 False Positive: A Novel]]For fans of Craig Johnson and James Lee Burke—False Positive follows up the powerful punch of Andrew Grant’s novel RUN with a staggering second dose of thrills and suspense that is just as smart, atmospheric, and soul-searing. Alabama detective Cooper Devereaux makes no apologies for his luxe lifestyle or the way he does his job. Most cops haven’t lived the kind of life he has—starting out as an orphan, raised by a grizzled cop savior—and most don’t use his kind of high-risk tactics. But he may have met his match in fellow detective Jan Loflin, who’s fresh off a long undercover stint in Vice when they’re partnered on a case that will test them both beyond their direst nightmares. A seven-year-old boy has disappeared from his home in the Birmingham suburbs. But the more Devereaux digs into the missing child’s background, the more he discovers about his own, eventually shaking loose a series of harrowing truths—about bloodlines, mass murder, obsession, and what two damaged detectives have in common with the innocent victim they’re so desperate to save. This twisty page-turner—the debut of the Detective Cooper Devereaux series—hurtles at a mile a minute through an action-packed search for a missing child, culminating in an ending that no reader will see coming.

title: Flicker and Mist by Mary G. Thompson
text: Young Adult Fantasy. 16 year old Myra has inherited her mother’s ability to become invisible, called flickering. Not good when flickering is against the law and cause for imprisonment - for life. Myra comes from a mixed ethnic family, her father is a political leader who fell in love with a persecuted minority. His political clout has protected Myra and her mother until there is a racial cleansing. A perfectly dramatic story for any 14 to 16 year old.I liked that not everyone was clear cut good or evil.

title: Because of the Sun by Jenny Torres Sanchez
text: Perfect for ages 15 to 17. I am always easy prey for books set in Florida where I lived for 21 years, add in New Mexico which I have driven trough 3 times (favorite stop is Las Cruces) and I have a sure thing. The opening was gripping to me and our teen reader. 17 year old Dani's abusive parent, Ruby, is mauled to death by a bear outside their home. Because she is under age she must move to New Mexico to live with her mother's sister who she never met. (right there I wish she could have a better social worker who could talk to her about emancipation options). The joy in the story is the emotional journey Dani takes, with her aunt and getting to know her mother's story in becoming the person Dani knew. Meeting new people, making new friends. The book is just gorgeous. Keeper.

title: Flip the Bird by Kym Brunner
text:
Best for ages 13 - 14. Fourteen year old Mercer has a real stick in the mud grump of a dad with a totally cool occupation, he is master falconer at his family’s raptor rehabilitation center. Mercer meets Lucy, her family belong to HALT, fanatical animal-rights activists, that look down at interaction between humans and animals. Mercer has a tough time keeping his own love of falconry and his beloved hawk 'Flip' a secret while trying to hook Lucy as his girl friend. Things turn violent and get real ugly when HALT commits a violent crime by breaking into the rehab center, causing property distruction and releases the birds.

A really well told tale.

title: Shattered Blue by Lauren Bird Horowitz
text:
YA fantasy novel, Book 1 of 3 in the Light series.

Set in Monteray California finds have a tougher time being in love, for one thing he is Fae (a truly illegal immigrant) a mythical being or legendary creature in European folklore, a form of spirit, often described as metaphysical, supernatural, or preternatural. 15-year-old Noa Sullivan returns to Harlow Academy after the death of her 17-year-old sister, with devastated parents and a 3 year old sisiter to seek comfort with.

title: The Veil (Fianna Trilogy) by Megan Chance Book 3
text:
Book 3 of 3 in the Fianna Trilogy Series. At first glance book one looks like the plot from the movie Titanic where 1874 New York City replaces the cruise ship. Then it goes out the limb adding ancient Celtic warriors awakening to free Ireland from harsh British rule of 200 years that resulted in starvation to death of 250,000 Irish from 1739 to 1741. Good dialogue and strong characters make it a novel I needed to finish.

Book #1 [[ASIN:1477847189 The Shadows (Fianna Trilogy)]]- Grace Knox is about to turn seventeen, and the world of Victorian New York society should be opening to her—a time of dances and parties and boys vying for her heart and her hand. Instead, Grace’s world is closing in: the family business is gone; her brother is drinking and gambling away whatever is left; her widowed mother cannot cope; and her grandmother is slipping into madness. And now Grace is having disturbing dreams of ancient battles. Grace’s only hope is to marry Patrick Devlin and let his fortune save them all. But she isn’t sure she loves Patrick, and she doesn’t share his passion to free Ireland from British rule. Why look to Ireland when there is so much poverty and despair here? Then Grace meets Diarmid, an Irish stableboy. Being with him means losing everything. But the secrets and mystery surrounding him are too compelling to ignore. Soon Grace is drawn into his world of legend and heroes, magic and prophecy—the world of her dreams—where her own choice between faith and fear holds the greatest power of all.

Book #2 - [[ASIN:1477827080 The Web (Fianna Trilogy)]] - In Victorian New York, seventeen-year-old Grace Knox is tangled in the web of an ancient prophecy. The Fianna, legendary Irish warriors, have been magically called from their undying sleep to aid Ireland in its rebellion against Britain. But the Fianna have awakened in New York alongside their bitter enemies, the Fomori. A prophecy demands that a Druid priestess—a veleda—must choose between these two sides. Grace is this veleda. But being the veleda means she must sacrifice her power—and her life—to her choice. On one side are her fiancé, Patrick Devlin, and the Fomori. On the other are the Fianna—and the warrior Diarmid Ua Duibhne, with whom Grace shares an undeniable connection. Patrick has promised to find a way to save her life. In three months, at the ancient ritual, Diarmid must wield the knife that kills her. Grace doesn’t know whom to trust. As dark forces converge on the city, she struggles to discover the truth about her power. Can she change her own destiny? Can she escape the shadows of the past and reach for a future she could never have imagined?

title: Hero Complex: A Keaton School Novel by Margaux Froley
text:
Book 2 of 2 in the Keaton School Series. Very Nancy Drew I think this would appeal to 12 and 13 year olds. I enjoyed Devon's relationship with her grandfather and the reveal at the end was fun. It might be a little childish for the 15/16 year old reader.

Book #1 - [[ASIN:1616951273 Escape Theory (Keaton School)]]16 year old Devon Mackintosh has always felt like an outsider at Keaton, the prestigious California boarding school perched above the Pacific. As long as she’s not fitting in, Devon figures she might as well pad her application to Stanford’s psych program. So junior year, she decides to become a peer counselor, a de facto therapist for students in crisis. At first, it seems like it will be an easy fly-on-the-wall gig, but her expectations are turned upside down when Jason Hutchins (a.k.a. “Hutch”), one of the Keaton’s most popular students, commits suicide.

title: I super impressive list of American super achievers of the last ...
text:
I super impressive list of American super achievers of the last 40 years. Nothing in depth rather a collection of reflections and storytelling, kinda like a really good issue of Reader's Digest. I put a star next to the stories that I have read and enjoyed so far.
