In spite of the danger drawing ever closer, Faith still dreams of a loving family and a home to call her own, if only she and Luke can stay together long enough to find their beautiful and bright ... Montana Dawn.

Texas Twilight (2011) Texas Badlands, 1886 Fresh out of medical school, John McCutcheon finds his stagecoach under attack by brutal outlaws. With the help of a feisty acquaintance, Lily Anthony, he manages to fend off the assault. Lily is attracted to the charming cowboy-doctor, with his chiseled good looks and teasing ways, then heartbroken to learn he's engaged to be married. Once settled in Rio Wells, Texas, John tries to ignore the fact that his cousin has taken a shine to Lily. When a bounty hunter shows up looking for a priceless jewel that Lily has found stashed away in her aunt's belongings, Lily fears her dreams of owning her own shop--and of finding true love--are about to go up in flames...or, could that just be the glow of a beautiful ... Texas Twilight?

Mail-Order Brides of the West: Evie (2013) The well-educated daughter of a lawyer, Trudy Bauer, arrives at the St. Louis based Mail-Order Brides of the West agency full of excitement for an adventure of a lifetime. She befriends the agency's maid, Evie Davenport, and the two form a strong and lasting friendship. They vow to stay in contact through letters when Evie takes hold of her destiny and arranges a marriage on the sly. Each brave young woman is ready to face whatever an unknown groom and life in Montana can throw her way. In Fyffe's Novel, house servant Evie Davenport travels by stagecoach to Y Knot, Montana in a McCutcheon Family Novel. In Holland's book, bride-to-be Trudy Bauer rides the train to Sweetwater Springs, in a Montana Sky Novel. Through their correspondence, the friends keep each other abreast of their hardships, trials and tribulations--some of heartbreak, some of love. (McCutcheon-lite - they show up on a dozen pages)

MAIL-ORDER BRIDES OF THE WEST: HEATHER (2013) Heather Stanford dreads the day the matron of the St. Louis bridal agency finds her a husband and sends her west. Heather actually has no desire to marry; she just wants to free her struggling family from the financial burden of another mouth to feed. Still, she holds true to her plan when the fateful day arrives and Mrs. Seymour sings the praises of her prospective groom. Heather girds herself to leave behind all she holds dear and wonders if anyone can live up to the matron's glowing description. After a mill accident leaves Hayden Klinkner's father injured, Hayden is faced with the challenge of a huge order to fill--short-handed--on a tight timeline. Further complicating matters, the handsome, dyed-in-the-wool bachelor discovers his meddling mother has a surprise to share with him--a wife! With the pressure he's under, a wife--even one as lovely and suitable as Heather Stanford--is the last thing he needs. Y Knot, Montana is set abuzz when the "Mail-Order Bride Done Wrong" goes back on the market and every eligible man for miles around is interested. Hayden's eyes are now opened. Can he win back her heart before she says "I do" with someone else? (McCutcheon-lite they show on a dozen pages).

title: speculative historic fiction & sweet lesbian romance
text:
Margerit Sovitre's life turns upside down when she surprised to receive the fortune of her godfather and relative, the Baron Saveze, upon his death.

Barbara, the Baron's very young Xena Warrior Princess of a bodygurd is now in servitude to Margarit (instead of being set free), she is now Barbara the bitter badass.

The Saveze title is bequeathed to the Saveze's nephew, Estefen, who also wants the fortune.

The Prince of Alpennia (think fictional European principality, ie Monaco, somewhere between 1680 to 1820) is not long for this world and not in good health.

The person who controls the divine power derived from 'The Mysteries of the Saints' (the ritual prayers) will gain the upper hand.

A romance (think Harlequin and not erotic) develops between Margarit and Barbara.

While I totally enjoyed the novel, the lack of depth and drama kept me from being enraptured. Margarit's problems resolved readily, Barbara's battles were settled readily and the innocent romance, while nice, is less than I look for in a romance novel. Maybe the intended audience is for young adults?

looking for a little more info? Search "Blu Reviews Daughter of Mystery"; `DAUGHTER OF MYSTERY: A NOVEL OF ALPENNIA' Review by Rita Salner; or by "HAWKWINGLB - Heather Rose Jones, Daughter of Mystery": "Lovers of fantasy and historical fiction - read on!" BY THE BOOKGEEK; "Blu Reviews Daughter of Mystery " reviewed Jun 24, 2014 by Cheri;

I enjoyed this author interview: "Guest blog - Author Heather Rose Jones on "Daughter of Mystery" and joining her Facebook page.

title: they deserved each other
text:
Intensely researched account of the life of Russian aristocrat Vladimir Chertkov (1854-1936), his major claim to fame was his devoted 30 year friendship, beginning in 1883, with iconic Russian author, Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910). I knew very little of Tolstoy the man, I knew him only through his works Anna Karenina and the epic War and Peace. In researching her biography of Tolstoy's wife, Sophia, the author also obtained access to the correspondence between Chertkov and Tolstoy.

I can't vouch for how unbiased the author is. I can say Chertkov comes off as a ingratiating parasite of the highest order. To Tolstoy he came on bended knee as his apostle. He was a Rasputin, eventually to influence or have a hand in every aspect of Tolstoy's personal and literary life even after Tolstoy's death at age 82.

Chartkov, A master manipulator, charmed and fawned over Tolstoy and as Tolstoy aged was able to bend Tolstoy's thinking to his own. One of the many things that make me shudder is that this hack thought himself able to edit Tolstoy's work.

For more on this subject look for "'The Diaries of Sofia Tolstoy,' reviewed by Michael Dirda"

I could not have said it better myself then SOPHIE PINKHAM `Tolstoy's False Disciple,' did in the NY Times.

title: Excellent choice for a book Club
text:
Debut author of a police procedural, serial murder and lesbian romance. You will also be craving a Tommy's Burger when you finish reading, lol!

Sydney Rutledge, 35 year old Los Angeles Assistant District Attorney, is the lead prosecutor on a serial murder case (12 victims over 4 years).

Alex Chambers, 38 years old, ex-military and over 15 years on the force she is a veteran LAPD officer who made the arrest in the case. Sydney finds Alex very attractive, much to her surprise as she has never dated women, and at one time was almost married to a man until she broke it off..= Alex might return her feelings but the heartbreak she suffered years ago makes her hide behind her badge, being attracted to the straight ADA seems safe enough because it won't go anywhere. A new serial murder, a copycat of the one now doing time, is murdering female lawyers - Alex is desperate to make sure Sydney isn't the next victim.

Alex and Sydney were terrific, both had tragedies in their family, but by the end of the book I didn't feel like I got to know them as deeply as you want in a novel. The dialogue was normal for a debut author. I am super excited the author is working on a sequel.

title: A memoir of a family and autism
text:
I read a blurb for this book and was hooked: "Using anecdotal stories, her book is a raw, real story, pulling no punches and offering no sugar coating of the challenges and successes of raising her autistic son to adulthood. It's a story of commitment, love and sacrifice. Educators, parents, friends and family members need to see what families with a special child experience on a daily basis."

The story was riveting, I am partial to memoir and autism is so ephemeral a subject to my generation. I was almost 30 before I even heard the word. Then to read in this book that Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experts estimate that 1 out of 88 children age 8 will have an ASD was shocking. So many unanswered questions, like why are Males are 4x more likely to have an ASD than females?

title: Sage advice on parenting regardless your tiny tot's age.
text: Pure insight from someone who has raised 4 children of her own and taught hundreds of kids ages 5 to 13. I know there are dozens of books on the subject. This one is special and at only 83 pages is not written by someone who is blathering on and on. Take advantage of the LOOK INSIDE feature. Look at the table of contents read a couple of pages and you will be hooked.

title: coming of age - 90 years ago - excellent book club choice!!
text:
One month shy of her 18th birthday Dorothy Frances Corbin "Frankie" tells the story of her summer coming into her own. The story opens in the south side of Chicago with this "tomboy" from East Texas working in her "snotty" Aunt & "gruff" Uncle's grocery where her parents have sent her to land a proper husband. Thing is, Frankie would rather dress up as a man and go to listen to the Blues at a speakeasy.

Jean Bailey, an African American, cross-dressing singer is belting out the blues, and Frankie is enraptured and smitten. We follow Frankie as she follows Jean to St Louis (chapter 5), to Memphis (chapter 8) to Mississippi (chapter 11) to Alabama (page 110) to Decatur, Georgia (page 113) to Augusta, Georgia (chapter 14) The Gulf of Mexico (chapter 18) New Orleans (chapter 19) to East Texas (chapter 20) and back to New Orleans (chapter 21) as Jean plays 'the circuit" July to September. A hard hitting no holds barred novel of the way things really were in that era. My only regret is the last 2 pages of the novel.

For a terrific review, search "a story of a Prohibition-era lesbian romance by Maria Browning".

For a short video book trailer on YouTube search "The New Book Trailer for The Palace Blues".

For a author reading from the novel during the Writers' Retreat for Emerging LGBT Voices, August 8-15, 2010, search "Brandy T. Wilson at the Fellows Reading"

title: Lesbian police procedural. Set in Northern Minnesota
text:
Book #1 in a series from this debut Canadian author, you have a rookie American police officer looking to solve two murder mysteries without the help of her chief but with the help of her Canadian girlfriend (who is a little freaked out by small town life in the great white north).

While I enjoyed the plot and the twists very much the fate of Fuzzy Fiona was too much for me.

Looking for a little more? check out The Atikokan Progress article "Makenzi Fisk writes a crime thriller with a genuine Northern small-town feel". Or view the book trailer on YouTube by searching "JUST INTUITION by Makenzi Fisk, Book One in the Intuition Series".

#2 Burning Intuition is scheduled for January 2015
#3 Fatal Intuition is scheduled for December 2015

* more info on these books can be found on the author website by searching "MAKENZI FISK".

title: Paranormal Lesbian fiction with a murder mystery to solve
text:
Debut Welsh author tackles life in the fictional town of Oppidum, Missouri. Read the opening chapter and you will be hooked (as I was). A very satisfying ending that sets up the next book in the series. The Main Character, Aeron is a strong and sympathetic person I look forward to reading more off. I would say more about the plot but part of the fun for me were all the reveals.

The Above & Beyond Series
Book 1: The Empath
Book 2: Blind Trust
Book 3: Untrained Eye
Book 4: Hindsight
Book 5: Midas Touch
Book 6: Black Ridge Falls
Book 7: Full Circle

For a terrific author interviews search "Guest Blog from Jody Klaire: The Essence of Home" and "A Different Voice with Jody Klaire";

What sold me on the novel was the author reading from the first chapter on YouTube "chapter 1 of The Empath";

Here is a snippet from the author's website, her main character Aeron's POV: "There are some folks in life who are just meant to tread a whole other path and I happen to be one of them. Now, I ain't saying that I'm better than nobody and I ain't pretending like being an outsider is a lot of fun. It ain't. What I am saying, in a roundabout kinda way, is that you can only be one person... yourself. So it stands to reason that you should make the most of those tools you got and use them to find your dream."

title: 7 to 11 year olds
text: my 9 year old astronaut enjoys flipping through the 300 pictures by herself, with friends, or with Mom & Dad (Mom got to look at it first - lol). She brings one fact from the book to the dinner table and we all have fun with her explaining it to us. Winner

title: Perfect for a Manhattan and Brooklyn weekend getaway.
text: Queens, Staten Island or the Bronx, not so much. 27 pages on subway travel are very key. I grew up in the suburbs of NYC but moved away 13 years ago. I use the internet to plan my vacation travel. This little book was a perfect accompaniment that we took with us on our recent trip. I kept it in my carry bag for easy consulting over lunch or in the evening back in the hotel. I am the kind of person who likes to circle things to do and this little book was right up my ally. With life being so busy I don't have alot of time to plan, so flipping through the book on the flight work out great.

title: Delightful, Passionate & fun
text:
A fun retelling of the author's beloved 1998 hit [[ASIN:0373241909 Wedding Ring Promise (Silhouette Special Edition , No 1190)]] "Dylan Black was the quintessential bad boy: handsome, sexy, clad in black leather jacket and faded jeans--a born rebel with a loud motorcycle to match. He was everything 17-year-old Molly Anderson wanted. Unfortunately, he was also her beautiful older sister's boyfriend. When Molly's sister married another man, Dylan affectionately gave his "buddy" Molly the gold wedding ring he'd bought for her sister and teasingly told her to give him a call when she grew up. He promised that one day they would have an adventure. Then he disappeared from her life. Fast-forward 10 years. After the worst week of her life, Molly decides to take a vacation. While packing, she happens across the gold wedding band that Dylan gave her long ago and decides to turn her vacation into an adventure. Gold band in hand, she tracks down Dylan and finds he's still drop-dead gorgeous and she's just as wildly attracted to him as ever. As luck would have it, Dylan is at a crossroads in his successful life, and Molly's request for an "adventure" dovetails perfectly with his need to get away from the pressures of his business. Besides, pretty Molly makes his temperature rise and piques his jaded senses. But neither of them could foresee the far-reaching consequences of their reunion, for although on the surface they are mismatched, Dylan soon finds that Molly's heart is a treasure he craves more than her curvy body. And Molly discovers in Dylan a kindness and depth of feeling she's never known before. Thrown together at crucial points in their lives, the two are forced to deal with life-changing decisions while nurturing their growing love. Author Susan Mallery's deft, smooth writing style works well in this emotionally intense novel."

The story is told from both Points of View which I enjoyed and that both Dylan and Molly are super likable made me enjoy it even more.

title: Ages 10 to 12
text:
12 year old sixth-grader Brendan Doyle has no family and is in Foster care. He is a bit of a loner and his long hair makes him stand out in school. That, and his belief in the legendary spirit, Green Man, who protects the forest, ensures he has no close friends. Luckily he is able to lose himself in his art. To escape from the ever more out of control bullies (and his elderly, talk show watching foster mother Mrs. Clancy) he builds a tree fort in the woods.

Brendan meets an elderly man, Ed, who might be 'the Green Man' and a 12 year old girl, Shea. To Brendan these two new friends seem so comfortable it makes the rest of his life seem surreal.

Nastiness takes over when Brendan is badly beaten by bullies. This is a unsparing look at the cruelties life can throw a child through no fault of their own. It created an excellent opportunity for instilling the importance of empathy for our family even though no one liked the ending.

title: 12 to 14 years old
text:
Plenty of football action mixed in with real life issues and ethics. Alex is the new kid in town (a suburb of Philadelphia). Starting high school in a new town after his parents divorce is a toughie. But Alex dreams large, first by shooting for first-string varsity quarterback! Does that happen in real life?

He may have to think again because the current QB is also the coach's son, so you know he is well versed in the plays and in peak training.

My 12 year old loved it.

title: New to me author
text:
Non-stop action. Set in Berlin Germany. Police Homicide Detective Tommen is framed for the murder of a prominent judge. He escapes police custody. In an attempt to find evidence pointing to the real murder he is stymied by the manhunt for him so he slips in to the city's criminal underground to hide. The murders don't stop with the judge and they are graphic. The only disappointment was I figured out the killer earlier than Tommen did.

What makes this story unique is the secondary characters who connect with Tommen in his life or death quest. Go into this and appreciate the unique humor, you should be in for a good read.

* translated from the German by Steve Anderson.

title: Ages 9 to 14
text:
13 year old Twin brothers, Tom & Eddie, are typical New Jersey boys, with a couple exceptions. They are half-alien. Their father is a captive of the dastardly Dr. Traum(atic). They live on two different planets. One is planet Earth of 2008 where Tom lives. The other is planet Earth of 1958 where Eddie lives. Eddie's Earth was created by the aliens. A Mark Twain quoting alien shows up in both worlds signally a potential apocalypse.

My 9 and 12 year olds loved it, both had read the first in the series. An adventure novel, the twins using their super powers provide comic relief.

This summary of book #1 may help those who are new to the series:
THE TWINNING PROJECT (2012): Tom is a smart, talented loner with a chip on his shoulder and a big secret: an imaginary twin on another planet. Eddie is Tom's opposite, a friendly, athletic kid who always looks on the good side. Tom worries sometimes: does confiding in Eddie mean he's nuts? The truth is even crazier than that. Eddie and his planet are just as real as Tom and his Earth, but fifty-some years in the past. And the twins are caught up in an alien master plan that might just mean Earth--both Earths--will be destroyed. Switching places and identities, "slipping" between planets and across decades, a desperate escape, and the unraveling of deeper secrets leave Tom and Eddie aware of the danger they're facing and the tools they can use to overcome it.

title: ages 11 to 13
text: 12 year old Jonathan's parents are a tad different then most on the street where he lives. Dear old dad is an actual Angel and mom is a kindhearted Demon. The best is that his grandfather is the archangel Gabriel. This doesn't mean his life is blessed. Seriously scary things happen to his family where he and his mom are attacked and flee to grandfather. Lots of action from demons wanting Jonathan to move the the dark side ala Luke Skywalker, with lighthearted comic relief coming from the residents of Angel Gabriel's town.

title: One woman's journey finding a way to meaningful prayer
text: Published by 90 year old Abingdon Press (a division of the 225 year old United Methodist Publishing House). This essay collection is a perfect gift for someone who may be new to your church or may be feeling prayer is not what it once was. Also a terrific book club choice for a bible study group. Terrific insight and fresh approach from the 67 year old writer living in western Massachusetts.

title: the story gets a bit gruesome at one point.
text:
Set in 1967, Watts riots, black militarism, hippies, Vietnam and J Edgar Hoover running the FBI. The author's ability to reflect the bigotry of the day without using an anvil make him a must read author.

Roger Frisk, special assistant to the LAPD chief of police, offers big money to Easy Rawlins* to search for missing UC Santa Barbara college student (and wild child) Rosemary Goldsmith, daughter of weapons manufacturer Foster Goldsmith (who could never be accused of being a helicopter parent). Easy is uneasy on the deal and susses out that the police think her companion, retired boxer Bob Mantle (now a black militant going by the name Uhuru Nolicé), kidnapped her. Art Sugar, the local Don Corelone, wants the low down on Bob Mantle from Easy before the LAPD get it. Rawlins goes up against the Federal government and the LAPD who want him to stop asking questions. Things get ugly when a robbery results in the shooting of 3 police officers.

Not enough? Etta Mae Alexander, Easy's ex, wants him to look for her friend, Alana Altman's son, Alton (Alton Altman). Add in an on the run counterfeiter (Mary Donovan) and Detective Melvin Suggs who wants Rawlins to find her for more than law enforcement - turns out he has been suspended from the force for getting hot & heavy with Mary. Readers of the series know Det. Suggs as Easy's contact in the LAPD.

* for those new to the series the first Easy Rawlins novel is 1990's "Devil in a Blue Dress" (Denzel Washington starred in the 1995 film). Easy is a black private investigator, and World War II veteran, living in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles. The series stretches from 1948 to 1967, with flashbacks to 1920 (the year Easy was born in Louisiana). The strength of the novels is in the people and place, the time period, less on the outcome of the plot.

title: from 1914 to 1936 - articles from the Vanity Fair Archives
text:
72 in all include celebrity profiles (Joan Crawford, Babe Ruth and others), articles on politics, poems, and human interest stories. Authors such as Dorothy Parker, F. Scott Fitzgerald, D.H. Lawrence, Edna St. Vincent Millay, Gertrude Stein, Jean Cocteau, T.S. Eliot, Ford Madox Ford, Aldous Huxley, Bertrand Russell, Walter Winchell, P.G. Wodehouse, and Thomas Wolfe. I have been having fun with this book over the last 30 days and plan to keep it on or near the coffee table for a long time.

News to me that the Great Depression resulted in the merger with Vogue magazine.

title: 1789 to 1808 Well told Historical Fiction
text:
I opened the book when it arrived, to look it over, and ended up spending the rest of the day reading it. The debut author is a terrific storyteller. Intrigue, sex, murder, treachery, not only in the Ottoman court but also the court of France via Aimee's cousin Rose aka Joséphine de Beauharnais (born Marie Josèphe Rose Tascher de La Pagerie on the Caribbean island of Martinique to a wealthy white Creole family that owned a sugar plantation) aka the Emperess Josephine wedded to Napoleon Bonaparte.

** received the book for free through Goodreads First Reads **

FYI - Aimée du Buc de Rivéry (born December 1768) was a French heiress, a cousin of Empress Josephine. She was the daughter of wealthy French plantation owners in Pointe Royale on the Caribbean island of Martinique. After being sent to a convent school in France, she was returning home the summer of 1788 however the ship never made port. Legend has it that she was captured by Barbary pirates, sold to the Bey of Algiers who gave her as a gift to the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid I aka Abdul Hamid I aka Abd Al-Hamid I (20 March 1725 - 7 April 1789), their son Mahmud II (20 July 1789 - 1 July 1839) inherited the title and she became the Queen Mother of the Ottoman Empire with the Turkish name Nakşidil (Nakshidil) and died in 1817.

Book #1 "The Stolen Girl" in 'The Veil and the Crown' series: The legend of Aimée Dubucq de Rivery, has survived on three continents for more than two hundred years. The Stolen Girl tells the first part of her extraordinary story, her adolescence on the Caribbean island of Martinique, and her voyage to Paris where her hopes of finding a husband are shattered. Resigned to live as an old maid at the ripe age of eighteen, she decides to become a nun and sets sail to visit her relatives on Martinique one last time. On the journey, she meets and falls in love with a dashing young Scotsman. But fate had other plans for Aimée, ones that were foretold by an African Obeah woman when she was fourteen years old.

title: exciting premise got bogged down in the details
text: Still, being a history geek and a political science major in college, I was riveted. A very ambitious debut from this author. The setting in Mainz, Germany, in the 1450's, is almost other worldly in it's strangeness to today. I did learn a lot of interesting facts for example: a complete Gutenberg Bible has 1,286 pages (in two volumes), 4 pages per folio-sheet, 322 sheets of paper are required per copy. The paper  imported from Italy, hand made with a watermark created by the papermold. That Gutenberg didn't do it alone, he had investors and master craftsmen working for him. It will be interesting to see what subject the author tackles next.

title: I enjoyed it - it was certainly topical.
text:
My first novel by this author, 22 year old Californian Patrick Norris has returned from Afghanistan serving with the Marines, First Division, Third Battalion, Fifth Regiment. His dream on discharge is to start his own business offering fly-fishing charters, about as different from his tour as he can get. The desk is stacked against him. Not only is Patrick struggling with PTSD, his parents are on the verge of ruin after a fire destroys 1/8 of the family's 80 acre avocado business, 3 people were killed and it looks like arson.

His older brother, Ted, is going off the deep end. Seeing conspiracies in his local government he's joined a group of racists who would love to drive every Mexican across the border back to Mexico - at gun point.

Add to that a love interest and his returning vet buddies the mix was as you would expect - explosive.

title: Ages 9 to 12
text:
Book 3 in a series - I had no problem following along but I did take a peek at the summaries of the earlier books and they helped*.

At the end of book #2 the sentient Castle hurtled 12 year old Celie, her griffin Rufus, 14 year old brother Rolf and 16 year old sister Lilah and friends into an alternate world where the Castle came from. On Thursday the siblings and friends encounter wizards, poisoned lakes, tombs, and forest fires to find a way home.

My 9 year old, and even the 13 year old, were entertained. I liked that the family was loving and caring of each other without a trace of being cloyingly sweet.

* Publisher summaries of the previous titles:
#2 Wednesdays in the Tower: When her brother Rolf dares her to catch magical Castle Glower creating a new room, Princess Celie takes the challenge! No one knows the Castle better than she does. But as usual, the Castle has ideas of its own. Celie finds the new room first, and inside it is hidden a giant egg. It looks like The Castle wants Celie to care for the egg and whatever creature it hatches! Celie hadn't bargained for a pet, and caring for this one will prove to be especially tricky, once Celie and her siblings realize what else the Castle is hiding....

#1 Tuesdays at the Castle: Tuesdays at Castle Glower are Princess Celie's favorite days. That's because on Tuesdays the castle adds a new room, a turret, or sometimes even an entire wing. No one ever knows what the castle will do next, and no one-other than Celie, that is-takes the time to map out the new additions. But when King and Queen Glower are ambushed and their fate is unknown, it's up to Celie, with her secret knowledge of the castle's never-ending twists and turns, to protect their home and save their kingdom.

title: "From-Aways" are what the locals call newbies to any small town in Maine
text:
A believable story. Nice Debut. Told in alternating chapters by Leah and Quinn. For me, it misses as a romance, and the story never grabbed me, however the writing was wonderful, creative. I am glad I ordered it, and will look for the author's next title.

Leah meets Henry Lynch (neither are over age 25) in a New York City bar, a whirlwind courtship results in marriage. Leah envisions a romantic life moving to his hometown on the coast of Maine. That's not exactly what she gets (Henry lives in the home he grew up in, his parents died in separate tragedies in the last 5 years). She finds work at the small town paper, owned by Henry's antagonistic sister (Henry's sister is the only thing that didn't ring true for me).

Quinn Winters is also a From-Away, hunting down her bio-father, Carter Marks (a folk singer). Quinn is the result of a brief affair, her mother now dead Quinn wants to meet Carter. She too is hired on the paper. Her snarky sarcastic self is a highlight of Leah's day.

How the townies, Leah, Quinn and their loved ones make it all work is the rest of the story.

title: 2005 - a Yank goes to Oxford (at fictional Fleet College)
text:
or Drink, Think, Lust. The author vividly portrays Oxford in all it's glory and oddities. Fresh out of Yale, William 'Will' Baker was a campaign worker for John Kerry's unsuccessful presidential campaign. As a consolation prize he heads to Oxford to read English literature, with a concentration in George Orwell's books.

Alison was his stateside girlfriend until he meets, Jess, until he meets Sophie, an Oxford student in a relationship (not with Will).

Tom shares a flat with, and looks down on, Will, however they become BFFs, while (cinder)Ella, falls for Tom.

Anneliese from Germany; Anil from India; Peter, Richard, Georgio and reality TV obsessed Timmo round out the crew.

This crew was so superficial I didn't care a wick about them, I was able to enjoy them as if they were all on the reality TV Show Big Brother.

title: romance in a small town in the mountains of West Virginia
text:
"Hometown Romance with Heart...and Heat" Yes please! You don't need to read the first book in the series to enjoy this one however I listed them below if you like this one. The only thing that kept from really enjoying it is the couple meet and two weeks later it is happily ever after. It lacked the depth I need to care for the characters. Julia & Paul are nicely passionate and erotic but the build up was missing.

#1 TAKE ME HOME (2012): the mountain town of Sanctuary, West Virginia, where a whisper horse leads two wounded hearts to a second chance at love. When Claire Parker left Satctuary, West Virginia, she thought it was for good. But now she's back, reeling from an ugly divorce. Readjusting to small-town life is harder than Claire expected, so she's surprised, and grateful, to find companionship in Willow, an abused Thoroughbred mare. Willow is Claire's "whisper horse," and they share a special, rare bond. Except Willow isn't the only one helping Claire heal; Willow's ruggedly handsome veterinarian, Dr. Tim Arbuckle, is sympathetic...and secretive. Devastated by his wife's death, Tim thought he'd never find love again. The stoic, sexy doctor was sure he'd left his heart behind when he came to Sanctuary. But Claire stirs up emotions he thought he'd buried long ago. For the first time, the doctor can see past his grief...until Willow falls gravely ill. Tim and Claire must save Willow's life and, surrounded by the majestic mountains of West Virginia, believe in a love so encompassing, so intimately intense, their lives will never be the same again. Amazon Editors selected Take Me Home as one of 50 Great American Love Stories. Gayle Wilson Award of Excellence Winner - Contemporary Single Title.

#3 THE PLACE I BELONG (2014): Fleeing professional scandal and a broken engagement, veterinarian Hannah Linden abandons Chicago for Sanctuary, West Virginia, hoping to put her troubles with men and the media behind her. But when she encounters world-famous chef Adam Bosch, she finds herself increasingly drawn to the charming but darkly complex man and his troubled teenage son, Matt. Adam, a recovering alcoholic, fears he can never be a worthy father to the surly, distant boy he has just come to know, and enlists Hannah's help in his struggle to connect with his son. Hoping to coax Matt out of his shell, Hannah introduces the boy to an ailing brown pony who has the power to change his view of the world. But can the determined little whisper horse prove to Hannah, Adam, and Matt that they were meant to be a family?

title: Cinderella meets Norma Rae in the 1830's Mill town of Lowell Massachusetts.
text:
Compulsively readable. A very realistic look at the life of a Mill worker in those times, including a very romantic plot. Alice leaves her going-nowhere-fast life on the family farm in New Hampshire. Jumping from the frying pan into the fire of a mill job (that at least paid a wage)and finds includes the rich mill owner, Hiram Fiske, allowing the workers, Alice, to air their concerns at his Beacon Hill estate without getting thrown out on her ear. While there, Alice meets the Samuel Fiske (aka Prince Charming). However when Alice returns to Lowell from Boston her BFF 'Lovey' is found murdered and the mystery turns into the OJ Simpson trial of it's day.

Want a little more? search "Novelist's 'Daring Ladies' focuses on Lowell's Mill Girls" By Samantha Allen , sallen@lowellsun.com for an terrific author interview.

On a historical note there is a terrific article you can read by searching "Spinning local history into fiction" by Joel Brown Boston Globe APRIL 19, 2014. It tells the reader of a similar murder mystery in 1832 Rhode Island.

title: #3 in the Blackberry Island, Washington Trilogy
text:
For 30 year old Nina Wentworth (who we first met in the second Blackberry Island book 'Three Sisters') nursing comes naturally, she has devoted her life to her beloved mother and sister (so much so that she gave up on her dream of medical school, and her lover, to stay with her irresponsible mother, Bonnie, and put her sister through college). Just as she thinks that her life is lacking, Dylan (her first love and now a successful doctor). Also a hunky fighter-pilot, Kyle, enter the picture (lucky!) if only he didn't used to crush on her when she babysat him (creepy).

Her sister, Averil, is a challenge to love (basically she is toxic at the moment), she is restless in her life (which she feels she has lived for Nina), is frustrated in her career (aren't we all?) and she is not honest with her husband, Kevin, about having children.

LOL non-spoiler moment for me in chapter one. Living in the Pacific North West myself I could totally relate to Nina's being in a cell reception dead zone, in the pouring rain, with a broken down car, and having to hoof it to help! The author nailed it.

FYI - Blackberry Island is a wonderful creation by the author tucked between Banbridge Island and Seattle - it's a bedroom community as well as a tourist destination via Ferry or Bridge.

* I added for a link to a graphic of the island from the author's web page in the comment section

title: Book #11 of 15
text:
I was completely charmed. "Fool's Gold, where a onetime fling could become the real thing...." Well, Alrighty then! The Fool's Gold series begun in 2010. Not to worry the books are all independent of each other and the author provides a really great who's who on her website plus a really cool town map. Perfect beach read or when you need a quick feel good story.

27 year old Felicia Swift (introduced in book #10 Just One Kiss) is a tall, attractive red-head with green eyes who "just might be the smartest person in the world, but after being raised on a university campus, she feels socially awkward. All she wants in the world is to be normal, to fit in." Literally - she grew up in a University Lab from the age of 4 after her parents freaked at how intelligent she was after she created a bomb! At 17 she joined the military to make some intense human connections, which she does but the guys all treat her like a kid sister.

33 year old tall dark and husky voiced Gideon Boylan is an ex-Special Forces Black Ops who "spent two years in a Taliban prison, where he learned that loving someone makes you vulnerable. He won't allow himself to go there." Ok, Gideon had me at "two years in a Taliban prison". That is nothing to play with. He was the sole survivor in his unit so he must have a lot of baggage to deal with. Friend's talked him into visiting Fool's Gold, saw the radio station for sale and bought it (He is now the host of a nighttime show).

At age 24, Felicia is in a bar in Thailand and seduces Gideon to be her first lover. Felicia finds her way to Fool's Gold asks Gideon to "help learn how to be in a real relationship", Gideons's "confident he can play boyfriend for a time without risking his heart".

The whole thing made me think What if 7of9 from Star Trek Voyager beamed down to planet earth today - she would be Felicia - I loved that idea!

title: The Mill River Redemption by Darcie Chan
text:
New to me author. Until the end, the story was downer for me (because my own beloved mother died so many years ago also at a relatively young age). I kept reading it (the story bounces between the past and present) and wondering 'what was I thinking to have read this' however the ending was spot on perfect. What was getting me down was the thought that two sisters (Rose and Emily) could spend their lives breaking their widowed mother's heart (a rift that isn't explained until more than half the book book is read) and not reconciling until it was too late. However the author made their reconciliation so wonderful that I was glad to have read it to the end.

If you enjoyed this you should try the author's debut novel "The Mill River Recluse" I added it to my wish list today.
Book #1[[ASIN:B00H3NNWXE The Mill River Recluse: A Novel]] From the outside, Mill River looks like any sleepy little Vermont town where everyone knows everyone and people never need to lock their doors. There are newcomers for whom this appeals, from police officer Kyle Hansen and his daughter Rowen, who are starting over after heartache, to Claudia Simon, the schoolteacher who is determined to reinvent herself. But on closer inspection, there are those in Mill River—including a stealthy arsonist, a covetous nurse, and a pilfering priest—who have things they wish to hide. None more than the widow Mary McAllister, who for the past sixty years has secluded herself in her marble mansion overlooking the town. Most of the residents have never even seen the peculiar woman. Only the priest, Father O’Brien, knows the deep secrets that keep Mary isolated—and that, once revealed, will forever change the community.

title: The whole series is consistent in packing an emotional punch or a laugh out loud moment.
text:
I became a Mitford, North Carolina "the little town with the big heart" addict 20 years ago and can't wait to get my hands on the 10th in the series. #7 in the series is titled IN THIS MOUNTAIN and begins 3 years after the end of book #6. Father Tim is turning 70 and none too pleased by it (the diabetic blackouts would make be a bit negative too).
My only issue is that the author be matched with an editor that can pull her away from cliche and repetitive phrases.

The Mitford books in publication order:

#1 At Home in Mitford, published 1994: It's easy to feel at home in Mitford. In these high, green hills, the air is pure, the village is charming, and the people are generally lovable. Yet, Father Tim, the bachelor rector, wants something more. Enter a dog the size of a sofa who moves in and won't go away. Add an attractive neighbor who begins wearing a path through the hedge. Now stir in a lovable but unloved boy, a mystifying jewel theft, and a secret that's sixty years old. Suddenly, Father Tim gets more than he bargained for. And readers get a rich comedy in which mysteries and miracles abound.

#2 A Light in the Window, published 1995: His attractive neighbor is tugging at his heartstrings. A wealthy widow is pursuing him with hot casseroles. And his red-haired Cousin Meg has moved into the rectory, uninvited. As you can see, Mitford's rector and lifelong bachelor, Father Tim, is in need of divine intervention. In this beautifully crafted second novel in the Mitford series, Jan Karon delivers a love story that's both heartwarming and hilarious. Only time will tell if the village parson can practice what he preaches.

#3 These High, Green Hills, published 1996: Mitford, a southern village of local characters so heartwarming and hilarious you'll wish you lived right next door. At last, Mitford's rector and lifelong bachelor, Father Tim, has married his talented and vivacious neighbor, Cynthia. Now, of course, they must face love's challenges: new sleeping arrangements for Father Tim's sofa-sized dog, Cynthia's urge to decorate the rectory Italian-villa-style, and the growing pains of the thrown-away boy who's become like a son to the rector.Add a life-changing camping trip, the arrival of the town's first policewoman, and a new computer that requires the patience of a saint, and you know you're in for another engrossing visit to Mitford, the little town that readers everywhere love to call home.

#4 Out to Canaan, published 1997:Father Tim, the Episcopal rector, and his wife are pondering the murky uncertainties of retirement; a brash new mayoral candidate is calling for aggressive development; a shady realtor with plans for a health spa is eyeing the beloved house on the hill; and, worst of all, the Sweet Stuff Bakery may be closing. Meanwhile, ordinary people engage in the extraordinary struggle of keeping body and soul together.

A New Song, published 1999: Father Tim, retires. However, new challenges and adventures await him when he agrees to serve as interim minister of a small church on Whitecap Island. He and his wife, Cynthia, soon find that Whitecap has its own unforgettable characters: a church organist with a mysterious past, a lovelorn bachelor placing personal ads, a mother battling depression. They also find that Mitford is never far away as circumstances back home keep their phone ringing off the hook.

A Common Life: the Wedding Story, published 2001: the wedding of Father Tim Kavanagh and Cynthia Coppersmith. Will Father Tim fall apart when he takes his vows? Will Cynthia make it to the church on time? Who'll arrange the flowers and bake the wedding cake? Laughter and wedding bells ring as Jan Karon takes her fans back in time to the most cherished event in Mitford!

In This Mountain, published 2002
Shepherds Abiding, published 2003
Light from Heaven, published 2005.
*The Mitford Bedside Companion, published 2006
Somewhere Safe with Somebody Good, Sept. 2014

The Father Tim Novels:
Home to Holly Springs, published October 30, 2007
In the Company of Others, published October 2010

Christmas gift books:
The Mitford Snowmen, published 2001
Esther's Gift, published 2002

title: New to me author -
text:
Like a romance in a 1940's movie, including no sex (I think it is called 'clean'). It really is a very sweet read I am very fortunate to have read it. These are good people and you are happy when they find each other. You get to know both Joe and Polly (and her niece Ellie) through their own Point of View. The epilogue is dear. Read a few sample pages and that should hook you.

I didn't have the opportunity to read the first volume of the King's Valley series so include a book summary from the publisher although there is no need to read it first as there is only a mention of characters once in the story.

Ethan's Bride (2013): For most of her life, Jessica Lind-Mallory. has played the role of the perfect daughter, perfect stepdaughter, and, ultimately, the perfect fiancée, concealing her true self behind the person she thought everyone else wanted and expected her to be. That all ends the day she discovers that her future husband is cheating on her. Her spur-of-the-moment escape comes to a grinding halt when her car breaks down on a lonely country road. But no gallant knight comes to her rescue. Instead, she's confronted by a handsome stranger who believes that she's a spoiled, self-indulgent, high society brat up to no good. Jessica is only too willing to obey the stranger's command to get out of his sight. But fate and a mischievous, matchmaking grandmother steps into the fray, and two stubborn people who have been unlucky in love may discover that true love really can change everything.

** received the book for free through Goodreads First Reads **

title: memoir of NYTimes columnist on growing up poor & black in a backwater town in Louisiana
text: Beautiful evocative and masterful prose makes this a keeper and a must read. Starting as an intern for the Shreveport Times and educated at Grambling State, by age 25 he was working at the New York Times. We learn about his strong mother who raised 5 children while plucking poultry to put a roof over their head, food on the table and clothes on their back and not much else. *SPOILER ALERT* his horrendous catalyst out was being sexually molested by a relative. You can feel for him as the hazing at college as a fraternity pledge had the potential to send him over the edge.

title: #17 in the series that inspired the TV show 'BONES', with the author a consulting producer
text:
Reichs is a new to me American author, and having enjoyed this novel I am looking forward to reading the series going strong for 17 years. The author knows her stuff, she is the forensic anthropologist for the province of Quebec, Canada (also serves on the Canadian National Police Services Advisory Council), and is professor of anthropology at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte.

If you are also new to the series this info may be helpful: Dr. Temperance "Tempe" Brennan is one of 85 active board-certified forensic anthropologists in North America. She investigates crime scenes Laboratoire des Sciences Judiciaires et de Médecine Légale for the province of Quebec in Montreal, Canada.involving victims of arson, mutilation, advanced decomposition, etc. A native of Chicago, she grew up in the Carolinas, she left her husband, Janis "Pete" Peterson, is a recovering alcoholic who drinks Diet Coke or Perrier. She divides her time between teaching at the University of North Carolina in Charlotte and advising on crime scenes. Brennan has a daughter in college, Katy, a younger sister, Harriet known as Harry (who has a son, Kit). Brennan's cat, Birdie, travels with her. Detective Andrew Ryan is her former lover (they have cockatoo named Charlie in Montreal), her husband Pete's dog, Boyd, spends a lot of time with her when she in in Charlotte.

Temperance Brennan Series:

Deja Dead (1997)

title: Memoir of an Iranian refugeee in the 1970's
text:
True story of the author's terrifying adventure at age 9 where his parents attempt to get him out of the war torn country (at war with Iraq). Instead of leaving the country with his mom, the author boards a plane to Turkey without her. He must make his way with limited funds in hopes the British Embassy will allow him to immigrate to England where he has a guardian. Even knowing that the child does survive does not take away from the drama.

I would say this is suitable for ages 10 and up.

A fictional account of the authors adventure was published earlier as THE LITTLE MAN:
THE LITTLE MAN (2005) What would you be willing to do to save your child's life? This is the true, heart-wrenching story of author Abbas Kazerooni, The Little Man. Faced with the dilemma of sending their seven-year-old son to an almost certain death as a soldier in the Iranian army, his mother and father did the only thing they could to spare his life, they sent him away. Left standing alone in the middle of the Istanbul Airport, the young child knew he had to make a decision. He chose to live. Against insurmountable odds and with danger constantly pressing in around him, he learned to survive with the hope that one day he might be reunited with his parents. Page after suspenseful page will keep you on an emotional journey through Tehran and Istanbul. Prepare to see the world as you have never seen it before, through the eyes of The Little Man. 225 pages

title: Ideal novel for those who want to see that there is light at the end of the tunnel
text:
Wonderfully uplifting (and not preachy!) book for those who are at a crossroad in their life.The author, a pastor, shares her story of despairing that she will ever make a family of her own. She continues to relay stories she knows personally, illustrating that even in the darkest of times if you endure (and share your burden with God and loved ones) you will come out the other side to a happier time.

Will make an ideal gift to anyone going through a rough period.

title: While not as awesome as earlier books in the series - still very enjoyable, especially if you are already a fan of the series
text:
Imagine '4 Weddings and Funeral' meets 'The Vicar of Dibley' and you will get a sense of this series going strong after 10 years. I was going to describe the "44 Scotland Street" series as a "Tales of the City" by Armistead Maupin but set in Scotland. I had to lol when I read the author's note on the beginning of the series:

"It was a chance encounter with Armistead Maupin (of Tales of the City fame) in San Francisco which inspired Alexander McCall Smith to write his serial novel about the residents of 44 Scotland Street, a fictitious building in a real street in the author’s home town of Edinburgh. "With its multiple-occupancy flats, 44 Scotland Street is an interesting corner of the city; a very Edinburgh mix of Bohemians, haute bourgeoisie, students and the more colourful members of the intelligentsia. 44 Scotland Street first appeared in daily episodes in The Scotsman newspaper in 2004, and was published in book form later that year by Polygon with great success. The adventures of Bertie the child prodigy, Cyril the dog with the gold tooth, and raffish painter Angus Lordie became an instant hit and a further eight series and book publications followed."

FYI a ninth book in the series was published already in the UK. - you will probably be more than a bit lost without something of a background so I included the author's book series summaries below:

44 Scotland Street: The story revolves around the comings and goings at No. 44 Scotland Street, a fictitious building in a real street in Edinburgh. Immediately recognisable are the Edinburgh chartered surveyor, stalwart of the Conservative Association, who dreams of membership of Scotland’s most exclusive golf club. We have the pushy Stockbridge mother, and her prodigiously talented five-year-old son, who is making good progress with the saxophone and with his Italian. Then there is Domenica Macdonald who is that type of Edinburgh lady who sees herself as a citizen of a broader intellectual world.In McCall Smith’s hands such characters retain charm and novelty, simultaneously arousing both mirth and empathy. 44 Scotland Street is vintage McCall Smith, tackling issues of trust and honesty, snobbery and hypocrisy, love and loss, but all with great lightness of touch. Clever, elegant and funny, this is a novel that provides huge entertainment but which is underpinned by the moral dilemmas of everyday life and the characters’ struggles to resolve them.

Espresso Tales: Bruce, the intolerably vain and perpetually deluded ex-surveyor, is about to embark on a new career as a wine merchant, while his long-suffering flatmate Pat MacGregor, set up by matchmaking Domenica Macdonald, finds herself invited to a nudist picnic in Moray Place in the pursuit of true love. Prodigious six-year-old Bertie Pollock wants a boy’s life of fishing and rugby, not yoga and pink dungarees, and he plots rebellion against his bossy, crusading mother Irene and his psychotherapist Dr Fairbairn. But when Bertie’s longed-for trip to Glasgow with his ineffectual father Stuart ends with Bertie taking money off legendary Glasgow hard man Lard O’Connor at cards, it looks as though Bertie should have been more careful what he wished for. And all the time it appears that both Irene Pollock and Dr Fairbairn are engaged in a struggle with dark secrets and unconscious urges of their own.

Love Over Scotland: Six-year-old prodigy Bertie perseveres in his heroic struggle for truth and balanced good sense against his insufferable mother and her crony, the psychotherapist Dr Fairbairn, going as far as to make a short-lived bid for freedom on a trip to Paris with the Edinburgh youth orchestra. Domenica sets off on an anthropological odyssey with pirates in the Malacca Straits, while Pat attracts several handsome admirers, including a toothsome suitor named Wolf. And Big Lou, eternal source of coffee and good advice to her friends, has love, heartbreak and erstwhile boyfriend Eddie’s misdemeanours on her own mind.

The World According to Bertie: Poor put-upon Bertie is still struggling to escape his overbearing mother’s influence, his yoga lessons and his pink bedroom while wondering why new baby brother Ulysses looks uncomfortably like his psychotherapist. The insufferably handsome Bruce has returned from London to land, on his feet and rent-free, in the arms of heiress Julia Donald. But all is not well among the residents of 44 Scotland Street: Angus’s dog and constant companion Cyril is under threat of execution, victim of a miscarriage of justice, while pretty, indecisive Pat and hopeless romantic Matthew are on the verge of making the most terrible mistake of their lives … Big Lou finds a new man, Matthew and Pat edge their relationship towards something more permanent – although this development is not without complications, when a glimpse of someone who just might be her handsome, caddish ex-flatmate Bruce sets Pat’s pulse racing – and Domenica’s friendship with Antonia is tested to the limit when an assortment of her belongings mysteriously appear in Antonia’s new flat.

The Unbearable Lightness of Scones: To the casual observer, the great enlightened city of Edinburgh, home of no-nonsense philosophers and cream teas, might appear immune to the rollercoaster of strong emotions. But at 44 Scotland Street, as Matthew and Elspeth embark on the risky enterprise of married love, the raffish portrait painter Angus Lordie has a premonition of disaster. And soon enough Irene Pollock is shocked to learn that her small son Bertie harbours a highly unsuitable ambition; the gloriously vain Bruce discovers a wrinkle and confronts rejection; and Angus finds himself facing the grave consequences of unbridled bliss, not to mention a large Glaswegian gangster bearing gifts …

The Importance of Being Seven: Despite inhabiting a great city renowned for its impeccable restraint, the extended family of 44 Scotland Street is trembling on the brink of reckless self-indulgence. Matthew and Elspeth receive startling – and expensive – news on a visit to the Infirmary, Angus and Domenica are contemplating an Italian ménage a trois, and even Big Lou is overheard discussing cosmetic surgery. But when Bertie Pollock – six years old and impatient to be seven – mislays his meddling mother Irene one afternoon, a valuable lesson is learned: that wish-fulfilment is a dangerous business.

Bertie Plays The Blues: Domestic bliss seems in short supply at 44 Scotland Street. Over at the Pollocks, dad, Stuart, is harbouring a secret about a secret society and Bertie is feeling kind of blue. Having had enough of his neurotic hot-housing mother, he puts himself up for adoption on eBay. Will he go to the highest bidder or will he have to take matters into his own hands? Will the lovelorn Big Lou find true love on the internet? And will Angus Lordie and Domenica make it up the aisle? Catch up with all your favourite faces down in 44 Scotland Street as we follow their daily pursuit of a little happiness.

#8 Sunshine on Scotland Street:
#9 Bertie’s Guide to Life and Mothers

title: Dark
text: Disturbingly dark. I wonder who enjoys writing novels where the innocent and helpless are tormented and tortured?  I wonder who enjoys reading novels where the innocent and helpless are tormented and tortured? I didn't enjoy it at all but this author certainly does an excellent job of it. Will try the author again if he writes a plot with a subject matter that makes me feel less sick to my stomache.

title: Nicely Amusing
text: not laugh out loud, but fun in a snarky sort of way. 80 short essays written by a mother (and successful mystery author) and daughter (and successful columnist for the Philadelphia Inquirer) duo.  It might make a nice holiday gift for your grandmother or aunt.

title: I thought the ending was rushed, too quick and too short.
text:
In the small town of Jericho in Northeastern Mississippi, a Cold Case from 1977. Rape, shooting and murder of a 14 year old girl followed two days later with the lynching of a homeless black man. The twist is there were two girls - one lived, 17-year-old Diane Tull, and the other died (her 14-year-old friend, Lori Stillwell) and now the one who lived is compelled to come forward, by the drunken father of the dead girl, and open the case.

34 year old ex Army Ranger and Afghanistan veteran Sheriff Quinn Colson also has to deal with Chains LeDoux, leader of the 'Born Losers' motorcycle gang who just spent 20 years in prison (fyi Lori Stillwell's father, Hank, was a 'Born Losers' biker. Then there is corrupt county commission chairman and crime boss Johnny Stagg who would love to see Chains take on Quinn. Staggs muscle, Ringold, will do all he can to make that happen.

Book# 4 in the series. Fans will be pleased to learn more about Quinn's past and his deadbeat father, Jason (a Hollywood stuntman), is in this novel along with Quinn's Uncle Hemp who was Sheriff before Quinn and at the time of the lynching.

There is A LOT of backstory, for those who are new to the series this info from the publisher should help a bit:
Book #1 THE RANGER: After years of war, Army Ranger Quinn Colson returns home to the rugged, rough hill country of northeast Mississippi to find his native Tibbehah County overrun with corruption, decay, meth runners, and violence. His uncle, the longtime county sheriff, is dead. A suicide, he's told, but others--like tomboy deputy Lillie Virgil--whisper murder. In the days that follow, it's up to Colson to discover the truth, not only about his uncle, but about his family, his friends, his town, and himself. And once it's discovered, there's no going back for this real hero of the Deep South.

Book #2 THE LOST ONES: Fresh from ten years as a U.S. Army Ranger, Quinn Colson finds his hands full as the newly elected sheriff of Tibbehah County, Mississippi. An old buddy running a local gun shop may be in over his head when stolen army rifles start showing up in the hands of a Mexican drug gang. At the same time, an abused-child case leads Quinn and his tough-as-nails deputy, Lillie Virgil, deep into the heart of a bootleg baby racket and a trail of darkness and death. And when the two cases collide, Quinn and his allies are forced to realize that, though they may be home from the war, they are now in the fight of their lives.

Book #3 THE BROKEN PLACES: A year after becoming sheriff, Quinn Colson is faced with the release of an infamous murderer from prison. Jamey Dixon comes back to Jericho preaching redemption, and some believe him; but for the victim's family, the only thought is revenge. Another group who doesn't believe him--the men in prison from Dixon's last job, an armored car robbery. They're sure he's gone back to grab the hidden money, so they do the only thing they can: break out and head straight to Jericho themselves. Colson and his deputy, Lillie, know they've got their work cut out for them. But they don't count on one more unwelcome visitor: a tornado that causes havoc just as events come to a head. Communications are down, the roads are impassable--and the rule of law is just about to snap.

title: Ages 9 to 13
text:
If you ever loved the movie The [[ASIN:B00006L931 Thief of Bagdad (1940)]], staring Sabu, you will enjoy this.

16 year old Zayele is about marry Kamal, the son of the caliph. She is devastated at the thought of leaving her brother who is blind.

Najwa, is a jinni and a member of the 'Eyes of Iblis Corps'. Najwa must infiltrate the caliph's home to learn about a weapon Kamal is creating. Zayele makes a wish and she and Najwa switch places causing all sorts of trouble with Najwa eventually being sent by Faisal to rescue Najwa.

The 13 year old thought it predictable, the 9 year old enjoyed it - the 50 year old thought it was a nice debut.

title: If Nancy Drew was to solve an Agatha Christie murder mystery with the cast of the TV show Glee and Scooby Doo.
text: New York State Catskills, 1982 & 1997. The book hooked me with the opening line "Her bangs are crispy with Aqua Net. Her ponytail is so tight her forehead aches. Her feet throb in shoes that are a size too small". Ok, I know that moment - lol. I only wish I could ask the author one question "what was with the glove?". Also, the gold teeth I could have done without - ick!

title: Ages 9 to 12
text:
A well told mystery adventure takes place (no spoilers) with lots of middle grade (and toilet) humor. Both my 9 year old (girl) and 12 year old (boy) were entertained.

12 year old Teddy "Roosevelt" Fitzroy is living at FunJungle,a zoo/amusement park (like Busch Gardens, Tampa Flora; or Walt Disney World Animal Kingdom, Orlando Florida) where his parents work (his mom is scientist and his dad a wildlife photographer).

Vance, is the school bully (I loathe bullies).

Summer, is Teddy's friend and he's kinda sweet on her.

Kazoo, is a koala on loan from Australia who, disastrously, goes missing.

Large Marge, is in charge of park security and has her eye on Teddy as the culprit.

J.J. McCracken is the billionaire investor in the park and wants more bang for his bucks.

Sequel to 'Belly Up' (2010): Publishers summary: Twelve-year-old Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt Fitzroy has murder on his hands and trouble on his tail. He believes that Henry, the hippopotamus at the brand-new FunJungle, has been murdered. The zoo's top brass claim the hippo went belly up the natural way, but Teddy and his feisty friend Summer McCraken have other ideas. Could the culprit be FunJungle's animal-hating head of operations? Or is it FunJungle's owner--Summer's dad--a man who is much more concerned about money than animal welfare? The deeper Teddy and Summer dig, the more danger they're in--because when it comes to hippo homicide, the truth can't be caged!

title: This title will be either a hit or miss
text:
For me it was a hit. First, I have a childish, snarky sense of humor. Second, I LOVE movies and literature. The author's and screenwriter's of Classics & Contemporary Literature, as well as Film and TV, rough drafts are lampooned. It was very funny.

My highest recommendation would be to read the sample offered. If you aren't chuckling or laughing or snickering give this a pass. Or take a look at Laudiero's website (same name as this book) his take on the writing process of JK Rowling's Lord Voldemort still cracks me up.

The artwork, illustrations and graphics are a bonus.

title: If you like the author's Christmas Hope series (and the movies they were made into) you will love this novel.
text:
Spoiler free review ahead: 4 families brought together through a small town church Nativity, I was somewhat distracted from the characters by the author's writing style, at times it read to me almost like it was being narrated or explained to me. Also, while the dialogue is spot on, occasionally it would sound stilted, where people would speak with such formality it was like they were reading from something they wrote down.
*Jennifer is a widow of 3 years, her 6 year old daughter Avery is missing her Dad BIG TIME.
*Ryan, is a divorcee after his wife left him, and their now 6 year old daughter Sofia, for another man.
*16 year old Kaylee is facing the biggest decision any teenager can, luckily she has a wonderful family.
*Stephen and Lily are happily married and desperate for children, but after being devastated by a horrible adoption proceeding they are despairing of starting another.

From the author's web page "Donna grew up in the idyllic small town of Medina, OH. She likes to read, cook and especially loves to spend time with her family around the pool and camping in the summers. She lives in Franklin, TN, with her husband, Troy, their children, Grace, Kate and David, two dogs, two cats, and a host of geese and ducks that use their pond as a pit stop on their way to prettier waters. Donna's mini-van is staring down 200,000 miles as she runs her kids to school, softball and baseball practices, Tae Kwon Do, church, and the grocery store all while promising her editor to meet her book deadlines (...which occasionally does happen). One of Donna's great loves is teaching and speaking. She has appeared at countless events around the country including keynote addresses at the prestigious Patricia Adams Lecture Series at Heidelberg University, Women of Faith, Among Friends Conferences and Extraordinary Women. Donna has won a Retailer's Choice Award for Fiction, a Dove Award, a Silver Angel Award, two Audie Awards for best inspirational fiction, has been a nominee for a Gold Medallion Book of the Year and is an inductee in the Ohio Foundation of Independent Colleges Hall of Excellence joining such luminaries as Coretta Scott King, Hugh Downs, Dr. Norman Vincent Peale and Senator John Glenn. She also serves on the board of directors for National House of Hope, a residency program that is offered in several states for abused and at-risk teens.Donna's brand new Christmas movie, The Christmas Secret (starring Bethany Joy Lenz) coming to Hallmark late fall 2014."

title: Good twist at the end of the book
text:
New to me author and I was a bit lost with so many characters, and their stories, - it turns out many are from the author's 20 earlier novels so fans of the author will LOVE this. What grabbed my eye was the cover art and then the summary of the book. From the author' website:

'Jess, winner of The David Porteous' Botanical Painting Award for Young Artists, little knows that when she accepts the invitation from the award founder's widow, Kate, that she will be opening Pandora's Box. Far from being a holiday in the west country so that she can build up a portfolio of botanical paintings, it turns into a search into the muddled history of her family: a history which has been kept secret from her. `It was such a shock,' Kate tells her old friends Cass and Tom on her return to Tavistock, `to see how like her grandmother she is. Of course, Jess is about the same age Juliet was when I first met her. It took me way back. I lost touch after Mike and Juliet went out to Australia but Jess was so thrilled to think that I'd known them. What an amazing coincidence.' Way back: parties at the Trehearnes' Georgian house on the banks of the River Tamar - and one particular party thrown to celebrate Dickie Trehearne's knighthood on his promotion to Vice Admiral which had spilled out of the house and onto the Sea Garden. Kate, Cass and Tom had all been there as had Alistair and Johnnie, Dickie's sons, and Mike, Al's best friend and rival. Officers in their uniforms and girls in long dresses dancing until dawn. But it was Mike who had married the beautiful Juliet and not Alistair as Old Lady Trehearne had so hoped. She is still mourning the loss of her eldest son in a mysterious boating accident and has always suspected him of having an affair with Juliet but she and Mike emigrated to Australia before the birth of their son who was to return to England and join the army only to be killed in the war in Bosnia shortly after Jess was born. When Jess reacts strongly to one face in old group photograph including Alastair, Lady T is convinced she has found her long lost granddaughter. But all is not quite so simple.'

Things that make you go, hmmmm.

I have ordered the earlier novels that feature characters in this book - looking forward to reading them very much:

Those Who Serve (Kate and Cass as young wives and mothers)
Thea's Parrot (almost a sequel)
The Courtyard (Guy as a young man and Gemma just left school)
Second Time Around (Kate and her other son Giles)
The Birdcage (Gemma and Guy)
Echoes of the Dance (Kate)
