title: Book#3
text:
A nicely unique and sometimes unbeleivable premise that I wasn't sure could be pulled off, but it was hard to put down. A straightforward adventure novel with a swashbuckling hero - think Errol Flynn in Captain Blood (but older and with more toys).

I've read all 3 in the series now and look forward to #4. For those new to the series here is the background info from the publisher:

Book 1 THE COLONEL'S MISTAKE :Publication Date: August 21, 2012
Mark Sava, former CIA station chief of Azerbaijan, lives a quiet life as a professor at Western University in the city of Baku. But his peace is shattered by both the assassination of a high-level American during an international oil conference and the arrest of CIA operations officer Daria Buckingham for the crime. Sava knows the Iranian American Buckingham well--he personally trained her--and doesn't believe she had anything to do with the murder, so he visits a CIA control center to discuss the situation with the new station chief. When no one answers the outside intercom, Sava overrides the security code and stumbles upon the grisliest scene of his career. Now, he can't help but wonder if he really knows Buckingham as well as he thought... Determined to find out, Sava soon finds himself and a partner caught in the middle of the new Great Game--a deadly intelligence war over oil that has Iran, China, and the United States clawing at each other's throats. Meanwhile, Colonel Henry Amato, assistant to the US national security advisor, is keeping a close watch on the situation from Washington. His stake in the Great Game is high--and personal. From the shadows of the world's most volatile region to the highest levels of Washington politics, The Colonel's Mistake takes readers on an unforgettable ride where the good, the bad, and the brutal play a deadly chess game of global espionage.

BOOK 2 THE LEVELING (2013) These days, Mark Sava spends more time in tutoring sessions than in cloak-and-dagger rendezvous. The former CIA station chief of Azerbaijan has settled into the modest life of a professor in Baku...until an assassin makes a brazen attempt on his life in the hallowed halls of the national library. The Azeri government deems Sava, with his complex past, a security threat and orders him out of the country immediately. At the same time, the CIA orders Sava back to the US. But when he receives cryptic photos that lead him to believe his friend John Decker has been kidnapped--Sava knows he has no option but to find Decker.He teams up with ex-CIA spy and former girlfriend Daria Buckingham, and the two soon find themselves being chased by Chinese intelligence agents through the underworlds of Turkmenistan and Iran, caught in the middle of a secret conflict over oil that has the US and Iran tumbling headlong into war.Filled with the espionage intrigue and pulse-pounding action that made The Colonel's Mistake a runaway hit, The Leveling brings to life in electrifying detail one of the most dangerous regions of the globe.

title: Horror
text: Compulsively readable once you get to the last 100 pages, before that it was touch and go for me if I wanted to continue. And just so you know, *possible spoiler* they all don't make it out of the cabin in the woods alive.

title: for the Buddhist believer
text:
This was a toughie to rate. I was disappointed that the book was not an unbiased biography. The book is written by a believer who embraces Tibetan Buddhist culture in all it's mysticism. That being said I do have friends who are Buddhists, I asked one to read it, and she loved it.

It wasn't an easy read, I would strongly advise to read a sample chapter before buying.

title: Elmore Leonard meets Breaking Bad in the Missouri backwoods.
text: Bloody offbeat thriller from the author of the debut title 'Frank Sinatra in a Blender'.  My Dad would have loved this novel.

title: Great gift giving book idea
text: The humor can be a bit 'blue' ('using baby wipes to give yourself a crotch bath' - er.. TMI!). The author is a entertaining blogger, search his name and the words 'beware of glass' or 'You Deserve a Break'. So good I bought copies for my cousins with tiny tots, and am keeping my copy on the livingroom coffee table for whenever I need a chuckle.

title: Satire on Reality shows and people who populate them
text:
What a train wreck! I loved every minute of it.

Handsome Eddie (that's his name) lives in quite suburbia trying to get his, less than supportive, wife Susan pregnant. Eddie was once a Hollywood hopeful, and is now a High School drama teacher. The only thing left from his dreams is his one time girlfriend is now a superstar. When Eddie needs cash, does he reach out to her for financial help? No. He prefers to have a sex tape that he made a decade ago go viral - giving him money and Fame. The fun really starts when Eddie gets everything he has coming to him.

My favorite's

on page 140 "tune in to the premiere of Desperately Expecting Susan..." which is the reality show his wife Susan finds herself in when she becomes pregnant with triplets.

page 28 "... Huffing and Cuffing, this new one (reality show) about cops addicted to paint thinner..."

LOL

title: Ages 11-13
text:
12 year old Grace's mom, Anna, was 17 when she and her boyfriend, Scott, conceived her. Grace believes her grandmother, Miranda, kicked her daughter to the curb. Before Grace was born, her father, and mother's father, died in a car accident (Grace's father's parents died in a fire when Scott was 16). Grace and her artist mother have never set down roots traveling to a new home what seems like twice a year. After her mother dies in a drowning accident, Grace is sent to live with the grandmother she never knew.

A very well told story, spoken with love, about the need for always showing your love, making sure there is never a doubt that your loved lone knows they are loved. Good ending.

title: Jersey girl in the Rockies
text:
Suspend your belief and enjoy the bus ride for a nicely plotted story with a likable heroine. I have always enjoyed the Angela Lansbury 'Murder She Wrote' series, and Agatha Christie (Murder On The Orient Express & Death on the Nile). Unlike Christie I was able to guess 'who did it' in this 'who done it'. Having been a Jersey girl myself and having traveled through the Rocky Mountains I am probably the perfect demographic for the book.

Originally published in Hardcover in 2005 and now in paperback in 2012.

title: "Is that a broadsword on your belt, or are you just glad to see me?"
text:
LOL. A fresh and interesting concept. Kind of like Outlander meets Sex in the City. Rowena is not having the best of weeks. Sure the sex is great. She loves Thane but he wants to keep her castle bound and Rowena needs her freedom. One complication, she is carrying Cedric's baby and he wants her for his own. Sure the sex is great, but he follows the dark arts and loves his power and magic above all things. Then there is the Viking invader Lars who has won her heart. Sure the sex is great, but he plans to take possession of her family's holdings. What's a good time girl to do? Well, go with the flow, make the best of things and learn as much as she can to navigate her new life.

I liked Rowena and Kendra and am very glad I got the chance to meet them. The summaries helped me and might help you if this is the first read in the series for you:

BOOK ONE - Rowena Through the Wall (2011): When Rowena falls through her classroom wall and lands in an alternate world, she doesn't count on being kidnapped―not once, but twice―and the stakes get higher as the men get hotter. Scottsale, Arizona area college instructor Rowena Revel has a magical gift with animals and a huge problem (apparently she has magic in her blood, from her mother who walked through a portal 50 years ago from Saxon era England). Now, gorgeous tunic-clad men keep walking through the wall of her classroom. If that isn't enough, she's being haunted by sexy dreams in a rugged land. Curious, she checks out the wall and falls through a portal into the world of her dreams. After years of war, women are scarce. Rowena finds herself in a heap of man-trouble when she 'accidentally' marries distant cousin Ivan. Enter Cedric, who dabbles in black magic and has an even blacker heart. Throw in a Viking, the local wolf-king, a band of brigands and a goth-clad student (eighteen year old Kendra) who follows her through the portal, and Rowena is off on a rollicking adventure. Unwanted husbands keep piling up, but that doesn't stop her from falling for the wrong brother. Not only that, she has Kendra to look out for and a war to prevent. Good thing she has the ability to go back through the wall. Or does she?

BOOK TWO - Rowena and the Dark Lord (2013): Dark magic...dark passions... When Rowena is abducted from Arizona and taken back to medieval Land's End, one thing is clear: she must learn to control her powers of magic. It isn't easy being a modern girl in an archaic land, and when Rowena accidentally conjures up a Roman Legion in mid-battle, Land's End is on the brink of a war that could jeopardize everything and everyone she loves. The stakes are raised when the Dark Lord reappears and traps Rowena in a cyclone of lust and passion. Once again she is torn between the man she loves and the mage who fires her desire.

** received the book for free through Goodreads First Reads **

title: Collection of 7 previously published short stories and 2 new
text: Poignant, tragic short story collection which I read over 9 evenings. The author has command of the English language that I envy. She uses words beautifully to paint a vivid picture. However, the people are like none I have ever met in my adult years so I never became fully engaged in the tragedy, abuse, sorrow, death, disappoints, grief and all the other downer events that occur in the stories. Still, I am very glad I ordered this collection (I had read Sylvia Brownrigg's review in the NY Times back in June) that exposed me to this talented author. * previously published in Granta, Ploughshares, Esquire, Zoetrope: All-Story, The Pushcart Prize, and The Best American Stories. My favorite - "The Lost & Found Department of Greater Boston".

title: #2 in medieval mystery series with Halfdan and his master, Winston the Illuminator
text:
Translated from the Danish author. English historical fiction is probably my favorite genre. I love the rogue Halfdan (I keep picturing him as Errol Flynn when he portrayed Robin Hood). I think it needed another 30 pages or so, for me there wasn't enough showing to make me love it and the mystery wasn't compelling.

A little background from the first book helped ground me so I post it here: The newly crowned King Cnut of Denmark has conquered England and rules his new empire from Oxford. The year is 1018 and the war is finally over, but the unified kingdom is far from peaceful. Halfdan's mixed lineage--half Danish, half Saxon--has made him a pauper in the new kingdom. His father, his brother, and the land he should have inherited were all taken by the new king's men. He lost everything to the war but his sense of humor. Once a proud nobleman, Halfdan now wanders the country aimlessly, powered only by his considerable charm and some petty theft. When he finds an unlikely ally in Winston, a former monk, he sees no reason not to accept his strange invitation to travel together to Oxford. Winston has been commissioned to paint a portrait of the king at the invitation of his new wife, and the protection of a clever man like Halfdan is well worth its price in wine and bread. But when the pair's arrival in court coincides with news of a murder, the king has a brilliant idea: Why not enlist the newly arrived womanizing half-Dane and the Saxon intellectual to defuse a politically explosive situation? The pair represents both sides of the conflict and seem to have crime-solving skills to boot. In their search for the killer, Halfdan and Winston find seduction, adventure, and scandal in the wild early days of Cnut's rule.

title: Police Procedural based in Israel - #2 in a series
text:
In a novel even more gripping than the 2013 debut, 38 year old Tel Aviv police inspector Avraham has a new commander, a mentor who is avoiding him, a relationship with a police woman living in Brussels, and a new case that will prove his worth (after the mess that was in the earlier novel which involved the death of a teen-age boy).

In a story told through alternating POV (Avraham's and his suspects), the new case involves a children's child care nursery, the nursery school teacher, an undetonated bomb outside the nursery, a seller of sandwiches, the threat that the next bomb will explode, a small time criminal, and a father of two children and lastly we come to find out the mother of the two children is MIA.

I was really hoping for more atmosphere of the city of Tel Aviv. I bit of a travelogue would have gone a long way.

title: 11-13 years old
text:
12 year old Jewel never knew her brother, he was 5 years old they day he died. Jewel's parents blame her Jamaican Grandfather for the family tragedy (he had playfully nicknamed his grandson 'Bird' and the consequences led to his death) and grandfather has not spoken a word in her life. It's clear to Jewel that her parents loved their brother more than her and that there has been no love in the home since the day Jewel was born and her brother died. Living in rural Iowa, the daughter of Mexican-Jamaican parents, Jewel feels like an outsider all the time. Luckily she discovers a neighbor boy when climbing in a neighbor's tree, he too is feels an outsider, an African-american adopted by parents who are white.

I can see this being a good book for a class discussion for ages 11 to 13. The unmitigated downer that everyone suffers for 90 percent of the book doesn't make for entertaining reading for a 11-13 year old.

title: Venice, 1576 the city is infected with Bubonic Plague.
text:
The premise gets even better by throwing in so much background with the Ottoman Empire, the writing and feel of place made for a most satisfying read.

Andrea Palladio, tasked by the Doge of Venice to build a cathedral as an offering to God to save the city before the plague claims all in it.

Annibale Cason, the city's finest plague doctor, is tasked with keeping Andrea alive to finish his commission.

Feyra, 21 years old, a doctor (and concubine) in the Sultan of Constantinople's harem escapes to Venice in the ship that carried the plague there. The sultan's mother had revealed to Feyra (just before she died), that Feyra is her daughter, Fayra is the granddaughter of the Venetian Doge, Feyra's mother had been kidnapped by the previous sultan from her husband (Feyra's father) a ship's captain. Fayra's father is the captain of the ship that brings the plague to Venice. While sailing to Venice Feyra survives the plague giving her immunity to further infection. Once n Venice she seeks audience with the Doge and though thwarted and almost killed it leads to her encounter with Palladio and Annibale. Annibale and Feyra share their knowledge and skills to halt the plague from wiping out a city.

title: Ages 12-15
text:
It's 1941 an 15 year old Kalinka has witnessed the murder of her family by the Nazi pogrom, because her family is Jewish.

Max should be thinking of retirement, he has been caretaker of a Ukrainian nature preserve all his life, created by a German baron, almost completely destroyed during World War I (1914-1919) and now the Nazis have invaded. In the preserve are a breed of wild horse that date back tens of thousands of years. Max harbors Kalinka and she bonds with the horses like young Velvet Brown once did with The Pie to win the Grand National. The Nazi commander has ordered Max to slaughter all the horses. This will make the breed extinct and Max needs to decide that he can do. Max sends Kalinks, the 2 rarest horses along wih a Russian wolfhound over the steppes, where they encounter danger and threat of death again and again and again, in hopes of reaching safety.

The 12 year old in the family loved it.

Possible Spoiler -

The preserve is an actual place and the horses exist there today.

title: Ages 10 to 11:  #3 of 4 in a series
text:
A bit too young for my 12 year old (he finished it but thought it a bit immature for him although he did get a kick out of Skip from Verminator Pest Control), but will give to my 9 year old next year.

In book 1 Nick and Tesla's High-Voltage Danger Lab published 11/2013, we met 11 year old siblings with a "knack for science, electronics, and getting into trouble and we see them make everything from rocket launchers and burglar alarms to mobile tracking devices. When their parents mysteriously vanish, they're sent to live with their Uncle Newt, a brilliant inventor. But it's not long before Nick and Tesla are embarking on adventures of their own--and engineering all kinds of outrageous contraptions to save their skin."

In book 2 they are in Half Moon Bay, California with Uncle Newt while their parents are far away on business. Uncle Newt takes a job at a 2nd rate amusement park and Nick and Tesla have an all access pass and also uncover a devious plot. They work with 9-volt burglar alarms, electromagnets, mobile tracking devices to foil the crime and the story has instructions and blueprints for five projects.

Book 3, 11-year-old siblings Nick and Tesla Holt need to expose a spy searching for secrets in the home of their Uncle Newt, a scientist. As in the previous books all sorts of cool tools are used from fingerprint powder to spy cameras and most enjoyable for my kids, instructions are included.

the 4th book will be out in October 2014. Nick and Tesla's Super-Cyborg Gadget Glove: A Mystery with a Blinking, Beeping, Voice-Recording Gadget Glove You Can Build Yourself.

title: Ages 12-13 fantasy/violence stretching back to 1938
text:
13 year old Margaret O'Malley lives in a remote mining town of Victory, Arizona. Her father John O'Malley has been sentenced to death by sadistic Judge Biggs. Father O'Malley was a geologist and exposed the harm by his company, Victory Fuels, when using Fracking to mine natural gas, he was fired and then framed for arson and murder Luckily her family has a huge secret and ability to time travel that they are forbidden to use. With her BFF Charlie, and his 88 year old grandfather Josh (a 2nd generation resident of Victory), she travels back in time to 1938 and the childhood of Judge Biggs to prevent him from growing into the cruel and corrupt adult he is. 1938, a time when Lucas Biggs turns against his pacifist father and evil enters his life. Back in 1938 13 year old Joshua was BFFs with Lucas Biggs who was known as Luke Agrippa. The story is told to us by Margaret and Josh.

Parents should be aware that violence and evil play a strong role in this novel, my 12 year old gobbled it up and we had a terrific dinner conversation about the book when he finished it.

title: A Must read BEFORE the wedding day
text: I highly recommend every parent give a copy to their children once they reach the age to marry. And remember to keep a marriage what it was when you first both fell in love a) you BOTH have to have been in love and b) you BOTH have to want to stay in love. Terrific topics that must not be shied away from like alcohol, sex, and pornography. Chapter end with questions for couples to reflect on together. And remember folks make sure you go on a date night once a week, just the two of you, even if it is a ride around in the car or a bus; anything that gives you the time to connect as a couple as you did when you first fell in love.

title: "Last night I dreamed of Nauquasset again."
text: not a good start for me and my sense of humor - I was ready to turn this re-staging of the Daphne du Maurier classic novel 'Rebecca' into a Calvin & Hobbes comedy. Instead I gave a nod to both authors and plunged ahead. Much to my enjoyment. I thought the choice of setting was unique, we vacation one week a year on Cape Cod the last 8 years and love the area. Then the author lost me making Maxim de Winter gay - WHAT!? Having read the book and watched the movie many times I just could not get it out of my head. I was expecting him to be married to Alena and then marry the curator - not the most romantic move for a gay man. So I put the book down for 6 months and read it fresh this week without compare to du Maurier and enjoyed it very much. Because it truly is more of a nod to Rebecca then a retelling.

title: best for ages 13 to 15: Book #1 in a trilogy
text:
Spiritual epic fantasy with a biblical base. 14 year old Archer Keaton is a dreamtreader who protects the waking world from the Nightmare Lord, he is one of only three selected from each generation. As the story unfolds Archer faces Danger and his life is at risk both in dreams and when awake.

Rigby Thames, the new kid at Dresden High School.

Kara Windchil is Archer's BFF and is fascinated by Rigby's English accent and blond surfer good looks.

I found the book very entertaining (Luficer's Lucid Walkers) but a little too dark for my 12 year old, so will wait a year to give it to him.

title: A New York family spends 2 weeks on the Spanish island of Mallorca.
text:
A breezy summer read, but I would rather have spent my time re-watching the Jimmy Stewart/Maureen O'Hara movie "Mr. Hobbs Takes a Vacation". Superficial rich people being snarky, witty and insightful without the melodrama and with excellent writing that kept me reading.

Franny is the alpha of the family (think Victoria Barkley of the TV show 'The Big Valley').

Jim, (Franny's 60 year old husband) has lost his job after screwing around with a 23 year old office intern (as you can imagine he does not have my heart). Franny says she will decide whether to dump Jim at the end of their vacation celebrating their 35th wedding anniversary.

Bobby is their 28 year old son who is into muscle building in South Beach Miami. He has brought along his trainer, 40 year old Carmen, who likes to wear sequined tops, hmmm.

The youngest is, Sylvia, an unlikable teenager heading off to college who has broken-up with her cheating boyfriend but lands a gorgeous Spanish tutor that helps her get over it.

Franny's BFF, Charles, is also along with his much younger husband Lawrence -- the token gay friends which is all the rage in novels now.

The author's debut novel her first novel, "Laura Lamont's Life in Pictures" was very popular.

Most memorable line page 173 - "The Internet was excellent for confirming one's worst fears about the human race."

title: Catherine Howard (1513 to February 13th 1542)  fifth wife (1540 to 1541) of Henry VIII of England
text: Fascinating historical fiction, the author tells a well written story of the age, painting Howard's life from childhood. She was the 10th child of Lord Edmund Howard (c 1478–1539) himself the 21st child of the Duke of Norfolk; so, while she had a name she had no wealth or position. Sadly, the 17 year old bride of the 49 year old, morbidly obese and impotent King  who named her his "rose without a thorn" had a pretty crummy life that ended when she was killed with a single blow from sword that beheaded her at the authorization of her husband when her adultery was exposed by her own letters to her lover, adultery being a capitol offense as it imperiled the line of succession.

title: #4 in the Ana Grey FBI series
text:
I liked this so much I orderd the rest of the series and already finished North of Montana.
North of Montana (1994),
Good Morning, Killer (2003),
Judas Horse (2008)
White Shotgun (2011)

White Shotgun has a complex plot that takes Agent Grey and her way too moody security expert lover Sterling McCord, to Siena, Italy. It turns out Ana has a half-sister, Cecilia Nicosa, and the Feds want Ana to spy on her shifty husband, Nicoli. Nicoli's mistress is MIA, possibly a victim of something called "lupara blanco" translated to "white shotgun" murder which was a new one to me.
There is also an attempted murder of Cecilia & Nicoli's teenage son. Then Cecilia disappears, Even the police can't be trusted. Rollercoaster!

title: A good place to start
text:
Ignore what isn't right for you, take away fresh ideas, enjoy confirmation of previously held beliefs. A strong point in it's favor is emphasis on asking your child or grandchild or neice/nephew how they feel and use leading questions so you understand truly what they are thinking and feeling. The other strong point in it's favor is the author's stories of children's reactions to dying and death. You can let these stories be a guide to what is normal or what may be cause for concern.

The part about support groups was wasted on me, it wasn't what I was looking for in this book. The author's take on religion I had to disregard also, I think that if the child is in a religious home it can be a huge comfort to them. Chpater 3 was interesting, I have found that most people find it too painful to think or speak of a deceased loved one and I didn't know that wasn't always the case.

title: #2 of 9 Detective Sergeant Jessica Daniel British police procedurals.
text:
The camaraderie and dry wit of the police enhanced the reading for me. I have read the first 2 in the series and am looking forward to reading the rest, The author gets the details right. Only slightly predictable, Detective Sergeant Jessica Daniel is believable. A solid story, it could have been tighter. Police procedurals are my preferred genre.

#1 JESSICA DANIEL: LOCKED IN When a body is found in a locked house, Detective Sergeant Jessica Daniel is left to not only find the killer but discover how they got in and out. With little in the way of leads and a journalist that seems to know more about case than she does, Jessica is already feeling the pressure-and that's before a second body shows up in identical circumstances to the first. How can a murderer get to victims in seemingly impossible situations and what, if anything, links the bodies?

1. Locked In (2011)
2. Vigilante (2011)
3. The Woman In Black (2011)
4. As If By Magic (2012)
5. Think Of The Children (2013)
6. Playing With Fire (2013)
7. Thicker Than Water (2013)
8. Behind Closed Doors (2014)
9. Crossing The Line (2014)

title: Excellent Book Club Choice!
text: 30 years with the Bird family. Don't expect heroes or beloved characters who you want to know in real life. Everyone is a bit bigger than life (or at least life as I know it) - mundane is not a word they know. You've got deception and brutal truths, suicide and joy, hoarding and beauty, adultery and love, adolescent confusion and familial bonds. The story is told from multiple points of view and switches back and forward in time. The back cover premise hooked me and once I started reading the writing compelled me to put the weekend on hold until the last page. New to me author, will look for her other titles.

title: Post Civil War era it was a wretched time
text:
1 year after the close of THE WARRIORS, opening in Spring 1869, takes us to 1878 and a last line I remember reading 40 years ago.

Book 7 in what would become an 8 novel series (The Kent Family Chronicles or the American Bicentennial Series) stretching by the end of book #8 to Christmas in Boston Massachusetts 1890, 5 generations of the Kent family concluding with Philippe's 48 year old great great grandson Gideon and his grown family. I read this as a teenager when it was first published in 1978, it was a tie-in to the excitement generated for the nation's bi-centennial in 1976. I was utterly consumed with the story telling.

The Lawless is centric to the great-great grandsons of Philip Kent, Southerners Jeremiah, Matt & Gideon sons of Jephtha, the only child of Jared who was the son of Abraham.

Amanda Kent's 30 year old son Louis has been murdered, his finances ruined, leaving his ex-wife Julia and son Carter.

26 year old Gideon (on the cover with the eye patch) is married to Margaret (who descends to insanity and alcohol) and is a the newspaper publisher fighting for union rights, with daughter, Eleanor, appalled at how he neglects his family and a young son, Will, hung out to dry by his abandoning them. Gideon reaches out to bring Carter & Julia back into the family, with unforeseen consequences. The whole story line is rather wretched and compelling you just wish you could stage an intervention.

25 year old Matthew Kent, the carefree bon vivant of the previous books, is now a tortured artist in Paris with his wife and son, Luke.

23 year old Jeremiah, thought dead by his family, has recently renounced killing after gunning down 9 people continues hunting buffalo with his Indian brother Kola.

In NYC Jephtha has married Molly.

Michael Boyle, Amanda Kent's right hand man, her son Louis' guardian after her murder, lives a hard scrabble life building the railroad then disappears from the novel after getting Jeremiah's share of Jephtha's 18 million dollar estate ($321 million adjusted for inflation).

Everything else was fabulous and epic and wonderful. I would say more about why but I try to keep the suspense going for the reader by not putting in spoilers.

The mixing of historic events and people with Kent family's day to day life is terrific and fun and very believable.

title: What a mess!
text:
Taking the reader 8 years after the close of THE FURIES, opening in 1860 with the country on the verge of Civil War and takes us to the first battle of Bull Run aka Manassas in July 1861.

Book 5 in what would become an 8 novel series (The Kent Family Chronicles or the American Bicentennial Series) stretching by the end of book #8 to Christmas in Boston Massachusetts 1890, 5 generations of the Kent family concluding with Philippe's 48 year old great great grandson Gideon and his grown family. I read this as a teenager when it was first published in 1976, it was a tie-in to the excitement generated for the nation's bi-centennial in 1976. I was utterly consumed with the story telling.

The Titans is centric to the great grandson of Philip Kent, Jephtha, the only child of Jared who was the son of Abraham. Jephtha's life is a complete mess and his sanity is hanging on by a thread. 10 years earlier he stopped ministering to his parishioners in Virginia when they did not support abolition of slavery. He deliberately alienated his wife and consequently his 3 young children when he enabled the escape from slavery of a woman belonging to his father in law. Even though he is a rich man from investments made by his father's cousin Amanda Kent and revenue from his father's gold mine he lives like a pauper. He doesn't share the wealth on his children but holds it over his wife's head that when he dies they will get it. Just give it to them now I want to shout. The story proceeds from there. It got to a point where Jephtha behaves horrendously blaming her for evil that befell him and this action incites his children to come to her defense so strongly that later actions by the children didn't add up for me. Jephtha is a bit too human, he is personally insulted that his ex-wife has remarried to a lowly actor. Still, everything else was fabulous and epic and wonderful. I would say more about why but I try to keep the suspense going for the reader by not putting in spoilers.

The mixing of historic events and people with Kent family's day to day life is terrific and fun and very believable for example Jephtha is a reporter for the Kent newspaper and is based in Washington so he has access and interviews President Lincoln and another time travels to Arlington home of Robert E. Lee for an interview. Very exciting stuff.

The prologue tells us that Louis, Amanda's teenage rapist son is now 24, married and has not responsibility for his actions resulting in the death of his mother 8 years earlier - this was pretty much a sure thing but still very sad considering what an honorable man his father was and what a delightful youth he was only 10 years ago.

title: Heartbreaker of a story set in a small coastal village in Haiti
text:
a motherless little girl, Claire, the daughter of a fisherman, is MIA on her 7th birthday, the same evening her father decides it's best for her to be fostered with a another family so Claire can have a brighter future. Her father and neighbors look for her revealing to the reader a modern day Payton Place of secrets and remembrances of brutality, and love, hope, despair and corruption.

Set before the earthquake of 2010 and told through interlocking stories of the townspeople, The 46 year old author was born and raised to age 9 in Haiti and has since lived in NYC and Miami. She has been fabulously lauded with the most prestigious awards in the arts community,

title: I love historical fiction and Blaze of Glory the Battle of Shiloh has enough information for a textbook.
text:
The Commander of the Confederate forces General Albert Sidney Johnston was the most real and interesting POV character, with US Army General under US Grant Don Carlos Buell a fascinating character as well. Sherman and Grant didn't come alive for me, but maybe that was the author's intent or perhaps I was spoiled by reading Grant's fantastic memoirs. I know I got spoiled by Ken Burn's Civil War series (which I have on dvd) and the two foot soldiers didn't do it for me (as the voices of the not so famous in the Burns series have become ingrained in my memory).

** received the book for free through Goodreads First Reads **

title: Book #2: Young Adult paranormal (dragons) set in England 1915
text:
I enjoyed this book much more than the first in the series.

16 year-old orphan Lora Jones (a drákon, a rare, enchanted being with astonishing magical abilities), is distraught from the events in book one, her first year as a charity student at the posh boarding school on England's southern coast finishes for the term.

Armand Louis (also in book one) whose father owns the boarding school asks Lora to summer with him at their estate now functioning as a military hospital for the duration of The Great War, aka The War to End All Wars ie World War One. Granted not the summer vacation of your dreams. Armand's brother Aubrey is a pilot shot down and now in a German prisoner of war camp. The adventure takes off when Lora & Aubrey hatch a plan to head behind enemy lines and rescue him.

If you have not read book one here is a synopsis that might help bring you up to speed:

BOOK #1 THE SWEETEST DARK: For fans of Lauren Kate and Libba Bray, The Sweetest Dark is filled with thrilling romance, exciting adventure, and ancient magic. Shana Abé brilliantly captures the drama of post-Victorian England, while unfolding a passionate love story that defies time. "With every fiber of my being, I yearned to be normal. To glide through my days at Iverson without incident. But I'd have to face the fact that my life was about to unfold in a very, very different way than I'd ever envisioned. Normal would become forever out of reach." Lora Jones has always known that she's different. On the outside, she appears to be an ordinary sixteen-year-old girl. Yet Lora's been keeping a heartful of secrets: She hears songs that no one else can hear, dreams vividly of smoke and flight, and lives with a mysterious voice inside her that insists she's far more than what she seems. England, 1915. Raised in an orphanage in a rough corner of London, Lora quickly learns to hide her unique abilities and avoid attention. Then, much to her surprise, she is selected as the new charity student at Iverson, an elite boarding school on England's southern coast. Iverson's eerie, gothic castle is like nothing Lora has ever seen. And the two boys she meets there will open her eyes and forever change her destiny. Jesse is the school's groundskeeper--a beautiful boy who recognizes Lora for who and what she truly is. Armand is a darkly handsome and arrogant aristocrat who harbors a few closely guarded secrets of his own. Both hold the answers to her past. One is the key to her future. And both will aim to win her heart. As danger descends upon Iverson, Lora must harness the powers she's only just begun to understand, or else lose everything she dearly loves. Filled with lush atmosphere, thrilling romance, and ancient magic, The Sweetest Dark brilliantly captures a rich historical era while unfolding an enchanting love story that defies time.

title: #22 in the Venice Italy based mystery series featuring Commissario Guido Brunetti, his work and his family
text:
I enjoyed it, probably because I am a diehard fan of the series going on 22 years. I think the author is a terrific writer but this one novel is not my favorite. I didn't feel the excitement of the mystery, the delight in the place or the love of family and food. I think if you are looking to try the series I would recommend my favorites "Death at La Fenice" or "The Anonymous Venetian (1994) aka Dressed for Death" or "Willful Behaviour" first.

This time out the mayor’s future daughter-in-law is under investigation for a negligible error and Brunetti has no interest stepping in that sticky wicket. At the same time Brunetti's wife asks him to look into the suicide of the mentally handicapped man who worked at their dry cleaner, that case gets real bizarre when he finds the dead man never existed on paper.

title: Ages 10 to 12
text:
Halloween fun goes bad leading to portals to other worlds and haunted houses - what's not to like? Throw in a mystery and let the adventure begin! 11 year old Cole follows his friends through the haunted House portal to 'The Outskirts' the 5 kingdoms.

From the author's web web page:

COLE: cares a lot about his friends and will do anything to rescue them. He is great at comebacks and not afraid of heights, both attributes help him survive in the Five Kingdoms. For better or worse, Cole is incredibly brave and often gets himself into dangerous situations in order to do the right thing. Hometown: The prosperous world, or Earth. More specifically, he is from Boise, Idaho and moved to Mesa, Arizona in the fourth grade. Appearance: Cole follows his friends into the Outskirts the night of Halloween so he’s dressed as a scarecrow with an arrow through his chest or, as Cole says, a scarecrow that had been used for archery practice. Fun Fact: In Skyport, Cole is allowed a special item to help him survive scouting the floating castles before they’re raided. At Mira’s suggestion, Cole chooses a jumping sword. As I’m sure you’ve guessed, the jumping sword lets him jump much greater distances than he normally could.

DALTON: is Cole’s best friend since the fourth grade. Dalton is dressed as a sad clown so he wears a trench coat and fedora and his easy smile is covered by an exaggerated makeup frown. Fun Fact: In the Outskirts, the slavers believe Jenna and Dalton have shaping abilities and are taken to the High King, where shaping slaves are very valuable.

JENNA: Cole had a crush on her last year, they are in the same 6th grade class together and have become good friends. Jenna is dressed as Cleopatra and a straight black wig with bangs covers up her dark, curly hair.

MIRA: the first friend Cole makes in the Outskirts, her many secrets,will be a big part of Cole’s quest to find his friends. hometown: Junction City, capitol of the Five Kingdoms. Mira is about Cole’s height and wears boots, corduroy pants, a collared shirt and suspenders printed with shamrocks. She has short hair, gray eyes, and is coated by a thin layer of dirt, like everyone in Skyport.
Mira started out as a scout but she showed shaping abilities and started training with Durny, the top shaper in Skyport. Shaping is a lot like magic. Depending on ability, Shapers can create semblances that act like humans or animals and they can create special objects, like Cole’s jumping sword.

JACE: unofficial senior scout when Cole arrives. Jace’s abundance of self-confidence and bossiness is often at odds with Cole’s more laid back personality. The two boys will become friends, however, when they are united by the same goal. Hometown: Skyport, the city on the very edge of the Outskirts. Jace is a little taller than Cole and has a bronze complexion and dark hair. Jace found the Golden Rope on one of his scouting missions. The Golden Rope is the only one in Skyport and is very valuable. Though it starts out the size of a small string, it can expand to any length and hold any weight without breaking.

TWITCH: a scout like Jace, he likes to keep his head down and stay out of trouble. Like Mira, Twitch has some secrets he keeps from the inhabitants of Skyport. For one thing, he won’t reveal what his special item for scouting is to anyone. Hometown: Elloweer. Short and skinny. Though he’s Cole age, he looks much younger. His real name is Reuben but he got the nickname because he’s jumpy and flinches a lot.

421 pages in length is is not a light read for the younger readers.

Rogue Knight Book 2: Coming October 2014

title: Texas in the 1870s
text:
A character driven novel. Superb book club choice. The novel starts out rich in historical detail and stays the course. There is one reveal after another. Prostitute, Lucinda Carter, escapes from a Ft Worth bordello and travels to a remote area named Middle Bayou. Middle Bayou took almost 16 hours to get to via riverboat from Houston to Morgan's Point at the entrance to Galveston Bay followed by a horse drawn wagon east, where she has amazingly arranged a teaching position and waits for her lover to arrive.

New lawman, Nate Cannon from Oklahoma is sent to find Texas Rangers, Capt. George Deerling and Dr. Tom Goddard. They have been tracking outlaw William McGill who has killed again.

All are heading in the same direction and the last 3 chapters are killer. I got to the last page and the next day re-read for sheer enjoyment of the what if's and wondering where will the characters be in 10 years. I know I will be thinking of Lucinda for years to come.

title: Ages 10 to 12
text:
Out of control Pranksters and 12 year old twins, Edgar and Allan Poe, are descendants of the famous poet, mystery and horror writer Edgar Allan Poe. In the first book of "The Misadventures of Edgar/Allan" series 'Tell Tale Start' the boys black cat, Roderick Usher, is catnapped. The boys track down the catnapper, evil Professor Perry, to his Kansas OZ-itorium Theme Park. I found the duo to be a bit obnoxious, and lacking empathy for just about everyone, their "joking" is mean spirited, their aunt & uncle guardians are clueless and the teachers are inept. This 2nd book is much more of the same. Buyer beware, there is a lot to laugh at and some behavior I don't encourage.

This time out they are joined in New Orleans by co-stars, Em and Milly Dickinson, in a movie on their ancestor. Lots of humor, mystery, adventure, history, paranormal and literary puns. Plus perfect illustrations by Sam Zuppardi.

title: Trust no one!
text:
On a hot June day the body of a brutally murdered girl washes ashore outside of Frankfurt Germany. Forensics show she was abused sexually and physically for years. She remains a Jane Doe.

Weeks later

A TV reporter, Hanna Herzmann working on an expose of child pornography and a child welfare organization, is raped and locked in the trunk of her car. Inspectors Pia Kirchhoff and Oliver von Bodenstein link the two cases, so much evil is revealed I found myself shuddering. Expertly written. Kept me reading compulsively until the very last page.

The series in order as written and published in Germany:

An Unpopular Woman - published 2006
Murder Friends -- published 2007
Deep Wounds -- published 2009
Snow White Must Die -- published 2010
Who Sow the Wind -- published 2011
Bad Wolf -- published 2012

If you liked this book you might want to try the first book to be published in English featuring these two detectives:

SNOW WHITE MUST DIE - In a small town in Germany a boy is accused of murdering his beautiful girlfriend. But this is no fairy story . . . On a September evening eleven years ago, two 17-year-old girls vanished without a trace from the tiny village of Altenhain, just outside Frankfurt. In a trial based on circumstantial evidence 20-year-old Tobias Sartorius was convicted and imprisoned for the murder of his childhood friend Laura and his beautiful girlfriend Stefanie - otherwise known as Snow White. After serving his sentence, Tobias returns home. His presence in the little German village stirs up the events of the past. Events that the locals would prefer to remain hidden. When the Sartorius family is subjected to a number of attacks, Detective Inspector Pia Kirchhoff and DS Oliver von Bodenstein are tasked with monitoring the tense atmosphere in the tight-knit community. As the village inhabitants close ranks it becomes apparent the disappearance of Snow White and her friend was far more complex than imagined. Then history starts to repeat itself in a disastrous manner when another pretty girl goes missing. The police are thrown into a race against time. Can they solve the mystery before it's too late?

title: Engrossing story of 3 men and 2 women who arrive in Shanghai from Malaysia,
text:
Ranging the gamut of society from factory worker to old money. Favorite line from one of the main characters "takeovers, selling short, asset stripping are these not rich people’s terms for bullying, gambling, and cheating?” Like reading a novel written 50 years ago about making it in New York City. The chapter headings that read like fortune cookie scripts were amusing. One of the unique aspects of this novel is the duel perspective of the same moment in time, sometimes told chapters apart. This is a novel to read at your leisure slowly over a long weekend vacation to truly appreciate the story telling.

>Justin, a stressed out property developer adopted by a wealthy family,buckling under the immense pressure to succeed.
>Yinghui, a successful businesswoman.
>Walter, billionaire author of the bestselling self-help manual Five Star Billionaire.
>Phoebe, a factory worker who finds herself without a job she believed she would have on arrival in Shanghai.
>Gary, a golden boy pop singer whose bad boy behavior off stag goes viral.

title: Ages 13 to 17
text:
What if Merlin was a new Christian? Epic World Building! Book #2 in a series (Merlin's Blade is book #1), and book #3 "Merlin's Nightmare" is now out from Christian publisher Zondervan.

From book #1 - Merlin's Blade When a meteorite crashes near a small village in fifth-century Britain, it brings with it a mysterious black stone that bewitches anyone who comes in contact with its glow---a power the druids hope to use to destroy King Uthur's kingdom. The only person who seems immune is a young, shy, half-blind swordsmith's son named Merlin. As his family, village, and even the young Arthur, are placed in danger, Merlin must face his fears and his blindness to take hold of the role ordained for him. But when he is surrounded by adversaries, how will he save the girl he cherishes and rid Britain of this deadly evil ... without losing his life? Book includes location map and detailed character index. From School Library Journal: In fifth-century Britain, during King Uther's reign, the druids attempt to rise once again and overpower their Christian monarch. A strange and deadly meteorite, able to bewitch anyone who gazes upon it, becomes central to the druid leader's plots. Only the mostly blind swordsmith's son, Merlin, is able to gaze upon the stone and hold off its dangerous powers. Only he can see with a clear head the deception and plotting surrounding the High King's visit to his small village. It is through Merlin's actions that perhaps Uther's family, including the young future King Arthur, can survive the pagan usurpers' designs on the crown. Treskillard crafts a new and unique prequel to the King Arthur legend, one that is rich in atmosphere and detail. Fantasy readers will find themselves beguiled by the young Merlin's story. The blending of history and religious mythologies makes this the start of an interesting perspective on Arthurian legends.

Now go and learn about the Merlin everyone else knows about. Watch the TV movie 'Merlin' staring Sam Neill before you are 15, read the Mary Stewart Trilogy (The Crystal Cave (1970), The Hollow Hills (1973),The Last Enchantment (1979)) before you turn 18; then read Avalon by Marion Zimmer Bradley while you are in college; and watch the movie Excalibur (warning rated R) to see a truly epic telling of Merlin.

title: Difficult to love something so dark
text:
Beautiful, elegant writing. Brutal and Gritty stories. Very dark and very moving. Murder and marriage, parenthood and death, marriage and alienation.Two of the stories deal with animal abuse so if that is something you can't read make sure to skip over the two stories: “Wanle,” where a young woman wants to follow in her father’s footsteps as a legendary cockfighter; and
"Road to Hana", where a Hawaiian native goes home and a long abandoned dog is seen on the way.

“The Old Paniolo Way” family members transition on several levels

"This is Paradise" the women of Waikiki tell of a young woman tourist and the dark side of nightlife the island offers.

"Portrait of a Good Father" was probably the one that almost brought me to tears.

"Thirty-Nine Rules for Making a Hawaiian Funeral into a Drinking Game", Very dark humor - I think anyone who has gone to a number of Irish wakes will find this a familiar story.

"I love you like a wave loves sand."
"Hungrily?"
"Powerfully."

title: Ages  8 to 11 - book 6 in the series
text:
Very Original - the book is told using letters, drawings, newspaper articles, and TV scripts. 11 year old Seymour Hope, Ignatius B. Grumply (old grump writer) and Olive C. Spence (a writer & a ghost) live in Spence Mansion in the town of Ghastly, Illinois. Each book has a moral to exemplify. The story was a pure delight and laugh out loud funny to read to my nieces & nephew ages 4, 6 & 8; my 9 year old neice got to read it to them again the next night.

This time out the new characters include:
Robb Z. Lott and his wife Liza Lott, small time hoodlums
Ben Bizzy and Mia Bizzy, security business owners
Paige Turner, the book publisher
T. Leeves, the butler
Nadia S. Richenov, Iggy’s long lost ex-fiancé looking for
Art Smart, an art historian

In case you are new to the series here is a brief summary provided by the publisher of the previous books:

#5 Hollywood, Dead Ahead In this fifth volume from 43 Old Cemetery Road, the trio at Spence Mansion leaves Ghastly for Hollywood, California . . . and for a shot at stardom! The film producer Moe Block Busters wants to make the 43 Old Cemetery Road story into a movie—and he promises it will be a sure-fire hit! Lured by the lights of Tinseltown, Ignatius B. Grumply, Olive C. Spence, and Seymour Hope pack their suitcases. But when they arrive in Hollywood, Olive has a sure-fire fit when she discovers how quickly fame changes Iggy and Seymour. Even worse, Olive has been written out of the script! “Little old lady ghosts are so yesterday,” says Moe. “What America wants is a terrifying ghost named Evilo.” Well, if it’s Evilo they want, it’s Evilo they’ll get. And Olive knows just the femme fatale to help her scare Hollywood’s most despicable director half to death.

#4 - THE PHANTOM OF THE POST OFFICE: The letter-loving trio at Spence Mansion has something to grieve about--Ghastly's post office is about to close, which will cut off their connection to their fans. A new invention called VEXT-mail is threatening to replace not only letters, but books, hair dryers, and even garage door openers! Could the mysterious occupant of P.O. Box 5 and his seemingly sinister plan save the doomed post office? Will he strike down Ghastly's beloved ghostwriter in the process?

#3 - TIL DEATH US DO BARK: When a dog arrives at Spence Mansion, Seymour is overjoyed. His adoptive parents, Ignatius B. Grumply and Olive C. Spence, are less enthusiastic--especially when Secret, the dog, begins barking all night long. Is it possible Secret just misses his old companion, the late Noah Breth, whose children are fighting like cats and dogs over their father's money? Or does Secret have a secret that, in the end, will make the entire town of Ghastly howl with delight? A runaway mystery told in letters, limericks, a last will, and loose change, is guaranteed to please anyone who's ever tried to keep a secret.

#2 - OVER MY DEAD BODY - The International Movement for the Safety & Protection Of Our Kids & Youth (IMSPOOKY) dictates that Seymour cannot live in the mansion at 43 Old Cemetery Road "without the benefit of parents." Ignatius B. Grumply tries to explain to Dick Tater, the head of IMSPOOKY, that he and Seymour are in a lovely living (and publishing!) arrangement with the ghost of Olive C. Spence. Dick Tater is not convinced. But this clever trio can't be broken up as easily as he imagines. Another spooky tale told in letters, drawings, newspaper articles, and television scripts.

#1 - April 2009 | Sisters Kate and M. Sarah Klise launched their lively 43 Old Cemetery Road series with, the story of the churlish, child-hating sixty-year-old children's book author Ignatius B. Grumply, who rents an old Victorian mansion in Ghastly, Illinois, for the summer . . . only to find it already inhabited. Enter eleven-year-old Seymour Hope and the vivacious, "old as dirt" writer-ghost Olive C. Spence. The ensuing tale of unlikely roommates is cleverly, seamlessly told in letters, newspaper articles, Grumply's work-in-progress "Ghost Tamer" manuscript, and winning illustrations by M. Sarah Klise. Alternately poignant and side-splittingly funny--and full of writing and publishing jokes--this charming title was nominated for nine state book awards and named a Junior Library Guild selection.

title: Nick and Kate Kavanaugh amazingly still living in Niceville
text:
Just Wow! Creepy spooky seat-of-your-pants paranormal speculative fiction mystery thriller. My advice would be just go with it and enjoy.

FROM THE AUTHOR'S PAGE: In the town of NICEVILLE people like to say that 'things go into Crater Sink, but nothing ever comes back out". This is not exactly true. Nick Kavanaugh, an ex-Special Forces soldier and now a cop, and his wife Kate, a family practice lawyer, will be taken to the limits of sanity by what will come out of Crater Sink, and what is required to make it go back. In THE HOMECOMING, Rainey Teague, orphaned by the events of Book One, comes to live with Kate Kavanaugh, over the strong objections of her husband Nick, who can't shake the feeling that something's "just not right" with that kid. As it turns out, Nick's instincts about Rainey Teague are right on the money, as Rainey willingly attaches himself to the malevolent presence that lives in Crater Sink. When Rainey comes down from that mountain-top meeting, he doesn't come home alone, and what now lives inside him has plans for the town of Niceville and all of its people that reach a shattering crescendo of conflict and supernatural horror in the final pages of The HOMECOMING. Niceville …... a city of around ten-thousand people, a Forties-style Deep South town with live oaks in the shady squares, Spanish-moss hanging from the branches, blue-and-gold street cars rumbling over the pavements, the down-town streets stitched together by overhead power lines and trolley wires, graveyards for the Confederate Dead and those misguided Union boys ... a misty and humid place with the scent of the distant sea a salt tang in the air, a soft golden light lying over it all, a river called The Tulip snaking through it, and everywhere the smell of ferns and flowers growing in fresh-turned gardens, exactly like the scent of a new-cut grave ...... and a small stand of original New World forest on top of the looming bluffs on the north-eastern edge of the town. In the middle of this stand of Old Forest is Crater Sink, a limestone pit ringed by stone cliffs coated in black moss and defining a nearly-perfect circle of cold black water a hundred feet across and a thousand feet deep. Niceville folk liked to say that things went in to Crater Sink but nothing ever came out of it.This was not entirely true.

Book 1 - Something is wrong in Niceville. A boy literally disappears from Main Street. A security camera captures the moment of his instant, inexplicable vanishing. An audacious bank robbery goes seriously wrong: four cops are gunned down; a TV news helicopter is shot and spins crazily out of the sky, triggering a disastrous cascade of events that ricochet across twenty different lives over the course of just thirty-six hours. Nick Kavanaugh, a cop with a dark side, investigates. Soon he and his wife, Kate, a distinguished lawyer from an old Niceville family, find themselves struggling to make sense not only of the disappearance and the robbery but also of a shadow world, where time has a different rhythm and where justice is elusive.. . .Something is wrong in Niceville, where evil lives far longer than men do. Compulsively readable, and populated with characters who leap off the page, Niceville will draw you in, excite you, amaze you, horrify you, and, when it finally lets you go, make you sorry you have to leave.
Read the first thirty-five pages. Find out why Harlan Coben calls Carsten Stroud the master of “the nerve-jangling thrill ride.”

my review of book one 1 - Writing that sucks you in! Back in the 1800's four families founded Niceville in the Southern United States and it's now 15,000 resident town. Nothing Nice happens in Niceville. Crater Sink, feared by the residents, is located on the cliff looming over the town. Years ago a young girl, pregnant, is sent to an insane asylum, does it have anything to do with all the kidnappings through the years? The cast of characters (I put together while reading)

title: If you like your crime fighters to be almost super human you will like our guy Joe.
text:
#6 Joe Hunter novel written by British ex-police officer, Hunter goes up against his nemesis from the first book 'Dead Men's Dust', ex-CIA agent Tubal Cain. Cain has kidnapped Joe’s best friend, Jared ‘Rink’ Rington and in the rusty hulk of a Russian container ship used by human traffickers moored off the North Carolina coast (where Joe's ex-sister-in-law is being held hostage) they will face off during an epic storm.

Joe Hunter books:

1 'DEAD MEN'S DUST' - Some may call me a vigilante. I think I've just got problems to fix. Right now, Hunter's big problem is a missing little brother, last seen fleeing the site of a gruesome killing. Hunter needs the help of an old army buddy, a whole lot of hardware and a trip to Little Rock, Arkansas, to fix this particular problem. A brutal encounter with some very nasty criminals leaves Hunter fighting for his life. And that's before he comes up against America's most feared serial killer, 'The Harvestman' and his grisly souvenirs of death.

book 2 'JUDGEMENT AND WRATH' - Joe Hunter doesn't like bullies. So his latest job - saving a young woman from her bully boyfriend - is a no-brainer. As it turns out, the vengeful father isn't the only one who wants the boyfriend dead. Soon Hunter is face-to-face with a contract killer who takes his work very seriously. Contract killer Dantalion has a talent for killing and keeps a list of his victims in a book chained to his waist. Each victim is numbered. And the body count is about to start rising.

book 3 'SLASH AND BURN' - Joe Hunter is enjoying some much needed r & r when a young woman approaches him to help find her missing sister. Kate Piers knows about Joe from her dead brother Jake, Hunter's former comrade in arms, and for that reason alone he feels obliged to help. The fact that Kate is very attractive doesn't hurt. Together they go to Imogen's Kentucky home where they are immediately attacked by a bunch of thugs, acting on behalf of local businessman Robert Huffman. Huffman is outwardly respectable but the psychotic twins he uses as his enforcers give the game away: he has links to organised crime and a deadly reputation with a blade. Huffman is also looking for Imogen, and kidnaps Kate to act as bait.

book 4 'CUT AND RUN' - Joe Hunter vs Luke Rickard, a killer who has stolen his identity and committed a vicious double murder.
His motive? Revenge. His method? A blade. His mission? Kill anyone Hunter holds dear. It is a deadly duel of wits that takes Hunter from the streets of Miami to the squalid barrios of Colombia to the jungle hideaway of a drug baron. And brings him face to face with his past. Revenge is a dish best served cold and Joe needs a cool head if Rickard is not to cut and run.

book 5 'BLOOD AND ASHES' - Brook Reynolds died in a car crash. Tragic accident, the police say. But her father Don Griffiths knows otherwise. And he wants Joe Hunter to find the men responsible. Joe is not convinced - until he is attacked by two troublemakers, and Don's other daughter is also threatened. Looks like more than coincidence. And sure enough, the entire family is soon under siege with only Joe to protect them. The ensuing blood bath is the beginning of a trail of death that leads right to the heart of a racist conspiracy.White supremacists want to hold the government to ransom; and they have got hold of a dirty bomb to add weight to their case. Joe is on countdown: can he stop the plotters before they reduce the free world to ashes?

book 6 'DEAD MEN'S HARVEST
book 7 'No Going Back'
book 8 'Rules of Honour'

title: 1996: a two-week Zen meditation retreat,  at Auschwitz
text:
for “homage, prayer, and silent meditation in the memory of this camp’s million and more victims.” I can't even imagine contemplating such a trip so I jumped on the chance to explore the lives of people who would. 140 attendees: rabbis; nuns; monks: biologists; Palestinians; elderly survivors; young Germans; Poles; Americans; scholars; witnesses, etc. gathering meditate on themes of evil and humanity. fyi - The author became a Zen Buddhist in the 1960's and later a Zen priest.

The story evolves around D. Clements Olin, a Massachusetts literature professor in his 50s gathering research for a work he is writing on the life and work of Tadeusz Borowski. For me, learning about Tadeusz_Borowski was a reward in itself. We also find out Olin was born in Poland to a Jewish mother (who may have ended in life in Auschwitz), taken to America as an infant and baptized a christian.

The 33rd book by the author, winner of the National Book Award for fiction "Shadow Country" and the 1978 book "The Snow Leopard, a spiritual account of the Himalayas, died aged 86 the date this book published. Along with George Plimpton, William Styron and Harold L. Humes founded The Paris Review in 1956, and would later disclose he was a CIA agent as well.

title: Ages 15 and up
text:
A solid debut effort that could use stronger characterization. I got this for my 12 year old but once I read it (and enjoyed it) I thought it more age appropriate for an older child.

1918, World War One (the war to end all wars) is over. The Spanish influenza pandemic hits. The first pandemic involving H1N1 influenza virus. It infected 500 million people across the world, including remote Pacific islands and the Arctic. In 1910 Europe and North American populations were 960 million, 15 million were killed in the war. 50 million were killed by the flu. Imagine in 5 years one in 12 people you know are dead.

17 year old Cleo of Portland, Oregon in the Pacific NorthWest tells her story (her brother is her guardian, their parents long dead) of volunteers for the Red Cross going door-to-door distributing informational pamphlets, masks, in search of the sick.

title: Fascinating look at Richard the Lionheart's final years
text:
I was vastly entertained by the author's perspective which held my interest for almost 700 pages. Except for his brief appearance in the 1939 Errol Flynn movie 'The Adventures of Robin Hood', Richard has never captured my interest, he seems to have been a crummy son, a crummy husband and a horrible king of England. Not only did he suck the wealth of the country dry, he didn't spend much time there (granted the other countries he ruled were gorgeous) and finally he didn't produce heirs to the throne.

I have to admit the cover art captured my attention for A Kings Ransom. I then researched the author, and after enjoying this novel I have gone back and ordered the previous novels in the Plantagenet series: When Christ and His Saints Slept, 1995; Time and Chance, 2002; Devil's Brood, 2008; Lionheart, 2011;

My enjoyment of English history extends 40 years to childhood and my mother's books non-fiction by Thomas B. Costain, The Plantagenet series aka The Pageant of England: The Conquerors (1949); The Magnificent Century (1951); The Three Edwards (1958); The Last Plantagenets (1962). Roberta Gellis fulfilled the romantic and the historical with her medieval novels: Knight's Honor; Bond of Blood; The Dragon and the Rose; The Sword and the Swan; Roselynde; Alinor. I have re-read them all many times.

title: Loved the cover - it caught my eye and compelled me to order the book
text: Our family spends every October on Cape Ann Massachusetts, so the New England setting truly spoke to me - well done Ms. Neggers.  Samantha Bennett, former resident of Knights Bridge, Massachusetts is staying in a cider mill long empty and in disrepair.  Justin Sloan is hunky firefighter, 2 Years ago Justin got her fired.  Samantha is looking to solve a 300-year-old mystery. He doesn't trust her. Justin came off as kind of a pill which is why I couldn't rate it higher.

title: Written by a retired navy commander whose final assignment was at the Pentagon in Naval Operations
text:
A submarine with 192 nuclear warheads on a three-month tour receives orders to travel to a location that will allow them to strike at Iran. They have been told it is retaliatory for a strike on Washington DC.

The president and the navy send rescind orders because the attack orders were were not from the Pentagon, they were sent by a rogue element of the Israeli Mossad who believes they must make a preemptive strike against Iran and this is the only way they can make it happen. Mossad agents on board the sub prevent any messages getting through.

U.S. national security adviser Christine O'Connor has 8 days to prevent the nuclear launch. All the book lacks is a Jack Ryan, Marko Ramius, Bart Mancuso, Vasili Borodin, and Jeffrey Pelt to make this a 5 star read.

title: Ages 10 to 11
text:
If you liked Joe Schreiber's "Lenny Cyrus School Virus" you and your tiny tot will enjoy it the same. Lots of juvenile humor. Perfectly illustrated throughout with black and white LOL drawings that exceptionally enhance the story.

Pete (who is somewhere between ages 10 and 13) is all set to sneak over to the game store and purchase newly released Brawl-a-Thon 3000 "XL". Sneak, because his parents will give him a hard time about spending more of HIS money on video games and they are away for the day (Saturday) at a softball game.

Trouble begins when he finds his mom has pilfered $20 from his spending money jar. He needs $50 for the game and he only has $30. The kid comes up with a great idea to hold an impromptu garage sale to raise the $20. He gets a bunch of stuff collecting dust in the basement. Smart kid. It starts to rapidly go down hill with Abbott & Costello, Bing Crosby & Bob Hope, Scooby-Doo humor. An exterminator passing the house buys an ancient gaming system his father hasn't touched in 20+ years. Then at the video store his own father is kidnapped right in front of him.

Their neighbor Mrs. Wertley tells him that Pete's dad is a CIA data analyst!
The gamimg system is his dad's cleverly disguised work computer!
Pete's mother doesn't believe any of this and (LOLOL for me) sends him off to a birthday party!
Turns out, the dad of Pete's BFF Wesley has the same gaming system!
They also get kidnapped!
By the guy who bought the system at the garage sale!
The kidnapper is going to use "Brawl-a-Thon SuperMax" and infect all of the computers in the world!
And for those readers of loved TRON, Pete's dad is "digitized" and is a character in the game!
Pete also gets digitized to save the world!!! and his dad.

My 12 year old boy thought it a bit juvenile but he finished it, my 9 year old thought it silly but also finished it.

title: From British writer/translator who has lived in Barcelona for over 20 years & is a superphotographer
text:
My only issues: Local knowlege tid bits were on the lite side; "hand-picked hotels and restaurants" was not as extensive as I wanted or expected from National G; and maps are too small to provide depth and breadth. I am going to print a few from on line graphics to take with me.

A friend who spent a semester in Barcelona 10 years ago said it was a start and her young son brought it to his Spanish class for show and tell.

title: Ages 10 to 12
text: Set in my home state of New Jersey, 'Behind the Plate' is a baseball umpire training school where 12 year old Casey lives with his dad (who manages the school), grandfather, and BFF Zeke. Casey's mom hated the place and left with another man. By the books end Casey and the reader learn that the qualities and rules that make a good umpire also make a great human and maybe lead to a reconciliation with his mom. My 12 year old finished it but said it wasn't a Home Run, however there weren't any infield errors to spoil the story.

title: I feel like I just had a weekend guest who knew almost everyone in Paris in the 80's & 90's.
text:
Memories of the golden child - a preeminent Gay American author's captivating 16 years in Paris. Telling me stories, from the absolutely mind-boggling grotesque; page 63 actor Dieter Schidor and writer Gary Indiana's (as told by Gary if it can be believed) depraved drug fueled actions at Dauchau) to entertaining; enchanting vignettes of gossip, reflection, naughtiness (observed and lived - sex - lots of it - lots and lots of sex), giving me an experience as vivacious as the movie The Birdcage (La Cage aux Folles). He had something to say on rainbow spectrum: snarky (the English) outrageous (Julian Barnes), provocative (Robert Maplethorpe), funny (the French); while his relationship with literary critic Marie-Claude de Brunhoff, embodies what it is about the French that White loves.

The author is a compellingly writer, literary biographer, essayist, teacher at Princeton University, and has received many honors in addition to literary awards presented in his name. Most notably for me he has two memoirs, 'My Lives' and 'City Boy'; non-fiction 'The Flâneur A Stroll Through the Paradoxes of Paris' (2001); and the autobiographical novel 'A Boy’s Own Story' (1982); Our Paris: Sketches from Memory, illustrated by his lover.

title: For ages 12 to 14. The story is set from 1906 to 1914.
text:
Elegant Poems and magical realism tell the story of the creation of the Panama Canal. Fourteen year old Mateo leaves Cuba, and his abusive father, for Panama when a recruiter makes false promises that result in Mateo working in a harsh labor camp. There he gets into a fight with Henry, a Jamaican who at first hates Mateo because Mateo's lighter skin color will mean slightly better pay and better treatment (the darker the skin color the worse the treatment in the camps). Anita is a Panamanian who sells herbs, (she is on the cover giving Mateo a second look). We also meet Augusto, a Puerto Rican geologist, and many of the poems are told by monkeys, hummingbirds, snakes, jaguars, and trees that reflect the canals impact on nature.

A follow up prose poem would be wonderful, allowing the telling of the story fully.

The author is a Cuban American (born Los Angeles) and her 2009 book 'The Surrender Tree: Poems of Cuba's Struggle for Freedom' was awarded a Newbery Honor (the first awarded to a Latino author). Search "Yarn Interview with Margarita Engle" for a terrific article from April 2014.

title: New to the epic 28 book series
text:
Good news and better news for new readers to the Shannara world. Good News is 'The High Druid's Blade' is book one in the Defenders of Shannara series. Better news it is set 100 years after the events in most recent book and the new series will be loosely-connected, stand-alone novels. The best news is that if you like this book there are 27 existing books to enthrall you until the next in the series is published in 2015. Now, the bad news is the author recommends reading them in order. However that didn't deter me once I went to the author's website and saw all the cool information available, I knew that if I got confused I could have all my questions answered quickly - you should check it out it really is a terrific website. And yes, I think that reading the series from the beginning would be the way to go, still I enjoyed this book and and guess I will enjoy the rest of the series even more,

I got this info from the web and hope it helps you.
