Meanwhile, several miles uptown and perched near the top of the Upper East Side’s social register, Luke McGavock has postponed his accumulation of wealth in an attempt to recover the sense of purpose now lacking in a life that often gives him pause—especially with regard to his teenage daughter, whose wanton extravagance bears a horrifying resemblance to her mother’s. But on a September morning, brightness falls horribly from the sky, and people worlds apart suddenly find themselves working side by side at the devastated site, feeling lost anywhere else, yet battered still by memory and regret, by fresh disappointment and unimaginable shock. What happens, or should happen, when life stops us in our tracks, or our own choices do? What if both secrets and secret needs, long guarded steadfastly, are finally revealed? What is the good life? Posed with astonishing understanding and compassion, these questions power a novel rich with characters and events, both comic and harrowing, revelatory about not only New York after the attacks but also the toll taken on those lucky enough to have survived them. Wise, surprising, and, ultimately, heart-stoppingly redemptive, The Good Life captures lives that allow us to see–through personal, social, and moral complexity–more clearly into the heart of things.

title: Ages 15 to 17
text: Sadly the book lost me when the dogs were murdered again and again. Innocent slaughter does nothing for me and even less do I want my young'ns reading about it. 25 years ago Birch Markle killed a woman and disappeared from the Missouri Ozarks village of Rowan's Glen which was settled hundreds of years ago by the ancestors of teenage cousins Heather and Ivy.  Deciding to celebrate May Day for the first time since then, Heather is crowned queen, and disappears. Ivy search for Heather is suspenseful and the resolution appropriate to the story.

title: Romance set in a rural campground 250 miles southwest of Denver, Colorado
text:
Missing the Oregon Series but having my BFF live outside Denver I was eager to try this new romance and evoke some fabulous memories. I highly encourage everyone to visit Colorado - there is so much to do (skiing, hiking, site seeing) and not to do (dining, hot springs, epic views from hotels).

Anyway, to the romance.for the most part a very believable story of neurosurgeon Dr. Maggie Sullivan hitting a very rough patch in her career (malpractice) and in home life (miscarriage) . She retreats to her family owned camp site for some much need R&R with her dad. And then her Dad has a heart attack, luckily for the good doctor it is always darkest before the down and good things are headed her way - in this case taking the form of Cal who is at a crossroads himself.

Disappointingly to me Cal and Maggie never came to life, for me, as people or a couple - bummer.

title: are equally horrible. At that point I am ready to counsel ...
text:
21 years ago Maddy Carmichael's twin brother, Marcus, set her up to be gang raped on the night of her prom. She escapes her small town Florida life after killing the sociopaths in a hit in run. Now she is living in Boston under a new name, Molly Hall, with a daughter, Kristen, a high school senior. At this point I am thinking - you go girl!

What happens next is just a horror. the man she married is abusive and his sons, Graham & Holden, are equally horrible. At that point I am ready to counsel her to take your daughter and burn the house down with them in it.

Then it get worse. Maddie gets a phone call and past is now catching up with her. Maddie finally rises to her inner strength but her staying in her marriage to an abuser was such a turnoff for me, that even though the author knows how to make a story compelling it just never captured my heart.

title: the suspense is well done
text:
Some really awkward writing (the writing seems rushed and certainly not as polished as one would expect from a writer of Neiderman's experience) got in the way of a smooth read and this reader carried away an enhanced anger at antisemitism in any form . Perhaps, that's what the writer intended. I get the feeling the Jewish characters were presented en masse as a people, while the terrorists were drawn as individuals.

The good guy and gal characters are flat, while Neiderman did much better rounding out and making empathetic the terrorists. Nevertheless, the moreal draws the reader in always cheering for the good guys while feeling sorry for the bad guys.

title: Book 2 - read book 1 first - it will make a MUCH better read.,
text:
I had not read book one, saw all the reviews and after finishing book 2 am very glad for reading book 1 first (see a summary below). Bobby/Adam is accused of murdering British businessman Jonathan Valentine in an alley. There is a lot of action in this book: The Arctic, Kiev, London, Moscow, the Russian mafia in NYC, Russian power broker in the former Soviet Union, Chornobyl, a psychopathic murderer, a YA romance, an adult romance, a reporter looking to break a huge story, and science fiction. Overall it was over and under whelming.

The Boy from Reactor 4 (2013) A twisting tale of greed, secrets, and lies, forensic security analyst Nadia Tesla’s memories of her father are not happy ones. An angry, secretive man, he died when she was thirteen, leaving his past shrouded in mystery. When a stranger claims to have known her father during his early years in Eastern Europe, she agrees to meet in Manhattan’s East Village,—only to watch the man shot dead on a city sidewalk. With his last breath, he whispers a cryptic clue, one that will propel Nadia on a high-stakes treasure hunt from New York to her ancestral homeland of Ukraine. There she meets an unlikely ally: 16-year-old orphan from Alaska, Aagayuk “Bobby” Kungenook aka 'Adam', a teenage hockey prodigy who honed his skills on the abandoned cooling ponds of Chernobyl. Physically and emotionally scarred by radiation syndrome, Adam possesses a secret that could change the world—if she can keep him alive long enough to do it.

title: Disppointing if you are looking for a novel that hinges on a biblical mystery
text:
The codex truly gets lost in this over the top thriller. So getting that out of the way, the novel is non-stop action and a quick read that Publisher's Weekly loved.

It never captured my interest. While this novel is advertised as book 3 in a series I looked the first titles up, and after reading the below summaries, I felt I wasn't adrift on any part of this novel:

THE HUNTED (2000) The Hunted introduces a number of characters that figure prominently in Alan Jacobson’s later novels, including Department of Defense covert operative Hector DeSantos and FBI director Douglas Knox from "Velocity" and "Hard Target," along with others who will be returning in future Alan Jacobson novels. Not just a thrilling read, The Hunted is an adventure that lays a solid foundation for many characters and stories slated to come in the Alan Jacobson universe.How well do you really know the person you love? How far would you go to find out? If there was one person in the world Dr. Lauren Chambers was sure she could rely on, it was her beloved husband, Michael. Recovering from an agoraphobic depression and prone to episodes of blinding anxiety, Lauren is a gifted psychologist for whom her husband's love and support mean everything. So when Michael suddenly and mysteriously vanishes, Lauren once again finds herself balancing on a knife's edge, haunted more than ever by an all-too-familiar paranoia. Is there more to it than paranoia, though? Private investigator Nick Bradley believes so. As the pair takes off on a cross-country journey in search of answers -- a search that yields a series of unsettling truths about the husband Lauren believed she knew so well -- bestselling author Alan Jacobson sets into motion a page-turning tale of concealed identities, an assassin's vendetta, and murderous revenge. Once again proving his mastery of the shocking twist and the ingenious turn, Jacobson leads readers on an exhilarating road thriller built for hairpin turns and unexpected detours as Lauren heads for a face-off with the most dangerous secret of all: the truth. A chilling follow-up to his breakthrough bestseller False Accusations: a high-velocity thriller of deadly revenge and psychological mayhem.

HARD TARGET (2012) An enigmatic covert operative. A skilled FBI agent with a dark past. And a terror plot unlike any in history. An explosion pulverizes the president-elect's helicopter on Election Night. It soon becomes clear that the group behind the assassination attempt possesses far greater reach than anything the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force has yet encountered and a plot so deeply interwoven in the country's fabric that it threatens to upend America's political system. But as Department of Defense operative Hector DeSantos and FBI Agent Aaron Uzi Uziel sort out who is behind the bombing, Uzi's personal demons not only jeopardize the investigation but may sit at the heart of a tangle of lies that threaten to trigger an international terrorist attack. Hailed by political thriller master Vince Flynn as a smart, complex novel that explodes from the page, and by blockbuster author Lee Child as a terrific thriller that's fast, hard, and intelligent, Hard Target is a ticking time bomb that keeps you clinging to the edges of your seat . . . and turning the pages. Hard Target also features National Bestselling Author Alan Jacobson's famed FBI Profiler, Karen Vail, in a key role affecting national security.

title: I should have loved it, but it never got to a point were you could cal it a 'page-turner'.
text:
Rosie, the transitioning receptionist is the best part in the novel. The author is a 30 year veteran of the Atlanta PD starting as a beat cop and retiring a lieutenant. The novel opens with Sarah's first day as a lieutenant, she's an action hero type who practices Aikido, in a relationship with Detective Bernard Wills, and loves dogs.

The descriptions of Atlanta are so well done they will give you the feel of having been there a dozen times yourself.

title: The cover had me at hello.
text:
Reading the summary I had visions of a gorgeous novel along the lines of the author RF Delderfield. Post WWI 28-year-old Lady Helena leaves all she knows in London and moves to Paris after surviving a near fatal illness and her broken betrothal to a war vet who was not deemed a suitable match in her social circle. Helena needs to let loose. She stays with her bohemian Aunt Agnes and gets admitted to a tough to get into art school.

The story never came passionately to life, including Sam the American she meets in Paris. Perhaps if I had read the two earlier novels by the author where Helena was a secondary character and then a featured character? But I think not, because her ex was the love interest in the previous novel who jilted her at the end after stringing her along for 5 YEARS, and let her suffer by letting others think she had jilted him.

c'est dommage.

title: Ages 12 to 14
text:
13 year-old Rosemary “Rosie” Bennett, is named by her parents after a line from Hamlet.

Rosie, Adam and his older sister, Shelby used to be tight, but Shelby has a boyfriend and after school activities, so they don't hang out anymore. In Rosie’s house they find a book in a locked cupboard. Sadly their rendering of the text creates a spell that erases Shelby and will erase their memories of Shelby forever. Hoping for answers they reach out to the cupboard's previous owner, the poet Constance Brook who is in a nursing home dying of Alzheimer’s disease.

Part adventure, part fantasy, part hard hitting fact of life issues. I give it an A for effort, while the 14 year old and the 10 year old in the family found they lost interest along the way.

title: Historical Romance Intrigue  1492 to 1501
text:
For fans of Phillipa Gregory said it all and it delivered. The Vatican Princess tells Lucrezia Borgia's story from her imagined POV. But only the first half of her life so that was an opportunity missed by me because she certainly had a very rich life the next 18 years. The drama and dialogue were more impassioned than I usually enjoy. I think I would have enjoyed the novel more if I came to feel it's truth. I would love to know who killed her brother Giovanni

What historical facts are known:
Father is Rodrigo Borgia Pope Alexander VI and her mother, his mistress, Vannozza dei Cattanei.
She was born:18 April 1480 - Died:24 June 1519 (aged 39).
Her brothers were Cesare Borgia, Giovanni Borgia, and Gioffre Borgia.
Married at age 13 to 26 year old Giovanni Sforza d'Aragona (5 July 1466 – 27 July 1510) lord of Pesaro and Gradara and annulled a year later
Married at age 17 to Alfonso of Aragon, Duke of Bisceglie, Prince of Salerno who died 2 years later. This part of the story is simply tragic.
one child Rodrigo.
Married at age 21 to Alfonso d'Este (Duke of Ferrara, Modena and Reggio) (1476 – 1534) until her death 16 years later at age 39 having had 7 more children.

After reading this historical fiction it created a hunger in me to read the biographies of this woman:
[[ASIN:0143035959 Lucrezia Borgia: Life, Love, and Death in Renaissance Italy]]
[[ASIN:1842126164 The Life and Times of Lucrezia Borgia (Women in History)]]
[[ASIN:B003R7K3JG Lucretia Borgia, according to original documents and correspondence of her day]]
[[ASIN:0812981618 Blood and Beauty: The Borgias; A Novel]]
[[ASIN:1849019940 The Borgias]]

title: Ages 12 to 14
text: reservations. 12 year-old Chris's adventure loving uncle takes him on a trip off the coast of Alaska a year after Chris's father has died in a car crash, their boat sinks and his uncle does not survive. Chris and 16 year old Frank, are the sole survivors. Frank is a bully and a misery to be around with issues of his own rooted in an alcoholic mother and an dead beat father. The fraught and scary, full of near death experiences going on for weeks, novel does not end happily for everyone.

title: Disappointed
text: an erotic romance without a soul. The heroine had no honor and neither did her lover. I love this period. I loved Laurie McBain and was hoping to find another author like her.

title: I was so looking forward to this
text: I wanted to enjoy this novel so much and I knew from the book blurb that it was the kind of book I enjoy, and I would have if, the two leads didn't leave me cold.

title: Rave reviews, the PNW locale and the historic period compelled me to order
text: I ordered this novel of the lawless turn of the century coastal lumber town in the Pacific Northwest after reading so many rave reviews. I am currently living in the same area and I was ripe to enjoy this novel. It had all the elements but the book was a real struggle to finish. Where the NYT noted the book's patient attention to even the lowest of characters, I found it a struggle to keep track of them all. Where Kirkus reviews a dense, deep and illuminating narrative, I found it a slog to get through. And I just wasn't interested in any of the characters - I don't need to like them but I should be interested. All the fabulous reviewers can't be wrong so I will hang on to try it again.

title: 8th romance of a series set on the southern Oregon coast.
text: In this the 8th novel in the series I was hoping for more detail to the area the book is set in the southern coast of Oregon, but I never got a feel of place (maybe because I just visited the area for the first time 2 months ago).  I just felt like it could set on any coastal town in the US. I was looking for more depth in character development maybe I am too demanding in my romances.

title: An excellent book club choice
text: As I was reading the novel I kept asking myself why did I order this book? Nothing was believable not the characters and not the plot. 29 year old Jensen is married to Nico even tho she is still in love with her boyfriend from high school. Her boyfriend back in high school, Ryder, is now a hot shot physician treating her deathly ill NFL Hall of Fame father, Sterling. Ryder is still in love with her even tho his girlfriend may be an issue. Jensen's brother, Will, was his BFF. Will has been dead 13 years. Jensen and  Ryder feel guilt over his death.

title: oops! I thought this was a title written by Ace 'Atkins' of Robert B. Parker continuity fame.
text:
Fyi, Abingdon Press is an imprint of The United Methodist Publishing House, in operation since 1789. For more than 200 years, Abingdon Press has continued a tradition in religious publishing for crossing denominational boundaries with thought-provoking and enjoyable books. In the early 1920s, Abingdon began publishing a wide array of high-caliber academic, professional, inspirational, and life-affirming religious literature to enrich church communities across the globe. Now beginning its ninth decade, Abingdon Press has a commitment to providing the best, most effective religious publications available.

The upshot being that christians probably won't find anything to object to in reading this title.

The story was intriging set in 1964 and flash forwarded 50 years later. The only negative for me was more than I could handle the dialogue didn't work. I would say try reading the sample and if you enjoy it then give it a try.

title: Didn't think Evelyn was strong enough
text: "Evelyn has waited eighteen years for a chance to investigate" I should have guessed from this tag line that I wasn't going to be satisfied with an investigator that can wait 18 years to solve a crime.

title: Highly respected novel
text: I read a terrific review at Publisher's Weekly so I was eager to start this novel. I have to wonder if I was reading the same book.  I thought the dialogue and the prose were both clunky. The beginning was, to me, overly implausible with laborious plotting. I can see where the author tried to bring the characters to life, but it shouldn't so obvious to the reader, it's a good effort and needs stronger editing. The best thing about it was the Minnesota setting. I am looking forward to reading his highly acclaimed debut novel THE LIFE WE BURY, a mystery thriller that garner all sorts of accolades.

title: 120 pages - a nice starter kit to plan your trip via car to Nîmes, Nice, Provence, French Riviera
text:
Plus a Paris city-guide and a Nice city-guide. Don't buy it for the pictures (too small and washed out) or the map (again, too small to be of any use).

4 days a round trip from Arles to the coast.
5 days through the Luberon and Vaucluse
7 days from Monaco to St. Remy de Provence.
7 days from Nimes to Vaison La Romaine

plus the usual travel guide stuff:
* tips from locals
* places to eat and sleep
* seasonal events

title: Still and all it was fun to read because I don't think these stories are included in “The Complete Stories of Truman Capote”
text: I wish I could tell you more about this edition however the preview copy provided was incomplete, lacking the 12 page forward by Hilton Als. Also, there is no perspective into any of the 10 short stories, such as when they were written or any context in regards to the writing of the stories which would have great improved the enjoyment of reading the teenage Mr. Capote. I wasn't looking for a critique, a couple paragraphs of background or appreciation for each of the 10 stories would have been perfect.

title: Terrific premise
text: A very ambitious novel that didn't work for me.  Gwendolen Harleth and Daniel Deronda, were created by the literary great George Eliot, it was her final novel published in 1876. Diana Souhami gives that novel, titled 'Daniel Deronda', a twist by making her book be told by Gwendolyn. The thing is, I never read Daniel Deronda and I think I would have enjoyed this so much more if I had. An absolute fun twist is Gwendolen becoming acquainted with George Eliot herself, with Eliot intrigued with Gwendolen's story.

title: Ages 9 to 11 (or younger if read to)
text: We finished this 4 weeks ago and no repeat readings by the 9 year old or the 7 year old.

title: Kidnapping mad cap cross country (Canada) thriller adventure
text: Think Remington Steele where he has a cop as a girlfriend, and worth reading to see how it ends, however you really need to go into this knowing you will utter the phrase "Oh, like that would really happen?" several times.

title: Nice
text: My 3 eager readers/listeners, ages 4 to 8m thought it was nice but didn't request a repeat read - I asked why not and they said the illustrations were 'kinda creepy'.

title: I think my expectations were too high
text: I thought this was going to either be an epic historical fiction or a deeply insightful, intimate internal story. It wasn't. It was a good debut novel set in  1928 Oklahoma. It is the story of 18-year-old Maud Nail, her family, and the lovers who drift in and out of her life.  The novel opens with the slaughter of the family cow. The family is mixed race Cherokee, Maud is an avid reader who dreams of something more then existing, subsisting, on the scrap of land her family was forced on after they were forced off their own land by the U.S. government. A romance with a traveling salesman, Booker Wakefield, holds promise that comes to naught (and the bit with the fate of the letter was eye roll material).

title: If there was ever a chick-lit novel this is the one
text: the only thing that struck me as odd is that while Anna Wyatt is just turned 40, she and her friends act like they are all on the first episode of the TV show "Friends', their behavior is too young for people with 20 years of adulthood under their belts. The novel had great bones and I loved the premise of Anna winning a major advertising account, teaming up with an illustrator, meeting a wonderful Lincoln Mallory (picture Colin Firth) sharing instant chemistry (the author captured this section perfectly including the Phoenix locale), parting to meet again in a year. It just didn't work.

title: World War Two - D-day espionage romance with a couple twists and surprises
text: Suspend your disbelief, don't be upset by the ending, and it will be a fun read. Madeleine Dirac (picture 25 year old Lesley Ann Down) is training as an agent for the British secret service organization in 1944 to be dropped behind enemy lines with transmitters and equipment for the French Underground with little chance of survival. Colonel Matthew Hammond (picture 40 year old Harrison Ford) tells us about Madeline, how she was his top gun, how they had a whirlwind romance in London before she heads to France and that communications went silent, and the discovery of a double agent.

title: England - absorbing novel of life on the home front in World War II
text:
First published in the UK 2014. If you like novels that weave past and present story-lines then this will be right up your ally. Roberta and her job at Old and New Bookshop are perfect for each other. She loves nothing more than finding scraps of memorabilia in the used books acquired from customers. As a sideline she dreams about her boss, Philip, while he becomes lovers with lovely Jenna. Complicating matters Jenna confides in Roberta that she is pregnant by her ex.

Knowing her passion for the hidden lives of owners of books, Roberta’s father, John, brings in an old suitcase containing his mother's books. Roberta's grandmother, Dorothea Pietrykowskii, is 109 years old and lives in a convalescent home under hospice care. Topping that off John is not in the best of shape. Roberta finds a letter from her grandfather Jan Pietrykowski, a Polish Squadron Leader, dated February 8, 1941 - a year after he was Killed in action - what a bombshell!

The story of family secrets and uncovering the mysteries of family members was a lot of fun for a Sunday afternoon however the ending was super odd.

title: psychological thriller and a nightmare
text:
3 years ago Hanna's husband, Joe, was beaten to death in their home in New York, leaving Hanna scarred physically,mentally and emotionally. Rud Petty, their daughter Dawn's boyfriend, was convicted but is getting a new trial on appeal. Dawn is living in New Mexico. Gail Nazarian, the prosecutor needs Hanna to testify but now Hanna thinks it wasn't Rud Petty she saw but a neighbor, Emmet Furth. Dawn's older sister, Iris, is horrified when Hanna allows Dawn back in their lives. The prosecutor and Iris think Dawn was involved in the murder and beating of her parents.

Very believable however I ended up up not liking Hanna all that much.

title: magical realism historical fiction
text:
The best thing about this book was it led me to google the main characters - fascinating people. This was a new genre for me magical realism historical fiction and I wave found that, for me, the magical realism element not not flow with the historical fiction genre.

Set in 1632 London England it's the fictionalized account of Venetia Anastasia Stanley Digby, renowned for her beauty she went to extreme measures at age 32 to remain young looking, to the extent of taking potions, the 15th century equivalent of plastic surgeons, the one that reputedly killed her overnight was a mixture of snake organs, pregnant mare's urine and opium. And that's not the weird part, the other characters in the novel are David Bowie, Andy Warhol, Naomi Campbell, even Neil Armstrong. Because her husband, Sir Kenelm Digby, was a scientist with a belief in alchemy that translated for this novel into the ability to bend time, to time travel.

title: Police Procedural # 3 of 36 titles in an on going series.
text:
I loved it but two things took away the pleasure - it needed editing for American readers - too many main characters names beginning with the letter V, compounded with their being too many characters. The 2nd was the gratuitous graphic violence mostly toward women.

What I did like was that it is a police procedural, with more twits and surprises than a reader could hope for and they all made complete sense. I also loved the last chapter and the shoot out - like Dirty Harry meets Die Hard - loved it.

Translated and originally published in 1997 featuring Deputy Commissioner Van In, his openly gay Sgt. Guido Versavel, his BFF forensics expert Leo Vanmaele, and his lover Assistant District Attorney Hannelore Maartens.

BOOK #1 The Square of Revenge: An ancient family name hides sinister secrets of love and betrayal, riches and revenge in the heart-pounding English-language debut by European crime sensation Pieter Aspe. The beautiful medieval architecture of Bruges belies the dark longings of her residents. When the wealthy and powerful Ludovic Degroof’s jewelry store is robbed, nothing is stolen, but the jewels have been dissolved in jars of aqua regia, an acid so strong that it can melt even gold. In the empty safe is a scrap of paper on which a strange square has been drawn. At first, Inspector Van In pays little attention to the paper, focusing on the bizarre nature of the burglary. But when Degroof’s children begin to receive letters with this same enigmatic square, Van In and the beautiful new District Attorney, Hannelore Martens, find themselves engaged in solving the mystery of a complex web of Latin phrases, a baroness’ fallen family, and Degroof’s unsettling relationship with a hostage grandchild, who is being ransomed for a priceless collection of art.
BOOK #2 ‘The Midas Murders’ Inspector Van In races against the clock to thwart a series of terrorist plots. One quiet snow-covered Sunday morning in Bruges, a prominent business executive is found dead in the streets, apparently due to an alcoholic hemorrhage, but for Inspector Van In, there is a something about the autopsy that does not add up. When he questions the businessman’s friend, a Dutchman, he too is found dead the next morning, burned to death in a house fire. When there is an explosion in the middle of a popular tourist area in downtown Bruges, Van In strives to find the connection between the three incidents, but no one is coming forward to claim responsibility for this terrorist attack. Just an anonymous letter to the police, threatening more bombings'unless they cooperate with a series of demands that would undermine the entire city government. Aided by the spunky and beautiful assistant DA Hannelore Maartens, Inspector Van In finds himself enmeshed in the case that threatens not just the lives of countless of innocent people, but the heart of the city he loves

title: Debut British Thriller
text:
That devolved, for me, to a sickeningly, unrelentingly violent with no apparent or worthwhile purpose, read - and made me want to re-read every Mrs. Pollifax I have (lol). But enough of the traditional British spy novel to be compelling. Reading to the end it felt cold, sadistic.

The Program is walled of from the populace because it contains the scum of society, until uptown girl Charlotte Alton takes on the persona of Karla, a sociopath thug, involves ex-spook and sniper Simon Johanssen and the two of them turn The Program inside out. The characters are emotionally stunted in the near future world much as I felt by the last page.

title: Dry, but easy to read verse
text: Jack Dana, Yale, Oxford and Harvard educated joined the Marines just after 9/11/2001, sees action in Afghanistan, ends up recovering at Walter Reed Medical Center. His only relative is a successful NY lawyer forced to retirement when he looks closer at the legality of the firm's top client. It get worse for his uncle Henry, much worse, Henry's secretary makes out no better, but the graphic description of the cat killing was enough to stop cold the enjoyment for me. Jack uncovers a vast criminal organization and the author does a terrific job of making the story beleive (although the characters seem rather naive, almost like they were raised in the 1950's.

title: Mainly enjoyable for me were the stories of her work with different ethnicities and cultures.
text: I think the authors heart is in her work I just don't think that the intended audience will ever pick the book up. I am trying to remember why I ordered this title, I think it was because it is so outside my usual reading material. And the cover is gorgeous. The author is a Ph.D., teacher, public speaker, counselor, raised in Austria and Germany, she has studied in India and in 1982 came to the US.  Her books include Aphrodite's Daughters: Women's Sexual Stories and the Journey of the Soul. The writing was oddly passive/aggressive with lots of judging going on in a non-judgmental way, odd.

title: British crime thriller from debut novelist
text:
Detective Inspector Helen Grace is on the hunt for a psychopath who has kidnapped a young couple, and tortures them ending in the death of one (revolting). It get much much worse when it happens again and again before the police can catch the sadistic killer. It gets super creepy when the detective finds the only clue linking them is that she has met the victims in the past. Helen has seriously harmful secrets of her own., not the least of which dealing with alcoholism, and this story may not be for those enjoy a damaged hero. Plenty of twists and surprises in this story kept me reading compulsively til the end.

What ruined it for me was the reveal of the killer - it didn't seem to fit, although it was a good surprise.

title: New to me author.
text: I loved the New England setting ( being a 10 generation New Englander myself). However the mom and daughter were not appealing or interesting. The plot never became believable for me and the pace was rarely compelling. I have read rave reviews of the author's other books [[ASIN:0061095052 A Woman's Place]]; [[ASIN:1416579567 Coast Road]]; [[ASIN:B00F1QX852 The Dream (Crosslyn Rise Trilogy Book 1)]]; [[ASIN:1451648413 Lake News]]; [[ASIN:B000OF06QE TOGETHER ALONE -OS]]so I will try another.

title: Fictional Emily Dickinson
text:
I was hoping for something fun to read and it started off great. We learn about her family and her home and her obsessions and fears. I visited the Dickinson home in October 2014 so this novel was a real treat.

The family hires a new maid, an Irish immigrant, Ada. Emily soaks up all things Ada. The story turns dark after this point for Ada. I think I would have enjoyed it more without the angst. Ada and Emily alternate telling the story, I have found that, for me, when this format is used I tend to not feel enmeshed in the characters and his was no exception - they just seem to come out a bit hollow.

title: death of an Orthodox Jewish woman in Rockland County, New York
text:
told in two voices - those of Aviva and Rebekah. I didn't love this one as much as the first novel (below). The story-line of Aviva's brother, Sam. seemed more far fetched then I could credibly believe. This is the author's 2nd novel which they say is the hardest so I still look forward to the 3rd in the series set in the insular communities of NYC. What saved it for me was the flashbacks from Aviva.

BOOK#1 INVISIBLE CITY (2014): Just months after Rebekah Roberts was born, her mother, Aviva Kagan an Hasidic Jew from Brooklyn, abandoned the Baptist seminary student she met in a New York City bookstore and newborn baby to return to her religion. Neither Rebekah nor her father have heard from her since. Now a recent college graduate, Rebekah has moved to New York City to follow her dream of becoming a big-city reporter. But she's also drawn to the idea of being closer to her mother, who might still be living in the Hasidic community in Brooklyn. Then Rebekah is called to cover the story of a murdered Hasidic woman. Rebekah's shocked to learn that, because of the NYPD's habit of kowtowing to the powerful ultra-Orthodox community, not only will the woman be buried without an autopsy, her killer may get away with murder. Rebekah can't let the story end there. But getting to the truth won't be easy--even as she immerses herself in the cloistered world where her mother grew up, it's clear that she's not welcome, and everyone she meets has a secret to keep from an outsider.

title: I just never believed it - any of it
text: Bailey Carpenter and her stoner brother, Heath, inherited their father's fortune. They are sued by their father's children from other mothers for their share of dad's wealth. Bailey, living in a Miami high-rise and driving a Porsche, is having an affair with her married boss (a lawyer). Bailey is a sort of Kinsey Milhone, while tracking a deadbeat Dad after midnight she is violently raped. Taking a leave from work and suffering panic attacks her sister Claire (who she doesn't know well) and teenage niece Jade, come to her rescue. Bailey has a craving for investigation and ends up spying on her neighbors through her windows, in a nearby high-rise he observes a man who enjoys sexual depravity which she clearly witnesses.

title: Thriller set in Exeter, England
text:
I could have done without the Killer's cruelty to the cat, the explicit killings, the at times implausible plot threads, otherwise I enjoyed it especially that it kept me guessing who done it til the end.

Kara Small, Livy Jackson's younger sister, was murdered 18 years ago when she was a college student. Livy, now finds Kara's BFF, Julie Dryden (godmother to Livy's daughter Hannah), dead - the police rule it a suicide. Livy doesn't buy it, Julie was too high on life. Robbie, Julie's twin, and Julie's estranged mother just want to move on. Julia's boyfriend, Damian Burton, thinks it's murder. Julie was on to Kara's murderer and paid for it with her life. Could it be Will, Livy's philandering husband?

Now the person I wanted to be the murder, Livy's bratty daughter Hannah, wasn't alive 18 years ago, more's the pity.

title: sequel to 2011’s Kill Switch, with Dr. Claire Waters a New York City forensic psychologist
text:
Claire, the suspense, and the reveal were all winners and highlights of the book for me. I was totally looking forward to this novel. I am a devoted watcher of the TV show Law & Order SVU . I am not sure where the disconnect is, what hampered my enjoyment were:

Rosa Sanchez's story. The woman could rival Melanie Hamilton Wilkes for goodness so I was confounded that she could possibly be convicted and put in prison. Detective Nick Lawler, for a person described as brilliant he makes some really amateur decisions and deductions. The same goes for his boss Det. Lieutenant Brian Wilkes.

The author is a writer and producer, known for the hit TV shows China Beach, ER and Law & Order SVU

BOOK #1 KILL SWITCH (2011) murder, mystery, and modern forensics. Dr. Claire Waters understands what motivates violent criminals, and she tries to prevent them from committing further crimes. Haunted by a childhood brush with a vicious crime that was never solved--the abduction of her best friend--she must confront her own worst fears when she takes on her first serial killer case. She meets with Todd Quimby in the bowels of Rikers Island prison and sets out to crack his tough exterior, but she overlooks his violent nature and recommends his release. Within twenty-four hours, Claire is horrified to realize that the body of a murdered woman in Times Square bears all the hallmarks of a Quimby victim. Soon the killer taunts her, her supervisors doubt her, the cops resent her, and her boyfriend questions her loyalty. Determined and daring, Claire agrees to be a decoy. Risking everything, she uncovers a devious medical conspiracy that threatens to disrupt the international balance of power. She must confront both a killer and a conspiracy--or die trying.

title: The Fitzgibbon Family of small town Oliver's Well Virginia
text:
Paddy is the owner of the landscaping business.

75 year old Mary Bernadette is his wife of 54 years. She has never unfrozen from the death of their child, 50 years ago.

Their daughter, Grace, is a nun - and my favorite character

Their son, Pat, a successful lawyer, and has been Mary Bernadette's target his whole life.

Megan is married to Pat, the mother of beloved golden child PJ and also a successful lawyer. She needed to frost her mother-in-law out years ago - she is also a terrific character.

PJ and Alexis are newlyweds living in the cottage behind the family home. PJ is managing the family landscaping business. Alexis feel's Mary Berndette's judging shadow in their daily life.

The delicious anticipation of how the cracks will manifest kept me reading. The stilted dialogue made this a read that you can easily put down.

title: set in the town of Serenity, South Carolina.
text:
More a woman's story than a romance. Adelia Hernandez, was in a loveless marriage to a no good cad, Ernesto. She packs up their 4 children (Tomas, Selena, Natalia & Juanita), she finds a job in a high end boutique after raising children for 15 years, and they move to South Carolina into a swank home in the historic part of town.

Gabe Franklin was, and maybe still is, Serenity's hunky bad boy. He's determined to quit boozing. Could they be a dream come true?

Not very deep, kinda superficial, but lighthearted with a HEA (Happily Ever After).

Part of the author's Sweet Magnolias (series):
Stealing Home (2007)
A Slice of Heaven (2007)
Feels Like Family (2007)
Welcome to Serenity (2008)
Home in Carolina (2010)
Sweet Tea at Sunrise (2010)
Honeysuckle Summer (2010)
Midnight Promises (2012)
Catching Fireflies (2012)
Where Azaleas Bloom (2012)
Swan Point (July 29, 2014)

title: Gay erotica romance time travel reincarnation historical fiction
text:
Book 3 stands on it's own but you will get more out of it by reading the 2 earlier titles. Arthur is now a 43 year old ex-marine. Jeremy is now 24 and a white hot mess, college drop-out, boozer and drug abuser, throwing his money away on users posing as lovers. If you have not read the earlier titles the plot summaries below may be interesting. A substantial read at almost 400 pages that never took off for me.

BOOK #1 STRINGS ATTACHED (2006 ForeWord Magazine Book of the Year Award Winner in Gay & Lesbian Fiction) - 17 year old Jeremy Tyler's father died when he was a child, his mother is in rehab and Jeremy is sent to live with his wealthy repressive relatives. This novel has a lot of plot - a mystery, teen angst, gay erotica. "Closeted teenager Jeremy is sent to live with wealthy relatives after his mother enters rehab. Struggling to fit into the posh world of Ballena Beach, Jeremy joins the high school swim team, dates a popular girl, and begins to think he may have landed in paradise - until his great aunt Katharine starts to dictate his every move...and a late-night phone call insinuates that his father's accidental death was not so accidental after all. As Jeremy grows accustomed to the veneer of a fabulous life, so grows his need for answers - as well as the danger of immeasurable harm. Weaving together a murder mystery, sexual ambiguity, and characters with hidden identities and agendas, Nick Nolan offers listeners a deliciously witty novel about the "puppet" who wishes only to be a real boy. Strings Attached is also a surprisingly heartfelt story about coming-of-age and coming out - not necessarily in that order."

BOOK #2 DOUBLE BOUND (2007 Reader Views Readers Choice Award Winner in Gay & Lesbian Fiction) - a modern tale of passion, deception, and danger: Because of Katharine Tyler's investment in a Brazilian island resort, she sends her handsome young nephew Jeremy with his lover Carlo to assess its progress. And though hunky ex-Marine Arthur Blauefee serves as their bodyguard, the trio strives against a charming trickster, sensual temptation, a kidnapping, and an unexpected double-cross, where Aunt Katharine plays puppet-master before getting tangled in her own strings. This is Arthur's story: his heartbreaking youth, his precarious days as a gay US Marine, then his treacherous--and deliciously fulfilling--journey to Brazil, where he is challenged to heroism, while agonizing between his conscience, and his blistering desire for the one man he's forbidden to love.

title: Vienna circa 1993
text:
Intelligent, well done writing. The setting of Eastern European atmosphere is picturesque. The slow pace hampered my enjoyment. The characters were rather wooden. Historians may enjoy the plot, others may tune out.

The Cold War has ended a few years earlier, Sam Kramer, an American foreign correspondent in Vienna. Reni Müller, former head of the radical partyin the German Parliament, and Sam's ex-lover who he hasn't seen in dacades, has killed herself. Sam flies to Bonn Germany for the funeral where he is contacted by her legal counsel that only weeks before Reni has named him the literary executor, she was working on a memoir when she overdosed. East German Intelligence officer, Peter Gorik, also turns up dead and also had a connection with Reni, which sets of Sam's investigative radar.

title: Told in the 1st person, you've got Russians, Mexicans and a retired agent - I think the market is over saturated at the moment.
text: Originally published under the name 'KROKODIL' in 2014. This version has been re-written and edited. "Five years ago, an unspeakable tragedy brought an early retirement to Jeremiah “Hawk” Tate’s career as a DEA agent. Without looking back he retreated from the desert sands of the southwest to the rugged wilderness of Montana, intent to live far from any connection to his previous life. His solitude is shattered when a client shows up at the door of his Yellowstone guide service asking him to help her track down her brother, lost somewhere in the Park. Against his better judgment Hawk accepts the job and is shocked to find the man they were seeking wasn’t her brother, but someone linked to a life he thought he had left behind long ago. Narrowly escaping with his life, Hawk is forced back into a world he hasn’t been a part of in five years. Calling on allies both old and new, he plunges forward on a case that will take him from California to Baja to Russia…and ultimately home again."

title: #4 in the thriller/romance series set in Sacramento California
text:
featuring feisty Private Investigator hero, 32 year old Lizzy Gardner, and her FBI lover, and soul mate, Jared. There is more evil and greed in this book then anyone should have to experience, violence from the inside emanating out. But oddly I didn't find it a compelling read. Not your average thriller. I included the summaries below and hope they help you as they did me if you are new to the series.

The good news for those who enjoy the series there are two more titles after this one.

BOOK #1 ABDUCTED (2011) - Elizabeth Gardner (Lizzy) is seventeen-years old when she tells her parents she's going out with her girlfriends. Instead, she meets up with Jared Shayne, her boyfriend of two years. As she walks home beneath an inky black sky, her perfect night becomes her worst nightmare. Kidnapped just blocks from home, she woke up to find herself at the mercy of a depraved serial killer. Imprisoned and tormented for months by the maniac she came to know as Spiderman, Lizzy narrowly escaped, the only one of his victims to survive. But Spiderman escaped too, outwitting police and cursing Lizzy to spend her life looking over her shoulder... Fourteen years later, Lizzy is a licensed PI known as the "one who got away." When she's not searching for runaway teenagers, working on insurance scams, or talking to her therapist, she's at the local high school teaching young girls to defend themselves. But her world is turned upside down for the second time after she receives a call from Jared. He's an FBI special agent now and he needs her help. The killer has resurfaced, this time with a very specific target-- Lizzy. And he's made it clear that she will not escape him again. So begins a chilling game of cat-and-mouse, a terrifying, heart-pounding hunt that only one will survive. Escaping from a madman should have been the end of her nightmare...but it was only the beginning.

BOOK #2 DEAD WEIGHT (2012): Twenty-one years ago, Carol Fullerton's car was found abandoned by the side of a California highway. The teenager hasn't been seen or heard from since, and the case has long since gone cold. Now Carol's mother is dying. But before she draws her last breath she wants to know, once and for all, exactly what happened to her daughter.... Six months ago, Diane Kramer emptied her savings account and vanished. According to her sister, Andrea, the only clue to her whereabouts is her obsession with a charismatic weight-loss guru known for his unorthodox methods. Now Andrea fears Diane's body issues may have cost her more than she bargained for....

BOOK #3 A DARK MIND (2013): They call him the Lovebird Killer, a merciless fiend unleashing a flood of unspeakable cruelty upon Sacramento's most loving couples, young and old. This real-life monster's reign of terror has left the city's residents paralyzed with fear. All but Lizzy Gardner. Because hiding from monsters isn't Lizzy's style, not since she faced the madman who kidnapped and terrorized her as a teenager. So when a routine workers' compensation case suddenly leads her and her two young assistants onto the killer's trail, Lizzy revels in the chase. She is determined to bring this psychopath to justice before he has the chance to claim another victim. She never imagines he could be two steps ahead, watching her every move and plotting his bloodiest, most triumphant conquest of all. He knows Lizzy won't go down without a fight. And that's just the way he likes it....

BOOK #4 - OBSESSED

BOOK #5 - ALMOST DEAD (2015)

BOOK #6 - EVIL NEVER DIES (2015)

title: #5 finds ex Army Ranger, ex-elite CIA operative recovering at home on the coast of Maine
text:
After reading all the fabulous reviews I have put this on the bookcase to try again in a couple years because I thought it was pretty silly, cliche and the characters kinda wooden. I guess I have read one too many novels with the Russian mafia, black markets, Mexican drug lords and terrorists (Chechen jihadists) with nuclear weapons. In fact I was going to rate it a 2 star review then I saw the other reviews and figured I was missing something. Maybe I will take it with me on my next vacation and it will be perfect. For those new to the series here are the previous book summaries - I found them helpful to me:

BOOK #4 EYE FOR AN EYE (2013): When Dewey Andreas uncovers the identity of a mole embedded at a high level in Israel's Mossad, it triggers a larger, more dangerous plot. The mole was the most important asset of Chinese Intelligence, and the head of China's Ministry of State Security, Fao Bhang, responds to the discovery by placing a kill order on Dewey himself. Dewey is tracked to Argentina, where he is on vacation with his fiancée, Jessica Tanzer, a U.S. national security adviser. A top-level kill team is sent in quickly and quietly, but their attack fails to take him out. The collateral damage, however, is both horrifying and deeply personal. Now, with Chinese Intelligence on his trail, Dewey goes rogue in his quest for vengeance--no matter the odds or the armies he must fight to get there. A former Ranger and Delta, Dewey is a man of great skills and cunning. His opponent, Fao Bhang, is ruthless and determined, and there is no limit to the assets at his disposal. In this conflict, there are only two possible outcomes...and only one Dewey Andreas.

BOOK #3 THE LAST REFUGE (2012): With time running out to stop the nuclear destruction of Tel Aviv, Dewey Andreas must defeat his most fearsome opponent yet. Off a quiet street in Brooklyn, New York, Israeli Special Forces commander Kohl Meir is captured by operatives of the Iranian secret service, who smuggle Meir back to Iran, where he is imprisoned, tortured, and prepared for a show trial. What they don't know is that Meir was in New York to recruit Dewey Andreas for a secret operation. Meir had been tipped off that Iran had finally succeeded in building their first nuclear weapon, one they were planning to use to attack Israel. His source was a high-level Iranian government official and his proof was a photo of the bomb itself. Dewey Andreas, a former Army Ranger and Delta, owes his life to Meir and his team of Israeli commandos. Now, to repay his debt, Dewey has to attempt the impossible ---to both rescue Meir from one of the world's most secure prisons and to find and eliminate Iran's nuclear bomb before it's deployed---all without the help or sanction of Israel or America (at the near certain risk of detection by Iran). Unfortunately, Dewey's first moves have caught the attention of Abu Paria, the brutal and brilliant head of VEVAK, the Iranian secret service. Now Dewey has to face off against, outwit, and outfight an opponent with equal cunning, skill, and determination, with the fate of millions hanging in the balance.

BOOK #2 COUP D'ÉTAT (2011): Wanting only a peaceful, obscure life, Dewey Andreas has gone to rural Australia, far from turbulent forces that he once fought against. But powerful men, seeking revenge, have been scouring the earth looking for Dewey. And now, they've finally found him - forcing Dewey to abandon his home and to fight for his life against a very well armed, well trained group of assassins. Meanwhile, a radical cleric has been elected president of Pakistan and, upon taking power, sets off a rapidly escalating conflict with India. As the situation spins quickly out of control, it becomes clear that India is only days from resorting to a nuclear response, one that will have unimaginably disastrous results for the world at large. With only days to head this off, the President sends in his best people, including Jessica Tanzer, to do whatever it takes to restore the fragile peace to the region. Tanzer has only one viable option - to set up and execute a coup d'etat in Pakistan - and only one man in mind to lead the team that will try to pull off this almost unimaginable task in the nerve-wrackingly short time frame, Dewey Andreas. If, that is, Jessica can even get to Dewey and if Dewey can get out of Australia alive...

BOOK #1 POWER DOWN (2010): A major North American hydroelectric dam is blown up and the largest off-shore oil field in this hemisphere is destroyed in a brutal, coordinated terrorist attack. But there was one factor that the terrorists didn't take into account when they struck the Capitana platform off the coast of Colombia--slaughtering much of the crew and blowing up the platform--and that was the Capitana crew chief Dewey Andreas. Dewey, former Army Ranger and Delta, survives the attack, rescuing as many of his men as possible. But the battle has just begun. While the intelligence and law enforcement agencies scramble to untangle these events and find the people responsible, the mysterious figure of Alexander Fortuna--an agent embedded into the highest levels of American society and business--sets into play the second stage of these long-planned attacks. The only fly in the ointment is Dewey Andreas--who is using all his long-dormant skills to fight his way off the platform, then out of Colombia and back to the U.S., following the trail of terrorists and operatives sent to stop him. Power Down is a gripping, compelling debut thriller.

title: Not as lol as I was thinking it would be
text:
and a whole lot more angst. Cassandra and Sylvie have known each other since high school and in 2003 graduated from ultra expensive and small Bennington College (founded in 1932 for the daughters of the well to do). Sylvie heads to NYC with the ambition of starting a business. Cassandra stays in Boston looking to have fun. after a couple years Cassandra moves to NYC and they share an apartment and have a grand time. then the jobs start to dry up in 2006 and in 2008 everything crashes including their relationship. Where the author took them next is what kept me turning the page.

It did make me feel great that even with amazing connections the struggle was as real for them as it was for me at that age and with no connections.

From the author whose memoir was published at age 20 "Charlotte au Chocolat" and, as you might guess, attened Bennington College.

title: Everything was kinda quaint and superficial.
text:
I felt like I was reading a book designed for young adults - like Nancy Drew set in Brooklyn NY 120 years ago, though exposing Thomas Alva Edison and JP Morgan as nefarious evil doers was unexpected in a YA book.

The author has 23 writer/producer credits on hit TV shows: Seinfeld, 7th Heaven, Roseanne, Fantasy Island, Family Ties, Saved by the Bell, Who's the Boss?,Trapper John, M.D. & Savannah.

title: Terrific concept
text:
The novel unfolds in four reveals. On the Upper West side of Manhattan, New York City, 11 year old daughter and 15 year old son of a philanderer open a package intended for their mother containing their father's steamy correspondence with his girlfriend - yeah a big ewwwwwww!

Where it missed the mark for me was the drama - the oomph! If the family had felt rock solid this would have been a wow! But it wasn't, the family was not rock solid so kicking his philandering butt to the curb would have felt so much more satisfying to this reader then what unfolded.

Then part Two flashed forward to the where are they now. While part Three flashes back to where part one ended.

The kicker was finding out that the father was previously married and the mother/now wife knowingly had an affair with him while he was married - lol - surprise - what goes around comes around.

title: #5 in the Hugo Marston series
text:
The author's 2nd novel The Crypt Thief was a 5 star read, this one didn't do it for me - I think it would have made a good buddy movie with Vince Vaughn and Jon Favreau. Hugo is now working at the American embassy in Paris, he and his CIA partner in crime solving, Tom Green, head off to Barcelona looking for MIA 19 year old co-ed/stripper Amy Driess step-daughter of an old friend Bart, instead they find a bloody Bart standing over a very dead young man, Rubén Casteñada, who had offered Amy a job there. I think Texas Hugo has been an ex-pat too long, he no longer talks like a Texan and poor Tom throws more f-bombs than I did in my senior year in high school.

THE BUTTON MAN (2014): PREQUEL to The Bookseller, former FBI profiler Hugo Marston has just become head of security at the US Embassy in London. He’s asked to protect a famous movie-star couple, Dayton Harper and Ginny Ferro, who, while filming a movie in rural England, killed a local man in a hit and run. The task turns from routine to disastrous almost immediately. Before Hugo even meets them, he finds out that Ferro has disappeared, and her body has been found hanging from an oak tree in a London cemetery. Hours later a distraught Harper gives Hugo the slip, and Hugo has no idea where he’s run off to. Taking cues from a secretive young lady named Merlyn, and with a Member of Parliament along for the chase, Hugo’s search leads to a quaint English village. There, instead of finding Harper, more bodies turn up. Teaming with local detectives and then venturing dangerously out on his own, Hugo struggles to find connections between the victims. Is this the work of a serial killer—or something else entirely? Knowing he’s being tailed, the killer prepares for the final, public act of his murderous plan, and Hugo arrives just in time to play his part. . . .

THE BOOKSELLER (2012): Max—an elderly Paris bookstall owner—is abducted at gunpoint. His friend, Hugo Marston, head of security at the US embassy, looks on helplessly, powerless to do anything to stop the kidnapper. Marston launches a search, enlisting the help of semiretired CIA agent Tom Green. Their investigation reveals that Max was a Holocaust survivor and later became a Nazi hunter. Is his disappearance somehow tied to his grim history, or even to the mysterious old books he sold? On the streets of Paris, tensions are rising as rival drug gangs engage in violent turf wars. Before long, other booksellers start to disappear, their bodies found floating in the Seine. Though the police are not interested in his opinion, Marston is convinced the hostilities have something to do with the murders of these bouquinistes. Then he himself becomes a target of the unknown assassins. With Tom by his side, Marston finally puts the pieces of the puzzle together, connecting the past with the present and leading the two men, quite literally, to the enemy's lair. Just as the killer intended.

THE CRYPT THIEF (2013): It’s summer in Paris and two tourists have been murdered in Père Lachaise cemetery in front of Jim Morrison’s grave. The cemetery is locked down and put under surveillance, but the killer returns, flitting in and out like a ghost, and breaks into the crypt of a long-dead Moulin Rouge dancer. In a bizarre twist, he disappears under the cover of night with part of her skeleton. One of the dead tourists is an American and the other is a woman linked to a suspected terrorist; so the US ambassador sends his best man and the embassy’s head of security—Hugo Marston—to help the French police with their investigation. When the thief breaks into another crypt at a different cemetery, stealing bones from a second famed dancer, Hugo is stumped. How does this killer operate unseen? And why is he stealing the bones of once-famous can-can girls? Hugo cracks the secrets of the graveyards but soon realizes that old bones aren’t all this killer wants.

THE BLOOD PROMISE (2014): Hugo Marston must figure out what lies hidden inside an old sailor's chest before a 200-year-old blood promise is revealed and claims another life. In post-Revolution Paris, an old man signs a letter in blood, then hides it in a secret compartment in a sailor's chest. A messenger arrives to transport the chest and its hidden contents, but then the plague strikes and an untimely death changes history. Two hundred years later, Hugo Marston is safeguarding an unpredictable but popular senator who is in Paris negotiating a France/U.S. dispute. The talks, held at a country chateau, collapse when the senator accuses someone of breaking into his room. Theft becomes the least of Hugo's concerns when someone discovers a sailor's chest and the secrets hidden within, and decides that the power and money they promise are worth killing for. But when the darkness of history is unleashed, even the most ruthless and cunning are powerless to control it.

title: Romance for readers who enjoy christianity in their fiction
text:
Taryn McKenna is woebegone and vows to stop living her life feeling like she has a kick me sign around her neck - she's a teacher of 11 to 14 year olds in rural North Carolina and is the first in her immediate family to persue a college degree. Her eloved grandmother, Jemma, has been given a terminal diagnosis. Taryn works with her grandmother to complete a story quilt of their family.

This could have been a fabulous read, it has all the elements. The exception was Taryn, she was a real Debbie Downer. Grammy was fabulous and so was everything to do with the quilt and the setting in the hills of North Carolina.

title: Terrific premise and a nice debut
text:
The combination of stories one set today and the other beginning in 1908 and flashing forward to the depression of the 1930's was more distracting then enhancing.

Claire “Neely” O’Neil flees her crumbling marriage, leaves New York City and returns to her hometown of Millcreek Valley, Ohio. Neely tells her story and we follow as she opens her own bakery 'Rainbow Cake' and it's a hit. Neely is very intuitive and when planning a custom pastry she can determine what combination of flavors will work best for the buyer enabling 100% satisfaction for both buyer and baker.

The other story, told in third person, is of Olive and Edie Habig and toward the end of the book the stories come together.

One word of warning, the pastries are deliciously vivid - be prepared to run out to your own local bakery for a treat.

title: small town, fairy tale, happily ever after fiction
text:
Broght to you by Abingdon Press, the book publishing arm of the United Methodist Publishing House which publishes sheet music, ministerial resources, Bible-study aids, and other items, often with a focus on Methodism and Methodists.

This family isn't the smartest folks in Missouri. Mom and Dad raise 5 children, their dream to retire from their day jobs and open a B&B in their own home - then they are surprised at the amount of work involved - didn't they research?

Daughter Landyn is a newlywed whose husband quits his job to be an artist - without discussing with her first - time for an annulment becuase anyone who did that is such a supreme egotist that the marriage is headed for misery. But no, she packs up a u-haul and moves home.

Lastly - none of the finances made any sense where is all the money coming from? Where is all the money going? How is there an issue with taxes when you are a starving artist.

this is a huge fan favorite so it might be yours also.

title: Ages 8 to 11
text:
The publisher's of [[ASIN:0765330342 A Dog's Purpose]] have taken that adult title, extracted a portion, and developed into a child's novel.

Ellie is a search-and-rescue dog. Jakob and Myra are her trainers. Well written and no one dies.

title: From the author of The Death of Bees
text: 11 year-old Michael Murray, living on a island off the mainland of Scotland in the 1980's, doesn't like the bruises on his mother's face, especially not knowing how they got there. Things are not easy at the moment, his father is out of work and living on social welfare, There is more than a little coarse language and behavior. I liked the ending even though I was expecting a twist.

title: 4 generations of tragedy
text:
tragedy culminating in extreme violence - so maybe not for the under 18 crowd. There's a lot of drama, heartbreak, depression and out of place violence for one book, so make sure you are in the right mindset if you are going to enjoy the novel of magical realism.

taking a family over 80 years from France to Manhattan to Seattle ; from Maman to Emileinne to Vivianne to Ava born in 1944.

The gorgeous writing didn't carry me through the slog of unhappiness but it did give me a new new author to try again.

title: what an amazing premise - how could I not want to read it - I had to know how it ended.
text:
Rose has dreamed of a magical island and a boy named Hugo since she was 6 years old, in her dreams they have grown up together and it has been wonderful.

During the day Rose has it pretty good also, mother to 3 children, her husband, Josh, a surgeon the only huge issue is he is not a 9 to 5 guy. However, her day life is looking less attractive to Rose, she is feeling tired, burnt out, and isn't fitting into her clothes like she once did.

Everything spins out of control when she actually meets Hugo! Hugo also is having a rough go outside the dreamscape.

The only disappointment in the book were Rose, Hugo and Josh - I wanted to like them and they were a bit too flawed for me.

title: Ages 15 to 18
text:
Physically Identical twin sisters Ella & Maddy. Ella is smart and quiet, Maddy is a Paris Hilton/Lindsey Lohan bad girl.

Picking Maddy up late on night, they argue, Ella loses control of the car and Maddy dies.

Ella awakes concussed, people believe she is Maddy so she does too. She keeps Maddy's identity even when her memory returns.

It's a bit mature for our house right now, and even though I caught myself rolling my eyes, I am sure when my readers reach high school age they will be enthralled.

title: I was delighted at the premise but the story didn't go where I had hoped.
text:
The War Between the States or The War of Northern Aggression aka The Civil War, a war that has never become history to some Americans.

1855 sisters Josephine & Libby, ages 14 & 13, BFFs until Libby is swept off her feet by her new beau Arden.

1862 and twenty-one year old Arden is killed in action at Sharpsburg, Libby goes mad, dresses in her husband's uniform intending to kill 21 Yankees. Josephine follows her. The become part of Arden's unit, the Stonewall Jackson brigade. They go hungry, suffer brutal cold.

Things go awry again, this time when Josephine becomes close to another soldier and they both plan to desert; an action that sends Libby spiraling out of her mind.

title: 1943, World War 2 London is in ruins after 4 years of war
text: Unhappily married Stella has a passionate romance with US airman Dan Rosinski. 70 years later Dan is in his 90's, with only weeks to live, and is once again trying to find Stella and writes her a letter. The letter is delivered to a home occupied by Jess, a woman taking refuge from an abusive boyfriend.  I think this novel just had too much drama for me, When they added the character of Will and all his emotional baggage it just got to be too much.

title: the 200th book in the series dating back to 1964
text:
This book promised much but is awkwardly written (or translated). I would like to like it, it's so simplistic , as if hastily written. The author passed away in 2013, was called the best-informed spy novelist. His SAS pulp-fiction series has sold over 150 million novels - it's hero, Malko Linge, an Austrian aristocrat, freelances for the CIA.

As this was the last book published before he died at the age of 83 I will cut him some slack. Those who like their spy novels heavy on erotica should find something to enjoy, however not a lot of action - except between the sheets.

His take on Vladimir Putin I thoroughly enjoyed.

The NY Times had a in-depth interview with the author "The Spy Novelist Who Knows Too Much By Robert Worthjan" published in 2013"

title: A huge 800+ page novel
text:
Sequel to "Natchez Burning" action-packed thriller, Book #2 in a trilogy featuring Mississippi lawyer, and former prosecutor, Penn Cage and fiance Caitin Masters. I have to say that I let the pretentious names bother me. You've got evil wealthy businessmen, corruption, the Ku Klux Klan led by the State's chief of police, his own father on a murder charge, the FBI and a murders stretching back to the 1960s aching to be resolved.

It had a lot I liked and a lot that didn't work for me. You don't even want to know the evil of “the bone tree.”

title: Debut novel - character study
text:
1980's Queens New York City. Josiah has different childhood than most, his father preaches to his followers of the looming Armageddon. Flash-forward 30 years and Josiah returns to his hometown to care for his dying father.

I liked it for the depiction of Queens and the closing chapter. The fabulous review by Ron Charles in the Washington Post led me to order a copy 1 year after it was first published.

title: hard to tell what age this is for.
text:
What an awesome premise! I loved the idea. A retelling of the 101 Arabian Nights, it turns out the story is not what we always believed, and this story makes a whole lot more sense.

Khalid, the 18 year-old Caliph of Khorasan.
Shahrzad the 16 year old bride.

the book is marketed to 12 year olds and up, but the story has themes that are target to 16 to 18 year olds. The premise is also intriguing to this 50 year old but the execution (pardon the unintended pun) is written for a much younger audience.

title: 12 year old grave robber in Victorian London
text:
What an odd, odd children's book. Thomas Marsden lives in Victorian London, he robs graves. Hmmm not exactly an activity I want my young ones to appreciate. The story throws Thomas a curve ball when a grave reveals a dead body who looks exactly like him, except dead. The story is filled with fortune-tellers, alternate worlds, mystics and Faery folk.

The 9 year old flipped through it, the 13 year old breezed through it - neither went back to look at it again.

title: prequel to 2010's "Who Fears Death"
text:
Prequel to Apocalypse. Phoenix was created two years ago as a biological weapon - she also looks and acts like a gorgeous 40 year old woman. Everything was fine until she realized her surroundings were a prison and she escapes from the lab. This is her story.

I had no expectations going into this new to me author. Maybe this will please readers who wanted more after her novel Who Fears Death. I found the story lacking, a bit silly and flat - maybe because the story is told as a history?

title: speculative thriller of World War III
text:
The title refers to old warships from the navy's "Ghost Fleet." China and Russia have there eye on claiming America's mineral rights to the Mariana Trench so it's pearl Harbor all over again. They get away with it becuase America's modern high tech has all been hacked. Enter the Ghost Fleet to the resue.

Way cool premise, all you need is a novelist to add the passion that was missing from the characters and the telling. P.W. Singer is a political scientist educated at Harvard and Princeton's Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs.

title: Excellent academic title - way too dry for anything but ...
text:
Excellent academic title - way too dry for anything but mandatory reading. The author is a Distinguished Professor at the University of Colorado at Colorado springs where it gives the following profile: Professor Tom Pyszczynski received his B.A. in psychology from the University of Wisconsin – Milwaukee (1976) and his M.A. and Ph. D in social psychology from the University of Kansas (1979 & 1980). His research has been funded by the National Science Foundation since 1989. He received an Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship for collaborative research with psychologists in Germany and several grants from the Dutch government for collaborative research with psychologists in the Netherlands. He and his colleagues have played a major role in the development of Experimental Existential Psychology, an emerging sub-discipline of social psychology that applies rigorous experimental methods to the study of human confrontation with existential problems such as death, freedom, isolation, and nature. He teaches a variety of courses in social psychology.

Dr. Pyszczynski’s research is focused primarily on Terror Management Theory, which he developed with his colleagues Jeff Greenberg and Sheldon Solomon. Terror management theory is concerned with the role of self-esteem and cultural belief systems in providing protection against core human fears, especially the fear of death. Over the years Professor Pyszczynski and colleagues have explored the role of terror management processes in a wide range of topics, including self-esteem, self-deception, prejudice, interpersonal relations, altruism, aggression, sexual ambivalence, disgust, depression, anxiety disorders, trauma, unconscious processes, aging, human development, and terrorism. He has also conducted research on how people fool themselves into believing that their biased views follow logically from the available facts and on the role of self-regulatory processes in depression and other psychological disorders.

title: not his best
text: Reich is a automatic read in our family, because he is such a great storyteller. This one is a disappointment, so much so that, while I did finish it, it isn't one I could recommend. Far fetched, slow, angst ridden, almost to the point it could be a spoof ala Austin Powers.

title: An acquired taste
text: You either love it or wish you hadn't spent the time. I think the fans of British farce will love it. Paddy is absolutely pathetic on the day we meet him, and the next 4 days of his life are one misadventure after another. I picture him being played exquisitely by Rowan Atkinson.

title: ages 15 and up
text:
16-year-old Phoebe Irving and her little sister, Tabby, move from San Francisco to her stepfather's run-down mansion, Arnaud Manor, in rural England. Madame Yollande was her new home's original owner and the locals tell Phoebe gossip of missing children and malevolent ghosts. Her new home gives Phoebe the creeps.

The story is told to us by Phoebe and adding a real time urgency and excitement to the story. Add to that there is a huge amount of family tension going on that keeps the reader guessing, what's up? Phoebe is pretty interesting herself, she is a champion swimmer and is crushing on the guy, Miles, she meets in her new home town of Grenshire, England. Throw in a little horror and schizophrenia, and you have a terror filled psychological thriller on your hands..

title: 1941 to  pre-civil rights America to the 1980s
text:
Stretching from Pearl Harbor to the 1960's, from Mississippi to Boston, the book follows Beatrice Dobbins whose brother Robert saved Morris Sullivan at Pearl Harbor (12/7/1941, for the millennials out there, this was your great-grandparents 9/11) only to perish himself.

Morris reaches out to Beatrice, a black trainee teacher originally from Mississippi and now living in Boston, while on leave. Morris, white, married in haste after high school when his girlfriend becomes pregnant, and also living in Boston.

15 years after the end of the war they have an affair to remember.

The novel was lacking for me in never feeling I got to know Morris and I have never found adultery attractive. Otherwise it is a terrific premise that will appeal to readers.

Turns out the author is as interesting as the novel. I read this from the website of her organization, Saving Promise:

L.Y. Marlow is the third generation in her family to have been a victim and survivor of domestic violence: a violence that almost took her life and the life of her unborn child. In her award-winning book, Color Me Butterfly, she tells the poignant and evocative story of four generations of mothers and daughters: the true story of her grandmother, her mother, herself, and her daughter; and the impact intergenerational domestic violence has had on her family for over sixty years.
But the story does not end there. When L.Y. discovered that her 22-year-old daughter and granddaughter, a little girl named Promise, now the fifth generation, were trapped in an abusive relationship, she founded Saving Promise with the intention of saving Promise which blossomed into a vision for the nation.
As a former corporate executive with 20+ years overseeing and executing strategic programs for the government and private sector, L.Y. has combined her corporate expertise and passion for community service into a rewarding career as a social entrepreneur and the visionary behind Saving Promise.
L.Y. is the recipient of numerous Leadership, Engineering, Project Achievement and Advocacy Awards. Her literary work has won multiple awards and accolades including the National Best Books Award. Her sophomore book, A Life Apart (Penguin Random House, April 2014), tells the poignant story of a decades-long interracial love affair between a white sailor and the sister of the black sailor who saved his life at Pearl Harbor.
Regularly featured on national and local TV, radio, blogs, and print, L.Y. is a dedicated and sought after empowerment lecturer and spokeswoman for domestic violence awareness and prevention invited to speak for multiple public and private organizations, including the United Nations, the International Peace Conference and many more. Her authentic voice--an ordinary woman with an extraordinary story and vision--sets her organization and mission apart.
L.Y. is a Project Management Professional-PMP®, a certified Project Manager and holds MBA, BA and AS degrees.

title: a true crime novel
text:
I never got over the ick factor of an author with 40 years journalism experience in television news and newspapers developing a close association with the killer the last ten years of his life.

All of Ross' victims were 14 to 25 years old, he strangled them to death and he confessed to raping all but one of them:
Dzung Ngoc Tu, 25, a Cornell University student, killed May 12, 1981.
Paula Perrera, 16, of Wallkill, N.Y., killed in March, 1982.
Tammy Williams, 17, of Brooklyn, killed Jan. 5, 1982.
Debra Smith Taylor, 23, of Griswold, killed June 15, 1982.
Robin Stavinksy, 19, of Norwich, killed November, 1983.
April Brunias, 14, of Griswold, killed April 22, 1984.
Leslie Shelley, 14, of Griswold, killed April 22, 1984.
Wendy Baribeault, 17, of Griswold, killed June 13, 1984.

Ross was executed in 2005. One of the more notable things I learned was Ross's family tried to stop the execution that Ross had hired a lawyer to hasten. Ross's father made a statement to the press that he didn't believe his son's statement that he wanted to hasten the execution to give closure to his victim's families and spare them further trauma of testimony. His father said he did not believe that his son was capable of compassion

title: A novel of longing to belong
text:
A gut wrenching story of Zal, born blond and fair skinned in Iran, and raised by his mentally daft mother in cage, as a bird, until he is 10 years old. When a adult sister discovers him she puts Zal in the care of a child analyst in hopes he can be integrated into humanity. The analyst adopts Zal and takes him to NYC. The book at this point trends toward magical realism. Zal falls in love with a woman, the woman suffers from panic attacks, anorexia and sees the future. The story also uses the events of Y2k and 9/11 to move the story forward.

The author is of Iranian descent, born in Tehran, Iran and grew up in Pasadena, California, and alumna of Sarah Lawrence College, masters from Johns Hopkins, and teaches at Columbia University NYC and is a regular contributor to The New Yorker. This novel is inspired by the Persian myth/legend of another Zal who was born albino, abandoned on a mountain, and raised by a great bird until he comes of age.
