An author interview in the Baltimore Sun lead me to order the book you can read it online at "After tragedy, Porochista Khakpour develops fanciful fiction".

title: It kind of creeped me out
text: It's like the authors re-imagined the courtship and marriage of Prince William and his wife but changed her from an English heiress to American. If that doesn't bother you, you will find the book to be a hoot but not much more, kind of superficial. Maybe I just wasn't in the mood - it got rave reviews from a variety of sources - I'll try reading it again in a few years.

title: Debut novel
text: I was looking forward to reading this book because, except for the movie the Godfather, the fact that Fidel Castro's government nationalized everyone's property, and the resulting embargo financially ruined an already impoverished country, I know nothing about the people and place. The writing never brought the country alive for me. The author was born in Cuba in 1935 and exiled in 1961 so this is a novel from the heart.

title: Ages 15 to 18
text: I loved it - the teenager not so much - too much romance for the 13 going on 14 year old in the family. Which is probably why I enjoyed it so much.

title: 53 times
text: in 450 pages - the main characters uses in a sentence the words "inner goddess", it proved to be 52 more times than I could take.

title: a mixed bag
text: The title and the cover art caught my eye and lead me to order the book. Let me illustrate the divide in our country in personal terms. My mother and her BFF (both church going christians) had spent the day in NYC spending a couple hundred dollars at lunch and a couple hundred more seeing a Broadway show. For my middle class mother this was a big treat, for her well-to-do friend a non-event. Heading back to their luxury car they passed a man begging, the well to do and sincerely wonderful person said "Get a Job", my mother gave him 5 dollars and and other $5 with apology for her rude friend. LOL. The ultra rich, like Marie Antoinette, are so far removed from the poor in their own country that they can't see that if the person was so mentally ill that they were more capable of pan-handling and living in poverty than having a job. Long story short, this country has no excuse for poverty when we have such wealth, and until government does something about it all the faith based giving will not be enough to conquer it. I had no expectations going into this book but was hoping Senator Dan Coats would have more to offer.

title: This wasn't a pleasure to read.
text: New to me author with a story set in Vermont. 11 year old Ruby and Nessa were what salvaged the book. The mother and father were not who I would want as friends or parents, they are not bad people, they are not people I care about or want to spend time with. Finally the plot elements were so far fetched at times they stretched believability. The ending was hopeful and believable.

title: If you have the time it's a interesting read - but really just one person's view.
text: Time magazine writer who covered the Middle East & Muslim cultures.  I ordered the book after listening to a segment on National Public Radio "Ancient Texts Argue For An Islamic Feminist Movement" you can also read or listen to it on the internet.

title: Ages 14 to 16
text:
15-year-old Phaet is forced enters the military to support her family plunged into poverty when her mother is quarantined when she becomes ill.

The setting, in the far distant future where the moon is a colony of earth.

Some really hard hitting subjects (oppressive government, intolerance, criminal soldiers, secrets and lies, as well as romance) pack some punch into the story that fascinated the 14 year old in our family, however he said the writing was a bit of a slog and the cliff hanger ending was not appreciated.

title: maybe a good movie
text:
In the near future New Jersey has a super collider

Jacob Kelley, a man with a hair trigger temper, is a Philadelphia Main Line academic, with credentials in the high tech research world.

Brian Vanderhall is also physicist, a colleague and a skirt-chaser who works at the supercollider.

To prove a theory, Vanderhall shoot Kelley's wife, Elena - the bullet goes right through her yet she is unscathed. Kelley freaks out and punches Vanderhall.

The book then evolves into a big hot mess, of doppelgangers, murder, jail, secret labs, murder and science fiction creatures, scientific breakthroughs and a Law & Order trial.

title: Fans of Candace Bushnell and Lauren Weisberger might enjoy
text: 40 year old Imogen Tate, is the editor in chief of 'Glossy' magazine. In a riff on the Bette Davis movie 'All About Eve' Imogene returns from medical leave to find her former office assistant, appropriately named Eve, has returned after getting her MBA and turned the magazine into a digital commodity with no room for an editor who who doesn't know what a 'gif' is (I'm ten years older then Imogen, with a career in finance, and I know what a gif is). A bit too far fetched even for satire.  Still it was good fun to see where the authors take the characters.

title: Cornwall cozy mystery
text:
In Willett's latest Cornwall cozy, a trio of aging siblings is threatened--but not enough--by their erstwhile stepbrother.

Brother and sister, Ed and Billa St. Enedoc, live in a renovated former butter factory inherited from their parents.

Dom, is their half brother who lives nearby.

Postcards from France arrive from step brother Tris. That sounds nice until you learn that they haven't seen Tris since Tris's father, Andrew (who was married to Ed & Billa's mother, Elinor), disappeared - 50 YEARS ago!

If that's not enough of a story we also have, Tilly, who is in business with Sarah and both are smitten with Clem the curate.

The story wasn't as gripping as the premise.

title: 50 Shades of Hedda Gabler
text: Throwing in Madame Bovary. Anna is an emotionally fragile woman, whose husband is as neutral as the country he takes her to, Switzerland. There she becomes isolated and out of her element, using sexual interludes to cope. The author's writing is gorgeous - I hope to read more from the author and hopefully with a main character that I can be more interested in.

title: A fascinating character study.
text: a protagonist with "sharp edges and cutthroat ambition", I was so riveted by Ani in all her sadomasochistic glory that I spent the entire evening after getting to the last page reveling via the internet in all things Philadelphia mainline.  28 year old Ani is far from being the luckiest girl alive. My heart boils for what she went through as an outsider in prep school, but she truly is a horrible person - this was such a fascinating novel that I truly am going to think about this for weeks.

title: Daisy's black humor was a winner for me
text: What freaked me out the most was a young woman, 22 years old with breast cancer 5 years later and in remission for 4 years and now at age 27 getting a death diagnosis that cancer had returned in between doctor checkups and her own vigilance so aggressively and with no symptoms leaving her with less than 4 months to live - that is terrifying. In comparison to that shocker the story of young Daisy trying to cope by finding someone to love her husband in the little time she has was rather unreadable. It probably didn't help that I kept thinking of the Doris Day - Rock Hudson - Tony Randell comedy where Rock is married to Doris (Tony Randell is the comedy foil) and Rock is a hypochondriac who thinks he's dying, and attempts to find a future husband for Doris, with accompanying hilarity.

title: It never carried me away
text: The lame cover should have warned me. I've never been to Nebraska, nor remember reading a novel set there, so that was fun for me as a reader. It was a long 3 weeks in the office and I was ripe for a romance, even one about a college age couple floundering in life. Still, a romance about a 3rd year dropout with on-demand social anxiety disorder never grew on me.

title: Ages 14 to 16
text:
In book #1, 16 year old Anya lives in the fairy Kingdom of Chrior and is engaged to marry the super nice Davic. Trouble begins when her aunt, the Queen, chooses Anya as her heir instead of her cousin, Illumina. Anya freely travels from the fae world to the human world of Warckum in search of the queen's half-human son Zabriel who has been gone for 2 years. While there she is attacked, resulting in the loss of her wings and thus her magic. Anya is is helped by a human family and becomes BFFs with the family's daughter, Shea, who ends up joining Anya in her quest. A thriller that left readers with a cliff-hanger ending.

In this 2nd book in the series now 17 year old Anya is in for more of the same as in the first book with another cliffhanger ending. My recommendation is to wait a year until the next book is out and then read them both - you'll be happier if you do.

The 13 year old in our family gobbled it up - I thought there was too much violence and dragged in places.

title: New to me author
text: So I had zero expectations. The book is a series of stories centered around an Italian wife, Josephine, beginning in 1888 when she is 14 and is married to a 25 year old who leaves for America 3 days after their wedding is consummated then one paragraph, and 9 years, later he sends for her. The chapters that follow give you vignettes of her life and the lives of her 7 children and grandchildren stretching to 1974. One thing that surprised me was the amount of sex (more than many romances) and that each of the episodes were nothing I would want to live through. I thought this was going to be a book along the lines of Barbara Taylor Bradford's A Woman of Substance, and while the author is as good a writer I did not get as engaged with the characters or story.

title: Not enough
text: A debut that is not funny enough, not despairing enough, not sexy enough, not original enough, not deep enough, not frivolous enough. Just as Giovanni had nothing if he couldn't mimic, the book never gave me enough reason to be be swept up in the story. The novel has been a hit with other reviewers so perhaps it is an acquired taste.

title: Nice
text: I have never heard of Wayne Dyer, so his daughter's (#6 of 8) book about her father's life work (his huge hit came out in 2001 the year he divorced his wife) was entertaining - I enjoyed it and am glad I spent the time to read it.

title: Ages 16 and up
text:
a rollicking adventure circa 1823 about a young man growing to manhood among the Native Americans of the Plains. I think you would call it a 'rousing yarn', if you don't check the facts you should have fun with it.

BOOK #1 - THE BLOOD OATH - Young Matthew O 'Malley returns from a day of hunting to find his mother killed and his family farm in flames. He leaves for the plains of Kansas, determined to seek blood and revenge. Blood he finds, indeed. He joins an unusual band of men who want a quiet place where they can live and forget the war. But there is nothing quiet about Kansas just after the Civil War. Matthew and his new friends create the first Texas cattle drive, build a hotel, own a farm, teach school, and fight to the death for what is theirs. Then Matt meets Lee. She can drive a stagecoach, shoot with either hand, and ride a wild horse. When Falcon Beck, Matt's blood enemy, swears to have Lee as his own, Matthew faces a test of courage and commitment that will determine whether he lives or dies.

BOOK#2 - THUNDER MOUNTAIN - action-packed adventures of Matthew O'Malley continue in this second installment of The O'Malley Saga. Matt and his brothers have moved their cattle west to Storm King Mountain (called Thunder Mountain by the Utes), and there they try to rescue a woman who has been taken hostage by a band of renegades. Matt is also having problems with his girlfriend, Lee, who is jealous of one of Matt's other lady friends. (Whether or not she has cause to be jealous is not exactly clear.)
During a deadly attack on Storm King Ranch, Matt comes face-to-face with his blood enemies Macon Beck and Nathan Kurlow. As the bullets fly, Matt and the rest of the O'Malley family fight for their lives.

BOOK #3 - PAHGOSA - The O'Malley clan has always bonded together when trouble is on the horizon. So when the Burdett gang threatens young Tom O'Malley and his sweetheart Lee Conall, his cousins, uncles and brothers come from all over to help.
The first run-in with the Burdett gang started over a puppy that Tom rescued. In an act of revenge the Burdett gang attacked some of the O'Malleys' friends and war was declared between the two rivals. Burdett begins to gather his ne'er-do-wells as the O'Malleys catch wind of the forthcoming trouble. From all over the Midwest and as far as California and Boston, the O'Malley clan bands together to defend their name and bring justice to the Burdett crew.

title: Wonderful premise - Debut author
text:
I am a sucker for a good historical romance. While this novel didn't sweep me up in the passion of Helen and Wils or the beauty of the magical Christmas of 1914 when the men on the killing fields called an all too brief truce to celebrate the magic of Christmas - I can see by the other reviews that the novel was a hit for other readers.

The author has a lovely intro to the book (you can find on the web) "Allegra Jordan: Love and war in the early 1900" in USA TODAY August 29, 2014 and also "7 Fascinating But Forgotten Facts From World War I" on 08/26/2014.

title: Teens, Vampires, witches, wizards and Irish Druids
text:
This is book 3, in a so far 5 book, paranormal YA series. The first 3 have at their center High School Seniors Tristan & Savannah, the next two books focus elsewhere. I recommend reading the first two books (summaries below) before beginning book 3. CONSUME is more character driven then the first two books, those looking for the action of CRAVE and COVET may be disappointed.

COVET - Enhanced Author's Edition, book 2 in The Clann Series: Word Length: 134,000 words; 23,000 extra words of bonus content & 20 photos: Dangerous to be together. Painful to be apart. Savannah Colbert knows she broke up with Tristan Coleman for the right reasons. Most of all, to keep from killing him with her new vampire abilities. But try telling her heart. Now, lost in a sea of hostile Clann faces, Sav tries to come to terms with what she's becoming and what that means for her future. And that someone is doing their best to bully her into making a terrible mistake. Tristan can't believe Sav won't even talk to him. If being apart is her decision, fine. Just don't expect him to honor it. But even as he prepares to fight for the girl he loves, forces beyond their control take them both in directions neither could have foreseen or prepared for. A reckoning is coming, and not everyone will survive. (This enhanced version of Covet features 168 bonus content items, including exclusive never-before-published deleted scenes and tons of fun, conversational commentary from the author explaining her real life experiences that inspired certain scenes, her celebrity actor picks for each main character, as well as detailed background information, photos, maps and website links to give you an insider's view of the real life historical and infamous locations and organizations that much of this story was set within and based upon. This special multimedia version of Covet has been designed so that it can still be read on any device that can read other Kindle ebooks, as well as to allow readers maximum uninterrupted enjoyment of the story with subtle links throughout that will take you to the bonus content only when you are ready to access it. Not interested in reading the bonus content? No problem! Simply ignore the small bonus content links buried within the main story's text! You can always go back later and read the bonus content when you're ready to. Also included are an author question and answer section and playlist, both of which are accessible directly from the interactive table of contents.)

CRAVE; The Clann Series 1 Enhanced Author's Edition Word Length: 120,000 words has an extra 18,000 words & 32 photos in bonus content Forbidden to Love: "Doomed to Fail. Savannah Colbert has never known why she's so hated by the kids of the Clann, a powerful group of families rumored to be modern day witches and wizards descended from Irish druids. Nor can she deny her instinct to get close to Clann golden boy Tristan Coleman. Especially when she recovers from a strange illness and the attraction becomes nearly irresistible. It's as if he's a magnet, pulling her gaze, her thoughts, even her dreams. Her family has warned her to have nothing to do with him, or any members of the Clann. But when Tristan is suddenly everywhere she goes, Savannah fears she's destined to fail. For years, the Clann has forbidden Tristan, its future leader, from even speaking to Savannah. Then Savannah disappears from school for a week and comes back... different, and suddenly he can't stay away. Boys seem intoxicated just from making eye contact with her. His own family and the Clann's members become stricter than ever. And Tristan has to fight his own urge to protect her, to be near her no matter the consequences. (The Enhanced Author's Edition version of Crave features over 200 bonus content items, including exclusive never-before-published deleted scenes and tons of fun, conversational commentary from the author explaining her real life experiences that inspired certain scenes, her celebrity actor picks for each main character, as well as detailed background information, photos, maps and website links to give you an insider's view of the real life historical and infamous locations and organizations that much of this story was set within and based upon. This special interactive version of Crave has been designed so that it can still be read on any device that can read other ebooks, as well as to allow readers maximum uninterrupted enjoyment of the story with subtle links throughout that will take you to the bonus content only when you are ready to access it. Not interested in reading the bonus content? No problem! Simply ignore the small bonus content links buried within the main story's text! You can always go back later and read the bonus content when you're ready to. Also included are an author question and answer section and playlist, both of which are accessible directly from the interactive table of contents. Get ready to immerse yourself in the world of The Clann Series like you've never seen it before with the Enhanced Author's Edition of Crave!")

I very much enjoyed the author speak about her book, you can find it here "Interview: Consume (The Clann #3) by Melissa Darnell Posted by Diayll - MotherGamerWriter on Aug 16, 2013"

title: fascinating
text:
"shocked at the adversity a young mother faces with a newborn," no fooling? Really? Did the author not read anything or talk to anyone before having her baby? If you are prone to drama you may love this novel and the author's journey through the first few years of parenthood. The one nice thing the author can look forward to is the child will be less dependent on her because he is away from her in the care of the grandparents and father.

Each chapter is a different Phenomena, so even new moms can read a chapter - when you can snatch 15 minutes for yourself. My sister gave up reading for 18 years - it wasn't until the child was in college that she finally had free time again (she also carried a full time job outside the home).

I would have enjoyed a longer author reading on youtube "Leigh Ann Henion reads from Phenomenal at #siba14" - but I really enjoyed hearing the author read from her work.

title: Published under the name of FRACTURED in the UK
text: Terrific melodrama. It's not that the story was unbelievable. I guessed the premise pretty quickly. It's the characters. Even the secondary characters act oddly. I think the author and reader would have benefited by a stronger editor to guide this debut author. I would like to go into a description but I think any specifics would give the story away. I really wanted to like this novel, the premise was awesome, it didn't pan out for me.

title: Kitty Kelley could not have written a more salacious book
text:
I am glad to have read this newest biography however it is investigative journalism at it trashiest. Having read [[ASIN:0226583570 Portrait of a Marriage: Vita Sackville-West and Harold Nicolson]] by Sackville-West's son I was looking for a new biography on this dynamo of a woman.

One that would offer a more academic look at her childhood and childhood home Knole, her youth, her writing, her friendships, her family, her old age, her social life, her home, her gardens. While I got some of that, I was looking for more. What I did get was a lot of her romances with other women, and while very interesting and important, it wasn't enough to make this into the great book I had been looking for.

I'll have to try [[ASIN:0688041116 Vita: The Life of V. Sackville-West]] even though it was written 32 years ago.

title: Debut novel of an epically dysfunctional family
text:
Like a Greek Tragedy this novel plays out. Translated in 2010 from Dutch to English and first published in Holland. This story is all over the place, literally. It alternates between narrators and country's Belgium, California, the Netherlands, and Shanghai.

Siem Sigerius, a professor of mathematics and judo champion, at one time living on Bonita Avenue in Berkeley, California now chancellor of a university in the Netherlands. Siem see's his oldest step-daughter, Joni, in a porno movie he is watching after he is dumped by his lover, a student, when he will not divorce his wife. Alrighty then. His oldest daughter's boyfriend, Aaron, is like the son he never had; the son he did have is a one that parental nightmares are made of. Believe it or not, there is a lot more, but that would spoil the suspense.

title: New to me author
text:
Queenie Hennessy, from the author's "The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry", in her own love story. I had two strikes against me, first I didn't read the first book (and you must because so much is wrapped in that first novel), and second you have to like the books of Nicholas Sparks (which I don't). Queenie St. Bernadine’s Hospice in northeast England, can no longer talk due to a tumor, but is able to communicate through writing, writing to Harold who she hasn't seen in 20 years. While I couldn't enjoy the story as much as other readers I did like learning about Queenie.

favorite quote “You don’t have to keep being the thing you have become. It is never too late.”

An article on the internet "Q&A with Rachel Joyce, author of The Love Song of Miss Queenie Hennessy" shed some light on the novel.

this recap of the first book may help: "Meet Harold Fry, recently retired. He lives in a small English village with his wife, Maureen, who seems irritated by almost everything he does. Little differentiates one day from the next. Then one morning a letter arrives, addressed to Harold in a shaky scrawl, from a woman he hasn’t heard from in twenty years. Queenie Hennessy is in hospice and is writing to say goodbye. But before Harold mails off a quick reply, a chance encounter convinces him that he absolutely must deliver his message to Queenie in person. In his yachting shoes and light coat, Harold Fry embarks on an urgent quest. Determined to walk six hundred miles to the hospice, Harold believes that as long as he walks, Queenie will live. A novel of charm, humor, and profound insight into the thoughts and feelings we all bury deep within our hearts, The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry introduces Rachel Joyce as a wise—and utterly irresistible—storyteller."

title: Crime, Christians & Quilts
text: This new to me author packs a lot of story in less than 200 pages. I would have liked this more as a romance if it hadn't seemed rushed to me - it kind of creeped me out the detective was attracted to someone who is helpless, lying in a hospital, who has been brutality beaten and her mother murdered in front of her. As a police procedural or mystery it was gritty and had more violence than I would expect from a Christian novel, I would rather read about love over violence any day. As for the characters back story it turned implausible very early when we learn that the main character is a 21 year old gymnast heading to her first Olympics, I just found it unbelievable. The series is very popular so I will try another title to enjoy. The novelist incorporated faith into the story throughout which should please faith based readership.

title: Ages 18 & up, unless you don't mind your child reading about someone being burned alive
text:
12,000 years ago humans were created by other beings, the sky people, and once their utility to the sky people was finished the sky people left, but foretold that they would return at the time of armageddon. At the armageddon the 12 cultures they created would battle in an ENDGAME to capture 3 keys left by the sky people, the victors would have life and the others would not. Generation after generation, the 12 cultures have cultivated the best of the best for THE ENDGAME. Terrifyingly the time has come with the advent of 12 meteorites striking the earth - each containing instructions on the first step in the quest to find the keys. Trouble is, the Endgame is battled by teenagers, ages 13 to 19 - meaning 11 out of 12 teens will be dead by the end of book 3. Meaning the fate of over 90% of the worlds population hangs on the actions of one teenager. That's a toughie.

The story may be right up your alley. I recommend reading the free sample and see if the prose appeals.

If you are intrigued by the story, the author has worked with Google+ Niantic and developed an ARG (Alternate Reality Game) tie in to the series, with the target being tens of thousands of players in the same game world.

There is also a shot at $500,000 in gold if you can spot clues in the book, solve the puzzle, locate the website and spend months working through the website to the key to the gold. The author estimates someone will find the key by the end of 2015 - as of this date a winner has not been announced.

The author is an interesting fellow which you can read more on by searching his name.

title: Ages 17 and up - #2 in a trilogy Fantasy Epic from Christian publisher Thomas Nelson  (#1 is Angel Eyes)
text:
This is one of those books without a lot of back story so to get the most enjoyment I recommend reading book #1. The writing is exceptional and it was only the shifting Point of View that I found disconcerting. Demon Damien, is a former angel (murder and child sex trafficking are his specialties) introduced in Angel Eyes. Not a book I would delight in seeing my teenager reading, too dark. Stratus is a small town where human, angels and demons co-exist.

Romantic couple Brielle and Jake are High School seniors who live there, protected by their "shield angels" (Canaan and Helene) . Jake also has the power to heal and Brielle can see through the Terrestrial Veil to the Celestial world. The trouble starts when Damien implores Lucifer aka The Prince of Darkness to get involved. Brielle's widowed recovering alcoholic father is enthralled in a relationship from Hades (literally). to tell you more would give too much of the plot away.

Book one "ANGEL EYES" summary: Once you've seen, you can't unsee. Everything changes when you've looked at the world through, ANGEL EYES. Brielle went to the city to chase her dreams and found tragedy instead. She's come home to shabby little Stratus, Oregon, to live with her grief and her guilt and the incredible, numbing cold she can't seem to shake. Jake's the new guy at school. The boy next door with burning hands and an unbelievable gift that targets him for corruption. Something more than fate has brought them together. An evil bigger than both of them lurks in the shadows nearby, hiding in plain sight. Two angels stand guard, unsure what's going to happen. And a beauty brighter than Jake or Brielle has ever seen is calling them to join the battle in a realm where all human choices start. A realm that only angels and demons, and Brielle, can perceive.

title: A 400 page epilogue to the 1500 page, 3 volume, series
text:
Set in the middle ages circa 1241-1242 and featuring the Russian Hero Alexander Nevsky and the epic Battle on the Ice (Lake Peipus). Being a history buff this novel was perfectly too my taste. I highly recommend anyone who hasn't read the preceding 3 novels to go to the website 'Foreworld' and take advantage of all the info there. I plan to read the 3 earlier titles too. Being new to the series, a more in-depth 'Cast of Characters' profile at the front of the novel would have helped tremendously.

Not having read any of the preceding titles I looked them up so I wouldn't be completely lost - I include them below for anyone like me who are new to the series. FYI, The Mongoliad series began as a social media experiment, combining serial story-telling with interaction between authors and audience during the creative process. Since its original iteration, The Mongoliad has been restructured, edited, and rewritten under the supervision of its authors to create a more cohesive reading experience and was published as a trilogy of novels.

THE MONGOLOID BOOK ONE published September 2012: An epic-within-an-epic, taking place in 13th century. In it, a small band of warriors and mystics raise their swords to save Europe from a bloodthirsty Mongol invasion. Inspired by their leader (an elder of an order of warrior monks), they embark on a perilous journey and uncover the history of hidden knowledge and conflict among powerful secret societies that had been shaping world events for millennia. But the saga reaches the modern world via a circuitous route. In the late 19th century, Sir Richard F. Burton, an expert on exotic languages and historical swordsmanship, is approached by a mysterious group of English martial arts aficionados about translating a collection of long-lost manuscripts. Burton dies before his work is finished, and his efforts were thought lost until recently rediscovered by a team of amateur archaeologists in the ruins of a mansion in Trieste, Italy. From this collection of arcana, the incredible tale of The Mongoliad was recreated. Full of high adventure, unforgettable characters, and unflinching battle scenes, The Mongoliad ignites a dangerous quest where willpower and blades are tested and the scope of world-building is redefined. *** The Kindle edition has bonus material: an illustrated character glossary, a Foreworld map, and 'Sinner', a prequel to the Mongoliad series.

THE MONGOLOID BOOK TWO published September 2012: The aftermath of the world-shattering Mongolian invasion of 1241 and the difficult paths undertaken by its most resilient survivors. The Shield Brethren, an order of warrior monks, search for a way to overthrow the horde, even as the invaders take its members hostage. Forced to fight in the Mongols' Circus of Swords, Haakon must prove his mettle or lose his life in the ring. His bravery may impress the enemy, but freedom remains a distant dream. Father Rodrigo receives a prophecy from God and believes it's his mission to deliver the message to Rome. Though a peaceful man, he resigns himself to take up arms in the name of his Lord. Joining his fight to save Christendom are the hunter Ferenc, orphan Ocyrhoe, healer Raphael, and alchemist Yasper, each searching for his place in history. Deftly blending fact and fantasy, with the indomitable will to survive against immense odds. *** the Kindle edition features an illustrated character glossary, a Foreworld map, and 'Dreamer', a prequel to the Mongoliad series.

The Mongoloid Book Three published February 2013: The personal stories of medieval freedom fighters to form an epic, imaginative recounting of a moment in history when a world in peril relied solely on the courage of its people. The shadow of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II hangs over the shattered Holy Roman Church as the cardinals remain deadlocked, unable to choose a new pope. Only the Binders and a mad priest have a hope of uniting the Church against the invading Mongol host. An untested band of young warriors stands against the dissolute Khan, fighting for glory and freedom in the Khan's sadistic circus of swords, and the brave band of Shield-Brethren who set out to stop the Mongol threat single-handedly race against their nemesis before he can raise the entire empire against them. Veteran knight Feronantus, haunted by his life in exile, leads the dwindling company of Shield-Brethren to their final battle, molding them into a team that will outlast him. No good hero lives forever. Or fights alone.

title: Sequel to 'No Child of Mine' (2012),
text:
Former British social worker Alex Lake/Charlotte Nicholls has fled England for gorgeous and remote New Zealand (the land of the Lord of the Rings and Xena) after abducting 3 year old Ottilie Wade, who she now calls Chloe, from a horribly abusive home (pedophile father and schizophrenic mother who was subsequently murdered by the father), after the authorities failed to help. Adding to that is Alex/Charlotte birth mother, Anna, who is now in her life.

I needed a lot more Alex/Charlotte time with Ottilie/Chloe to make the story emotionally satisfying.

Excellent Book Club choice.

NO CHILD OF MINE: Alex Lake’s life is centered on helping people. Her job as a social worker in a British seaside town is more than a career: It’s the very essence of who she is. And though there are frustrations, Alex takes to heart the rewards of placing a child in a safe and loving home. But when she encounters three-year-old Ottilie Wade, Alex is completely unprepared for the effect the sweet, shy little girl has on her. Though on the surface Ottilie seems to want for nothing—she’s perfectly healthy and lives in a very nice home—she’s mysteriously silent and asocial. Alex knows that something is not right in the Wade house. And the deeper she looks into the case, the more Alex comes to feel that she and Ottilie are being drawn together by fate. As disturbing evidence mounts and Alex’s superiors seem unwilling to help, Alex knows she will have to risk everything—her job and the life she loves—to save Ottilie. But Alex will also have to wrestle the demons of her own past before she can secure a future for this child in need.

title: Gets going about 100 pages in
text:
New to me author. I loved the premise. I didn't know it was written for the "New Adult' genre, which I have not been for 30 years, however I clearly remember when I was. The story had great promise for me but what killed it was 24 year old Daniel 'Ty' Tyler's attitude to his ex girlfriend. They were both teenagers not looking for marriage or kids when they got pregnant. She goes through with the pregnancy, for his sake, while he thinks negatively of her for not wanting to raise the child with him. Get over it Ty - let it go. In the end it just didn't deliver the emotional oomph, I never really felt the deep love from 20 year old Nadia I come to expect from a romance title, maybe more character development - more showing and less telling?

I Want It That Way (2B Trilogy #1),
As Long As You Love Me (2B Trilogy, #2),
The Shape of My Heart (2B Trilogy #3)

what sold me was the author interview you can find on youtube "BEA 2014 Podcast: Ann Aguirre on I Want It That Way"

title: Not a Detective Maria Kallio novel
text:
Leena Lehtolainen is Finland's bestselling female crime author, her series starring feisty detective Maria Kallio is compelling and always a must read. This is a new trilogy that the author explains "questions identity and concealment. Who is each person really? What disguise is each person using? What does it mean to be family? Who is on whose side? Who can be trusted? What is each person's price? Who is each person willing either to betray or to save?" That is a lot of asks.

The mystery thriller aspect comes secondary to the expose on the main character, Hilja Ilveskero, with the other characters stereotypes and cookie cutter stock, also having the story told to the reader by the main character made the novel a hard sell for me. The wrap up and the last chapter were disappointing and kinda lame. I will try the 2nd in the trilogy just to see if the author's story telling returns to form.

title: #1 of 13 in The Sullivan Series published as an ebook in 2011
text:
"emotional, sexy and fun contemporary romance" - sounded great to me. But the author lost me early when Chloe is masturbating in a bathtub (the sexy part?) in a guest house and Chase walks in watches (the contemporary part?) then they both laugh about it (the fun part?). The romance part could have brought me back in but there wasn't any - it was just BAM! we love each other. I have been reading romance since Kathleen Woodiwiss was fade to black, and Bertrice Small since The Kadin and Sky O'Mally, so I know sexy and I know romance. While this is the author's 1st Sullivan book I think it is the author's 13th written novel. I'll try another before I move on because so many readers rate the storyteller so highly.

I found a fascinating article from 2011 in the Washington Post where the author and her novels are featured "Novel rejected? There's an e-book gold rush!"

title: Ages 9-11
text:
My 9 year old thought the graphics were wonderful. Fight to the death between Nnewts (think frogs) and Lizzarks (think reptile).

Herk is a young Nnewt (a tadpole), the Lizzarks invade and there is violence galore ending with Herk's escape after his mother's brutal death.

Think of Herk as Bambi and the Lizzarks as Darth Vader and you get the gist of the story. It gets worse when we learn of the evil Snake Lord, who magically disabled Herk!

A couple disappoints colored the 9 year old's reading, frustration at plot points never followed and the introduction of a storyline without a resolution to the original.

title: debut author of lesbian romance
text:
Kate is a surgical nurse who has raised her niece, Megan, for the last 10 years. She is also a deeply closeted lesbian, so sexually repressed she allows only work and Megan in her life.
Megan's mother, Kate's sister, died tragically young when Megan was 8 years old.
Tommie is a sportswriter Megan works for as an intern, she's also a lesbian who has played the field, think George Clooney, and is only 11 years older than Megan. By the end of chapter one you understand she also has the libido of an 18 year old boy.

Terrific premise, this is not a lighthearted read and there is a good amount of angst up til the end. Not so much a romance (up until the last 10 pages) as a turning point in everyone's life. The main conflict is that Tommie believes Kate is straight so they dance around each other for most of the book. At 260+ pages it's a good size read and yet I was needing more in the way of character development, maybe what I needed was less plot and more people profile.

One thing I really felt bad about was Kate worrying about paying for Megan;s college tuition, as the most coveted surgical nurse on staff I figured she would be pulling down at least $77 thousand a year by now. I am guessing that Megan's mom had no life insurance *sigh*

title: Excellent Book Club Choice
text:
Young Adult book. Told as a memoir looking back at her high School years from 1975 to 1979 (and flashing back even further to the events of her childhood where by her 6th birthday she was already emotionally traumatized). Topsy Turvey. That's how I felt reading this novel. It opens with a fascinating chapter. Then the rest of the book seemed too unbelievable for me ie the Fairy Godfather (who I thought was terrific). I think the teens and their dialogue were more mature than I remember being at that age so it just felt off. And I guess it bothered me that Ella's relationship with her mother and father were never explored in depth. While I am lucky to have read this, I can't say I would recommend it, but I would love to be in a book club that discusses it.

From the author's website:
"The Story Thief is a beautifully accomplished multi-level coming of age novel, a quietly building, powerful story that will resonate with anyone reading its pages, whatever age they may be. Some of the finest work being published today is in the young adult world of books, and in my book The Story Thief belongs there among the best of them ... an insightful, wise, tender, altogether wonderful novel that captures the confusion and terrors and triumphs of teenage years, and best of all, beautifully depicts that most difficult of all quests, the discovery and acceptance of our own personal identity."
- Katherine V. Forrest, LAMBDA award-winner and author of Curious Wine and the Kate Delafield mysteries

title: Debut author
text: From New York City, during the Great Depression, to the southern coast of England, Nazis, Lesbian Romance, Reincarnation, ghosts and a murder whodunit - this novel is action packed. The author's writing style is very picturesque. I look forward to her next novel, I think I would have liked this one more if it had less elements, or another 300 pages.

title: Ages 9 to 12
text:
11 year old Albert Flynn his father sends him into a forest to deliver a letter, simple enough until ends up on a journey to the center of the Earth. He is inducted as a "Balance Keeper" the 'guardians of the underworld' where tokens create super powers and monsters are part of a battle that can destroy them all. Albert joins with other Balance Keepers, Leroy and Birdie, in this adventure story.

The nine year old found it boring and the 12 year old isn't interested in reading more in the series.

title: Debut author from Austria
text: Set in a town south of Salzburg, a dead woman is found at the bottom of a ravine - tattooed on her body are longitude and latitude leading Det. Beatrice Kaspary and Florin Wenninger to a gruesome find containing further coordinates. The suspense is killer (pardon the pun) and worse the psychopath is texting Kaspary in a game that surprised me in the end. The pacing was a bit slow and the characters a tad one dimensional. Will try the author again as the premise was a winner.

title: Stella!
text: Tells us her story (and the ending is action packed!), how she valiantly fought to keep her groove pure. How she was terribly beaten by her father (who is thankfully terminally ill). How her new husband, Kade, will be taking over the clan when her father dies. It was questionable to me that Kade would care for Stella so quickly and intensely that he vows not consummate their marriage until Stella is ready (I didn't know they grew highlanders like that). Kade is one of the fiercest warriors in the highlands so it was touching to see how gentle he was in wooing Stella. The situation is a toughie because Stella had already developed a crush on the blacksmith in her father's employ. The big surprise for me was how totally turned on Stella is when her husband gets aggressive in their marital bed (I hope she has a safe word!), it just seemed creepy after a lifetime of abuse. hmmmmm. And don't me started about Stella's wretched sisters, the most despicable being Maisie.

title: Best to read book #2 OUT OF FOCUS first
text:
because it really is the first half of this novel. I enjoyed the murder mystery more than the romance. For me the romance was a bit undeveloped, I liked Cody more than Kasey. I don't know as I will be reading the rest of the series, I never got wrapped up enough in the story, maybe it was me - over 300 readers loved it.

If you haven't read the first book sin the series these summaries from the publisher may help in your enjoyment:

SWEET TEA AND SECRETS, is the first in the Adams Grove series (2011): Adams Grove, Virginia, where the worst crime to hit the small town in a decade was hunters bagging too many deer. So when word gets out about a break-in over at Pearl Clemmons's place, the townsfolk go on high alert, locking their doors and firing up the rumor mill. Adams Grove is mourning the loss of Pearl Clemmons, known for her award-winning Chocolate Pecan Pie and the best unsolicited advice in the county. When Jill returns to settle her grandmother's estate, she's greeted by a Clydesdale-sized guardian dog who doesn't seem to be earning his stripes (although he drools on them pretty well), and Garrett Malloy, the ex-fiancé she left behind a year ago. Jill insists on staying at Pearl's amidst a string of break-ins that have sleepy Adams Grove wide awake and locking its doors. Jill's past with Garrett becomes the least of her worries when she learns that she is the only person standing between a desperate conman and a secret from Pearl's past. Will Pearl's past kill any chance of Jill and Garrett's future together? Pearl's granddaughter Jill certainly has enough on her plate, what with tending to Pearl's estate and coming face-to-face with sexier-than-sin Garrett Malloy. Also known as: The Man Who Broke Her Heart. But now that she has to contend with no-count thieves, everyone agrees she can use all the help she can get. Somebody thinks Pearl had something worth stealing, and it's clear they'll stop at nothing to get it - even if it means hurting Jill. Now, with Garrett's help, Jill just might have a chance of unearthing Pearl's secrets...as well as her own deep, conflicted desire for her ex. Garrett may have been the last man Jill wanted to see, but now, she may not want to let him go.

#2 OUT OF FOCUS (2011): Kasey Phillips thought her biggest problem was deciding whether to photograph Cody Tuggle's honky-tonkin' tour, until an accident on Route 58 claims the life of her husband. Hurricane Ernesto threatens the region. In a desperate race against time they search for Kasey's three-year-old son who is missing from the wreckage. The community and friends rally to help, but someone knows more than they are telling.

#3 WEDDING CAKE AND BIG MISTAKES (2013): For years, Carolanne Baxter dreamed of a life beyond Adams Grove. Being the daughter of the town drunk was no picnic, so when college offered her a chance for escape, she took it. Now Carolanne has returned home, finally ready to make amends with her father, Ben, and to celebrate the wedding of her best friends Jill and Garrett. Of course, the fact that Connor Buckham, her sexy new law partner and Garrett's best man, happens to be the same guy the town matchmaker named as Carolanne's perfect match...well! That's just icing on the cake. But Carolanne's hopes for a fresh start are dashed when a dead body surfaces during Jill and Garrett's wedding reception...and Ben Baxter becomes the prime suspect. The murder throws the town into uproar, threatening to destroy the tentative peace between father and daughter--and to derail the budding romance between Carolanne and Connor. Has the matchmaker's perfect streak come to end? Or will the truth finally bring Carolanne the happy ending she's dreamed of for so long?

#4 PECAN PIE AND DEADLY LIES (2013):

#5 MINT JULEPS AND JUSTICE (2014): All the four-leaf clovers in the world couldn't make Brooke Justice feel lucky these days. When her soon-to-be ex refuses to stay out of her business, she decides a fresh start will turn her luck around. She retreats to the small town of Adams Grove, Virginia. But when someone breaks into her new home, she immediately suspects her ex. Frightened for her safety, Brooke calls a private investigator - but she doesn't expect her whole body to tingle when he asks if she needs his protection. For years, Mike Hartman refused to let love into his life. Still reeling from a devastating loss, he never expected to fall for a client. Yet the more time he spends with Brooke, the more he grows to care for her. And when her life is put in danger, Mike knows he must act quickly - before history tragically repeats itself.

#6 BARBECUE AND BAD NEWS (AVAILABLE 2/2015): Savannah Dey politely agreed to attend her ex-husband's wedding, but she'd be grateful for any reason to get out of it...which is why the speeding ticket from the handsome sheriff of Adams Grove is both a surprise and a reprieve. With one quick call to her editor, the aspiring columnist finds herself with a new assignment and the perfect excuse to get closer to the man who pulled her over. Now, all she needs is a way to deal with all the bad memories the small town dredges up... Sheriff Scott Calvin can't forget the woman who set off his radar, but he's determined to send Savannah on her way. He's done making bad choices, and this beautiful city gal is sure to leave Adams Grove once she finishes her story. By the time she's stirred up a hornet's nest, he's already falling for her. Will trouble bind them together, or will her secrets tear them apart?

title: was hoping for more after reading good reviews for the first book in the series
text:
I thought it was going to be a Charming Romance & a Compelling Cozy Mystery set in a small town in Virginia. I got the small town but I never felt the very mild romance and the mystery was almost a footnote - I would say give this a pass and get the first in the series.

#3 WEDDING CAKE AND BIG MISTAKES (2013):

#4 PECAN PIE AND DEADLY LIES (2013): America's beloved country superstar Cody Tuggle never expected to be one of America's most wanted. At least that's how he feels since he's been accused of murdering his scheming agent. Desperate to prove he's innocent, he turns to his only alibi, award-winning photographer Kasey Phillips, who recently toured with him and his band. After an exciting life on the road, Kasey has settled down in small-town Adams Grove with her five-year-old son. Unexpectedly reunited with Cody, she finds herself open to love again. But just when she's ready to fall, everything she ever believed about him is called in to question, and she's faced with more than just being his alibi. Cody has waited a long time for genuine love, and he can't let this chance with Kasey slip away. But as the evidence stacks up, the accusations against him put a damper on the sparks flying between them. Can he convince Kasey he's innocent, and will she clear his name in time? Or will their dreams of the future be the victim of a deadly lie?

Will trouble bind them together, or will her secrets tear them apart?

title: What a train wreck!
text: A religious (catholic) family is tested to the limits. I felt sorry for everyone involved but really, Mary brought it all on herself. It seems a shame she has this wonderful life but has lived in fear of losing it all for over ten years. I can see why she kept her secret, she should have put it behind her or confessed before she married Tom. She did neither and now everyone suffers. Like a Lifetime movie of the week.

title: Erotic Lesbian Drama
text:
first third is angst the rest is erotica. Olivia is a lawyer, Micah her hazel eyed (you won't forget this because it is mentioned 42 times) intern. When Micah's grandmother dies she turns to Olivia for emotional comfort, Micah channels her crush on Olivia into a physical kiss. Olivia, while returning the attraction, recognizes the impropriety of a relationship with her intern - things get ugly and Micah disappears for a year.

WOW!

looking for a little more? find an author interview by searching "The Liz McMullen Show Episode 46".

I found further info on the authors' web page when I was looking for a picture of Micah (because she was never clear to me):

"When Olivia Holden first met Micah Connolly, she knew it was a bad idea to take her on as an intern at her law firm. The intelligent and darkly handsome young woman reminded her that there was more to life than work, and less in her life than she wished she had. She really shouldn't have led the young intern on, not when she knew she couldn't act on her desires, but she also couldn't let her just walk out the door and out of her life either. Besides, the rules were about to change. With her father's pending retirement, the strict rules laid out by the senior Holden would no longer keep her from telling Micah just how much she wanted her. The only problem was, she never got a chance to.
Micah Connolly had spent most of her life trying to please others, starting with her family, and ending with Olivia Holden. When she found out that her beloved grandmother had passed away, she was bereft and sought solace with the only other person she thought might offer her comfort. Olivia Holden was full of mixed messages, none of them clear, but most of them leaning towards a keen interest in Micah. Their first kiss was a disaster, overwrought with emotion. She had let things get out of hand. She had meant to tell Olivia she had to go home and get her grandmother's affairs in order, but instead, the night ended in a volatile exchange of words that sent Micah running.
Well over a year had passed since that fateful night, and Olivia still regretted her strict adherence to a set of rules that had made her lose the one woman she felt she could love. Chance and fate changed everything when she recognized Micah weaving her bike wildly through the busy streets of New York. Olivia had expected to find her practicing law somewhere, not working as a lowly bike messenger. It didn't matter, though; she had found Micah again, and she had to at least try.
When Micah and Olivia finally meet again, it isn't your standard happy reunion. Micah had changed, a lot. She was darker, edgier, and carried herself with an air of experience that Olivia found intriguing. This new Micah also wasn't the sort who let Olivia take charge of their budding relationship. Micah had found herself, and found out a lot about herself over the last year, including a great deal of things that she wasn't so sure the high-powered attorney would be game for. A subtle and erotic game of power play ensues, with Olivia discovering just how much she enjoys giving up control for a change. Just how game Olivia is both surprises and delights Micah, but leaves her with a difficult choice...one that threatens to break past all of her carefully constructed walls and leaving her more vulnerable than she had been since leaving the first time, all those months ago. She had come full circle, but there were a lot of things that had happened in that span of time, things that would require an explanation she wasn't sure she could give Olivia. "

title: Like an Greek Tragedy stretching from 1974 to 2014
text: New to me author - Oh my! did I feel sorry for this immigrant family living in Astoria, Queens NYC. Over 300 pages you learn about the horrible fate of a Greek family (Basil, Livana, Dmitri, Cassandra and Fedor & Niklaus). Just when you think things in the new country are starting to shine it all goes horribly horribly bad, and through no fault of there own. Tragedy after tragedy befalls them. A very exciting ending. And interesting to learn that Blackberry is still the go to tech for the FBI.

title: how to push yourself forward written by a compulsive goal seeker
text:
An excellent gift for someone at a crossroards. Divorce, job loss, health crisis, loss of a loved can all lead to overwhelming inertia, the author acts as a coach, guide and mentor to help those who need it to "GET UP & GO!" Chris Guillebeau is Host of the World Domination Summit (an international gathering of creative people), his 2012 book “The $100 Startup” was a New York Times bestseller, and he has traveled to every country in the world before the age of 35.

Excellent book club choice. I brought it to read on vacation with my sister and had to make sure it returned some in my suitcase. Although it offers nothing that you haven't heard before it still is a very good push. I also wish money wasn't a central premise. I once had a nice paying job: but not for 18 months now. I am far happier now living simply, making every penny count and loving the things I do have.

title: I have been reading historical fiction for 40 years and love it, this book was right up my alley.
text:
However this one did not sweep me off my feet. The novelization of Joan of Kent, granddaughter of Edward I of England, niece of Edward II, marrying the son of Edward III, and eventual Queen Regent for her son, Richard II. Joan was the daughter of Edmund of Woodstock, 1st Earl of Kent & Margaret Wake, 3rd Baroness Wake of Liddell. The book begins in childhood (born 1328) until her marriage to the heir to the throne of England (1361), fyi she went on to live another 24 years.

Considering what is known about her from a distance of almost 700 years is simply amazing, I would have thought a novel on her life would have been a compelling must read. However the plotting and dialogue didn't draw me in as I would have hoped. The setting was also not a richly detailed as the best of historical fiction can be. I also didn't buy into the depiction of the Black Prince (after what I had read of him previously).

Still, I was glad for the read and hope that another book about Joan and her full life will one day be written.

title: 130 pages covering 3 story-lines
text: For me I needed the book to be over twice as long for that amount of story to be told - I am looking forward to seeing the made for TV movie (made in 2002 with Rob Lowe). **possible spoiler - the mother dies - I still can't believe the mother dies - I figured the way this would play out was the rich lawyer would get the poor mother the operation and a Christmas miracle would happen - nope)**

title: With a Killer named Mongo, I was ready for a good read
text:
and that was exactly what I got. The ending was weaker than the rest of the book so that took my enjoyment down a bit. From the author of the five Ben Tolliver mysteries (now available on kindle). Mongo is an assassin who cleverly murders movie star Catherine Delure (lol, love that name too) and her assistant.

A task force is formed to ID and capture Mongo the murderer. NYPD Det. Jeb Barker doesn't buy that theft is the reason for the killing. He goes to Los Angeles and contacts Delure's secretary Dana Laramie.

My one question, didn't Mongo know that Toyota back seats fold down for extra trunk storage?

Will be picking up the Ben Tolliver series when available at the library.

title: Ages 10 to 13
text:
Adventure story of Courage, Honesty, Faithfulness and Growing up. The first transcontinental Canadian railroad (circa 1885), a deadly avalanche and murder.

In three years time 17 year old Will Everett's family has made it rich. Now he on the maiden trip of the new 900 car luxury locomotive 'The Boundless'. Will is an artist, unlike father (who manages the railroad). Will has the key to the railway owner's, Cornelius Van Horne, funeral car, which puts him in extreme danger from criminals who want to raid the car for it's purported wealth.

Aiding Will are:

Dorian, is ringmaster of the 'Zircus Dante'.

Maren, is a tightrope walker (and escape artist!) with the circus.

Mixing in Canadian folklore add to the adventure.

Will has the behavior of a 10 to 13 year that struck me as very odd for someone heading off to college in a year.

title: a little bit funny, a little bit Christian, a little bit memoir
text:
If you love the author's blog, 'The Big Mama'(new to me) you will delight in this collection. I wanted a couple opinions so I shared with my aunt & uncle (married 30 years), they read a few chapters and but weren't delighted enough to continue.

How I miss Erma Bombeck!

A New York Times Best Seller (which is why I ordered it)so you may love it.

title: AGES 11 to 13
text:
The Feral Child is the first of a trilogy of Irish folklore. 13 year old Maddy's parents have died (right off I was ready to cut are a lot of slack) and she is not happy living with her grandparents in the small town of Blarney, Ireland.

On All Hallows Eve, Maddy sees a faerie (troublesome beings who live in an alternate world) whisk her 3 year old neighbor, Stephen, into the faerie world while leaving another faerie, a changeling, in Stephen's place.

Maddy sets off with her loathsome cousins Danny and Roisin, to bring Stephen back to their world. They enter the faerie world via forbidden castle grounds. Along the way they encounter and sometimes battle, faeries, elves, and spirits.

The 12 year old loved it.

A helpful glossary of Celtic words is at the end of the book

title: Police Procedural set in Barcelona.
text:
Sadly I didn't read more of the summary before ordering it because if I had read about the bodies of dogs hung to death from a tree I would have left it for someone who enjoys, or is not bothered, by that kind of thing. Instead I skipped over that unsavory plot point and ended up enjoying the rest of the novel (although the murder of an infant almost ended it for me).

This is the 2nd Inspector Salgao thriller (after 2013's The Summer of Dead Toys): 'Inspector Hector Salgado is a transplanted Argentine living in Barcelona. While working on a human trafficking case, Salgado's violent temper got the best of him and he beat a suspect within an inch of his life. Ordered on probation, he fled to Argentina to cool off for a few months. Now he's back in Barcelona and is eager for another big case. But his boss has other plans. He assigns Salgado to a routine accidental death: a college student fell from a balcony in one of Barcelona's ritzier neighborhoods. As Salgado begins to piece together the life and world of the victim, he realizes that his death was not all that simple: his teenage friends are either overly paranoid or deceptively calm, and drugs might be involved. Hector begins to follow a trail that will lead him deep into the underbelly of Barcelona's high society where he'll come face-to-face with dangerous criminals, long-buried secrets, and, of course, his own past. But Hector thrives on pressure, and he lives for this kind of case--dark, violent, and seemingly unsolvable. Gripping, sophisticated, and wickedly entertaining, The Summer of Dead Toys introduces a charismatic new detective and announces Antonio Hill as a new master of the crime thriller."

title: Arizona Territory in 1872
text:
Cash McLendon, his drunk of a father didn't give him much of a childhood in Saint Louis, Missouri. Cash claws his way out of poverty and much like Rory Armagh in Taylor Caldwell's 'The Captains and the Kings', in 1872 Cash finds himself the son-in-law and right hand man to industrial mogul Rupert Douglass. There is no deed too unsavory for Cash when it comes to pleasing Rupert Douglas. When disaster similar to Taylor Caldwell's 'The Testimony of Two Men' takes it all from Cash he escapes to the Arizona territory while his father in law hires a hit man to take him down.

In the mining town named Glorious he locates Gabrielle, the woman he abandoned years ago. How small a town? Do a search on the town of Superior AZ and you can see how isolated it is now and imagine how isolated it was 140 years ago.

I only wish the ending was worthy of the Gary Cooper movie 'High Noon', the novel concludes with a setup for a sequel and indeed there is a planned trilogy.

title: Ages 12 to 13 horror novel
text: Kara was six years old when her brother Taff was born and she witnessed her mother, Helena, executed for being a witch.  Now age 12 she, her sunken wreck of father, and Taff are feared, loathed and abused by the people in De'Noran, their village aka 'the Children of the Fold'. The cult like villagers have isolated themselves from the rest of the world and the sinners who populate it, they follow 'The Path', living on a island surrounded by a forest known as the Dark Wood, or Sordyr's Realm, but called 'the Thickety'. Everyone lives in fear of the Thickety and the creatures in there.  Kara is lured into the Thickety and finds a book that may have been her mother's. She comes to understand the magic of the book and it brings her in great conflict with Grace, the daughter of the most powerful man the village. Things escalte from bad to very grim when Grace gets access to the magic book. The 12 year old in our family 'felt gipped' by the cliffhanger epilogue.

title: featuring  Alice  from the Men Of Honor series
text:
#2 in the author's four book Undercover series. Alice has escaped being kidnapped by human traffickers. Naturally she only let's her guard down with her neighbor, police detective Reese Bareden. While attempting to save a girl from the same fate she escaped, Alice uncovers a drug cartel. The next thing I would be doing is moving out of town that place is full of hard core crime!! Still a good sexy passionate read with realistic language, so if a few curse words scattered throughout are something that throws you out of a story you should give this a pass.

LOVE UNDERCOVER SERIES:
> RUN THE RISK (September, 2012) Detective Logan Riske & Pepper Yates' story. Logan Riske is a detective going undercover to find a witness to murder.
> BARE IT ALL (April, 2013) Reese Bareden is Logan Riske's friend and also a detective, who hooks up with a familiar female character from the previous series to fight against injustice. Detective Reese Bareden is drawn to Alice, a familiar female character from the Men Of Honor series.
Alice appeared as a secondary character in Trace of Fever. Trace visits Alice in Bare it All.
> GETTING ROWDY (September, 2013) Rowdy Yates is brother to Pepper Yates from Book #1 RUN THE RISK. He's still walking a fine line between breaking the law, and enforcing it, until he meets the right woman.
> DASH OF PERIL (March, 2014) Lieutenant Peterson & Dash Riske's story. Dash Riske is a brother to Detective Logan Riske from Book #1 RUN THE RISK , and friend to Detective Reese Bareden from book#2 BARE IT ALL while Lt. Margaret Peterson is superior to Logan and Reese.

title: 1930, 11 years after the last person has died in WW1 combat
text:
and the US government has made funding available for mothers to visit the graves in Europe of their children who died in battle. In 3 years almost 7,000 women over the age of 50 made this trip in a time that coincided with the Great Depression. I am a history major and an avid history reader but had never heard of this. So, I was hooked.

The story focuses on 5 mothers who make the journey:

>Cora Blake (from a small fishing village in Maine, her son Sammy was killed in the final days of the war) who meets American journalist, Griffin Reed (who hides his horrific scars behind a metal mask).
> Boston Brahmin socialite Mrs. Bobbie Olsen,
> Irish Catholic housemaid Katie McDonald (a Boston housemaid whose 2 sons were killed),
> Jewish farmer's wife Minnie Siebert (traveling from Bangor Maine against her husband's wishes),
> Middle class house wife Wilhelmina Russell (is recently released from a hospital and mentally fragile) is scheduled to make the journey however Selma Russell (a African-American seamstress who is such a stereotype that I wanted to stop reading) shows up to take her place.

2nd Lt. Hammond & nurse Lily Barnett are chaperoning the group (I very much enjoyed hating Hammond's dastardly senior officer).

This is the author's sixth novel (her other titles are thrillers in a series starring 'Ana Grey'. I have to say I felt unfulfilled when I finished reading the story - I think I needed to feel or know more about the characters, for me they were like ships that passed in the night. not memorable enough to linger with me. That was a surprise as I figured that an author with a talent for thrillers would have compelling characters in this historical novel.

title: I really wanted to like this novel
text: The cover art alone compelled me to enjoy it. Rick rescues Pax the puppy, a German shepherd mix, after Pax's mother (a stray) dies. Rick marries Francesca and they are a family. The World War 2 wrecks Rick's career as a rising baseball star. I almost stopped reading when Rick's wife gives up his dog for military service - I can't even imagine. Saying anything more would be rife with spoilers but I will say that PAX makes it out of War alive, however Rick was so bitter and the jump in years didn't help in making him more appealing. Luckily for other readers I appear to be in the minority.

title: 69 episodes, 2006-2009
text:
This is the first of a two novel series written in 2008 based on the TV show but not written by the show's writers. The Unit is a top-secret military unit much like the U.S. Army special operations unit known as Delta Force. i think this might have been more enjoyable for me if I hadn't like the TV show so much, the book doesn't have the flavor of the characters nor the home life interaction that made the show so appealing.
