title: 'Dating for the first time in 50 years' might be a better title
text:
A bit basic - I expected more from this series. The earlier titles were excellent and in depth, like Wine for Dummies, Desktop Publishing & Design For Dummies, Excel for Dummies,

Example: "The exciting part of dating again after age 50 is that the relationship can take any shape you want. There's more communication, more honesty, and fewer assumptions about what "dating" means or where it's going. Nevertheless, you still may need help navigating the dating and relationship world. Check out useful tips on writing an awesome online profile, and be inspired by ideas for inexpensive dates. Lastly, peek at some pointers on how to have great "first-time" sex."

Example: Affordable Date Ideas for Over-50 Daters - Most people date quite a bit before they find "the one." Even if all your dates are just dinner and a movie, dating can get expensive. Some men and women split the bill, but if the man or woman is traditional about who pays, dating can become very pricey for the guy. There are quite a few ways to have an inexpensive date that doesn't feel cheap. Here are a few ideas for inexpensive dates to consider:
>Search the city for great food trucks. Finding them is fun, and the food is always reasonably priced.
>Go to new wineries and get free tastings. The fancy established ones may have a tasting fee, but the newer ones are trying to build up a fan base, so they're usually free.
>Join your local film society and go to free or cheap screenings of movies. This is one of the best values, and if you're a movie buff dating another movie buff, this could be the best date possible.
>Explore "intellidates." There's so much talent giving free lectures or performances on university and college campuses that you'll have a hard time choosing among your options. Check the websites of local institutions for free or inexpensive music, theater, dance, and lectures.
>Do something outdoors to preserve nature. Join a conservation crew for a day: Participate in trail cleanup or other environmental group activities.
>Attend dog shows, horse shows, or agricultural shows. If your date is an animal lover, these events are typically free -- or at least inexpensive -- and a great way to bring out your date's softer side.
>Go to your local poetry society, library, or bookstore and listen to free readings from visiting authors. Sometimes they're well-known, and the readings are usually intimate affairs where you can have good conversation about the poems or book.
>Do something a little quirky and fun. You can put up a tent and camp -- even if it's just in your own backyard! Or plan a picnic in your living room if you're not interested in really roughing it.
>Experience the everyday majesty of nature. Get up very early and watch the sun rise, and enjoy a nice breakfast afterward. Or go see the stars on a clear night, preferably a bit out in the country where the city lights don't obscure the view.
>Cozy up together. Rent the first season or more of a great TV series or miniseries, and make your own popcorn.
>Cook together! Baking is particularly fun and sensual because the aroma is tantalizing long before you actually get your first bite.

title: Downer
text:
Opening 13 years after the end of THE REBELS, in Boston the summer of 1794 and ends 20 years later in late fall 1814 on the Missouri River west of St. Louis Missouri. Book 3 in what would become an 8 novel series (The Kent Family Chronicles or the American Bicentennial Series) stretching by the end of book #8 to Christmas in Boston Massachusetts 1890, 5 generations of the Kent family concluding with Philippe's 48 year old great great grandson Gideon and his grown family.The novel was made into a wonderful 4 hour made for TV 4 hour movie of the same name.

I read this as a teenager when it was first published in 1976, it was a tie-in to the excitement generated for the nation's bi-centennial in 1976. I was utterly consumed with the story telling.

The seekers covers 3 generations of Kents. 37 year old Philip born in France the illegitimate son of the 6th Duke of Kent. To a greater extent then then book #2 the story reads like Peyton Place meets the new nation. Philip is a hardened controller completely out of tune with his own family. It was a crushing disappointment to me. His 19 year old son Abraham by his first wife wants adventure and takes his spitfire bipolar step sister 16 year old Elizabeth with him. They meet with little success but do have a son, Jared. Back home Philip son Gilbert with second wife Peggy is a good man who takes on the family business he marries a heartless woman, they have a daughter Amanda. Terrible things happen and happen some more. Rape, lots of Rape, detailed rape. turnoff. Even the ending was a downer *sigh*. Abraham makes bad decisions, Jared makes bad decisions. On the bright side I did like what happened to Gilbert's wife in the last third of the book.

Such a disappoint because the author's is such a tremendous storyteller! He just isn't writing what I want to read. I's like to give him some happy pills because I love his writing.

The mixing of historic events and people with Kent family's day to day life is terrific and fun and very believable and includes:
>General Anthony Wayne
>William Henry Harrison
>Lewis & Clark
>Tecumseh
>George & Martha Washington
>John & Abigail Adams
>Thomas Jefferson
>Henry Clay
>Abraham Lincoln as a young boy.
>Andrew & Rachel Jackson
>William Rogers Clark

title: Terrific story idea, but Ellie is coming off as sour, superior, smug and ill-tempered.
text:
Not the Ellie I have come to love. Excellent Book club choice. Carrie Black and her law firm read like an episode of the show with James Spader & William Shatner "Boston Legal". Still, I love the NYC setting and the author has a way with dialogue so I know I will be ordering her next title.

For those who are new to the Ellie Hatcher series here are the book descriptions that should give you the background you need:

DEAD CONNECTION (2007): In this electrifying thriller, a rookie detective goes undercover on the Internet dating scene to draw out a serial killer targeting single women in Manhattan When two young women are murdered on the streets of New York, exactly one year apart, Detective Ellie Hatcher is called up for a special assignment on the homicide task force. The killer has left behind a clue connecting the two cases to First Date, a popular online dating service, and Flann McIlroy, an eccentric, publicity-seeking homicide detective, is convinced that only Ellie can help him pursue his terrifying theory: someone is using the lure of the Internet and the promise of love to launch a killing spree against the women of New York City. To catch the killer, Ellie must enter a high-tech world of stolen identities where no one is who they appear to be. And for her, the investigation quickly becomes personal: she fits the profile of the victims, and she knows firsthand what pursuing a sociopath can do to a cop--back home in Wichita, Kansas, her father lost his life trying to catch a notorious serial murderer. When the First Date killer begins to mimic the monster who destroyed her father, Ellie knows the game has become personal for him, too. Both hunter and prey, she must find the killer before he claims his next victim--who could very well be her. Expertly plotted and perfectly paced, Dead Connection advances Alafair Burke to the front ranks of American thriller writers.

ANGEL'S TIP (2008): Thrilled to spend the final hours of her spring break in the VIP room of an elite Manhattan club, fresh-faced Indiana college student Chelsea Hart remains behind when her girlfriends call it a night. The next morning, joggers find her body in East River Park, her blond hair brutally hacked off. NYPD Detective Ellie Hatcher believes the group of privileged men last seen plying Chelsea with free-flowing alcohol most likely includes a murderer. But after building a tight case against a young hedge-fund manager, Ellie has her doubts, because Chelsea's slaying is eerily similar to three other murders from nearly a decade ago. Continuing the investigation long after the department brass is satisfied with their case, hard-headed Ellie plunges into a late-night party world of conspicuous wealth and hedonistic consumption to catch the real killer--unaware that a psychopath is watching her every move...and eager to kill again.

212 (2010): In New York City, Nights Are Dangerous. Days Are Numbered. When New York University sophomore Megan Gunther finds personal threats posted to a Web site specializing in campus gossip, she's taken aback by their menacing tone. Someone knows her daily routine down to the minute and is watching her--but thanks to the anonymity provided by the Internet, the police tell her there's nothing they can do. Her friends are sure it's someone's idea of a joke, but when Megan is murdered in a vicious attack, NYPD Detective Ellie Hatcher is convinced that the online threats are more than just empty words. With smooth, straight-talking partner J. J. Rogan at her side, Ellie tries to identify Megan's enemies, but she begins to wonder if the coed's murder was more than just the culmination of a cyber obsession. Phone records reveal a link between Megan and a murdered real estate agent who was living a dangerous double life. The detectives also learn that the dead real estate agent shared a secret connection to a celebrity mogul whose bodyguard was mysteriously killed a few months earlier. And when Megan's roommate suddenly disappears, they know they have to find her before another young woman dies. Exposing the darkness that lurks beneath the glamorous surface of New York City,

NEVER TELL (2012): Detective Ellie Hatcher will be forced to uncover the truth behind the apparent suicide of a teenaged girl with intriguing connections to both New York's wealthiest--and its most dispossessed. This addictive thriller from acclaimed suspense writer Alafair Burke draws its details from the author's own experiences as a criminal law professor and deputy district attorney, creating an exhilarating, true-to-life tale of crime and its consequences that is perfect for fans of Laura Lippman, Harlan Coben, and Burke's breakout standalone thriller Long Gone.Even a perfect family has its secrets. Sixteen-year-old Julia Whitmire appeared to have everything: a famous father, a luxurious Manhattan town house, a coveted spot at the elite Casden prep school. When she is found dead in her bathtub, a handwritten suicide note left on her bed, her parents insist that their daughter would never take her own life. But Julia's enviable world was more complicated than it seemed. The pressure to excel at Casden was enormous. Abuse of prescription drugs ran rampant among students. And a search of Julia's computer reveals that she'd been engaged in a dangerous game of cyberbullying against an unlikely victim. NYPD detective Ellie Hatcher is convinced the case is a suicide, but she knows from personal experience that a loving family can be the last to accept the truth. As she is pressured to pursue a case she doesn't believe in, she is pulled into Julia's inner circle--an eclectic mix of precocious teenagers from Manhattan's most privileged families as well as street kids from Greenwich Village. But when the target of Julia's harassment continues to receive death threats, Ellie is forced to acknowledge that Julia may have learned the hard way that some secrets should never be told.

On top of a failed marriage and whether she will return to graduate studies, she is caught between family feuds over bad business decisions, the Singapore dating scene and a romance with the son of a client, a fraught reunion with an old college roommate and her mother’s health problems after a lifetime of heavy drinking. Good resolution

title: Historical Fiction 1200 AD
text:
500 pages translated from Spanish to English. Tells the story of a very young man in China who for the first 250 pages has one bad thing happen to him after another. Te second half we find his life turning around and responsibilities growing as he comes to the attention of the Emperor's court as a man of acute intelligence and insight in one specialty determining how someone died and if it was natural or murder based on physical evidence. 500 reviewers give it a thumbs up and I enjoyed it also.

Inspired by the historic Song Ci (1186–1249) a Judge and forensic (use of scientific knowledge/methods in solving crimes) medical expert in China who wrote a groundbreaking book "Collected Cases of Injustice Rectified" and is considered to be the father of Forensic Science.

title: Not the book I thought it was going to be
text:
It will make a terrific movie of the week but it lacks the details that make reading a book like 'The Winds of War' so good.

FYI the author lives in Surrey England and should not be confused with the author of the same name living in Arkansas (titles in the Quest for Love series: Seasons to Grow; Love's Mountains to Climb & Secret in the Cellar).

Still, for those who loved it there are 3 more titles in the series:

#2 (9/2014) 'WAVE ME GOODBYE' A compelling story of tragedy and triumph in WWII. Perfect for fans of Katie Flynn and Annie Groves. When war is declared, four plucky girls from Dartford – Grace, Sally, Rose and Daisy – are keen to do their bit on the Home Front. For orphan Grace, it’s a chance to start afresh. She’s always has a soft spot for Sam Petrie, brother of Daisy and Rose, but realising that he is in love with their friend Sally, she puts her own feelings aside, and signs up for life as a Land Girl.
Mucking out and early morning milking come as a big shock and life is harder than she expected. But Grace is nothing if not determined and though their lives will never be the same again, the four girls know they will always have each other – no matter what the war throws at them…

#3 (4/2015) 'ON A WING AND A PRAYER' The third in a series of books featuring four young women whose lives will be forever changed by WWII. Perfect for fans of Katie Flynn. Rose Petrie is desperate to do something for the war effort. Despite the daily hardships and the nightly bombing raids, her sister, Daisy, and their friends all seem to be thriving in their war work. Rose is doing her best down at the munitions factory, but she is dealt a blow when her childhood sweetheart, Stan, tells her he doesn't feel the same way about her. Determined to get away and make a new start, Rosie decides to put her mechanical skills, learned from her father and brothers, to good use and signs up for the Women's Auxiliary Service, or ATS. But Rose discovers that delivering fruit and veg in her father's greengrocer's van is very different to driving trucks for the army in a country under seize. While learning the ropes, Rose will learn that things never go according to plan, either in love or war. But with grit, determination and a bit of luck, Rose is determined that she, and the rest of the country, will keep shining through...

Book 4 (10/2015) 'A CHRISTMAS GIFT' The fourth in a series of books featuring four young women whose lives will be forever changed by WWII. Perfect for fans of Katie Flynn. When WWII is declared, Sally, Grace and twins Daisy and Rose are desperate to do their bit for the war effort. Their hometown of Dartford in Kent will be in the frontline of Britain's defences against the Germans and the girls will need to draw on all of their resources if they are to hold their own. As the war deepens, each of the girls will face heartache and pain, triumph and tragedy, but their friendship and their strength will see them through Britain's darkest days.

title: Romance in the Florida Keys
text:
Abby, Luke, and Hannah were high school BFFs, Abby and Luke were couple until college, 25 years later Luke and Hannah are the couple and Abby has returned home newly divorced and on a mission. Nor for Luke as Hannah fears, Abby wants to build 10 eco-friendly houses on land her parents left her however the Mayor has fears of over development.

Thirty something Seth is newly arrived to town, he was a buddy of Luke's in Afghanistan and the team leader. He is healing from the the killing in the line of duty of his girlfriend in Afghanistan.

A lovely fade to black romance that never really excited me.

title: Ages 10 to 12
text:
killing animals is a personal turnoff for me, so I wish I knew that before ordering this for my 9 and 12 year olds. 12 year old Kester is a prisoner and hasn’t spoken since his mom died 6 years ago. The world is a nasty place with most animals dead and the environment no longer able to easily support human life. Kester escapes with a personal mission to save the small creatures of the earth that still survive.

The really creepy part? His father may hold the answers to the survival of Kester and the animals, he may have been the cause of all the destruction. Kester and his animal buddies set out to find him.

title: well written and violent
text:
What a bizarre premise for a Star Wars Fan, a Star Wars adventure where they are all bad guys and you wouldn't think it a bad thing if they all were loaded on a death star that they then blew themselves up. I will have to read the summary closer next time - it never occurred to me that there only be bad guys in it. Does George know? Does Steven?

Inconsistent with other bits of story, this tale of Darth Maul could be any black ops book but would have been a better chapter or maybe a short story. There's an inherent problem when your main character is a villain. While Star Wars has oft celebrated the "bad guys" and Darth Maul's unceremonious introduction and death in Ep I makes you wonder if he really was a bad ass after all, this book seeks to give him some legend in the world of hand to hand combat. Pitting him against various creatures from the universe, the only way to keep him the protagonist is to make everyone around him even worse than he is. There is no showdown between Maul and some villain worse than he is. Just criminals and scum and since you know he won't die, there's no real mystery. If you've read other Star Wars books, the outcome is predictable. A few inconsistencies with what appears to be cannon but the book is otherwise unremarkable. If you must read them all you can get through this quickly but there are no truly memorable new characters to come from this story.

Sadly, the word Maul always associates the way my tiny tot pronounced "oatmeal" when he was 3 years old "Oat-Maul". More accurately the title "Maul - Lockdown" flashes me the the spate of Mall shootings we have had in the world, one this year close to home so "Maul - Lockdown" flashes me to "Mall Lockdown" and I am already tense. *sigh*

Extended Author Bio: Roland Warren was appointed Care Net President & CEO in October 2012. With 1180 affiliated pregnancy resource centers, Care Net is the nation’s largest network of centers providing a Christ-centered and compassionate support to those facing unplanned pregnancies. Prior to his tenure at Care Net, Roland served as president of the National Fatherhood Initiative (NFI), where he was dedicated to the mission of improving the well-being of children by increasing the proportion of children that are raised with involved, responsible and committed fathers. His national media appearances include The Oprah Winfrey Show, The Today Show, CNN, C-SPAN, Dateline NBC, Fox News Channel, and Black Entertainment Television. He has been interviewed by major radio and newspaper outlets such as The Wall Street Journal, USA Today, The Washington Post, O Magazine, Ebony, Sports Illustrated, Christianity Today, Essence, the Tavis Smiley Show, and Janet Parshall’s America. He also has written a monthly column called “Pop Culture” for The Washington Times. And, he is the author of a new book, Bad Dads of the Bible: 8 Mistake Every Good Dad Can Avoid. Roland, an alumnus of Princeton University, brings to Care Net over two decades of experience in the business world, more than a decade of experience in the non-profit world, and an M.B.A. from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. Roland is married to Dr. Yvette Lopez-Warren and has two sons, Jamin, a graduate of Harvard University and Justin, a graduate of the University of North Carolina, and Indiana University of Pennsylvania.

title: psychological thriller
text:
Dr. Taylor is a found dead in his hotel room. He specializes in wives, 3 of them (that we know of) at the same time in different cities. How does a renowned plastic surgeon in treating disfigured children and an active community spokesman manage that in the day of google and facebook? Well, his first wife didn't want a divorce so she arranged his schedule for wife #2 (earth-mother MJ Taylor) and wife #3 (pediatric oncologist Dr. Helen Taylor). The best part is each chapter the narration is taken over by a different wife. Palo Alto detective Samantha Adams is in charge of the investigation and she gets to chime in from time to time.

I loved the premise and the author can certainly spin a story but I think this would made a better Tarantino movie than a novel.

title: Nice non-erotic romance set in Colorado
text: 5th in the 'Hope's Crossing' series (after Current Creek Valley). Nothing disturbing or ugly. An enjoyablysmall town romance. I would have enjoyed it more if they had more than one date before the end of the novel (I assume they will be living happily ever after). The main thing that kept me from loving the novel was there was so many pages dwelling on what was and what could have been. It would have been more enjoyable for me developing Charlotte and Spencer in the here and now. However 65 reviewers either loved it or like it so you might also.

title: Debut, 4 star writing
text:
Jules Marvin, is a professional dog walker, she enjoys the freedom of the polyamory relationship she has with Claire and Toni, and has no plans to change, monogamy just holds no appeal for her.

Sylvia Ramirez is a clinical social worker in San Francisco working with the mentally ill. Even though she is still hurting from a recent breakup with her girlfriend she is looking for her happily ever after in a more traditional coupling of two people who love each other so much they only want to be with one person. Sylvia & Jules meet when Sylvia is dog sitting for friends. It's the year that passing the marriage equality bill, the civil right to marry in California, was a success and then Proposition 8 threatened to take it all away. This is a very readable debut. When Jules & Sylvia are attracted to each other, somethings gotta give. I think polyamory is fascinating, however I have now learned that I personally would enjoy reading about it in non-fiction or in general fiction. For me it doesn't work as a romance. Want a bit more? Search 'Lizzie's Bedtime Stories Episode 31: Kathleen Knowles' for a video interview with the author or 'Kathleen Knowles Love, Marriage, Commitment and Prop 8' for an article by the author.

title: I'd say the only thing missing from Fool's Gold series is some ethnic diversity.
text:
Passionate escapist romance from small town in California

Yes this is a idealized slice of life but it is so feel good that you can't help but enjoy it for what it is. Except for the part about about Issbel losing her husband to another man and the friends when they get together for lunch seeming a bit vapid and Ford having more ego than most. The author is totally rocking out this series - there is even a website totally dedicated to the series (with author video interviews) with a who's who in the entire series (just ignore the character pictures - I totally thought they got them wrong).

Ex-Navy SEAL 33 year old Ford Hendrix opens a 'defense academy' with his military buddies. Ford's mom would love to see her boy never go a wandering again and thinks a wife is just the ticket, Ford thinks it is too soon and that's year's of repeated tours of duty have hardened him too much to be marriage material. 28 year old Isabel Beebe manages her parents' bridal shop, she has been crushing on Ford for years. Back in her teens, when Ford was serving our country she wrote him letters sharing her dreams. Freakily, he never replied, so she is doing all she can to avoid bumping into him.

title: Ages 13 and up
text:
18 year old Eva and her twin brother Eamon are the children of the ruler. Eamon is now dead and Eva takes his place in the event called The Testing. The Testing is an Iditarod like dogsled journey over snow and ice to Boundary Lands the land of the previous civilization whose corruption brought down the fury of the gods and the flood. The goal is to bring back artifacts buried in the ice that support the claims of the government for the cause of the flood.

Rulers an Arctic country named 'Aerie', are dictatorial fascists of a medieval society. 250 years earlier a flood destroyed almost everything and everyone, and all technology. The people believe the flood came from the worship of a false god. Lukas is one of the Boundary People who are the servants to the ruling class. Lukas was Eamon's trainer for The Testing and now prepares Eva. Jasper is of the ruling class and betrothed to Eva.

Sounds terrific. But in this first novel that is all there really is. An epic story deserves epic characters and while their actions are huge their personality didn't hold. My 13 year old took longer than usual to finish; I'll hold on to the book for my 9 year old in a couple years to read, maybe she will think differently.

title: Before there were calories or cholesterol,
text:
there were State Fairs! The editor was the Public Relations Manager for Pillsbury and judge of the Bake-Off. Do they still have them?

Also, some people were in there more than once - I figured with thousands to choose from we wouldn't see the same person twice.

Still, for the nostalgia and fun this was an excellent pick.

text:
The pacing is off. I never felt compelled to read on and in a mystery that can be deadly (and not in a good way).

Light on character development and I never felt a real sense of place it could have been anytown, anywhere USA.

title: The story was fun and the ending was too
text:
Romantic Comedy from Prolific new to me author, 10 titles in 16 months, 'Bridesmaid' being the most recent. I got it because of the 5 star reviews. Is it only me who gets stuck on the title? I always thought you were either a bridesmaid or the Maid of Honor? I had never heard the term Bridesmaid of Honor.

'Britton's sister announces she's getting married in the same month and her maid of honor is none other than her best friend Daphne, the same woman that has tormented her sister for years.' I am guessing the sisters aren't close - I would have dumped my BFF long ago if she made my sister miserable. 'What her best friend failed to mention, was the fact that her cousin Daphne was going to be a bridesmaid.' Shouldn't it be 'Daphne 'is' going to be a bridesmaid.' ? Grammar questions cropped up for me while reading and kept taking me out of the story. I thought the story was well paced and the dialogue well done. At 174 pages with a large easy to read font it's a nice quick read.

title: Thank goodness this wasn't my Christmas
text:
Set on the romantic island of Nantucket off the coast of Massachusetts at Christmas time featuring a 3 year old, an abandoned dog, newlyweds and a couple expecting their second child, you would expect a terrific story. hmmmm, What I got was Kennedy, married and 8 months pregnant with her 2nd child. And for some god forsaken reason she wants to inflict on her father the pain of remarriage to her mother - her cold as ice mother - who left their marriage for another man. Oh, and BTW he is already happily newly married to a lovely woman.

The novel just lost me there. Also it was about 100 pages shorter than I thought it needed to be a deep satisfying read.
Nicole, is a 50 something widow newly married to Sebastian who needs to stand up for herself
Sebastian is a 60 something retired Attorney who needs to convict his daughter for immaturity
Kennedy is his daughter who really needs to be swept out to sea
Katya is the exwife who needs to go to sea with her daughter
Snix-Pooh is the dog who needs a new name
Max is the tiny tot who needs to get dialogue suited to his age and not someone much older

title: Jenny and Caleb deserve each other
text:
Difficult to enjoy a romance when you think the grown woman is a self centered brat who doesn't care when she hurts her 4 year old half brother and neglects her mother who has found happiness in a new marriage. Especially when it is the holidays and I am missing my own mother who died 12 years ago at the same age as Connie, Jenny's mother.

Even more difficult when the man in her life cheated on her, went into rehab and you still think he's not marriage material.

The author certainly can write a compelling narrative and is great at dialogue.

I see from the other reviews that alot of readers loved the story so you might also.

PS - I love the Chesapeake Shores series I moved from Maryland 20 years ago and miss it.

title: Ages 12 to 14 appropriate
text:
13 year old (I am guessing) Hilary is living in the make believe land that is similar to England 200 years ago. With Magic. And Pirates that aren't scary. Hilary is the daughter of an Admiral. She can not follow her father into the Navy because that is for boys only. Her father the Admiral is an self-important egomaniac who blusters and firmly believes that daughters should not be seen or heard. That's about the worst of it. The rest is pretty funny.

Hilary wants to go to pirate training school V.N.H.L.P. "Servin' the High Seas for 152 Years" rather than Finishing School for 'Delicate Ladies' and "Where Virtue Blossoms". Like the Navy the pirates are boys only too. It being the times Hilary loses so she and the family gargoyle take off for Miss. Pimms. For the next 250 pages we have pirates and governess, captains and first mates, BFFs and bullies. It all ends great except for her parent who was never a parent to begin with.

I know the publisher is going after tween audience but the humor and the story line won't be readily apparent to any that are younger than 12. For me the story was just a tad off. Half of the elements seemed designed for kids ages 8 to 12 the other half seemed designed for kids 12 to 16. My 12 year old finished it but it never grabbed him, could be a guy thing but we at least got a dinner table chat about equal opportunity. Will try it with the 8 year in a couple years.

title: I am probably over reacting to the ending
text:
but when we try and instill in our little ones not to bully and not to steal, and that is the resolution Sheriff Bart chooses to get the Bull in the Wild West Show to act bullish, it just seems to send the wrong message to me.

Otherwise, I loved the humor and the unique illustrations. I think age 8 and above can read this on their own - the younger ages would want to be read to.

Your mileage may vary.

I will say that I enjoyed the humor enough to check out other books by this author in our Library.

title: So I don't get it. *sigh*,
text:
I was hoping for something close, or better than, the first novel or close, or better than, the TV show. By the end I wasn't even sure that this wasn't ghost written, but then I know from experience that fan fiction writers are often as good or better than the TV shows that have a team of writers.

If you need a Dexter fix watch Season one or better yet read the first Dexter novel "Darkly Dreaming Dexter" 2004: Meet Dexter, a polite wolf in sheep's clothing . . . a monster who cringes at the site of blood . . . a serial killer whose one golden rule makes him immensely likable: he only kills bad people. Dexter Morgan isn't exactly the kind of man you'd bring home to Mom. Though he's playful and has a wonderfully ironic sense of humor, Dexter's one character flaw (his proclivity for murder) can be off-putting. But at heart Dexter is the perfect gentleman, supportive of his sister, Deb, a Miami cop, and interested only in doing away with people who really deserve his special visit. Dex is quite good-looking but totally indifferent to (and, frankly, a bit puzzled by) the attentions paid to him by women. Despite the fact that he can't stand the sight of blood, he works as a blood-spatter analyst for the Miami police department, a job that allows him to keep tabs on the latest crimes and keep an eye open for his next quarry.

title: Might be best served in a 2 child house where the 3 year old can read to a younger sibling.
text: Nice basic indestructible book for your baby/toddler. When you want to have a short book that you can read to your littlest child this is for you. It's a very basic book. the colors and shapes are kind of bland but maybe that is best for babies - I think having one word per page is all a baby/toddler would be able to absorb at a time.

title: How to say why i didn't love it
text:
without giving the plot away?

I snapped this book up after reading the publishers summary, it sounded right down my Alley with having read Kathleen Woodiwiss, Daphne DuMaurier, Laurie McBain and countless other romance novels the last 35 years.

And to read so many loving reviews I really thought I had a winner for me.

*possible spoiler alert* but really the Earl's behavior was below the pale toward Rachel. I can't say more without giving part of the story away.

title: The messages are not what I would want for children

the son wants to drive the car. Father says no. Car breaks down. Car fixed by a repair shop.

A reapir shop managed by a gorilla and run by grase monkeys (lol!).

Owner says that the father won't have to pay the huge bill if he lets the son drive - so we see the son drive off rather than pay the bill.

See what I mean?

Graphics were fun and retro (reminded me of illustrations from the 60's.

title: Target age 3 to 8 year olds
text:
Today is a huge day for little Lola's older sister, it's Eva's 15th Birthday celebration 'Quinceanera'.

Being the baby of the family and also cute and full of energy makes Lola more than a little spoiled and undisciplined by everyone. She gets in trouble and it impacts her sister's big day.

All is resolved and hopefully the reader learns that no one is happy when it's all about me me me.

I got this for my eight year old but will read it to the 4, 5 & 6 year olds so I can make a point on being self centered.

title: 14 year old Florian
text:
This is a German Young Adult novel so many of the things I found off-putting for a 12 or 13 or even 14 year old you can probably chalk up to as cultural perspective.

Florian is 14 and in his mind it's all about him, has enough of being a supportive younger brother. His sister is gravely ill, her care has drained them family emotionally, physically and financially.

He ditches his sister on her birthday, steals a large sum of money from his cash strapped parents and heads off to camp to party like an 18 year old and act like a 8 year old, example: using the word 'retard', I don't expect that in a 14 year old.

Not exactly what I would want to share with my 12 year old.

However this could be an excellent learning tool for parents to discuss improper and selfish behavior.

You mileage may vary.

title: seedy police officers and vicious underworld criminals
text:
What's not to like? Well, my dad would have loved this premise - me not so much. I grabbed the novel because the title was catchy and it was described as "from Sweden's internationally best-selling crime novelist" and a "riveting second installment of the Stockholm Noir Trilogy."

I found the story unrelentingly depressing and violent so I will probably give the next book a pass.

loathed the result. I guess the author and I had different idea on where this premise could go, lol!

title: Paranormal and Urban Fantasy series 'Dead Is ...'
text:
Very surprised this is book 8 in a series. After reading it, I find nothing compelling me to go back and read the original seven.

SERIES TWO featuring Jessica Walsh:

DEAD IS A BATTLEFIELD: Jessica Walsh is starting her freshman year at Nightshade High and trying to forget about the tragic events surrounding her brother's graduation. She wants to have a normal high school experience. But that's easier said than done in Nightshade. There's a new guy at school who seems to be turning the girls into lovesick zombies. And Jessica has other worries--like her crush on a cute but moody lead singer, and the mysterious tattoo that appeared on her arm one day that lets her know whenever there is trouble brewing. Jessica learns she's a Virago, a woman warrior chosen to fight evil whenever it threatens her hometown. But does a lowly freshman really have what it takes to keep Nightshade safe?

DEAD IS A KILLER TUNE: High school freshman Jessica Walsh is a Virago-a woman warrior who must protect her hometown from danger. And in Nightshade, California, trouble is always lurking. At the town's Battle of the Bands, Jess's boyfriend, Dominic, and his band, Side Effects May Vary, are up against Hamlin, a band so popular, their fans follow them everywhere. Soon, the competing musicians are doing risky, illegal, and even fatal things-and claiming that they heard strange music that compelled them to do it. Can Jess and her friends track down the tuneful tyrant before it's too late?

Dead Is Just a Dream is a book 3, in series 2, of the 'Dead Is ...' series.

While 'Dead is a Battlefield' and 'Dead is a Killer Tune' were appropriate for 13 year olds I think this particular title dealing with a 15 year in high school might be better served to ages 14 and 15 year old. There is a large difference in life experiences between a 12 year old in 7th grade and a 15 year old in High School. I'll give the book to my child the summer before high school.

SERIES ONE feature Daisy Giordano:
DEAD IS THE NEW BLACK
DEAD IS A STATE OF MIND
DEAD IS SO LAST YEAR
DEAD IS JUST A RUMOR
DEAD IS NOT AN OPTION

title: Book 3 of a trilogy
text:
I liked it but I am not the target audience. And that is my only quibble. The story is about a 17 year old, so why would I want a 12 year old reading this book? There's a lot of death and destruction & blood.

However if you have a 15, 16 or 17 year old in the home (or as a gift) - get them the whole series - they will love it. The author is a terrific talent and I loved the use of Irish mythology made real to new readers.

If you didn't read the first two novels please consider doing so. If you can't here is some information on the first two novels to help your understanding:

BOOK ONE: From School Library Journal: Gr 8 Up-Ancient Irish myths and legends mix and mingle with the modern world in this fast-paced fantasy. Teagan Wylltson's got her life in order. She has a great job at the local zoo and is heading toward a college scholarship. She doesn't need boys distracting her from her plan. But then one day Social Services shows up with them, Teagan's 17-year-old cousin, Finn Mac Cumhaill. Teagan's mother is Irish and was brought to the States by a group of Irish Travelers, but she hasn't had any contact with them for many years, until now. After her mother dies of mysterious causes and her father is abducted by truly evil forces, Teagan, her younger brother, and Finn set off on a dangerous and frightening mission to rescue him. Through the events that unfold both in the modern world and in the world of Mag Mel where Fear Doirich rules and the sprites and goblins live, Teagan's family history unfolds, and she is able to make sense of incidents from her past that have always seemed puzzling. Hamilton has created characters who are quirky and complex. Their stories are tightly woven together and riveting, and readers will look forward to the next installment in the series. From Booklist: Hamilton uses the Celtic saga of Fionn Mac Cumhaill as a basis for this promising new series about goblins and the Travelers who fight them. Chicagoan Teagan has always been too invested in science--particularly animal behavior--to believe in her mother's Irish superstitions. When Finn is sent to live with them, he brings a dangerously seductive sense of wildness into Teagan's life. Finn claims to be destined to fight goblinkind, but before Teagan can fully accept his story, goblins attack and force them into Mag Mell, the kingdom of the evil Fear Doirich. Hamilton's convincingly idiosyncratic characters are the heart of the book, though a focus on dialogue occasionally distances readers from an emotional connection. The setting, too, is barely there, despite seeming important to the story. The romance is more successful, starting off heated but cooling quickly into a mild, but tension-filled, relationship. The hints of a tragic fate will keep romance fans reading, while the promise of more magical thrills involving Irish folklore will draw in others.

BOOK TWO: Teagan, Finn, and Aiden have made it out of Mag Mell alive, but the Dark Man's forces are hot on their heels. Back in Chicago, Tea's goblin cousins show up at her school, sure she will come back to Mag Mell, as goblin blood is never passive once awoken. Soon she will belong to Fear Doirich and join them. In the meantime, they are happy to entertain themselves by trying to seduce, kidnap, or kill Tea's family and friends. Tea knows she doesn't have much time left, and she refuses to leave Finn or her family to be tortured and killed. A wild Stormrider, born to rule and reign, is growing stronger inside her. But as long as she can hold on, she's still Teagan Wylltson, who plans to be a veterinarian and who heals the sick and hurting. The disease that's destroying her--that's destroying them all--has a name: Fear Doirich. And Teagan Wylltson is not going to let him win.

title: New to me author - The Streets of San Francisco
text:
Will try his other novels "The Survivor" & "The Crime Writer" as they are raved about.

I loved the premise but the telling either had me yawning or rolling my eyes.

Daniel counsels 6 ex-cons who we learn about in their group sessions. However the telling doesn't compel me to read on.

Daniel finds an envelope in his office inbox, a note threatens a woman, an address and including the time of death MINUTES AWAY! It's the 2nd such envelope - the first envelope ended in murder. Daniel calls the police - they can't get there in time. But Daniel does! WTW? He sees the murder and the masked killer.

More envelopes head Daniel's way. Could it be one of his group members is the killer?

Add in Daniel's wife and mother get along like oil and vinegar, each with their own back story you can see the story has potential.

My guess is this was a unpublished novel written early in a career, taken off the hard drive, dusted off, given a quick polish and just didn't pay off. I think it might make an excellent Bruce Willis movie.

plus, Satanists, Vampires, ex-pat Americans in Mexico and movie geeks, oh my!
