title: "Shamil schlimazel, hasenpfeffer incorporated!"
text: This was my kind of subject matter, my kind of reading material but I was never engaged. At the end of the story I can say it a nice long read and that I wish history had been different. I got a nice overview about the history behind the story by going to the Smithsonain website: chavchavadze.si.edu(shamil)

title: I am glad so many of my favorite authors enjoyed it so very much.
text:
8 years married and still beloved strangers. I loved the premise. But too many questionable for me moments left it an ok read and a likable debut effort.

You are a city girl, you fall in love in college and marry. You move to your husband's hometown in rural upstate New York, your mother in law doesn't like her son, and you even less. You have not managed to make any close friends in the 8 intervening years. You awake one morning to find your husband a suicide in your home. He is a police officer but the brotherhood is not there for you emotionally or otherwise. You start looking for answers on your own. You find that he had a unmentioned brother who died 25 years ago...

title: A remarkable writer
text:
If you enjoy or love creative writing you will be delirious with this collection of stories. Short story writing is a craft that requires great skill. I can't say that this author's style of short story telling is for me. I looked forward this collection after reading the review in the NY Times. However, the stories didn't take hold of my imagination. Perhaps, like my creative writing college course 30 years ago, I am not in the right mindset to appreciate them at this time I will hang on to the title. A remarkable writer, I may appreciate them more as my life unfolds.

My favorites 'Exhortation' will have meaning to anyone in the corporate world and 'Al Roosten' will have you questioning who are you really?

title: most suitable for girls or boys ages 12-13
text:
Because it deals with a girl age 13 and a boy age 15 I thought I would read this to share with my cousin's 11 year old.

I know the 11 year old enjoyed it more than me.

I was disappointed mostly with the ending that brought the 13 year old right back to where she was at page one. That left me thinking, all that? For what?

I knew going in this was set in the appalling world of pagent parents and children, however I think I was hoping to show growth and change but that isn't what happened.

title: for Girls or Boys ages 9 to 12
text:
Well written outlandish plot, but my cousin's 11 year old liked it.

My only concern is that one of the twins, 'Tom', is the sort of kid I wouldn't want to hold up as a shining example to a child.

For me it was a good book to talk about over the dinner table with the family.

title: Gorgeous children's book not suitable for children
text:
I know this makes no sense.

The illustrations and simplicty of the prose make this seem targeted for children. However, the story and text are better suited for ages 16 to 20, and I can't see anyone that age wanting to hold this book in their hands as their friends would tease them to no end.

So I have to say I think the only group that would appreciate the book are someone grandma's age, like me, who can enjoy the graphics and not be dismayed at an artist who went through women like they were crudites.

title: WARNING from series fans - do not read book 3 until you read books One & Two
text:
So I did. I found the first book the best of the lot. The second book was good and might have been a better conclusion to the series. The third book was ok - my personal take was that it was too violent (especially for teens) and by the end I wasn't liking them as heroes very much (least of all Heather). Still they all read very quickly and the 2nd half of WORMHOLE was non-stop action and nukes - might be a fun movie.

For those who have not read the first two books these brief summaries (culled from the publisher descriptions) might be useful for a high level background:

The Second Ship (Released: October 2, 2012 | The Rho Agenda - Book 1): Three teenagers discover a spaceship buried inside a remote canyon, they are changed forever. With a single touch its technology is uploaded into their minds. Together they are thrust into a violent world of secrets and corruption, becoming reluctant soldiers in a war destined to alter what it means to be human because they now know the frightening truth about `the Rho Project': In 1948, an alien starship fell from the New Mexico sky--and immediately vanished behind the walls of the Los Alamos Laboratory. Since that day the US military has endeavored to reverse engineer the ship's alien technology through top-secret research known only as the Rho Project. For sixty years the government has spent billions trying to unlock it's technology and now the government is prepared tell all. Or so it claims.... However the teens, Heather McFarland and Mark & Jennifer Smythe, know the frightening truth about the Rho Project.

Immune (Released: October 30, 2012 | The Rho Agenda - Book 2): In just a few short months the three teens who first exposed the Rho Project's evil agenda have seen life as they know it stripped away, trapping them in a confusing new reality where human DNA is modified at an alarming rate. Struggling to understand what they are becoming and on the run for their lives, the teens and their remaining allies must stop the Rho Project before it alters the very fabric of humanity. In the final pages of book one, NSA director Jonathan Riles failed to halt the Rho Project's infiltration of the US government. Now the Project's alien nano-serum is loosed upon the world, disguised as a miracle cure and leaving too many people--good people--dead. Anyone still alive to challenge the Project won't be for long: an assassin known only as El Chupacabra is systematically eliminating any and all opposition. At the top of the hit list is NSA fixer Jack Gregory, and the teenagers.

Wormhole (Released: November 20, 2012 | The Rho Agenda - Book 3): Now a trio of altered humans, the teens, must infiltrate Dr. Donald Stephenson's government mandated wormhole project and stop it, no matter the cost. At the end of book two the world dared to hope the threat posed by the Rho Project's alien technologies is finally over. Stephenson, the Rho Project's lead scientist, had been imprisoned for his crimes against humanity. However, scientists working in Switzerland on the Large Hadron Collider discover a new threat, a scientific anomaly capable of destroying the earth and only Rho Project technology can stop it. In exchange for a full pardon, Stephenson agrees to create a wormhole that will send the anomaly into deep space. But his promise masks the alien agenda that brought the Rho Ship to earth. The ultimate battle has begun and, this time, mankind cannot afford to lose.

title: Terrific premise
text:
It was just too unbelievable and the writing kept tripping me out of the story. It was OK but I probably will not read another by this author. I have read better fan fiction on the internet.

Nuclear weapons in a terrorist country. An ancient prophecy of the end of times. The two are connected with a beautiful condemned woman and a hapless Irish journalist (tracking his rogue IRA bomber uncle) the only ones who stand a chance of preventing the apocalypse.

title: The cover caught my eye
text:
Sixteen year old Benjamin is a twice failed suicide. His parents leave him at "The Roaring Orchards School for Troubled Teens" a boarding school in upstate New York.

Aubrey, the founder and headmaster, is the anti-Dumbledore of Harry Potter fame. Stable and Sage he isn't. Aubrey's creed is a list of seven approved feelings, and that teens need structure and limits; however his curriculum often pits the already fragile and/or unstable students against each other. Then Aubrey falls ill and the school goes haywire.

The story is told by Benjamin, in memoir with assist from others. With the black humor of One Flew over the Cuckoo's Nest I am glad to have the chance to read this. The scariest thing for me was the adults - they appeared as disassociated and confused as the teens.

Let's just hope this is unmagical realism and not fact made fiction.

title: miserable people, behaving miserablely
text:
David & Jo Henniger live unhappily in London. Old "friends" Richard & Dally invite them to their annual weekend decadent party, worthy of Roman emperors, in the Moroccan desert.

At lunch David, in a foul mood, drinks too much. As dusk approaches they search the dark road for their hosts, out of the darkness two figures appear on the roadside.

David freaks and swerves, killing one of the young men. David and Jo show up late to the revels with the body of the young man.

The Moroccan locals already had developed a disgusted view of Richard & Dally's godless infidels aka guests.
The weekend unfurls with increasing tension from the Moroccan staff, the hedonist guests with their own secrets, coming to a head with the father arriving to take his son's body.

David is forced to return to the young man's desert home to atone for his actions.

The prose was perfect and the reveal at the end was excellent but I developed no empathy or sympathy for anyone, and my strongest feeling is I thank my lucky stars I don't run in their horrid little circle. Miserable people, behaving miserablely.

title: It's a Mad Mad Mad Mad Baja World!!
text:
Archaeologist Digby Rigby finds the legendary `Jesuit Treasure' of jewels, then is kidnapped. Digby's sister gets worried when she doesn't hear from him and she hires the intrepid Arizona PI Toozie McGill. Toozie beguiles her buddy the billionaire attorney Atticus Fish to use his seaplane in the search. Atticus & his boy Friday/mescal bootlegger, Skegs, had been using his mini submarine to shutdown illegal fishing...

And They're OFF! An outlandish cast of characters but a compelling and entertaining plot enough for a day at the beach or by a pool.

From the first Atticus Fish novel `Wahoo Rhapsody" - Atticus Fish may be the only crime-fiction hero who ever sued God--and won. It was a class-action suit, against organized religion, really, and the out-of-court settlement made Atticus a very rich and very hated man, prompting him to abandon civilization and retreat (with his millions stashed here and there) to a sand-dune island in Baja, California. Along the way, he almost drowned before being rescued by a maverick charter-boat captain, Winston Weber, skipper of the Wahoo Rhapsody. So, naturally, when Winston finds himself in a scrape, Atticus is ready to help. And what a scrape it is! Unbeknownst to Winston, his first mate, Weevil Ott, has agreed to smuggle marijuana aboard the charter and has planted the dope in the stomachs of a whole lot of freshly caught yellowfin tuna. Yes, we're deep in the heart of crazy-comic-crime-caperville here, and first-novelist Morey capably mixes a bit of Donald Westlake with a little Brad Smith, a touch of Elmore Leonard, and a healthy dose of Carl Hiaasen (Atticus has a lot in common with Hiaasen's off-the-grid ecowarrior, Skink). The caper only gets crazier as a supporting cast of drug dealers, bent prosecutors, and addled tourists get in the way of an elaborate plan devised by Captain Winston and Atticus to buy off Weevil's bosses, dump the drugs, save the boat, and return to their sea-loving, casually hedonistic lives. Morey walks the line between absurd fun and over-the-top silliness with the dexterity and superhuman balance of a veteran drinker acing a highway sobriety test.

title: Not exactly a match dot com dream couple
text:
Six years ago, at age 19, gorgeous college student Regan Martin (daughter of an illegal Mexican immigrant mother and French father) fell in love with a married man - only she didn't know he was married to the daughter of the powerful DeLuca family. He took off with millions in family money, she is left an unwed mother and the DeLuca's see to it that she loses her career, reputation and home.

Now she has a home in the St. Helena Napa Valley, the career she wants & a beloved daughter.

Then she finds out the Deluca family own the winery she now works at. And St Helena is Deluca family central.

Oh no! epic fail! How could she be so savvy in the wine business and not know this information?

Why did the winery hire her? What kind of vetting process do they have?

Greg DeLuca goes out of his way to destroy her again. Not exactly a match dot com dream couple

But reconsiders when he wants to use Regan to recover the money stolen from his sister, and starts to reconsider that Regan maybe the one wronged the most.

title: Not sure I will read another by this author
text:
No crime needed - there is already enough drama for a soap opera. Celeste and Adam have been married over 10 years, Celeste has lost Adam through his addictions and when her violent compulsive gambler husband cannot grow up she needs to walk away for the sake of their son, and does. Jake witnesses Adam chocking Celeste and steps in to help her. Jake has been in a series of bad relationships and is currently involved with Sara a married police detective.

I think the thing that didn't do it for me was Celeste hooking up with a new man so quickly, what kind of example is that for her young son? I would have enjoyed it more had she been a success going it on her own. And I think I needed to see more of the marriage unraveling, I think I never got to know Celeste or Adam as well as I wanted. Jake was also a not very well defined person for me to be interested in.

title: Or, the Perils of Pauline
text:
Hayden lands a dream job with Marin Design Engineering thanks to college buddy Shane. They had lost touch and then Shane shows up with a terrific job offer.

Next thing you know Shane OD's on drugs and Hayden learns the lead project designer on the top-secret project committed suicide. The only clue an encrypted file Shane emails to Hayden right before his death. And it gets worse when the police suspect Hayden in Shane's death.

Great idea! Totally believable storyline.

Hayden and Rebecca, not so great or believable. The writing was engaging and I will try another of the author's novels, I just hope that the author can populate the next with more reasonable and intelligent characters with plausible actions. What started off for me as a good weekend read ended with more eye-rolling than I expected.

title: refreshing story in a period of time I enjoy
text:
It's the eleventh-century England and the son of William the Conqueror now rules. Philippe le Peregrine is the king's emissary. He was cursed by an evil sorcerer resulting in the death of his wife. The curse keeps him from caring for another person as protection against the curse.

Leonie of Bosewood is a human child of a Faerie (tall, radiant, angelic beings), as was her mother. Leonie is an orphan raised by a wonderful family. Philippe has been assigned her protector and through a series of events they are gifted with each other by the king.

The curse on Philippe will compel them to be no more than friends but fate will unite them in preventing evil from overrunning their world.

A nice romance, it's not Mary Stewart or Roberta Gellis, I can't see reading the author again but is was a refreshing story in a period of time I enjoy in a genre that is my favorite.

One of 82 titles published in October via Amazon's Montlake Romance imprint, the author is a 3 time winner of the Romance Writer's of America Golden Heart Manuscript submission Award. For those who enjoyed this title the author has 3 other titles in print.

title: When weren't there Globe Quakes?
text:
Pretty much on the dry side - I would recommend it for academic reading. Or perhaps read a chapter a week. Fascinating look at the beliefs held by one man of great influence.

Wallace Henley authored over 20 books, worked in the Nixon White House, is the teaching pastor at Houston's 59,000-member Second Baptist Church, and develops Christian leaders for church & homes as well as business, education and government.

If you are interested in the author's apocalyptic end of the word view this book is for you. If you are having a crisis of faith this may be for you.

The chapter on Government was very pleasantly not what I expected while the one on education was just what I expected to disagree with (LOL!)

My main disagreement is I don't think this era is so different from others, this is just a different kind of scary. Look at history, there have ALWAYS been upheavals, it's impacting me for the first time and is freaking me out.

title: 12 stories that are all over the map
text:
Sylvie, Anna, Frances, Maureen, Vita - meet at Oxford University, they move to New York where dates, crappy jobs, unplanned pregnancy, roommates, failure, haunted houses, jealousy and cancer take their toll.

Laugh-out-loud momments and mordent humor make this a book easily enjoyed. Top notch writing. The amount of sex, women behaving badly, men behaving badly and smugness may not appeal to a large audience - When I look back at my twenties and add a factor of 10 to my misbehavior I can come close to keeping up with these women.

title: ermahgerd!
text:
This is a sequel to the debut novel `The Dummy Line'. Stockbroker Jake Crosby, we are told, is an outdoorsman. Eighteen months ago in a rural Alabama hunting camp Jake killed two vicious thugs trying to kill him and his young daughter. Criminal Ethan "Moon Pie" Daniels took exception to Jake saving his daughter's life and is plotting further violence.

Set in Mississippi and filled with many caricatures you have seen in movies set in the Deep South I wasn't sure how to take this. Is it serious? Is it funny? Mysterious? A little hunting, a little fishing, Southern Baptists, Football, abusive boyfriends, Mexican drug cartels, Asian drug lords. And plenty of side stories: A million dollars gets stolen and the mob wants it back; three men & a woman in their 80's think up an idea that reminded me of an old George burns movie; and Moon Pie's half brother Levi trying to make it as new lawyer.

It was ok. The writing was what you would expect from a new writer, if you are looking for a change from the ordinary and are looking for a no brainer this might suit you fine or even better.

title: Rape, grisly Torture, Sexual abuse, Gruesome details, emotional Abuse
text:
Too much rape - too much graphic rape - had to give this a pass after only a few chapters, that was too bad because the author can write complex, interesting stories.

Back in 2003 when originally published (BTW I LOVED the cover of the 2011 edition I bought) this was the third in a series set in small town in Heartsdale, Grant County, Georgia where Dr. Sara Linton is a pediatrician (medical examiner for the county); her ex-husband Jeffrey Tolliver is the police chief. His infidelity killed it, sadly Sara is still crushing on him.
The good doctor is brought into examine a suicide (mutilated body) of a young man at Grant Tech, the local college. Her pregnant sister Tessa, under circumstances known only to the author, goes with her to the scene and while by herself is viciously attacked. Next there seems to be copycat suicides. Nope. Turns out the town has a sadist on their hands, no clues, no motive - just terror and appalling violence.

Lena Adams, a campus security guard & former police detective - might hold the key to unlocking the mystery, but she has torment and a past of her own to deal with (her sister was murdered and Lena was tortured and rape by the killer). Horrific crimes go on from there.

If reading about emotional Abuse, Rape, grisly Torture and Sexual abuse (all with Gruesome details) has appeal - this is for you!

title: Always excited to try a "Man Booker Prize" winning author
text:
This novel just didn't do it for me.. The prose was gorgeous at times and over-wrought at others.

I probably would have enjoyed it much more if I had read the first two novels in this series.

I am very glad I read to the end.

ANCIENT LIGHT is the 18th book from the Man Booker Prize-winning (THE SEA) Irish novelist.

Alexander Cleave (in two previous novels ECLIPSE & THE SHROUD) is a stage actor in retirement (years earlier he froze on stage and his career ended) offered his first film role, playing Axel Vander. Before he died, Vander had a relationship with Cleave's wild-child daughter "Cass" (a suicide in Italy 10 years ago).

Cleve is at the point in his life where he is thinking back on his life when he was 15 and had an erotically intense affair with the 35 year old married mother (Celia) of his best friend (Billy Gray). Friends like that I don't need! 50 years on, Cleve is so gonzo by this time in his life he can't determine if the specific memories are true or not. Add to the mix one of the co-stars, Dawn Devonport, is a self-destructive young actress who calls to mind his daughter. Oddly enough the movie is titled "The Invention of the Past". Odder still her character is named "Cora" - hmmm. His wife is pretty much a cypher which I found to be a disappointment.

I wonder if this book will stay with me and require that I read the previous two novels. If I do I will have to change the rating to 4 stars.

title: ok first novel
text: I really felt like I got to know Grace, Michael, Bea and the others - however their actions left me flummoxed. Especially the ending. The stories start when all of Europe is on the brink of World War 1 that has been looming for a decade. The best part is over the next 4 years we see from their Point of View as Bea and Grace make decisions and live their lives. The ending in 1918 and epilogue in 1923 to me were just tragic and the actions of Bea just made me shake my head. Lives had changed but characters hadn't grown. I can see myself thinking on the ending for a while and still not liking it - lol!

title: We have a stiff, also stiff language, stiff characters & stiff plot
text:
I was really looking forward to this new to me author. Maybe it's the translation or a Finnish style. To me, the narrator droned on, making a police procedural a little different and a lot uninteresting.

The main character is more a drifting law student with an unappreciated job (rather than a cop). She seems to have no personality or deep feelings.

There is a crime, a victim and an accusedbut they all appear aimless and depressed so the crime and the successful solution were deeply unsatisfying.

title: I had to know how it ended :)
text:
Atlanta museum curator Deborah Miller (Hartley's The Mask of Atreus also features her), is leading the Ek Balam Mayan archaeological dig of a reconstructed pyramid in Mexico's Yucatan. However she isn't an expert in archaeology or field work. WTW? They find the unexpected, rubies not native to the region.

They are stolen soon after discovery and and the Mexican police try to resolve the murder of a worker with Mayan ancestry whose body was mutilated as if in sacrifice. Miller finds their history stretches back to 1622 northern England where the jewels played a role in the Lancashire witch trials. Archaeologists, Hispanic Mexicans, occultists, Mayan Mexicans, the CIA, MI5 and arms dealers are now in a race to claim them for themselves.

So many plots and sub-plots that the characters and the stories never have time to develop (graduate assistants and fellow archaeologists were stereotyped I thought, geeky, nerdy not much to redeem them). Deborah was neither Indiana Jones or Marion, I did like her intelligence and her tenaciousness, she wasn't someone I would like to share an airplane seat next to. I also never felt like they were ever in Mexico, it wasn't evocative.

title: Good Guys, Bad Guys & Helpless Women buried in descriptive narrative
text:
A political thriller without the thrill. "murder, corporate cover-ups, and corrupted justice that masks political money-laundering" Congress and the Supreme Court. I was super excited to read this novel, my college degree is political science. However by page 147 it was difficult to tell one character from another. I has bored and wanted to stop reading by page 300. By page 506 things hadn't gotten alot better.

It must be just me because this is the Third in the very popular Graham Gage Private Eye series. Bummer!

I did enjoy the angle about corporations and their senior management concentrating so much wealth without creating jobs and impoverishing the citizens. The guided tour of the San Francisco ay area was a nice reward for reading the book.

title: Looking forward to this author's next novel
text:
An ethereal family saga and a novel of Southern California - Epic and yet intimately personal

"The tree is where you leave the bad memory behind so that it doesn't poison your life."

The story opens with the most beautiful writing.

Tragedy has struck a California citrus ranching family at a time when all their dreams are coming together. By page 78 the cruel events of one night tears the family apart. We see them 15 years later gone their separate ways and Claire, who so loved her husband, children and the land, is left only with her beloved land. Her husband, Forster, who once loved the land so much suffers to be near it. Claire hangs on for dear life. At a phase in life when she is most in need physically and emotionally arrives Minna to fill the role of care giver and confidant. It evolves into a relationship eerily similar to that of Rasputin and the Empress almost 100 years ago. A solid ending that you don't always get with novels this etheral.

The only distraction for me were the chapters on Minna's heritgage, I found myself wanting to skim through them - for me they weren't as intense, others my feel differently.

title: Tales of the city - Venice at it's most surreal, Carnival!
text:
Paintings by Victor Carpaccio of Saint Augustine & Saint Ursula, a dog, murder, suicide, mistaken identity, the occult, sex, madness, stalking, quirky characters, and some terrific short stories.

Teresa Lupo, the chief pathologist from the author's Nic Costa series, is Rome's senior police `the Questura' forensic specialist. It's a cold February and Carnival, Venice's celebration for those who died during the Plague in the middle ages is a annual 40-day costume extravaganza that ends at Lent.

After receiving mail from her Aunt Sofia saying she may have to disappear, she and her mother show up. They find Sofia's apartment empty and due to her aversion to organization they can't tell if it is ransacked or not. Chiara leaves and Teresa stays to investigate. Sofia is only ten years older than Teresa and a bit of a wild thing. Teresa reads Sofia's diary, the entry from last week reads "The Goblin". Teresa deduces it's regarding a statue nicknamed The Hunchback of the Rialto.

A manila envelope containing a short story is slipped under the apartment door. After a day hunting leads Teresa reads a story about Sofia but Teresa is also in it. Overnight the ink disappears. WTW? She finds clues in a series of paintings of saints. She reaches a dead end and a new story appears with another clue perhaos leading to Sophia. Teresa learns the author is Arnaud, a legendary French "immortal" stretching back centuries.

Not the routine police procedural, not your run of the mill mystery (although the last chapters tidy everything up) - try the sample and see if it's your cup of tea.

title: Satirical look at government covert operations
text:
This is like one of those Saturday movie serials of the 1940's where each of the 85 chapter sleaves our heroes on the brink of danger with the next chapter resolving the predicament rather tidily. Drummond is a retired appliance salesman now suffering from onset from the dreded Alzheimer's. His son Charlie plays the horses, rather poorly, leaving him in debt to the Russian mob to the tune of $20,000.00 dollars. Drummond wanders from his Brooklyn home, Charlie takes him back only to see their home blown to smithereens.

they survive a hail of bullets unscathed. Was it the Mob? If so, they are lousy shots.
Drummond temporarily breaks loose of dementia's grip and hot-wires a car (I always suspected appliance salesmen had many skills).
the appliance Drummond most recently sold was nuclear detonators to terrorists.
they were faulty nuclear detonators.
Drummond was a spy
he is still an excellent marksman
the CIA is concerned that Drummond's knowledge of the "appliance" is dangerous in combination with the Alzheimers.
Charlie and Drummond on a wild cross country escape
Charlie transform into a chip off the old block

If you enjoyed this, the author's next book `Twice a Spy' should be what you are looking for. Or to get your weekly fix the author is a Huffington Post columnist.

title: Completely enjoyable and mostly unbelievable
text:
Set in Regency England circa 1800? Emma was a foundling raised by the grudging local squire and his wife, eventually working as servant girl and now companion to the widowed Countess of Holmeshire.

The dowager Countess is the sister-in-law to one of the King's sons.

Wil (Wilton) is a wonderful young man, the only child of the dowager Countess who earlier brought a young boy home to raise as a personal debt .

Nicholas is Wil's ward & heir and the toddler is beloved of everyone.

Genny is Wils betrothed, since childhood, and a bit of a wildcard.

Wil and Genny share no interests *sigh*.

With lots of surprises along the way this is a quick read to pass the day. Completely enjoyable and mostly unbelievable.

title: somewhere between Robert B. Parker and Janet Evanovich
text:
If you like a book with lots of stories going on at once & a slew of twists at the end, this is for you! Solid writing and details from this author who is new to me.

After a million dollar lawsuit payout, because Jane can't reveal a source (a call girl with info on a low-life but rich businessman), her TV station where she is a success is forced to fire her. The first assignment to revive her career, at the local Boston newspaper, is to investigate why the Massachusetts Senate candidate's wife is no longer campaigning. Jane proceeds to pursue her own story and not one assigned to her - LOL!

Add to that she is crushing on her new hottie boss and Jakey the cop she worked with earlier.

If you are looking for something between Robert B. Parker and Janet Evonavich this is for you.

title: Loved the cover
text:
I read the review in the NY Times and snapped the book up.

It was ok, but lacked the excitement I was expecting. It seemed to be written by someone who must never have enjoyed the original, because you can't help but be disappointed at how Jim Hawkins ended up.

I kept reading because I thought the idea was so great, but the adventure just wasn't. And I ended up not really caring about Jim or Natty, the end was kind of boring *sigh*. Maybe it needed a entertaining villain like Long John Silver? Maybe if Natty and Jim had some chemistry.

title: Bummer
text:
I read the Sentinel (the second book in this series) and enjoyed it enough to want to read more. I think my expectations were moderate knowing 'Spycatcher' was the debut novel for the author and the series.

Come to find out the two books are clones of each other not alot of difference to keep me engaged - color me disappointed.

title: life at the Russian Royal court circa 1760
text:
I really think the author caught what life, and the people who lived it, was like at the royal court of Empress Elizabeth of `all the Russias' toward the end of her reign circa 1760. It was an enjoyable, interesting read with little depth of character - I felt I knew the era better than the characters by the end.

I can't say that the novel is about St. Xenia mostly because it is told as a memoir by her cousin who she grew up with. I goggled Saint Xenia of St. Petersburg after I finished and very little is known of her. After finishing the story my take away is she was a child/woman of her times who had a psychotic break after two tragedies truck in a short amount of time.

I selected the book solely on the author's reputation from her novel The Madonnas of Leningrad. Gorgeous cover, the story was not what I expected, just go with it - put aside your reason and enjoy the magic.

title: blackmail, corporate espionage, and murder
text:
A job for Hercule Poirot because it seems everyone is a suspect!

35 year old Josefa Rehmer is as smart and ambitious as they come, she works long hours as a executive events manager at an exclusive privately held Zurich leather goods company, Loyn. Werner Schulmann has just been handed the job that Jo was in line to get. Years earlier Schulmann's sexual harassment almost ended her career, now he is her superior and Jo resigns. Next thing you know Schulmann is murdered & Loyn's CEO a suicide (not such a bad thing really).

Slow-going but interesting, however the prose just didn't do it for me, not sure if it was the writing or translation. A complex plot, for me there were questions that weren't answered by the last page, maybe it would improve for me with a second read? The move from Switzerland to Canada was nicely unexpected, and the tour of Zurich and the Swiss country was excellent. I was also surprised at the direction the mystery went.

One thing threw me, the strained relationship with her dad was well told, but what was the deal about her mom dying when Jo was 14 and Jo not remembering her much?

Finally, would you go alone, in private, to confront a friend you think is a killer? Not me.

title: Recovery with help from spirits of departed loved ones in the Pacific Northwest
text:
Planning to retire to the Oregon Coast I was totally into reading this novel set in the Kitsap Peninsula of NW Washington town of Cedar Cove (think Port Orchard near Seattle) at the Rose Harbor Inn,.

I hadn't read the bestselling author and this was the perfect opportunity.

Thirty-something Jo Marie Rose, with her new dog Buster, purchases one of the local bed-and-breakfasts looking for a new life after the death of her newlywed husband while serving in Afghanistan.

Her first guests are Joshua and Abby.

Years ago Joshua's stepfather, now dying, kicked him out of home right before high school graduation. Josh (still bitter, still angry) is back to get some personal stuff left behind. His former neighbor, Michelle (a social worker) will put a crimp on those plans.

Abby is home for her brother's wedding. 20 years ago she skidded on an icy patch of road killing her `Best Friend Forever' Angela. Thinking that everyone blames her, she has not been home since.

Slow to start with three downer stories. The novel becomes a nice attempt to capture the feel of the novels of the 1940's and 50's by Lloyd C Douglas and AJ Cronin, (passionate feelings, but not actions, with tough emotional and/or social problems to deal and resolve). Except the resolution takes 3 days instead of 3 or 30 years. Oh, and the added visits by spirit of departed loved ones.

The details of running a bed and breakfast are fascinating. My dear friends ran a very successful B&B on the Oregon Coast, I'll have to ask them what they think.

While I never came to feel I knew the people deeply, with writing that can be descriptive and beautiful it was a very nice way (warm and cozy) to spend a rainy day at home (with no political ads - lol!).

title: I can't see labeling this as romance
text:
Billy, Sean, Gabby, Izzie, and Sean start kindergarten at the exclusive Atwood School in San Francisco, the hook up is totally cute and you really look forward to 20 years of mostly ups, some major downers, and a happily ever after for each. In the years that follow they are inseparable and become known as `The Big Five'. In this world of privilege the five families are social also as The Bigs become young adults and leave their Atwood home of 13 years for college life. At graduation they make a pact to stay Friends Forever.

I can't see labeling this as romance. Drama, Tragedy, Literature, Fiction, yes - not a romance. As such, more depth for each of The Bigs would have compensated for the alphabet soup of tragedy: alcoholism, anorexia, anxiety, betrayal, car accidents, death, divorce, drugs, depression, failure, hopeless, overdose, suicide, etc.

**SPOILERS ** There is no happily ever after for many of the The Bigs. So much so I went back and read my first Danielle Steel love `The Promise' and watched my dvd of `Crossings' to get that feel-good back from chapter one. My expectations was something along the lines of the movie `The Big Chill' where The Bigs reunite as twenty-somethings, share their tragedys, and celebrate their triumphs, but it wasn't to be *sigh*. And, those that do survive to 25, they get a chapter of happiness, I know I needed a bit more.

PS - I think the author could benefit from a change in editor, someone who isn't intimidated with her legend or maybe the author can go back to her first 10 novels and see the magic she once shared with her adoring readers (one who was, and is, me). With all the entertainment she has given me over 35 years I would relish a new novel from her where the passion and love are epic and true (and I hope she finds the same for herself), this hope will keep me buying Danielle Steel novels.

title: * Natalie is a 30-something artist in NYC unable to make a living with her art (bummer)
text:
* her wealthy aunt has a home on Dragonfly Lake in the Massachusetts Berkshires (sweet!)
* Natalie is house sitting and living her dream while her aunt globe trots for a year (score!)
* Natalie not only learns to swim on the lake she gets rescued by cute neighbor Ben (win!)
* Natalie's brother Slade is a hottie, wears black and rides a motorcycle (DANGER!)
* Natalie and Slade's absentee mother shows up (oh no!)
* Morgan & Josh O'Keefe newly moved into the biggest house in the hood (sweet!)
* 30-year-old Morgan, is now a stay-at-home mom to one year old son, Petey, (aw!)
* She is not liking the full time mother thing (bummer)
* She's missing her job at Weathersfield College outside Boston (oh no!)
* Josh is working late, thinks Morgan will like decorating & being a perfect hostess(DANGER!)
* Slade, is he making moves on Morgan? (rut roh!)
* Can this marriage be saved? (stay tuned)
* Louise and Dennis Barnaby live next door (nice)
* Hunky Ben swims and is a professor at Amherst (sweet!)
* Bella, is a school teacher in Austin, Texas (hmmm)
* She's on sabbatical to care for her mom who has broken her leg (bummer)
* Also running the small family curiosty shop (aw!)
* Bella loves her boyfriend Aaron (win!)
* and he might have a gorgeous job in San Francisco (score!)
* Sadly Bella appears hotter for the store & family then Aaron (really?)
* Slade discovers valuable items at the shop that help Bella pay for renovations (ok!)
* Even though Bella loves Aaron, she is attracted to Slade. (DANGER!)
And there you have it. Superficial, one-dimensional and unbelievable. A little romance, nothing above a G rating. Predictable with little excitement, or surprise (if you don't count mine when after a couple of dates they are talking wedding!), alot of drama, an abrupt ending, picnics and cookouts, a bit boring with a lovely cover. Even the lake setting was just there, nothing more. Nothing here of interest ok to move along.(sigh). Just didn't work for me, I had never read Nancy Thayer but understand her other books are terrific:
Between Husbands and Friends
Bodies and Souls
Moonshell Beach
Morning
My Dearest Friend
Nell
Three Women at the Water's Edge

Nothing here of interest ok to move along

title: Great title, story idea & writing
text:
30-something, Van Hollinger, finds herself twenty years in the future thanks to her friend Jill's custom SUV / Time Machine, which she wrongly assumed was not working! RUT ROH!

Van is ANGRY when she finds out it is no longer 1988. Her friends and girlfriend Patsy are now in their 60's. She tracks them all down and everyone is freaked - when she disappeared 20 years ago all but Jill thought she was gone for good. Jill has been working on time travel ever since to find a way to get her back in time. Van is hopeless and starts a new life for herself no home, no job, no money, and no id. Patsy spiraled out of control when she lost Van and is now a sodden drunk living in a trailer. Bennie, once a hot young thing with no compunction in coming on to a woman in a committed relationship is now a 38 year old hot young thing and wanting Van's action as much as she did 20 years before.

My favorite chapter was the race from the Feds to get back to 1988 ( I only hope they told Van to pick up stock in Microsoft and Apple, Oracle and Amazon). Great title, story idea & writing. Other than that, I didn't find the characters appealing,neither their humor, life choices, interactions with each other or decisions they made. However, if you enjoyed this novel make sure to grab book 2, `Rescue at Inspiration Point'.

title: the world of stalkers, rapists and serial killers
text:
FBI Special Agent Rainey Bell has been on medical leave for over a year and hasn't had a solid sleep the whole time. A serial killer, the `Y Man', kidnapped, mutilated, and left the almost 6 footer for dead. To block out the horror the 40 year old Rainey drinks alone and a lot. To fill her days and evenings Rainey manages her murdered beloved father's bail bond company with 67 year old Ernestine `Ernie' manning the phones and the office while 6'6" Vietnam Special Forces Vet Mackie handles the rough stuff.

It's summer and Rainey is asked by a moneyed high school friend, now State Representative, JW Wilson, to investigate the stalking of his wife of ten years, Katie. Sickeningly Rainey realizes the `Y Man' is back!

The next days are filled with the southern charm and cooking of North Carolina and attraction between two women at crossroads, neither suspecting the depths of their feelings until they can think of no other love.

While the prose isn't as polished as some debut novels can be, the chapter where the sadist gets what they deserve was thrilling.

title: mundane political thriller & conspiracies abound!
text:
30 year old Beecher White is a archivist with the U.S. government. Clementine, Beech's childhood crush, comes to the archive for help. After her mother died, Clem found a document with her father's name on it, turns out the father she never knew was Nico Hadriam! Nico, the would be Presidential assassin from "The Book of Fate", who was committed to a psychiatric hospital ten years earlier.

Beech tries to impress her by showing her the vault where the US President reviews classified documents, they knock the Presidential chair over, a book falls out from a compartment in the bottom, pages have been torn out. It's a dictionary that belonged to George Washington! Soon, the guard who let them in turns up dead. Beecher, is on the run.

Clemmi visits her father, Nico knows about the book! The book was used by presidents since Washington to communicate with 'The Culper Ring', a spy organization that would provide truthie information and advice only to the President. And, there is another inner circle protecting the current President from blackmail!

With the plot overly convoluted, unnecessary side stories, flashback on flashback, buildup at every chapter (121 of them) and not knowing who to trust I finally, in exhaustion, stopped caring.

title: Not the Best police procedural - Nice review in the NY Times
text:
The staccato writing didn't work for me by this author.

The descriptions of the locations were excellent, characterizations not so much. Probably easier to read and keep track if all the characters had names I could easily pronounce and there are A LOT of people populating this book. It only added confusion that two main characters (cousins) had the same last name and first names both starting in `A'. It was a slog through the first third but good enough to read through. Still not decided if I will read another by this author, I probably will though.In an interesting telling, the story unfolds via Sara, as she sits by Detective Fredrik's hospital bed.

Taking place over three weeks and beginning when Arvid Treanus, a vicious arrogant businessman, returns home to his estate in the Baltic Sea on Gotland Island, Sweden after 10 years in Tokyo, ten year after his daughter's, Stefania, death. Four days later his mutilated body is found on the living room floor of his home, alongside his wife, Kristina. Or is it him? Is it the cousin once in love with Kristina? His wife is clearly identifiable while his body is not. Detective Fredrik Broman and partner Sara Oskarsson lead the investigation first notifying the remaining children Rickard who no longer lives on the estate and Elin at school in Stockholm. The `who' in this whodunit was a nice surprise, for myself some of the `whys' went unexplained.

title: Epic - our heroine does not have a pleasant time of it though
text:
Read the series when I was 15 and remember it vividly today! Still think the best was the first book.

Marietta Danver Trilogy:
Love's Tender Fury (1976)
Love Me, Marietta (1981)
When Love Commands (1984)

I know I read these stand alone novels:
Dare to Love (1978)
Once More, Miranda (1983)

The Slipper (1987)

title: heartwarming and fun
text:
A tall brunette, the petite blonde and the sweet, non-explicit love scenes make this a stand out romance

North Carolinian Librarian Margaret Murphy `Syd' takes a temporary position in the Appalachian Mountains of Virginia to get a new start in life after her marriage ends.

Maddie Stevenson, is the local Dr. Quinn Medicine Woman having returned home to take over her late father's practice.

Neither is looking for romance, both are looking for friendship. These strong women find their way to romance, medicine, music and food. Plus, misunderstandings, secrets, death, and a small child needing a home.

David and Michael, own the local Inn and Maddie's dog Pete made the book memorable for me. Maddy and her mother had me missing my mom big time.

title: a Franco version of Peter Falk's Detective Columbo
text:
Set 13 years ago in 1999, It's a `partly' novel, partly a thriller, partly a suspense & partly a mystery - kind of a blender creation thrown together by a new chef.

Klaus Reiner, a hitman with four identities & a resume in accidental deaths, brutally murders four North Americans vacationing in France, it isn't until the last part of the book the reason is revealed.

Inspector Paul Mazarelle (a Franco version of Peter Falk's Detective Columbo) proceeds to investigate what will come to involve the NATO bombing of the Chinese Embassy in Sarajevo and trade agreements between France and the African country Chad.

Because the reader is given what events are coming the suspense comes from seeing the plot unfold. The writing style needs more show and less tell, it just wasn't suspenseful and had more cliché's then I could suspend my disbelief for.

title: I think it would make an excellent movie!
text:
Debut Novel. I really wanted to like this and it is a nice story I just had problems with believability.

We find Army Reserve Captain Madison Brown in a makeshift hospital in Iraq. Luckily the story takes her home to Boston Massachusetts where she is working in a VA clinic

Isabella Parisi, an idealistic young social worker at the same clinic. She part of a devoted Catholic family who adore her boyfriend Ben, even though she doesn't. Isabella and Madison become close through their shared passion to right the wrongs suffered by many veterans. Isabella begins to question her sexuality and starts to re-think her life. Madison is not looking for love, even more so with a straight woman with a boyfriend who is a lawyer. They fall head over heels, then Madison is deployed to Afghanistan.

title: For a debut author the story was original but I couldn't put it in my top ten of 2011.
text:
The reality of falling in love with someone you can't live without.When I first received this book and saw the cover I was appalled - it looked like something I would try to photoshop and fail at. I don't put spoilers in my reviews but this is not a romance with a happily eve rafter which I took by the cover that it would be. Gray Edwards, her parents career military, has set her path on a career as a pilot and she arrives for basic training in New Jersey. Gray goes through basic with Dani Brown and Annie Randall. After the 13 weeks are up Annie continues her education to be a doctor. Gray and Dani qualify for Officer Candidate School. The rest of the novel concerns the journey the three take in their personal lives and careers.

Update 2013 - new cover HUGE improvemnet

title: How much do we truly know about those we love?
text:
friendship, motherhood, work, and marriage - How much do we truly know about those we love?

In the crazy world following 9/11, Washington DC based Kate vacations with her husband Chris and their two young children on Great Rock Island, New England. Like a lot of people Kate struggles with her needs, the needs of her husband and children, and how to mingle them with her career as a pastry chef.

Kate inherits a trunk of journals, from her close friend Elizabeth (dating back to her teenage years) who had died the year before in a plane crash aged 37! Kate and Elizabeth had much in common, both as wives and mothers. The journals reveal an almost parallel universe Elizabeth to Kate. Kate is astounded by the extent of what she didn't know about her friend. This leads Kate to question their friendship, the concepts of loyalty & honesty, and also her own marriage.

It's compelling story especially when you add to it that Elizabeth's husband wants to read the journals, he doesn't know what his wife was doing or going the day she died. It's also slow-moving, thought-provoking, and beautiful. Not just for women, it doesn't speak to all women but I recommend to any guy who is befuddled by the women in his life.

I have been reading a lot of crime, non-fiction and romance so this was a anticipated & welcome treat.

I wish I could pinpoint why it was a struggle to finish. Because it is a by a debut novelist? Maybe I was expecting a book that would resonate with me 30 years from now and this didn't do it for me. It was however a nice weekend read and I will surely give the author's next book a try.

title: Was looking for a police procedural and just couldn't get into this
text:
I gave up after 40 pages, I just couldn't get into the story, the characters or the writing. Was looking for a police procedural, maybe I'll try again in a few years.

John Turner is a retired psychotherapist, a Vietnam vet, former Memphis Tennessee cop who spent 11 years in jail after being convicted of shooting his partner. Now living in solitude (wouldn't you after all that?) in remote Cripple Creek, Tennessee in an even more remote cabin. Laconic local Sheriff Lonnie Bates shows up at the cabin with a hum dinger of a murder and a lovely bottle of bourbon. The body of a young male drifter has been gruesomely murdered and is asking for Turner to aid in the investigation. In the course of the story we also meet the banjo-playing female district attorney.

I had heard of the author's series set in New Orleans and African-American PI Lew Griffin. Cyprus Grove is the first in a Turner trilogy published in 2003, followed by Cripple Creek in 2005 & Salt River in 2008 (or you can get all 3 in one volume "What You Have Left").

title: I like to give every debut author a try
text:
"Alicia Sanders has suffered constant humiliation at the hands of her unfaithful husband and, as a consequence, has been the victim of malicious gossip in the small town of Creswell Falls."

UT OH!

Supermodel Christina Brewster returns to her roots, also in Creswell Falls, after she retires. Christina had a terrible childhood so I would think it would be the last place she would end up.

Lots of plot threads entangle the two, including Alicia's son, Christina's father and Alicia's mother, Christiana's wretched mother, Christina's friend with benefits, Alicia's husband's BFF and an surprising link between the two families.

I think this would have made a better day time televison drama than a novel.

Loved the cover art!

title: I tried to love it so I kept at it
text:
Autumn day 2006, the Isle of Wight, in the English Channel, I'm thinking cold wet bleak. Jack is notified his beloved brother, Tom, (younger by 8 years and unseen for the last 12 years) has been killed in combat (Iraq). Jack, now nearly 40 years of age, was once a dairy farmer, the son of a farmer, in the beautiful North Devon countryside. Mad Cow and Foot-and-Mouth diseases destroyed their former livelyhood ("Jebb Farm" for generations in their family, gone). He and his childhood sweetheart Ellie now run/own a vacation/holiday trailer park, Lookout Cottage, 32 units strong.

At the end of the first chapter we have Jack lying in bed with a shotgun. The thing is I had to read the chapter three times to figure out what the heck was going on - I think it might have made a better movie? We come to find Jack's mother, Vera, died when they were children. She had overseen the farm. The father, Michael, not the warmest of guys to begin with became a bitter old man, driving Tom out of the house at age 18. And it only gets worse.
This is a novel worthy of Eugene O'Neil and an acquired taste - save for a long weekend when all you have is time to read.

I will try Waterland which is considered the best fiction from England in the last 70 years or LAST ORDERS, which won the Booker Prize in 1996.

title: Paid off after 100 pages or so
text: I almost didn't stick with it - I plodded, then skimmed, through the first 100 pages or so and then it finally found it's grove and got as good as the 5 star reviews said it would.

title: travelogue fit for a spread in the NYTimes Sunday Magazine
text:
At 90 pages this was a fun read over morning coffee (or diet coke as I prefer). I got so interested that I googled the website. $2178 per person gets you the author's journey. I love the concept of train travel that comes with the Gold Service -

*Outback Explorer Lounge Car for relaxation and refreshments
*Queen Adelaide Restaurant Car dining and waiter service included in the fare
*Quality wines and beverages for purchase
*Welcome Reception with complimentary glass of bubbly, wine, beer or soft drink
*Cabin Steward service
*In-cabin music and detailed journey commentary available
*Complimentary tea and coffee

Now that I have got a glimpse from the author and his wife (who I am still laughing at only lasting 1 night of a 3 night trip) I think if I have the funds, and have the opportunity to take the trip, I might upgrade even more. The Gold "Superior" Cabin with surcharge of $830 per cabin per night sounds lovely (total $7,000.00)if things aren't woeking out so well in the lounge or restaurant -
*Double size Gold cabin
*Lounge area with a table with armchairs
*3/4 Size double bed additional fold-down single bed
*Complimentary chocolates & Bowl of fruit
*mini bar with complimentary refreshments & Plunger coffee
*Toiletries pack
*DVD player and selection of titles
*Optional room service for meals
*Complimentary bottle of wine with dinner

title: Fascinating but Just didn't do it for me, maybe too introspective?
text:
We have an emotionally distant and internalized 40 something New Yorker. At the request of his BFF from college (who has just died from cancer and who he hasn't corresponded after she left for Paris after graduation) he travels to the Berkshires and meets an equally fragile, emotionally distant and completely internalized widow of 10 years. These are two lost souls who are intensely drawn to each other, which they both find surprising as they are already in relationships where neither is required to be emotionally engaged. They have a whirlwind 2 weeks together, soulmates. Yet you aren't sure til the very last page if they are going to run from, or to, each other. By the parts, the premise sounds wonderful, I just never cared for them, maybe they were both a bit too odd. I got to the end and thought `what was that all about'. Perhaps it would have been a better read if I were more introspective myself?

In the end it just didn't seem real. I put the book on a shelf to reread one day.

title: It made me very sad
text:
When the book begins it was like Adam and his daughter Anne were teetering over the pit of hades (located in Leonard, Texas) determined to dive in and Maurene, the wife/mother, was merely a shadow in her life and theirs.

I had never read any books by the authors, but it appears by the other reviews that this story did not contain the time and care of their earlier books. This story needed more depth, more chapters, more nuance, something that would give you reason to believe that this family can be saved. Dialogue was fine, the characters were very believable, just the plot wasn't. It just seemed like the foundation of the relationships had been tentative from the beginning and got progressily more strained and unhappy for 18 long years - I just couldn't see how anyone could overcome that. I did care for the characters but I didn't like them very much. The father, who is a pastor, blames his daughter for his failures in his career - right there I am thinking he deserved to fail. I didn't care for the daughter who calls her dad by his first name - just disrespectful. The mother reminded me of the wife in the movie The Country Girl - exhausted with life, with everything and everyone.

It was a super positive ending however, I was happy for the family and I am glad I read the book. But would have liked more of an epilogue, those three deserved it (smile). Hopefully the movie can do better. And, I thought the cover art was perfect.

title: A little bit Murder She Wrote and all to the good!
text:
Jane Bunker, the 42-year-old marine insurance investigator and deputy sheriff, formerly a Florida police detective now living in Maine. She is investigating vandalism on a research vessel, that becomes a missing person case, then involves a fatal heroin overdose and an attempted murder. The novel brings her in contact with Maine fishermen, Native American oystermen and a lot more.

This is Ms. Greenlaw's second nautical mystery ("Slipknot" was the first in 2007) and she herself captains a lobster boat because being a novelist rarely pays the rent.

The ending was exciting, the writing natural and the characters interesting or endearing. I am hoping she writes another in this series soon.

title: Casting for Recovery
text:
I love a good romance before any other genre and this suited nicely. I had recently travelled to North Carolina where the novel takes place and I particularly enjoyed reading so much detail about mountains near Asheville. A favorite movie of mine is A River Runs Through It so the fly fishing aspect attracted me also.

Thirty-eight year old, Mia Landan, is a public relations director for the Spoleto arts festival in Charleston, South Carolina (about a 5 hour drive southeast from the river cabin where the story is set). When the book opens we learn she recently had a mastectomy where they removed her breast "Recovering from breast cancer the shock of her diagnosis had left her heart as numb as the white scar on her chest". Her older sister Madeline gifted her a three-day fly-fishing retreat designed especially for breast cancer survivors. She has a fabulous time, feels rejuvenated. At the point I would have signed up for another 2 weeks, Mia instead heads home early to share her joy at coming back to life with her husband, only to find him with a woman in their bedroom. Mia is pole axed, drives for hours and finds herself back at the river. The fly-fishing instructor Belle Carson provides Mia with a deserted cabin she recently inherited from a grandmother she never knew who had became a pariah when she was accused of murdering her lover and then became a hermit after the stock market crash of 1929 wiped out her savings.

I don't want to give more away so just my thoughts on the rest of the book. I didn't have high expectations, I didn't know that the author Mary Alice Monroe was a New York Times bestselling author when I selected the book to read, and I truly enjoyed it. I loved the leisurely pace of the story telling. I especially enjoyed that by the end of the book Mia had more in every way than she had at the beginning. My only reason for not giving the book a better rating is that I never felt I got a full picture of any of the characters, it felt to me like I only skimmed their personalities and I wanted to know them better.

title: Very original! Very sexy!!
text:
The self titled romantic adventure is a farce wrapped in a roller-coaster of scams! This novels flys from one outrageous moment to the next.

Ginette Felstrom is the girlfriend of the 497th richest woman in America - or is she?

Mickey Rapowski kidnapped Ginette to get back at the CEO of her company when she is fired - or does she?

Victoria Greshem is the 497th richest woman in the country and a conniving soulless executive, or is she?

Mickey is in the driver seat - or is it Victoria? or is it Ginette or is it BJ?

Like watching a ping pong match this novel goes from one outlandish moment to the next.

If you enjoyed this novel check out the author's other book 'Falling Star'

title: If you enjoyed this novel don't miss the author's other title 'Green-eyed Monster'.
text:
Rollicking fun. Solid first book from this author. This 186 page novel in the publisher's Matinee line is packed with characters, plot and action. Solly Raynor has taken her three children to visit her sister Janie and Janie's lover Marsha at their Hollywood beautiful resort home. Solly is escaping her no good philandering lover. Into the mix arrives Marsha's good friend and Hollywood stunt woman extraordinaire Gin Ito. The paparazzi arrive in the form of the aptly nicknamed Sniper, along with Solly's cheating spouse Danielle making this story a rip roaring adventure.

Gin and Solly are attracted to each other and while it is probably the wrong time for Solly to get involved Gin is ready to begin living again after a crushing heart break. Packed with passionate encounters and some unusual sexual imagery. This is an emotion packed novel that keeps the characters and the reader always engaged and in the end you are happy to see everyone get what they deserve. Including Sniper who meets her match in Solly and Janie's sister Grace.

title: ER on a Large scale
text:
At almost 300 pages this is a mammoth read!

The novel starts off with a most dramatic chapter and never lets up!

This is the second book in the author's 'That Healing Touch' series and even though I have not had the pleasure to have read 'The Fellowship' first it didn't hinder the reading of this novel.

The novel is set in 2001 Pittsburgh Pennsylvania, amongst the drama of emergency medicine life and the ups and downs, the highs and lows of the daily life that is fraught with embarrassments, tragedy, as well as screwball comedy.

title: Lovely New England Setting
text:
This was a enjoyable quick read with surprising depth.

26 year old Emma has ambitions and is attending Harvard University for a Masters in mathematics. She is close to her mother, as her father deserted them when she was 16 and she has not heard from him since.

Enter professor Nicole Davis and Emma is smitten. As luck would not have it Nicole is engaged to marry. As luck would have it she needs a wedding planner and enlists Emma.

Along the way we meet and understand the families and friends whose lives entwine theirs. Several big surprises and some terrific dialog make this read fly by.

If you enjoyed this novel don't miss the author's other novel -

Face of the Enemy

title: Fascinating
text:
Wealthy 29 year old Victoria lost her family twenty years ago in a fire, and she has spent the intervening years plotting her revenge against the man she holds responsible. No one is safe from her path of destruction, even Danielle who she adored when they were children.

The story takes many twists and turns. At times I was reminded of the romance novels by Rosemary Rodgers I read as a teenager. The novel is loaded with angst, tragedy, passion and huge transgressions against innocents.

If you enjoyed this book don't miss the author's other novel -
For the Love of a Woman

title: Rollercoaster read!
text:
Vivid story full of angst and heartbreak from South America to North America.

If you liked this story you will love the author's new novel 'Compensation'.

From the publisher: In a world where oil is supreme, passions run high and there is always the threat of civil war. It is a world where men rule like kings, but one of its masters -- Raisa Andieta -- is a woman.

Carolyn Stenbeck doesn't understand this world. She is just trying to keep her marriage together. But a storm is brewing. Civil war is in the air and passion, like the coming storm, will soon erupt.

S. Anne Gardner has lived all over the world, and some would say looks at life and lives it in her own fashion. Anne has lived most of her adult life overseas, but now permanently resides in the East Coast of the United States. She guards her privacy, adores her children, and is madly in love with the woman who fills her life.

Anne works in the field of finance. She enjoys reading and writing, horses and her music, among other things. Her love of communication and discussion makes it easy for those who have read her stories to talk with her. She loves to hear from her readers, so please feel free to email her and visit her web page.

title: Owie!
text:
Not for the faint of heart - and totally NOT Vanilla!

These are truly hardcore stories.

The terrific part of this anthology is the story by Radclyffe about a first time visit to a sex club. It is unlike any by this author that I have read. Intense and Raw.

This collection delivers on the promise to be Dark and Dirty,

title: Essays that examine lesbian sexuality, identity, art, pop culture, family and politics
text:
I bought this book as it was noted as having "broadened the parameters in which lesbian sex is discussed." by the author Tee A. Corinne in her book `Courting Pleasure'.

Very engaging and well written

From the back of the book - Brining together the important and controversial ideas of a new generation of lesbian authors. These essays present entertaining and dramatic evidence of the extent to which `the lesbian' is shifting definition...A vital contribution to the ongoing dialogue that records the evolution of lesbian life." - Lillian Faderman

Publisher's Note - This collection of essays illustrates both the vitality and the variety within the lesbian community, with topics such as the politics of butch-femme identity, lesbian pop music stars, and class differences in the lesbian community

title: Enlightening and well written essays
text:
Especially well written was the thoroughly researched essay by the artist and Lambda Award winning author Tee A. Corinne `How Lesbian Artists Support Their Art".

As a bonus each of the essays are accompanied by photos of those profiled and the essayists.

Other outstanding essays -

Alison Bechdel interviewed by Marny Hall

Joan E. Biren 'JEB' Lesbian Photographer, Video producer, Activist

Elana Dykewomon `Changing the World'

The Jewelle Gomez Stories as Told to Amanda Kovattana

Barbara Grier: A Burning Love for Lesbian Literature

Daughters of Bilitis and The Ladder that Teetered Del Martin & Phyllis Lyon

From the publisher's website - Everyday Mutinies is an essential resource on the history and practice of lesbian activism. It also contains valuable ideas for any political lesbian who has wondered how she can possibly pay her bills and make the rent while remaining a full-time activist.

Who are the women who struggled to form lesbian communities--and how did they fund their activism? In Everyday Mutinies: Funding Lesbian Activism, two dozen lesbians--including well-known activists such as Martina Navratilova, Alison Bechdel, Dee Mosbacher, and Jewelle Gomez--tell the stories of their activism, with an emphasis on how they support themselves and fund their political activities. Their examples can help you deal with raising and allocating money. Less than 0.3 of all philanthropic dollars are awarded to lesbian and gay projects each year. Yet Everyday Mutinies shares amazing success stories of women surviving, thriving, and making an impact by using the resources they have with intelligence and skill. You will be moved and inspired by the stories behind Naiad Press, The Ladder, Straight from the Heart, and the National Center for Lesbian Rights.

Everyday Mutinies presents the voices of scientists, political strategists, artists, writers, fundraisers, and community organizers. These courageous women discuss their strategies for getting and using money to pursue their visions, including:

* funding scientific studies in creative ways

* liberating corporate resources

* encouraging responsible stewardship of inherited wealth

* getting paid for working on lesbian causes

* choosing a job to support activism

* financing lesbian media from magazines to documentaries

* giving time versus giving money

title: Anthology of essays from 1980 to 1993
text:
I bought this book to read the essay by Tee A. Corinne "Artist's Statement: On Sexual Art". It provided wonderful insight and was entertaining - as a bonus the editor included 6 pages of the author's work (4 of the pieces I had not seen before).

Excellent introduction by the editor.

This is a Keeper!

From the publisher's website -

An overview of the field of lesbian studies, tracing its history and providing a summation of current work.

". . . offer[s] a wealth of information on lesbian and women's history while providing a comprehensive look at a field of scholarship that is certain to continue to grow in influence." --Sojourner: The Women's Forum

The lesbian is now an accepted subject for scrutiny--she exists, but how do we define her history, whom do we include, and when did it begin? These essays, primarily drawn from Feminist Studies from 1980 to 1993, trace lesbian studies from its beginnings, examining the difficulties of defining a lesbian perspective and a lesbian past--a culture, social milieux, state of mind.

Essays range from studies of such well-known figures as the Harlem Renaissance poet Alice Dunbar-Nelson, to studies of specific historical moments, such as the regulation of sexuality in the Women's Army Corp during WWII. Other essays treat well-known authors such as Virginia Woolf and Gertrude Stein, lesser-known writers from the early nineteenth century to the present, Postmodern definitions of the Lesbian "Queer Theory", and Lesbian invisibility.

MARTHA VICINUS is Eliza M. Mosher Distinguished University Professor of English, Women's Studies, and History and Chair of the Department of English Language and Literature at the University of Michigan. She is author of The Industrial Muse and Independent Women, and editor Suffer and Be Still and A Widening Sphere.

title: Diverse Anthology
text:
I enjoyed this anthology especially the short story by the always well written Lee Lynch and Lucy Jane Bledsoe.

"As important as a lamp" by Carol Seajay was excellent.

My favorite title for a short story "The revenge of Chunky Beef" by Emily A. Levy.

The other authors I was less familiar with so I was happy with the opportunity to read their work -

This is a keeper!

From the book jacket - . This anthology of lesbian

short stories includes works by both new and established writers.

Seventeen storytellers explore such diverse themes as racism, death,

lesbian parenting, prison relationships, and interracial love and

sex. They don't flinch from controversy: their stories also deal with

role-playing, fat-positivity, and intergenerational affairs.

title: Anthology by women about their first time experiences with other women
text:
I bought this because it had a story by -

Honey Lee Cottrell - `Honolulu barefoot submission, 1973'

I had seen her art and was interested in what the writing would be like. I was not only delighted but the book had selections by authors I had read and enjoyed -

Susie Bright - Confessions of a teenage lesbian

Lisa Palac - Low-cut

Marcy Sheiner - Filling up and spilling over

Carol A. Queen - The happy baby

Even the introduction by Shar Rednour `Virgin whispers ` is fun.

Also included are entertaining stories by -

Mimi Freed

June Letoile

Stephanie Rosenbaum

Jackie Strano

Blake C. Aarens

title: Great Opinions on Diversity & Caste Systems, But Slow at Times!
text:
First Thoughts:

Ann Leckie’s style of writing and her gender-bending pronouns take a heck of a lot out of me, a guy who is used to reading normal English. But hey, it’s sci-fi and it’s an interesting story. Ancillary Sword is a tough read in many respects, tends to be over-burdened with detail and mundane goings-on with the inhabitants of Athoek Station, rather than the current civil war with half of the Lord of the Radaach, a conquering race, with a goal of “spreading civilization.”

Story & Plot:

As with most sci-fi authors, there are hidden themes and topics brought up that are disguised in a sci-fi window-dressing. Or in this case salad dressing!

The Radch (I keep wanting to say The Radish), spread their civilization much the way we as the American civilization spread ours. Other races and cultures need to be absorbed, assimilated if you will (to borrow from the Borg of Star Trek) or else not be considered civilized.

There are the conquered races of the planet below, people being used as virtual slaves. In the station there is an area called the Undergarden that is where the undesirables live – little food and water and air, except what they can make themselves. Even the Station Artificial Intelligence doesn’t really give a darn about them. But Breq does!

Themes and Intrigue:

Though the plot tends to drag, the importance of racial diversity, cultural prejudices, and an inner, bitter feeling toward the conquering race without having the nerve to say so, really comes across in the tale.

As well, in the previous book Breq had murdered Lieutenant Awn, an officer of a Justice ship (and Breq was the AI with many ancillary bodies – cool idea) on the order of his Lord and then he turned the gun on her (her?). This resulted in Breq as Ship being destroyed. He preserved his existence in an Ancillary and here he is today, on Atheok Station making amends to the Lieutenant’s sister who is on board the Station.

Anyway, we Readers can see what Breq sees and hear what Breq hears since he is not human and can hook himself into the network. What a way to do a third party narrative!

Some themes:

• Slavery, abolished by the Radch – or was it? Is someone still profiting?
• Breq’s invisible gun which bullets can pass through anything – how will he use this? His Ace in the Hole?
• Relationships between cultures and races. Why live in squander when you can have freedom? The local governor is not too keen about that idea.
• Serving two masters – which Lord is the right one? Whose side are you on?

Final Commentary:

It’s a tough book to read, no doubt! The use of certain words to clarify what their versions of military groups, as we use battalions, or ancient Rome used terms to define their many Legions, so too does this civilization. Takes a while to learn what a Decade is, for example. Best to search Google.

The Author could give us a decent glossary! Her view of Breq as a flawed savior of the dregs of their society is a fascinating look. I don’t like how we have completely ignored that there is a civil war on, but her descriptions and introspection of cultures and world-building is definitely worth the read.

Recommended, though as a second book of the trilogy, so far the first is still the better.

title: Divergent Games, or Tris Meets the Sorting Hat!
text:
First Impression: The Movie was Better!

***

Divergent, a book review

I picked up Divergent on the recommendation of a friend of mine. I had already seen the DVD of the story of the same name so I thought I’d give it a try. Actually, the movie was better!

Story & Plot:

Basic themes of family, groups, betrayal and self-sacrifice pepper the story. Unfortunately you have to also put up with the main character’s whiny self-deprecating, clueless dialogue throughout much of the story.

But I Digress:

A city in the Midwest, Chicago perhaps, is a remnant of its former self. To survive, a large wall was built around the city and a civilization was built based on four merits that cancel each other out. They’re divided into factions: Dauntless, Abnegation, Candor and Erudite. The words speak for themselves.

Beatrice belongs to the selfless group Abnegation and wants to be free of restrictions and go with Dauntless, which seems to be having all the fun. Airhead that she seems to be, she chooses Dauntless rather than the family group Abnegation, thus upsetting her parents and her brother (who also abdicates Abnegation and goes with the smart guys, Erudite.).

Faction before Family is a slogan that is also strewn about the novel and as in the movie is cause of tension between the factions.

Beatrice (Tris) is just a clueless 16 year old in this book. She falls for one of the leaders, “Four.” Yep, that’s his name and don’t give him a hard time about it, darn you!

He falls for her too, but when they see each other in the Dauntless cafeteria, he ignores her. She gets all introverted and wonders why he did that and then comes up with a wrong conclusion.

She does this a lot. Makes a bad call and acts on it.

This character is more frustrating than Bell on “Twilight”! (Actually, I take that back: No one is as bad as Bell on Twilight!).

Movie & Book

The movie is better. In the movie, Tris is naive but not clueless. We get to the end with her in conflict with the bad girl who wants to raise an army of Dauntless mind-controlled zombies. Tris handles it. The end, with a door open for the next film.

In the book, Tris does NOT handle it, but runs away on a train. Oh boy.

I’m leaving a lot out. The point is, you won’t be missing much by skipping the novel and watch the films. Way more entertaining.

And you don’t have to put up with the clueless conclusions of one dizzy Dauntless dame!
