Ok, that's oversimplified, but that's what it felt like. And as I already said, the main character in Arena Road is horrible. He's passive, he's dumb, he's unprepared, he goes into long mental soliloquies. He was just plain unlikeable as far as I was concerned. Worse, I could see no real reason for his first harem participant to join him other than the needs of the plot as constrained by the author.

And the woman isn't any better. Honestly, she was so little developed that I didn't want to care for her. She might have been written to be pretty and athletic, but that was it. She had no personality, no drive, and the dialogue was painful to read.

Lovers of this kind of fiction will enjoy this tale, but its definitely no better than average even for the genre. I can just barely give this 3 stars. I knew that I had been avoiding the author for a reason, but took a risk, and eventually regretted allowing Amazon to convince me that this book just might interest me.

title: I finished it, but wow.
text:
TLDR: Its average for the genre, with a lot of action, but little to no character depth.

Ok, the basics are out of the way. However, the key issue for me was the world building. This tale has a world which appears to have a full backstory and which is a major plot element. Into this world a young man is transported without having prior knowledge and of course he gains powers that no one else has.

In this case the powers are actually based on the plot elements and the world history. We don't know the full history of the world, but at it unfolds during the adventures we learn quite a bit.

Honestly, the amount of background the world has impressed me quite a bit. Great care was put into having a unique world that was more than just a simple fantasy realm.

But that shift seemed to also twist the story. Once again plot armor shows up and its thick. Worse, the characters were weaker than they should have been. It was interesting, but failed to impress me on that front.

Still its not a bad read. Just never felt like one I could compare with the best tales I've read.

title: I feel like I've read this before
text:
I think the only new aspect to this tale is the fact that the girls lay eggs which hatch monsters after a session with the tales hero. Beyond that this was very much a typical Isekai tale where a man who doesn't deserve to become a ruler is transported to another world and is an instant hit with women who will fight for him as he comes into his power and prepares to fight a big baddie who is far too powerful to face in book 1.

Its well written, but otherwise there was nothing special that I want to talk about or recommend.

title: I had worries, but its still not a bad read.
text:
Not a bad read doesn't mean I hated it, but on the other hand it clearly says I didn't exactly love it either.

This is a dungeon core novel that tries very hard to avoid the danger of the core being an emotionless killing machine. Instead Azaria becomes a conflicted tortured soul who is a better killer as a dungeon than any other one I've read about. She wipes out party after party. This is not a case where the adventurers turn back and leave after delving to their limit. No, Azaria always sets up overwhelming ambushes and wipes the party out so there are no survivors.

And in this world, that is almost accepted. Because unlike most dungeon tales that are either Isekai or start in a fantasy world, this world is a future Earth were dungeons were added by alien forces. Although honestly that didn't matter, except for a few references to the death of the US and the city this occurs in being Neo-Chicago.

The side tale with Lance also mostly did not belong. Yes, Lance and Azaria work together, but that generates two otherwise separate journeys for two vast different characters. It left out a lot of individual character growth and interaction. Both Lance and Azaria move around the plot in bubbles where they don't create any long-term relationships.

It just felt a bit stilted, as if the author knows of many of the problems with dungeon core tales and over-corrected. I did enjoy this book, and I bought the sequel, but it was merely a 3 star book overall.

title: It was a snoozer
text:
I don't know what to say here. The grammar used in the writing is good. The story is well edited. The plot actually had a bit of imagination put into it so it wasn't quite as trope-filled as some tales I've run into.

Yet, this story really never impressed me. I think part is that for a "base-building" tale, there was almost no real base-building. And the characters were very bland with development that never felt organic, but was more forced by the story. It just left me snoozing through trying to read this tale rather than riveted by it.

Its still a fair read, so I grant it 3 stars.

title: No new elves, and their still stuck in the bloody apartment (and the secret dungeon.)
text:
This tale has been interesting, but the lack of true character development and plot expansion really rankled. Yes, the MC did leave the apartment (by teleportation) eventually, but for the most part we continue to get the same tale of a morning spent in bed, an afternoon that might have light training and then an evening delving a dungeon that gives out no experience considering the number of monsters fought.

Its become a bit "wash, rinse, repeat" and only makes the character's lack of depth noticable.

I like the idea and the overall plot, but this was definitely more than a bit of a disappointment due to the way the plot is so restricted.

title: I find reviewing this series hard.
text:
I do enjoy this tale. I like the main character, and his harem is interesting, even if they lack depth in so many ways. At the same time I found the near constant displays of at least sections of the stats to be mind-numbingly repetitive. The hero doesn't increase in power often enough to justify the regular displays of the stats.

But it was still an interesting narrative with some plot twists that kept me wondering how this must end.

I can't quite give this 4 stars because I feel that the tale required more attention to the character depth and development. Yet, it is solid, so I give it a high 3 star.

title: Another OP main character discovering his phenomenal cosmic power
text:
I seem to make a fairly regular complaint about the average "harem" fantasy. I dislike when the main character is more about his great powers rather than having him be someone with real flaws and personality.

This book ended up being almost all about how a young chemistry grad student discovers that his grandmother was a powerful sorceress and at her death has given him all of her old magic books. He immediately starts using modern chemistry to discover substitutes for elements of the magical formulas and is the most powerful wizard ever. Yes, as some might say he's "The greatest Evea'!!!"

But I don't really like reading about the greatest ever. I want to read about someone who is challenged to learn and grow, not someone who reads a book once and can immediately summon and capture a greater demon.

And that left me wondering if I want to read more. This is like many harem fantasies a decently written book with a good flow, easy to read prose and no major flaws. At the same time it had flat characters who don't grow and a plot that felt like I had read it thousands of times before. the power of the main character removes almost all the tension, and the usual "Fix" authors have is to raise the power of the challenges the hero must face. Here, that was avoided as its mostly the OP characters massive ignorance of the world he's been thrust into that provides the challenge. But the setup was there as was the usual fawning women with their panties around their ankles (except for the succubus who doesn't wear them anyways.)

For lovers of the genre who just want another serving of mostly the same, this will be a pleasure. But I want more.

title: Just seemed to be more of the same
text:
I've noted that I read quite a few dungeon core and harem tales, and that after a while they seem to become mundane with the plots and characters blurring because the authors just don't put the effort in to make them special. Sadly, this tale definitely slid into that pit.

Its not that the author did not try to make things different with the hero actually fighting against some of the delvers, and his harem remaining small due to the way he adds women to it, but sadly there just wasn't enough of a plot to flesh the characters out. it was more "add rooms", "defeat the evil delvers" *wash, rinse and repeat*. And while our core was a bit resource starved at first, in the end he felt a bit overpowered.

It all added up to a story that never felt unique or special. its not in any way "bad", but it had nothing to make me raise it up over others I've read. Its merely more of the same. If you love the genre, its worth the read. Others may find that there isn't much here.

title: Solid world, but not much character development
text:
It was interesting, but I found that it seemed to lack a really strong build on the characters. Robert himself is pushed around quite a bit by events and circumstance. He's written as someone who can clearly grow to be a great hero, but even at the end of this book he allowed events to occur around him rather than pushed events along on several occasions.

His harem was not a lot better. Yes, they are very clearly and carefully delineated from the rest of the cast thanks to transformations they undergo, but that seemed to be the majority of their development and again I never got a strong feeling that they could drive the plot.

This is not a bad novel. Its a very strong start considering its flaws, but the flaws are there and they impacted my enjoyment just enough that I felt this only deserves a very high three stars.

title: I'll give it 3 stars, but I'll never read a Chris Tullbane book in the future.
text:
I know, I'm saying this is a 3 star book, but I'm also writing off the author. This one is both easy and hard to write. I found the plot idea to be as good as the original, but a combination of 3 choices the author made has left a rather bitter taste with me. And because of those while I'll admit that some people will enjoy this book, I did not and don't want to try any more books by this author.

Warning, I will be mentioning details about things in the early part of the book. Some might call them spoilers, but honestly, they are not significant parts of the plot.

So I had 3 issues, and 2 are editorial details rather than major issues with character and plot.

First, at one point early in the story John gets into his car and its implied he starts driving. Then while driving he starts checking his text messages. It might have been that I missed him stopping, but this is one action that I NEVER want to read about. I have known people in real life injured by people who texted while driving. It does not belong in any book. Honestly, even if John had stopped the car the action would have still annoyed me. Have him check before he gets in the car. For me this was an early major strike against the entire narrative.

Second, This is another minor one, but became a bit of a quibble as I know the San Diego area in our world and the fact that Chris tried to use it, but clearly was willing to play with the geography of the major roads drove me crazy. Early on he has John get on the 52 and then cross both the 5 and 15. The 52 ends at the 5, so you can't cross it while driving on it. (you can cross the 805 though.) If there had not been problem #1, this would have been something I could have overlooked, but after the texting and driving, it just added to my annoyance.

Finally, and this was the one that really got me to throw up my hands. Chris has to quit with the flash-forwards. He had multiple mini-chapters that would be all in italics and which were clearly not in the same timeline as the rest of the tale. it was a side story clearly designed to confuse the reader. Honestly, it felt like an attempt to "subvert expectations." The problem was that I had no expectations on those scenes that could be subverted. All I knew is that the mystery that was slowly unfolding would be interrupted for a scene that appeared to add nothing to the current plot.

It was a trifecta of little problems. The story itself is interesting, although its far more complex than it needs to be, and John is not a good film noir type hero. But I think many readers who can ignore the quibbles I had will enjoy this.

I just don't want to keep struggling through Chris Tullbane's editorial and plot choices. Only once has he given me a hero that I enjoyed reading about, and that was just barely. I think his preferences for character and heroism just don't match with mine, so this will be my last book.

title: I was quickly reminded why I never finished this series.
text:
Man, I've got to stick with my instincts. I read the first 4 books in this set of 8 many years ago. that put me 12 books into what looks like a 24 book series. And this was actually before I tried Michael's other series the Kutherian Gambit which went 27 books long and was broken into 3 arcs of 9 books each.

I rated the Kutherian Gambit arcs as "Solid" "Passable" "Bad". And the first arc in this series "Protected by the Damned" I mostly rated "Good", but as I worked my way through this 8 book arc, I grew bored year ago. Yet, I decided to try finishing the arc and bought the Omnibus.

and soon was reminded what I dislike about Michael's writing style. He just doesn't do characters well, and his villains always seem to operate under a ton of plot armor and infinite resources to cause trouble for heroes that gain power rapidly so they can handle the threats being thrown at them. Its fun, for certain values of fun, but it has a strange mindlessness to it that I struggle to enjoy.

Its not bad work, and for those liking stories that run on high energy, low plot motifs these are probably fine examples of the art. But I've always wanted more character and introspection and I dislike OP heroes and villains and these books switch between villains who can't seem to be stopped and a hero who gains new powers simply so she can stop the latest OP villain constantly.

I just grow weary of the lack of pacing and stop trying to read. Which did happen here again. I will give it 3 stars, as my lack of interest is due to a personal foible and I expect those who can tolerate the OP nature of the characters will enjoy these books. However, I find that I personally just can't recommend them.

title: Its an Eric Vall tale, expect pages of bad erotica surrounded by a half-way decent plot.
text:
The plot idea is interesting. A young man from Earth is somehow spiritually dragged into another world where 3 young women claim to be his priestesses await. Of course, the devoutness of his priestesses vary, as does his own belief in his divinity. But he's a gamer so he plays along and near the end, discovers he can manifest in the world, where he behaves as one might expert if they have read many harem fantasy tales.

Sadly, while the idea is good, the rest suffers from the usual flaws from the genre. The female characters have no depth, and are fantasy fodder most of the time, with the main character often obsessively observing how much flesh is revealed by their priestess garb. The hero himself is worse. He's not intelligent, he's always thinking with his lower head, he is condescending to the girls multiple times. He's just a jerk of the first water that honestly I didn't want to read about.

And after he can manifest in the world I wanted to snooze through the rest of the book as it seemed to become one very long and boring sex scene.

Its not terrible.
Its actually well edited and flows rather well.
but even if this could be considered "porn with a plot". I find that I want a story first, and any sex scenes need to feel organic to the story. The ones here are just there to annoy, or at least I felt that way.

Its 3 star by my standards. not terrible but hard for me to recommend.

title: Must I say nice things?
text:
TLDR: Too much sex, too much illogic, no depth of character, but interesting idea and well edited tale. Can't recommend.

***
So the TLDR pretty much explains how I felt. Honestly I was very hesitant to pick up this book based on the description and realizing that there was a risk the author was going for a subversion of expectations. And that much we definitely get. The "hero" ends up a slave to oversexed women who treat him more as a prop for fetish sex than a real character. And there is a lot of this. Honestly it surprises me to say, but there was more sex and more kinky sex in this book than I find in the more juvenile harem fantasy works that permeate the LitRPG world.

Now this isn't a LitRPG tale, although there are a ton of creatures that appear to have been inspired by a Dungeons & Dragons campaign setting. Honestly, because of the way the plot unfolded this story could have been set anywhere. Sure its underground and primarily in some massive city in the underworld, but this could have been set in some tropical rainforest or great steppe desert for all that the setting mattered.

And that probably is what I took away from this tale. The hero despite a few scenes that are meant to be tense never appears to be in great danger. The other characters are bland and never offer enough pathos to engage with the plot, and the sex was excessive and dragged down an otherwise interesting plot.

Some people are going to say offer many superlatives about the plot and sex and.... That is their opinion. I did not really enjoy this tale, although it is not terrible. I just felt that the bondage/sex slavery antics were off-putting and unnecessary. Honestly, I had forgotten that the author was Regina Watts, but after the second or third sex scene my thought was "this is written by a sexually frustrated woman who wants to dominate a man". While I guess writing out your deviant sexual fantasies can be good therapy, I don't have to enjoy reading it.

title: R.J. was stretching a bit to keep this on course
text:
Another book, and it looks like R.J. is trying to flex her previous plots to allow for the creation of some new villains (she keeps throwing her villains away or converting them) and new plots. (I get a feeling the plots in space didn't play the way R.J. hoped.)

So let's take the Deadly Darlin's, one of the more popular character sets in her universe and add in their adopted "son" and say they are going on a "Road trip."

Of course, this group includes Skyestep so nothing is normal, or routine (unless you consider insanity routine.) The group barely manages to do all of the things they have planned while behind the scenes the Anti-Super Society rises up to cause trouble by going after the class D and C capes who have been trying to live a normal life.

Of course there are cameos by just about half of the characters we've seen so far.

But it felt a bit empty. Honestly, there are too many characters in this series, and none seem to have a great emotional connection to anyone else. Instead we get a lot of characters who just don't appear to have much depth. Even if earlier they got a book dedicated to them, they now play a rather simple role in a story that meanders around without a true resolution. Honestly after book 27 in the series I had avoided getting this book because I had a feeling. Its not bad, and if you love the series its worth collecting, but I think the series has run its course.

title: Amateur writer displays his lack of experience
text:
Let's start in the middle, return to the beginning multiple times, repeat entire scenes, but then reveal its at two different points in the timeline (time is repeating itself.) Worse, we'll have a over-sexed but virgin lust monster who despite being written as a fairly smart nerdy type comes across as a barely functioning moron with an IQ less than 80.

But I'm sure this is not the story the author tried to put together. He has an idea and it isn't all that bad, but he needs desperately to get serious editorial help. the timeline loops on itself in ways to make scenes duplicate in a bad way. Worse, the "hero" spends far too much time whining about how the beautiful Kendall has permanently "friend zoned" him. I can understand how a teenage boy virgin might have that kind of crush, but I've said multiple times that angst and indecision are major turn-offs for me. So for me those scenes are annoying at best and maddening in general.

But my biggest issue is the timeline. It's just badly defined and results in stories going around and around multiple times. This story was readable, and as I said, had potential, but it wasn't nearly as good as the author thought. This is a very low 3 star due to the desperate need for serious editing.

title: I can't do it.... I can't give this story 4 stars
text:
And my title says it all, but of course the question some might have would be "why". There is a simple answer.

Whiny "I can't do it" main character.

Yup, once again an author decided to insert a character who can't just pull on his underpants and do what needs to be done. Instead he dithers, and whines and moans, and.... in general just acts like a little boy being told he has to eat his vegetables. Its not all that heroic and quickly generates a near permanent antipathy towards the character with me.

The story itself has huge flaws, with the villain being far more OP than most, and the people the hero is supposed to be supporting being some of the most venal, cowardly and backstabbing twerps I've seen in a novel in half a decade or more.

But even while I consider so much of this a train wreck, it isn't terrible. It just wasn't fun to read, and I find that it is not a series I'm going to continue, so its 3 stars. There are signs of considerable talent in the writing. But the plot and character choices made by Mike Truk generated a story that I found to be disappointing at best.

title: I don't think I can find a "clue-by-four" big enough...... Not for this MC.
text:
Oh, what a STUPID main character.

Yes, another review and another main character who I felt needs to have his skull checked to see if there is a brain in his head. I'm beginning to wonder why so many authors just can't write about an intelligent man when they write these still fantasy tales about the harem they wish they could have. (I wonder if they ever consider the fact that they write main characters who are over-sexed, buffoons is why no girl wants them.)

Sorry, that was unfair, but it does fit my feelings when reading this book. The MC starts out as a failure and a drunk, who supposedly failed out of some military boot camp partly due to his drinking his life away, but due to some back room politics ends up on a special scouting mission with a female trainee who feels an obligation to him because he stopped a bully early on in the boot camp. And of course, he sobers up for her (not that he had a choice there was no alcohol around.) And discovers that on the new continent he's visiting females with power need a male to Bond to, and he soon has multiple women of power bonding to him as he stumbles through a number of intrigues and set pieces.

Honestly, the action isn't bad, although the villains have less brains than the main character, which I would have though impossible. But that's a product of some truly bizarre world building that definitely didn't meet my, "could this happen in real life" standard by a huge margin. Its just inconceivable to me that Leo believes his world makes sense.

Its not a bad tale overall, but with the horrible start and an MC who should never have been written about, I found that the action and plot (and yes, there is a plot, huzzah!) couldn't completely redeem the story. I can give this 3 stars. Some people are going to like this especially with the sex scenes (honestly, if I want to read sex scenes I know where to find true erotica, not the watered down teenage fantasies in books like this.) But I read for plot and character. Plot we do have here, character..... not so much.

title: It somewhat recovers from a bad start and horrible main character
text:
This book is a "Harem fantasy", worse its written by someone who is entirely too enamored with a couple of specific Manga series and that resulted in an editorial decision I found extremely annoying. But the last third ended up being filled with enough action that I'm willing (grudgingly) to give this a very low 3 star rating.

Honestly, part of me wishes I could force every man who is going to write a harem fantasy to read what I have to say past this point, there were a number of huge issues with this book, and they came down to sloppy thinking on the part of the author.

First, Scott here (for some reason I originally put Tristan, but he's the MC in a different but frighteningly similarly bad harem book.), as is entirely too common with harem fantasy tales is a barely functioning moron. He is dumb. I almost used a line I've actually used in some other recent reviews of wanting to channel Kuni from the movie UHF. "Stupid! You're so STUPID!". Seriously, I get that a huge part of harem fantasy is that the main character must think about girls, girls, girls and occasionally even..... girls! But there is a point where there must be some thought about, I don't know, survival? Food? What is safe to be doing at that moment? Tristan just stumbles from set piece to set piece thinking with his "meat and two veg" and that really makes him a flat character. He doesn't actually engage with the story much early as he's a passenger in it.

Second, this was more unique to Edward, but there is a "fourth wall" in entertainment for a reason, and breaking that is just stupid. Edward has Scott almost thinking to the reader, and its often about Scott's obsession with a manga series about.... Monster Girls. (go figure.). I get that Tristan is supposed to be a barely functioning virginal moron who's only thought is to put his tab A into any monster girl's slot B. heck, even after he's repeatedly warned that the hybrid women of the world he finds himself on don't like being called "Monster Girls", he uses it repeatedly.

Third, in the beginning there was a bit of a continuity flow problem. The attempt to set up a bit of backstory and the heroic death of Scott so that his rebirth in the Monster Girl world made sense jumped around the timeline a bit. He mentions that he started going to the comic book shop at age 11, got a job there at 15, but before that mentions being 20. The flow was choppy, and while I honestly didn't care about the MCs age (mentally he's too immature for it to matter.). I do prefer that stories work with a logical timeline, and this didn't really have one for that section, or at least it wasn't presented in a logical way.

Fourth, kill the sidekick. In this case is an invisible, intelligent piece of parchment that only the MC can see and read. It did serve the purpose of being the "author ex machina" character that drove the plot by dropping in all the information required to force the MC to panic constantly while always withholding information that the MC should have tried to obtain before jumping off the cliff without a parachute. But it also was just annoying. The sidekick characters in harem fantasy tales tend to be dumb, boring and capable of sucking all the life out of a tale, and Parch does that constantly. Once again, its a product of the extremely low intelligence of the characters. They have no sense, common or otherwise. Its not fun for me to read.

Edward did remove the sex from the story ending many chapters with "and a good time was had by all", but offering free access to fully written out sex scenes via the web. I don't read these books for the sex, so that actually was a plus in my book. The problem is that the story did not have a lot of character, and the main character was just well below the very low average that can be found in most books in this genre.

Some might enjoy this, but I honestly feel it lacked on many levels. It's just not fun until late and even then it honestly didn't impress me much. I've read so much better.

title: So much wasted potential
text:
I'm sure Dante sees my name attached to a review for one of his books and starts cursing since my standard rating is just 3 stars and I think he's only managed to get a 4 star review from me once.

The truth is that I find his ideas interesting, and I have to admit after reading Dragon Breeder 1, that his MC here isn't as terrible as most of the MCs you find in harem self-fulfillment fantasy tales.

The problem is that while Mike the MC is better than most you find in the genre, the rest of the cast is extremely lacking in development. And when you combine that with a long and convoluted start that just never came together for me, I found that I had to fight through the story to finish it. Honestly, the big climatic fight from this story was something I skimmed as I was just no longer interested in what was happening.

Dante is a skilled writer, but he does skimp on character development and his story pacing tends to be more sleep-inducing than it should be. This tale just dragged early and the ending was very much lacking in emotional punch as I didn't know enough about the characters to care about them.

This is a fairly average Harem tale, which puts it deep into the mid 3 star range. I can recommend it to anyone who likes Dante's writing style, but I expect many reading this will find it slow and just lacking a good hook to get the reader immersed.

title: Disastrous third act, MC devolves into whiny, angsty wimp.
text:
50% in and I would have given this story a low 4 stars. Even at 70% in I was still enjoying the tale. However, at that point one of his "loves" vanishes and is assumed to be kidnapped. The MC immediately morphs from a slightly shy and low self-esteem hero to a whiny "I can't do it" angst bot with negative belief that he can do anything. And this after he defeated one of the hybrid champions in a challenge fight.

He instantly became the kind of character I loathe. I despise the idea that a 29 year old adult male who is supposedly a hero can turn into a complete zero who will dither and complain about the impossibility of saving someone. Heroes don't suffer from angst when there is heroing to be done. The hero steps up to the plate and does what they have to do. A Sean Connery said in the movie "The Rock". 'Losers try their best, Heroes get it done and then go home to bang the prom queen.' This MC spends 6% of the book in an angst spiral while we wait for him to do anything.

I'd almost give this story 2 stars for that, but the thing is the rest was rather good. Unfortunately, the author decided to pad the length of his tale with completely unnecessary character devolution that should not have happened.

Others will forgive the author because he sneaks in a few sex scenes and the overall idea is great fun. Sadly, my hatred of angst and dithering makes it impossible for me to forgive the scenes I reference here. I just hated what he suddenly became.

Low 3 star due to the angst that started act 3.

title: Even better than book 1, but the same flaws dragged it down to 3 star.
text:
Honestly, I don't like Damian. He's just not a likable MC, and his constant hints that "Yes, I committed all the terrible things I am accused of." have gotten sickening. Honestly Chris needed to decide some time ago if Damian is a villain writing a tell-all from prison the day before his execution, or if Damian managed to avoid the "crow curse" and become a long standing hero. And then stop with the bloody hints that he's still at best a wild-card/anti-hero.

But anti-heroes almost always make terrible main characters. I can't think of any book I've picked up in the last 3 years that managed to make an anti-hero character work well. And Chris is not experienced enough an author to pull it off here.

The constant asides hinting about the future returned from book 1, and again often failed to pay off and the events hinted at don't appear in this book.

Its still a very entertaining series, but the ambition of the author was too high to have me give it anything more than 3 stars. The flaws bothered me too much.

title: interesting, but flawed tale written.... poorly.
text:
Man I want to give this a better rating. This is one of the few superhero tales that approaches a level of realism regarding the intensity of the fighting that must occur. The characters are mostly interesting and have some depth to them, which again holds them well above the standard found in the genre.

Unfortunately, once you get past the good parts, the flaws are there and they leave a bit of a bittersweet taste.

I'll start with the basic one. The "hero" isn't. He's not a hero. He's a passenger in the tale. He's unpleasant. He's unsympathetic. Honestly, I could not find much of a reason to care about him. I was interested in what happened to him, because he is interesting, but I definitely didn't care about him at all.

And the writing style made that worse. Chris would occasionally end a chapter or section with an aside that jumped from the first person past tense, to a strange first person present tense. Many also hinted about events that don't appear in this book or book 2. It is one of a few stylistic things that has always bothered me. If you are going to write first person you need to make it very clear where in the time line the writing is, and then don't jump around. Here, there are flashbacks that are clearly indicated through italics, but the asides are just used seemingly randomly. It's disconcerting and annoying.

Beyond that this book was fairly good. It was an easy and entertaining read. it just ended up feeling a bit less due to some editorial and style choices.

title: Somewhat interesting, but same problems as book 1
text:
There just is no depth to this plot. Yes, Rogan is supposed to "save them all" even though who is included in this "them all" is yet to be defined.

Of course, that results in a plot that appears to have no foundation. This story drops the bad guy from book 1, to have the very cavern they are in fighting them with stone shifting to force the party deeper into the depths. Of course, the rather generic harem doesn't provide much excitement because we never spend time with them sitting around a fire. The few periods where there is much conversation are mostly devoted to the endlessly trite fights between Gamma and Rogan. (sorry, not a new plot device for me. - BORING!)

And the conclusion was just not a climax. It is an ending to this part, but paid nothing out for the time involved. This was readable, but not exactly fun and I give it a low 3 stars.

title: Needed more length, needed more character, needed depth
text:
This one is just below 4 star for me. The biggest issue is that we have an MC who is angsty enough to drive me crazy, along with a time travel / rip van winkle element that wasn't developed enough to help raise the story up. Instead we get what felt like a boiler plate "I fell through the looking glass" type of man in new world, saving damsels and removing their dresses tale.

The characters don't get enough page time to develop, the relationships lack any kind of depth with the sex happening because the MC can "recharge" the girls if they bounce on his happy stick until it spurts rather than from any real relationship. And the way the timeline jumps was a bit of a jarring clash with the rest of the early plot.

Most of this is little. The book is good, and written fairly well, but for me the feeling that the story could have had so much more was always there. I give it a very high 3 star. I think others have done this storyline better, but this does rise up a bit out of the morass that the harem fantasy genre has become.

title: It felt like an outline, with a bland main character
text:
Beige, I shall paint the main character of this book beige.

Not really, but at times he had all the personality of a brick. He's supposed to be an orphan who fell into the job as a mafia don's bodyguard and who gets sent to Brink City to start up a new organization. There is quite a bit of potential in that, if the story can hold to building personalities.

But the only personality that seemed to get any work in depth is the goblin sidekick. I'm sure he's meant to be comic relief, but he reminded me more of a Jar Jar Binks type than any of the more interesting and memorable comic sidekicks that have appeared in fiction over the decades. And this kind of sidekick has become a rather reviled trope with many because of its overuse, or its outright misuse as I'd argue happens in this book. Honestly, while the goblin sidekick is responsible for the MC gaining his great and unusual power that makes it possible for him to win a couple of truly outlandish fights. I would have preferred if the goblin caught a grenade in his mouth and became one with the landscape. I HATED that character.

The rest was rather good. The climatic fight scene starts a bit early and goes way too long, but the overall idea made it so that I'm intrigued about what might happen next. But I can't say I'm on the edge of my seat waiting for the sequel. Its a very slightly better than average tale which makes it a mid range 3 star. Its definitely a book that no everyone will be pleased with.

title: blah, blah, generic, blah, blah, bland
text:
Eric Vail had an idea here. This world is definitely well inspired by the Disney versions of the various princess tales, with this story covering the characters from Aladdin (Jessamine and Jamar) and Cinderella (Cienna) The names are different, but the descriptions of the realms and marriages and lives... etc.

But he wrote this as a bit of a "man transported to magical land" tale, dropping in Joe the Plumber who thanks to his limited knowledge of things manages to rise up and be the hero the land needs.

Of course, this is a harem offering, which means that the princesses get to take off their clothes with the hero. (sadly, I can't say that those scenes were all that exciting.) The rest was a very basic tale with a few twists and turns, but not much more. Eric did try extremely hard to keep the hero underpowered (too hard in my opinion, the characters seem to run away a lot.). And the princesses didn't exactly throw themselves at his feet. (They doth protest too much, me thinks.) But trying to improve the story by not holding to the formula for the genre just made the story more bland than normal.

Its not bad, but there is no real life in the tale. I found that I couldn't care for the hero (he was closer to a zero), and that the relationships didn't seem to have a foundation so they never sparkled and shined. It was just a tale, much like so many others.

Its not bad, so its 3 stars, but I just didn't find much to excite me.

title: Somehow its repetitive
text:
I think Eric has run out of ideas in this series. Once again this whole book seems to play around the MC and his current monstergirls looking to maintain their secrecy to protect him from the Duchess, while discovering that another woman in the town is a threat they must deal with by transforming her in his machine.

Its fun, but the conversation and antics haven't changed much since the first tale. I want to see something new. There are hints of other storylines and plot threads, but those seem to be mostly for setup and potential future books.

Its not a bad series. I just don't know how many more books of hte same I feel like reading.

title: Its a strange and magical world, but the story isn't
text:
This ended up being a story I liked, but didn't "like". If that makes sense. Its a decent idea, and while the characters are collectively not very intelligent, there are a few who are interesting and entertaining at times.

I think the problem is that the characters are thin and lacking dynamically. There just wasn't a lot of substance to many of them, including the main character and his original bunnygirl. Its not that they aren't described. Its rather that they just don't seem to have any life to them.

And with that lack of life, the plot threads just don't appear to work all that well. It was a major problem in the action sequences, which relied on some truly ludicrous levels of magical power and plot armor to work, but which reminded me so much of a CGI'd blockbuster movie where there is little plot, but the director uses technical wizardry and explosions to cover up for the limitations built into the story.

Its not bad, and the idea definitely has a ton of promise, but sadly for me the story didn't work.

title: Mostly felt like filler
text:
I know some readers and reviewers are going to gush about this tale and try to make it sound like the plot advanced dramatically. However, for me the story is so contained and constrained that I felt that no much happened. Yes, the tribe grows, but not through anything really special. Yes, a couple of new far away villains were created, but they didn't bring an immediacy to the plot.

It just felt like this whole book was filler for future books. And I'm not interested in purchasing more filler. Its not bad, but it will be my last in this series for a while. I need to see that its progressed towards an ending before I pick up another book.

title: Almost gave this 2 stars for the cliffhanger ending
text:
There are two big things that this book left. First was the fact that despite some changes and developments the story overall never seemed to move. This read like one giant filler episode from a bad action TV series. There is some necessary plot development, but overall the story is very light despite the number of pages.

The second was the big one, and that is the ending. I've noted in other reviews that cliffhangers tend to be something I have a negative reaction to, and this story ended on a cliffhanger that was also an obvious plot device for the next book. I tend to take stars off when that happens, and this book definitely is very low 3 stars because of the ending.

Its not bad, but there isn't anything to make this story special anymore. The characters are largely disappointing and lack any depth, and the plot feels like its not moving.

title: Editorial Decision made this hard to rate
text:
I like a couple of Laurence's series. His Bonesetter as well as his Hyllis family tales are interesting and fun with good characters and a simple plot.

Sadly, while I think Ell Donsaii was a fairly good character, I found that Laurence's decision to have multiple long segues to examine the mindset and personality of one of hte side characters just felt wrong. I know that many authors recently have had chapters follow someone other than the main character, and that occasionally it does work, but in this tale I found that I did not want, nor did I need to read about this particular character. Every scene involving him until he actually meets the main character would not have been missed had they been left out.

And that leaves me in a strange position. The parts actually about Ell are good to great, probably mid four star range. But with large sections being wasted words, I can't give the overall tale that high of a rating.

Its good, but not as good as Laurence's other works I've read and with the fluff parts, I give it 3 stars. Not sure if I'll try the rest of the series. This one left me a bit too unimpressed.

title: I just don't quite see this as 4 star
text:
Its a good follow up to book 1. It once again has compelling characters. It has drama that many harem tales don't bother with.

and yet, its just not a 4 star book. I think part of the problem is that so many of the characters don't get enough page time to grow and the actions of the characters sometimes didn't quite make sense to me. With that happening, I just didn't get into the book as much as I wanted.

The editing is good. The words flow well, although the sex scenes are as almost is always the case a bit of a joke. It just left something behind that I can't quite put a finger on. I liked it well enough, but that's it and for me that means its an average 3 star tale.

title: An improvement over book 1
text:
Eric Vall is an author that I find myself very ambivalent about. He does come up with interesting plot lines and can spin a compelling tale like he does here.

But at the same time characters in his stories tend to be tropes stamped out by central casting rather than compelling constructions. He also has a major problem with continuity at times, which is apparent in this book as he tries to use flashbacks to complete some of the world building.

Yet, this is a fun if very light book. He does plop in a few sex scenes that add little to nothing to the actual plot, but which were probably expected by most people who enjoy this genre.

In the end, I put this at a very high 3 star. I don't quite feel right giving it four due to the thin characters and meandering plot. But it is a very solid improvement over book 1 and I'll almost certainly check out book 3 when it is available.

title: I find myself wondering what to say about this.
text:
This book just doesn't seem to have left much of an impression which surprises me because it had an epic "Man against an empire" start with a good foundation and characters that might have been great.

I think what diminishes this book is the age of many of the characters. The hero is centuries old, as is the empire and as are many of the leading villains. And they feel old in the reading about them. There is a poignant sadness to their actions and relationships that just drags the book. It makes too many sections maudlin.

Its not bad, although the action scenes get disjointed more than once, and the power levels of main characters turns battles into massive 1v1 fights rather than tactical and strategic contests. (which isn't uncommon in fantasy tales, but it just seems too obvious here, for some reason.)

I liked this tale, but at the same time, I just didn't care about the characters, the situation or what is to come, and that's not exactly good. 3 stars for now. Review of book 2 might not happen.

title: The author's choices really left me annoyed.
text:
wow. Great idea, but.....

First the story started very poorly with a ton of disjointed and confusing action. It fits the fact that the main character doesn't understand what's going on, but it made the first 20-25% of the book very hard to get into, as there was little connection to the main character.

But after that the true huge problem appears. The author chooses to go with the "main character traumatized and turned into angst-bot" plot twist. And as I've said multiple times, I HATE angst-bots. Worse, this one was clearly the "I know this character is a Mary-Sue and I'll use angst as my counter".

That one part made it very difficult for me to want to give this book a high rating. Its not terrible, but the angst levels as well as the faceless overwhelming enemy left me with a very negative impression of the overall plot.

Not bad, but should have been better.

title: man to dragon to........ zzzzz (sorry, fell asleep)
text:
This story is designed to be high adrenaline action with the reader through a seemingly endless series of crises which the hero manages to muddle through.

The problem i have with that, is that the characters end up leaving so little impression that I find my interest in continuing the series is very low. I just don't feel a need to get back into the story as I was bored by the action.

Its well written, but was lacking just a little.

title: Its a product of the genre
text:
This genre has such a wide expanse of possibilities. The authors can really try just about anything. Unfortunately most stories end up like this one. The hero feels a bit unlikable, the world is too malleable, and the side characters lack depth and dimension.

Its not a bad tale, just didn't have anything that really made it stand out. The villain is a distant irritant planning and plotting without getting too active (hasn't he heard the Handbook of the Evil Overlord?) The direct threats are either numerous and weak or temporarily powerful until the hero discovers how to defeat them after which he (or his minions) slaughters them in bunches.

I like the idea that is the foundation for this story, but so far not much is being done with it. Its a 3 star tale. Solid, readable, but that's it.

title: I almost gave this 4 stars
text:
This series isn't easy to describe. It plays in the dungeon core and LitRPG areas, but doesn't fit either exactly. The "hero" is closer to a master gamer who dabbles in both RPG and "god" games. He's given a dead planet to upgrade, but ends up setting up a slow process and then heading to a world for adventure that will hopefully help him grow stronger and be able to add more to his world.

And all to stop some ultimate evil who is described as being so powerful that none will ever defeat him.

Yes, we can perhaps see why I downgraded this to 3 stars despite enjoying the tale. There is a lot of plot armor and overpowered villains going on here.

But the characters are better than you see in many books that dabble in these genres, so I give it a high 3 star and am going to watch for more books in this series.

title: average for the genre.
text:
Well, I'm not sure what I can say about this one. I disliked the start. Never got into the main character. And soon ended up just finishing the tale to be able to say I finished it.

I know this was one of the last "harem fantasy" tales I picked up and that I've been trying to avoid them for some time. Too often I end up hating the main character while figuring that the girls are nothing more than window dressing to help the hero overcome some poorly thought out conflict with a far too powerful villain.

And this story was nothing more than that.

Its average for the genre, but you need to really like the genre to want to read it.

title: Author needs to hold off on adding more plot.
text:
I like the main character. I like the idea of a pantheon with a "outcast" diety. I even like the main's characters spouse.

What this book did wrong for me was rush a huge plot twist and advancement without really giving the characters time to fit into the roles set up for them. We get a few new characters introduced, but none are as strong as they could be because the author is already juggling so many characters. Worse, a few twists were added to build extra tension which were completely unnecessary in my opinion. The "hero" has enough challenges and having more and more dumped on him didn't increase my passion to see if he can overcome this high stakes game of "chicken". It just had me thinking that I should start putting together a "book" on when each plot line will be closed, twisted to avoid closure without penalizing the hero or mysteriously dropped. I don't expect this to happen in any kind of orderly fashion.

Its still a fun read, but Tamryn really needs to stop adding characters and new plot points and needs to look at weaving the ones already being into a sensible tale.

title: End of an arc, but somehow wasn't a fulfilling climax
text:
I ended up feeling like this story didn't really come to an end. There is a huge epic fight and many plot threads get their final moments as the story advances to the end.

But at the same time, it wasn't all that satisfying. I'm not sure how to say more without spoiling the tale.

The characters remain strong, but the intrigue was either overdone or felt like it was an afterthought. Both problems crop up and make the characters less dynamic than they should be.

Just not one of Benjamin's best.

title: I just can't
text:
I can't describe this one. I'll be honest this story is one I could probably give one star to and walk away saying it is a fair rating. Oh was this one a mess.

Of course I do have a saying "Endings are hard". To write that is, and this story ends on what I felt was a very sour note.

But that is partly because the author here went far out into left field to find an excuse to build up to the final climatic battle that is anything but climatic and requires a lack of knowledge of MMOs. In my mind there is no way any MMO programmer would have allowed this finale to even be a possibility. It violates so much of why people play MMOs, that....

Well, let's stay away from that rant and just say "suspension of disbelief" was impossible for me. And that led to an ending that generated a massive "shrug" from me.

Its not unredeemable, but it was definitely not what I look for. I'm going to be generous and give it 3 stars. As I said, I could have gone lower and not felt that I was being unfair.

title: Someone needs to smack sense into this author
text:
Once again my review of this book is simple. There is a solid 4 star story here, but I will never give a book that has all the sex scenes this one does 4 stars (unless the sex scenes are really incredible and these ones are so repetitive and unromantic that I wonder if they could get a sex starved housewife's motor going.)

So like most of this series, I give it 3 stars. Its a good story, ruined by a really bad decision by the author.

title: Just didn't offer anything new
text:
This is a bit of Alice through the Looking Glass combined with a strange flavor of Pokémon or Digimon. Not explicitly, but in the way the plot is developing. The hero is a young man headed to check out something his father told him in a letter. It leads him to a cave and the cave leads to a world where there is magic and girls with powers having been enslaved by an evil being.

Of course, as the hero advances through the plot, he rescues girls and then uses them in the next fight against other enslaved girls, etc. It's in its own way very cliché.

And I have to laugh a bit at the ending. I don't want to spoil it, but I have to say that the cliffhanger at the end made it very clear that the main villain has clearly never read Peter Anspach's Handbook of the Evil Overlord.

Its not bad, just nothing special, so 3 stars.

title: He whines, he whines.  Does he ever quit whining?
text:
I think I've made it clear in other reviews I've done that I consider angst filled main characters to be abominations. I read to escape bad feelings and the kind of inconsistent cipher character that is the MC in this book just annoy me.

It's not a bad story. Heck, the potential of the tale was very high, but the need to write a "harem" tale rather than a good story with harem aspects resulted in a truncated emotional range for the main character.

So I did make it through the book, but I just am not excited about the book and the angst of the MC has me solidly against trying out any sequels.

I'll give it 3 stars, as it is well written, is a good idea for a plot and will probably please a less picky reader. It just wasn't the kind of tale I could enjoy.

title: Not like the first book
text:
The first book in this series is a bit of an origin tale, introducing Oracle and his three female companions. It is more about establishing the characters and growing the relationships.

That's what made it a solid book.

This story was a but too much smut. By chapter 5 there had already been 2 extended sex scenes that added little to the overall plot. There were several more, none particularly interesting to me, and all taking up pages of prose that should have been working to develop the plot and characters. (although there was some character development in the scenes, it was largely stuff that could have been left out or brought out in much shorter scenes.)

The villain also was not well established. The idea of a villain with similar (but greater) powers to what Oracle had was interesting, but it felt extremely misused and led to a very unsatisfying climactic battle.

This just didn't appear to have the care put into it the first book did, and in the end, left me disappointed.

title: Forgettable
text:
I never finished this series. The idea had merit, but the writing ended up just too dull to captivate me. The characters were a constantly shifting group of almost interchangable puppets who supposedly "helped" the hero while also offering him challenges to help him grow.

I tried to stay with this series, but finally had to give up, the story just lacked depth and character.

title: It seemed to just lose focus
text:
The story started out with a few plot holes. Solutions to a couple were hinted at, but overall the story seemed to lack a good foundation. The reason the three big cities were called Paris, Geneva and Rome was never really clarified. It was made clear this was post-apoc and post-nuclear war so a reasonable person might infer that those three cities had been on the mushroom cloud hit list.

And I think that is this tales big problem. There is a story, there is a bit of intrigue. However, I don't think the author had a clue as to how it all really started so once he started trying to put together the story of the various factions and action, he had to keep introducing things that made it clear, we were missing a huge part of the story.

After a while, I just gave up. Its not bad, but it wasn't for me. I want a coherent plot and this just doesn't have one that I can accept. There is too much story missing from the start.

title: I don't think mystery is Benjamin's best genre
text:
When I think of what is Benjamin's best book or series there is no question that his Ancient Dreams trilogy and the Marin's Codex 4th book are by far and away the best of his work. But they are more of action/drama with some romance.

This series starts out as a bit of a spy/thriller with Isalla going to a meeting about something only to be ambushed by other angels and then dropped from Heaven to her supposed death. This story does play up the budding romance between Isalla and Kanae, but the main story is who is involved in the conspiracy and what is the true goal.

Unfortunately, while I enjoyed the romance and the drama of Isalla healing up and wanting to help, the conspiracy just never felt organic. It was necessary for the plot to get moving after a long and slow second act smoldering romance buildup (that seemed to get dumped by the wayside far too quickly.) But I just felt that it wasn't strong.

I think it comes down to where Benjamin's strengths as a writer are in my opinion. He does great building up characters and their relationships, but even in the Ancient Dreams trilogy I found that when he tried to build up the web of intrigue, the story suffers. He just doesn't put enough into the bit characters that have to carry the intrigue and the story feels unfocused.

Heaven's Fallen is good, but we have seen much better from Benjamin Medrano

title: Its.......... (honestly I can't think of a good word to use here.)
text:
I'm supposed to start out by saying a lot of nice things about the story. The funny thing is that as I try to put together what to say I realize that I'd be using "faint praise" for most of my comments.

Super Hero Academy isn't a bad story. That isn't my issue. The problem is that it felt like a bunch of plots that were all equal in their lack of depth and development.

I guess part of this can be explained by comparing this tale to others. The "Academy" part isn't terrible, but Drew Hayes magnificent 4 part Superpowereds tale did the school part far better. Even the Kid Sensation series which only has limited academy moments did it far better.

The villian's kid at a super school even has been done with the Renegade X series and while I thought the main in that book descended into angst far too often, he was a far stronger character than Nick Gaeton is.

And the harem part while cute, also felt like it had little depth. The girls were all lacking in the depth of character necessary to make the relationships seem dynamic. I just couldn't really get into them.

There is humor that isn't forced, but it isn't laugh out loud funny, more "smile briefly and move on" type quick asides.

For a first published story this is not bad. It just isn't spectacular. So it gets my usual 3 star rating. People who love super hero tales and want a slightly different take on the idea of a super hero academy will likely enjoy this one. But it isn't very deep and will leave some readers wishing for more.

title: Its a genre smashup, that isn't a total failure
text:
We have a world of fantasy and magic that manages to go LitRPG not with someone from Earth, but with a general from the army of the main king in this universe. The kingdom's top wizard has somehow created a cut off area of the world where there are LitRPG rules and scoring. The general is sent there as "punishment", but of course he's going to fight back.

And it runs into some of the usual LitRPG problems. The problems are stupidly big and overblown with huge fights breaking out that somehow leave the hero and his closest companions alive (if not completely unwounded.). there are others who quickly side with the hero and he gets the usual bevy of beautiful and sexy women who aren't just capable in some way (2 wizards, 1 archer), but who want him in bed as often as possible (and if another girl joins, so much the merrier.)

Its' a teenage virgin's fantasy in many ways.

Its not terrible, the writing is good, and the main character actually has a personality. But it just doesn't stand out as anything special. it's a LitRPG that uses the genre smashup to try to avoid people pointing out that there is nothing new to make it different from the 200+ other LitRPG tales available.

title: It was lacking something.
text:
The villains ruined this one.

I'll be blunt. I really like the characters R.J.Ross has nurtured in her Cape High series. There have been a surprisingly large number of relatable storylines and characters built into the now 22 books in this series.

However, one thing she cannot seem to do well is write villains. They tend to be way over-the-top in their antics, can hide while standing right next to a hero, and have motives that almost force them to interact with the heroes in ways designed to get them caught.

This isn't a case where a Lex Luthor type openly mocks the heroes while subtly funding the work of a shadow organization that is designed to help them take over the world. In fact other than Herold none of the villains have that level of imagination. Rather its a hidden super trying to manipulate one of the cape high students just to prove they are better than anyone else.

It could be interesting, but the villains end up completely ineffective most of the time despite their supposed great skill. (Nico's abilities tend to unbalance this part of the hero/villain matrix.) And the characters they manipulate are always more put-upon than really bad, which makes them objects to be pitied.

I really wish R.J. would allow her stories to push outside the restrictive boundaries she's placed on them. The other superhero tales I generally support have all had characters die and fights tend to be far more serious because there is a bit of "no barter, no banter, no quarter" aspect to fights which R.J. writes tales with almost antiseptic fights where no one suffers permanent harm.

title: It was what it was, but I can't say what that is.
text:
The sheer thickness of this omnibus is impressive, and the quality of the artwork inside is solid.

However, for reasons I just can't explain the story itself never excited me. It was interesting at times, but most of the time I drifted through looking at the artwork and not really paying all that much attention to the dialogue or what was supposed to be happening. I can't really even say why I did that, only that I wasn't excited by it.

And that is all I can say. It wasn't impressive as a story to read.

title: Writing seemed to not want me to care.
text:
Aaarrgh, just.... *sigh*

I wanted to like this story. It has a very interesting foundation, even if its very similar to Tamer of Dinosaurs and other "man snatched from Earth to fight in war with very high attrition rate."

The problem is that unlike many other stories in this genre, this one doesn't try to show the hero working and succeeding at bringing down the death rate at first. Instead, the appearance of the hero is followed by a comedy of failures, that leaves just about every minor character dead.

Its hard to have a good story when there are no characters. Yes, I can think of a couple of movies that pulled it off, but most fail badly, and this tale definitely limps into the final act with a badly damaged narrative.

In the end, I just don't care for the characters or the direction that Sam clearly wants to take the plot. Its his world, and I hope he's happy, but I'm one and done on this series.

title: Lots of sex.
text:
This story had potential, but just way too much sex. I've read other books where reviewers complained and wondered what they were thinking because there were just a few scenes. This story seemed to rarely go more than 4 pages before the main character and one member of his growing harem were throwing their clothing on the floor and....

And the "magical" powers the main character had surrounding sex and his "seed" were more than enough to have me shaking my head as well. It was clearly well thought out, but I wasn't reading this tale for that kind of story.

Perhaps I just choose the wrong tale. I don't mind sex in my stories, but I wasn't expecting it in this story for some reason. At least not in the quantity that was forced on me while reading this tale.

Still the writing quality was good, and I get a feeling I might feel differently about the tale when I try reading it again. So I can give it 3 stars for now.

title: It's a waypoint in the series, but doesn't do more than hit plot points.
text:
I love this series, but I did not love this book. It starts slow and seems to build on plot threads I found slightly creepy and more than a little disappointing in previous books.

But this seems to be the pattern. RJ will have 2-3 books that disappoint me before publishing one that really impresses me and brings me back to being fully interested in the series. This is one of the ones that falls into the disappointment side.

It's hard to say much more without making more direct complaints about the specific plot points and I want to avoid spoiling this tale. It definitely shows R.J.'s imagination and how expansive the universe could be. Sadly, its not nearly as tight as I believe it needs to be, and that makes me give it a 3 star rating

title: It's a story in need of some focus.
text:
So many books are written about characters with interesting stories. This book definitely falls into that category. There are several characters in this tale who definitely have interesting stories to tell.

Sadly, we never really get to see those stories. T.W. Piperbrook and Bobby Adair committed one of the biggest errors in writing I can remember running into in the last decade. They never decided on a focal character or a main plot line.

This story jumps from character to character and situation to situation. at times it seems to believe we should already know all about past events that helped create the Dystopian society we are reading about. Other times it seems to start opening up the tale of one of the characters, only to slam the box shut and jump to another character as soon as the next chapter starts.

It's a very disjointed way to tell a tale and that is what I remember most.

The proofreading is superb, and the story reads relatively smoothly. My issue was more that the lack of a clear narrative or plot to follow meant that I grew increasingly less interested in the words I was reading. There was a story there, but... It was closed off behind the lack of focus

title: Too many dangling plot threads.
text: It could have been a contender for my best book of the year, but then it seemingly descended into a weird maze of convoluted motives and intrigues.  The demons in this story just didn't seem to have a real presence in the tale.  They existed and did a ton of real harm, but their connection to the characters was a bit too loose in my opinion.  I do understand that the whole world is based on some great war of the gods from some time before and that will drive the overall plot, but the lack of a clear tie between that and the characters took points off.  With a clearer tie to the main arc I think I would have rated this one of my highest four stars for the year.  Instead, its a midlevel 3 star.  I'll real the sequel, but I'm hoping it manages to tie up the loose ends a lot better

title: Weak.  Very, very weak.
text:
Wow. The author had an interesting idea where he had an elderly man pass away, but almost immediately reincarnate as a tiny blond haired faerie with all of his memories from his old life.

It was an idea with a ton of potential. And yet, I can completely understand the poor grades this story has received.

I think I can pin the problem on 3 areas.

1) the author really over emphasized some of the physical changes. Emmy constantly worried about how her body looked and how to do things with a body he/she wasn't familiar with. It was understandable, but it dragged the story down quite a bit.

2) The author seemed to want to have a romance stuck in and one between Emmy and a male faerie, but the approach was so contrived as to leave the romance out of the story. It didn't feel real and it never seemed to fit the character.

3) There is no ending, partly because there is no real conflict in the 3rd act. This was probably my biggest mark against the story. It builds up decently, especially at the start before Emmy runs/is chased away from the first faerie "nation" she visits. But once you leave there, it almost seemed like there was no direction. And after Emmy leaves the second nation there is no real "enemy'. Yes, there are primal forces that demand a response, but they aren't living, breathing enemies. And the nature of the tale meant that the couldn't feel like Emmy and the other characters were fighting against nature. They seemed to just be preparing for something that would or would not destroy them depending on the author's whim.

In the end I just think the writing was weak. Michael did not look into where he wanted to take this and the whole story suffered

title: Too many characters thinned the tale.
text:
Oh, a school for super-powered kids, but this time written from the point of view of one of the teachers/assistant principal. THis has so much potential.

At least that's what I thought. Sadly, it didn't work out that way. Template here never manages to bring back the magic from the first book, and the rotation of characters through the school ended up being a distraction from character growth or a solid plot.

This even more than the first book read like a series of connected short stories without a good main plot to tie them together. The school was often almost an afterthought for the scenes.

This story is well written, but lacked much of what made the first one fun for me to read

title: It did more than books 6 and 7, but still not great.
text:
They moved!

Ok, after more than two books where so many calamities were inflicted on Daniel and his companions I shouldn't be happy that they started moving again, but for me that was the first thing I noticed. A tale that seemed to have them trapped near the home of the Giant Butterflies finally starts moving.

Interestingly, as they move Alexander has several days pass, which appeared to be a way of making up for the fact that so much "action" had been packed into books 5, 6, and 7 that only a few days had passed. This did allow him to move his villains around as well as reintroduce Daemon and his growing band as they discover the horrors being inflicted on the land by the Gemini.

This story pushed the tale far away from harem comedy. The harem aspect is there, as is the fetish based sex scenes (which I personally don't care for, they add nothing to the story at this point.) It's much darker than the first few books, but sadly not any more adult.

I do like some of the character interactions. When Alexander gets away from the fetish play and "punishment" he actually can write interesting scenes. The problem is that his adherence to the tropes of harem comedy in a story that really isn't one anymore result in more than a few chaotic scenes that don't add much to the plot.

The foreshadowings in this tale are strong, and seem to indicate many future problems. However, the lack of a good editor to make sure that continuity of plot threads is maintained makes this a difficult read at times. Just not as good as it could have been.

title: Lots of words, but no payoff.
text:
The story switched away from the darkness that permeated the appearance of Gemini and the massive battles with various insane monsters that filled much of the plot for the last 2 Acts. Instead we now end up blessed with a story that almost never moves in a book that apparently covers only 1-2 days of time.

Yes, For all of this book's length the actual plot doesn't move that much. Daniel and friends continue to travel around, trying to find more friendly monsters and especially ruling monsters who may agree with his quest to get humans and monsters to work together in a peaceful world. Of course, the fact that he has by now 4 lovers (Triska, Alyssa, Squeak and Specca) and another 3 monster companions who are impressed by him (Kroanette, Luna, Falla), there is always plenty of asides, fights, anger issues and poorly written not all that erotic sex scenes. Honestly, this tale wanders into fetish territory a bit too often and many of the fetish scenes are a bit off-putting rather than interesting.

This part of the story also shows the increasingly one-dimensionality of the characters. Even the characters occasionally make observations about how another character has a certain personality. They are all different in some ways but there isn't all that much depth, which makes the romance fall a bit flat.

It's still an interesting tale, even as the one-dimensional characters and overused tropes make it sometimes frustrating to read. I kept working through the series so I can give this part the usual 3 stars

title: A hard tale to like
text:
The "hero" is broken. Even the author admits it through some of the many long soliloquies the hero agonizes through.

And that is the problem. Daniel is such a broken and hateful character that it becomes increasingly difficult to be interested in what will happen next.

The rest of the cast isn't treated much better. Lara disappears for extended sections of the tale. Daniel's children are never given enough page time to really develop beyond a certain point and the love of his life seems to be there mostly for the author to find ways to abuse her gentle and caring nature.

The villains aren't any deeper. There are plenty of hints as to their real nature, but I couldn't get past the lack of any real motivation for the villains. The idea of intelligent trees who have humanoid "seeds" is interesting, but I couldn't figure out how or why the rest all came into being. I read it, and I could if I wanted nod like a bobblehead and say "Yes, I get it.", but while I understand what Michael Manning was trying to create, it just doesn't sing to me. I felt that it lacked a real foundation and forced the plot to unfold a certain way.

It just left me thinking that there had to be more and there wasn't.

I can understand the 5 star reviews. I just don't agree with them. This story will be a one time read for me, its been removed from my Kindle. It's interesting, but I just can't recommend it highly.

title: Nothing gets resolved in this disjointed multiple point of view tale.
text:
Benjamin has the skill as a writer and the imagination to possibly get a 5 star rating from me. someday. Sadly, this story not only didn't get that lofty score, but issues I had with his narrative style and his inability to stick with one person or even one plot dragged this down to a low three star level.

They writing itself is good. I have some quibbles about word choices, but they were minor. The story flowed well and I never got bogged down trying to force myself to read more pages. It was overall a light, but engaging read.

Sadly, while the writing was good and the reading smooth, the plot is a convoluted mess with elements of what felt like six or seven different major plot threads being knotted up around what was either a giant macguffin, or one of the strangest romantic sidekicks ever created. Or at least that was what I felt. Honestly, I can't figure out who is supposed to be the main character. Each switch of POV appears to be a hard switch to a character who could lead their own tale. And while there are a couple of deeper plots involving major nations or their leaders. So little is resolved in this book that its impossible to figure out what Benjamin is trying to say or who are the heroes in his own mind.

It made for a disappointing ending and a book that in the end failed to rate highly in my mind. I can see a ton of talent and imagination, but this story needed someone to focus it and to limit the POV changes so that there is one clear story, rather than a jumble of disjointed plot ideas.

I also will say I saw very little "romance" in this tale lesbian or straight. There is some hinted at parts, but like so many other plot threads those twists are dropped to rush into another plot before the first one is resolved.

title: The character was just like the book, mediocre.
text:
I liked the first book in this "series" a bit more. D.L. Harrison has a very interesting idea here, but the nature of the plot really removed a lot of the emotion from the tale. Yes, there is a romance, but it felt like it was overshadowed, but some of the other plot threads.

Add in the fact that Cassandra just doesn't seem to be focused on anything other than avoiding conflict and you end up with a tale that lacks the bite of Former Dark Mage. Still, I like the lands and world D.L. has created and I'm interested in what might happen in the future.

title: Meh, its a filler-episode was what I thought.
text:
This was just..... meh.

Yeah, I'll go with Meh.

The sad thing is that I ended up feeling like the title was a complete lie. Yes its about Maximum, the character who in previous books had been a man with a mouth and a smile. He made a great showboat and "villain" in the Cape High world as he really didn't hate anyone, but loved to put on a good show.

And the sad thing is this story is supposedly about him putting on a show for his "graduation". That tale had so much potential for him to ham it up with a microphone that I think anyone who loves this series would be looking forward to the tale.

That isn't the tale we get. Instead, we get a bit too much angst and girlfriend confusion. A villain who isn't really defined and worse still doesn't exactly make sense. We even get a couple of scenes were I had to wonder who turned off the IQ of a couple of characters. I ended up not as immersed as many of the earlier stories got me and when the tale ended I didn't want to read it again or read the next book, I just thought. Meh.

Not a sterling recommendation. But I'm not saying its a bad book, it just didn't feel like it fit the characters or the universe properly. I'm not sure what R.J. Ross was writing towards, but this ended up being a filler book rather than a main course of good plots and characters

title: Its not the first book is so many ways.
